patterns.name: Australian Mobile Number
patterns.description: Identifies Australian mobile telephone numbers in domestic (04XX) and international (+614XX) notation. Uses lookaround boundaries to prevent embedded numeric matches. Supports space-only separation between digit groups for high precision.
patterns.operation: Lookaround-bounded regex matching Australian cellular subscriber numbers. Domestic prefix 04 is followed by 8 digits, or international prefix +61 4 by 8 digits, with optional single-space separators. The bare format is discovery-only at 65, generic phone context enforces at 75, and a mobile-specific label plus independent contact-record context reaches 85.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the 04 prefix is Australian-mobile-specific but 10-digit numeric sequences occur in other contexts. Lookaround boundaries reduce false positives from embedded numbers. Corroborative keywords elevate confidence.

should_match.description: Low-tier probe - domestic mobile structure without context
Medium-tier probe - international mobile structure with generic phone context
High-tier probe - mobile-specific label in an independent customer-record context
Medium-tier mobile label without independent record context

should_not_match.description: Embedded in longer number — leading digit prevents match
Prefix 05 is not a valid Australian mobile prefix
Only 8 digits after prefix, too short
International landline prefix (+61 3) is not a mobile (+61 4) number

should_not_match.value: Documentation example: customer record mobile number 0412 345 678
should_not_match.description: Structurally complete but explicitly documented example must not enforce

false_positives.description: 10-digit sequences starting with 04 in reference numbers or dates.
false_positives.mitigation: Lookaround boundaries prevent embedded matches. Corroborative keywords required.

patterns.risk_description: The canonical Australian Mobile Number regex returns a single cellular telephone number in accepted national or international notation. Someone who acquires it may send spam, place unwanted calls, or combine it with public information to target the apparent user. Number portability and routine sharing mean the digits do not reliably identify a person, and the match carries no messages, location history, or service credential. Risk 3 and OFFICIAL therefore fit the ordinary contact datum, with richer subscriber or communications records assessed separately.

classification.rationale: Risk 3 maps to OFFICIAL and Low tiers because the regex exposes only a commonly exchanged contact route whose current holder is not established. SENSITIVE is not met without subscriber attribution, communications content, location data, or another private record that materially raises likely harm.

generic.rationale: One Australian cellular number is generically Low with Low DLM because it permits contact but does not independently reveal a protected profile or secret.

patterns.name: Early Childhood Education and Care Incident, Injury, Trauma and Illness Record
patterns.description: Completed incident, injury, trauma and illness records kept by education and care services (long day care, kindergarten, family day care, outside school hours care), including council-run centres, under the Education and Care Services National Law and National Regulations (regulation 87, record; regulation 86, notification to parents; regulation 183, storage - regulation numbers as listed in ACECQA's Incident, injury, trauma and illness policy guidelines). A populated record names the child (name, date of birth or age), the date and time of the incident, the nature of the injury, trauma or illness, first aid or medication given, action taken and when the parent or guardian was notified. The records must be kept confidentially until the child turns 25. ACECQA guidance, service policies, the regulation text, blank forms and training scenarios are decoys. School incident reports are covered by au-qld-school-incident-report.
patterns.operation: Primary: "incident, injury, trauma and illness record/report/form/register" or an early childhood setting (education and care, early childhood, childcare, family day care, kindergarten/kindy, OSHC, outside school hours care) followed by incident/injury/illness/accident record/report/form. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces policies, guidance and blank forms. 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a child field (child's name / name of child followed by a two-word name, a date of birth, or an age in years or months) or an incident field (dated or timed date/time of incident, injury or illness; nature of injury, illness or trauma, body part, symptoms, first aid given, medication administered or action taken with a word value; or parent/guardian notified with a date or time). 85 requires a child field AND an incident field AND an independent corroborative term (educator, nominated supervisor, approved provider, responsible person, witness, room, first aid, ice pack and similar). Blank lines, bracket placeholders, n/a/tbc and "Yes / No" tick-box prompts are rejected as values. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude policy, guidance and regulation wording (this policy, policy guidelines, policies and procedures, Quality Area 2, approved provider must, must ensure/include, acecqa.gov.au, legislation.nsw.gov.au, Penalty:).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "incident, injury, trauma and illness record" is the prescribed record title and is distinctive, but ACECQA guidance, service policies and blank forms repeat it, so enforce tiers require populated child and incident fields. Regulation numbers are taken from ACECQA's published policy guidelines rather than the regulation text itself (the legislation site was not reachable this session), so they appear only in metadata, not in the detector. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a completed early childhood incident, injury, trauma or illness record that ties a named young child to an injury, illness, trauma or medication event, together with the service's response and parent notification. It is health information about a child, is often relied on in insurance claims, child protection referrals and litigation, and must be kept confidential until the child turns 25. Disclosure exposes a child's health and can reveal family circumstances. Policies, guidance, the regulation text, blank forms and training scenarios are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a completed record ties a named young child to an injury, illness, trauma or medication event, often later relied on in child protection referrals or litigation. PROTECTED is not met by one incident record without protection findings.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling covers a child's health event and the service's response, which must stay confidential until the child turns 25. High would need child protection or bulk content.

patterns.risk_description: The canonical certificate detector recognises one Australian citizenship certificate number through defined prefixes and numeric layouts. The identifier may help correlate a person with citizenship administration or lend detail to a fraudulent verification story when other identity facts are already known. patterns.name: Draft Climate Statements and Sustainability Report (Pre-Release)
patterns.description: Draft mandatory climate-related financial disclosures before release: annual sustainability reports and climate statements under Corporations Act 2001 Part 2M.3 (s 292A who must prepare, s 296A contents, s 296B no material climate risk statement, s 296C compliance with sustainability standards, s 296D climate statement disclosures including the s 296D(2B) two-scenario analysis, s 301A audit) and AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics and targets: Scope 1 / 2 / 3 emissions, transition plan, climate-related scenario analysis, climate resilience, physical and transition risks, internal carbon price), when the document carries a pre-release marker (DRAFT, not for release, embargoed, subject to Board approval, board paper) and populated metrics or scenario results. Published sustainability reports, AASB S2 and ASIC guidance are public and do not reach enforce tiers.
patterns.operation: Primary: climate statement(s), (annual) sustainability report, AASB S2, climate-related (financial) disclosures, climate-related scenario analysis, climate-related risks and opportunities, climate resilience assessment, or a section reference to s 292A, 296A-296D or 301A. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface published reports, AASB / ASIC guidance and commentary. 75 requires a pre-release marker (case-sensitive DRAFT, "Draft v0.x", "Draft for Board / audit committee review", not for release / distribution / publication, EMBARGOED / embargoed until, subject to Board / directors' approval, for Board approval, board paper, pre-release, Commercial-in-Confidence) plus one populated structure within 300 characters: a Scope 1/2/3 emissions figure in t / kt / Mt CO2-e, a percentage reduction target against a year, or a scenario result (1.5 / 2-4 degree C, SSP, RCP or NZE scenario with a dollar or percentage impact, or an impairment / carrying amount / financial impact / internal carbon price / closure or retirement date with a value). 85 requires the marker plus two distinct populated structures (two different emissions metrics, or a metric and a scenario result) plus independent evidence (directors' declaration, climate resilience, transition plan, scenario analysis, physical / transition risk, location- / market-based, limited / reasonable assurance, audit committee, Climate Change Act 2022, Part 2M.3). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude standard-setter and regulator text (aasb.gov.au, asic.gov.au, legislation.gov.au, "Exposure Draft", Illustrative Examples, Basis for Conclusions, "this Standard", compilation headers, article disclaimers).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary terms are statutory and distinctive, but published sustainability reports carry the same terms and populated metrics, so enforce tiers require a pre-release marker as well as populated metrics or scenario results. A draft circulated without any marker stays at 65, and a published report that leaves "Draft" in a footer would be a false positive. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Australian Clinically Coded Episode Record (ICD-10-AM / ACHI / AMT)
patterns.description: Episode-level clinically coded records using the Australian classifications: ICD-10-AM diagnosis codes, ACHI procedure codes (nnnnn-nn), AR-DRG groupings and Australian Medicines Terminology (AMT) concept identifiers, attached to a patient episode or separation - the coded abstracts, coding query worksheets, QHAPDC and Admitted Patient Data Collection extracts and casemix / activity-based funding files produced by health information services. Each record ties a patient or episode identifier to diagnoses and procedures. Boundary: code lists, tabular extracts and coding standards with no episode belong to no classifier here and stay at 65; US ICD-10-CM / ICD-10-PCS codes belong to global-icd-10-cm and global-icd-10-pcs.
patterns.operation: Primary: ICD-10-AM, ACHI, AR-DRG, Australian Refined Diagnosis Related Group, Australian Classification of Health Interventions, Australian Coding Standards, clinically coded, clinical coding, coded episode / separation / data / record, QHAPDC, Admitted Patient Data Collection, Australian Medicines Terminology, AMT code. 65 (discovery only): primary alone, which surfaces coding standards, code lists and education material. 75: primary plus a populated episode / patient field (URN / UR number, MRN, patient name, DOB, episode or separation number, admission or separation date, length of stay, care type, mode of separation) plus a coded value (ICD-10-AM code with decimal such as J18.9 or E11.65, ACHI code nnnnn-nn such as 13882-00, an AMT / SNOMED CT-AU concept ID in the 1000036 namespace, or a labelled PBS item code such as "PBS item 2622B"). 85: the episode field plus two distinct coded values plus a populated coded structure field (principal diagnosis, additional diagnoses, procedures, condition onset flag, DRG, NWAU, WIES). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and coding standard, tabular list, education, index and training framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: ICD-10-AM, ACHI and AR-DRG wording is specific to Australian clinical coding and the enforce tiers need an episode or patient field plus code values in the published shapes, which code lists and coding standards lack. ICD codes without a decimal point (I10) are not counted as coded values, to avoid matching ordinary alphanumeric tokens; a record coded only with such codes reaches 75 through another code or stays at 65.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier recognises Australian clinical coding (ICD-10-AM, ACHI, AR-DRG, AMT) and enforces only when an episode or patient identifier sits with code values in the published shapes, with 85 needing two distinct codes under coded fields such as principal diagnosis or procedures. A coded abstract is a compact statement of a patient's diagnoses, comorbidities and procedures for an admission - including mental illness, HIV, substance use or pregnancy outcomes expressed as codes that anyone with a code book can read. Coded extracts move in bulk to casemix, funding and research teams, so a single file can carry many episodes. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect the per-episode health disclosure; a bulk unaggregated extract would justify stronger handling in the receiving system.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a coded episode ties a patient or episode identifier to diagnoses and procedures that any coder can decode. PROTECTED is not met by the detector, which establishes one coded episode rather than bulk scale; the code values themselves are public classification content.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling protects a patient's coded diagnoses and procedures for an episode. High would need a bulk identified extract.

patterns.risk_description: The detector finds a nine-digit Australian Company Number in grouped or continuous form with company-number context. An ACN is a public corporate identifier displayed on ASIC records and company documents, not a secret, filing credential, or authority to act for the company. False filings or corporate impersonation require identity evidence, account access, and other controls, so the company faces bounded harm from the atomic number alone. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL fit that correlation value, while combination with private director, banking, or authentication data would raise the context toward SENSITIVE.

patterns.description: Detects populated compliance assessment and audit reports: the report title (compliance assessment / audit / review report, regulatory compliance assessment, gap analysis report) together with populated finding, control, status, rating and remediation fields.

patterns.risk_description: The keyword detector targets a compliance assessment or audit report containing obligations, gaps, findings, status, and regulatory-risk analysis rather than an everyday statement of compliance. A true report can disclose breached duties, control failures, evidence weaknesses, and remediation priorities that help a regulated party conceal deficiencies or prejudice enforcement and legal strategy. The affected unit is normally one organisation and assessment, producing serious but bounded legal, operational, and reputational harm. Risk 8 SENSITIVE Legal is appropriate; PROTECTED is not met without a protected investigation, critical-system weakness, or credible significant damage beyond the assessed matter.

patterns.name: Employee Conflict of Interest Declaration and Management Plan
patterns.description: Completed employee conflict of interest declarations and conflict management plans that name the declaring employee (or panel member or contractor), describe the private interest or relationship, and record how the conflict is managed: procurement and tender evaluation declarations, selection panel declarations required by Directive 07/23, discipline decision-maker declarations under Directive 05/23, and Queensland public sector declarations tied to the work performance and personal conduct principles in Public Sector Act 2022 (Qld) s 40. Built conservatively: 75 already needs two populated structures. Councillor conflict declarations in published meeting minutes and registers of interests are public and are treated as decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a conflict of interest phrase (conflict of interest declaration/disclosure/register/management plan/form/statement, declaration of an actual/potential/perceived conflict of interest, actual/potential/perceived/declared conflict of interest, COI declaration/register/management plan/form). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, BOTH a populated declarant field (declarant, employee, staff member, officer, person declaring, panel member, contractor, declared by, position title/number, with a non-placeholder value) AND a populated interest field (nature/description/details of the interest, conflict, relationship or association, interest declared, private/personal/financial interest, relationship to the party/supplier/applicant/matter, with at least three words; or type of conflict: actual/potential/perceived). 85 tier additionally requires a management field (management plan/action/strategy/arrangements, proposed management or action, action taken/agreed, approved or endorsed by, approving officer/delegate, supervisor decision/comments with at least two words; or a date declared/approved or review date) AND an independent corroborative term (supervisor, delegate, procurement, tender, evaluation panel, secondary employment, gifts and benefits, Code of Conduct, Public Sector Act 2022, research integrity, review). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a public-register/guidance exclusion (Cr, seconded, carried unanimously, left the meeting, returned to the meeting, declarable or prescribed conflict of interest, register of interests, register of councillor interests, Register of Members' Interests, fact sheet, this guideline, training module, case study). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium, conservative build: the legal anchors are thin (PSA 2022 s 40 principles, and the COI declaration requirements in Directives 05/23 and 07/23; no standalone Qld COI directive was found), and "conflict of interest" saturates codes of conduct, council minutes and parliamentary registers. 75 therefore needs both a named declarant and a described interest, 85 adds a management plan or approval, and public council/parliamentary declarations are excluded. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic declarations.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's employee / staff id format (see docs/identifiers.md#employee-id). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Corporate Purchasing Card Statement or Acquittal
patterns.description: Corporate purchasing card (purchase card, P-card, corporate credit card) statements, transaction reports and purchasing card acquittals for an identified cardholder: the cardholder name, a masked card number, transaction lines (date, merchant, amount), cost centre or general ledger coding and the supervisor or delegate approval. Queensland Government agencies issue the Queensland Government Corporate Purchasing Card under the Treasurer's Guidelines made under the Financial and Performance Management Standard 2019, which require cardholders to acquit each statement with supporting documentation and supervisor review. A statement reveals where and when a named officer spends, the merchants an agency uses, card limits and coding, and is the record reviewed in card misuse investigations. global-top500-092-expense-reimbursement-claims anchors on expense claims and corporate card acquittal / reconciliation phrases; this SIT anchors on the card statement and transaction report structure, and a purchasing card acquittal can match both.
patterns.operation: Primary: [corporate] purchasing / purchase / corporate [credit] / P- card [monthly] statement, transaction report / listing / register / statement or activity report; purchasing / purchase / P-card acquittal; cardholder statement or transaction report / listing. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one of a populated cardholder field (cardholder [name], name on card, employee [name], staff member followed by a capitalised name), a masked card number (XXXX XXXX XXXX 1234, 4111 **** **** 1234, card ending 1234) or a transaction line (date, merchant text and a decimal amount on one line). 85: primary plus any two of cardholder, masked card, transaction line, populated cost centre / GL / account code / WBS / project code, or populated approver (approved by, approving officer, supervisor, delegate, certified / authorised / reviewed by), plus card-statement evidence (merchant, tax invoice, receipt, business purpose, statement period, credit limit, transaction date, GST, cardholder declaration, misuse, personal expenditure). Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a policy / guidance exclusion (guidelines for the use, this procedure, this policy, policy guidance, training module, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, media release). Field values are placeholder-guarded.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Card statement phrases are specific, but card policies, procedures and training material repeat them, so enforce tiers need populated statement structure and policy framing is excluded. Transaction lines resemble other dated ledgers, so 85 also needs a second structure and card-statement evidence. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a corporate purchasing card statement, transaction report or acquittal for an identified cardholder with a masked card number, dated merchant transactions, cost coding or approval. It reveals a named officer's spending pattern, travel and suppliers, and is the core record in card misuse reviews. The full card number is normally masked, so the record does not enable card fraud by itself; a statement carrying a full card number is covered by the payment card number SITs. Policies, procedures, training, blank forms and aggregate audit findings are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 5 supports OFFICIAL, in line with global-top500-092-expense-reimbursement-claims (risk 4 OFFICIAL); bulk statement extracts across many cardholders, or statements inside a misuse investigation, warrant SENSITIVE handling.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL and Low because a purchasing card statement shows a named officer's business spending with a masked card number, comparable to an expense claim. SENSITIVE is not met for a single statement; bulk cardholder extracts or statements held in a misuse investigation should be handled as SENSITIVE.

generic.rationale: Low handling fits one officer's masked-card business transactions; bulk extracts and misuse investigation files deserve stricter handling.

A malicious recipient could turn the resulting blueprint into a plan for boundary bypass, targeted access, or disruption of an essential service. The likely impact can extend from the asset operator to large service populations and public safety because the matched unit is a composite design. patterns.description: Detects populated data breach reports and assessments under the Commonwealth Notifiable Data Breaches (NDB) scheme (Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC): breach report / notification / assessment titles together with populated breach record fields (entity, dates, individuals affected, information involved, incident reference). patterns.risk_description: The pattern finds a labelled Australian deposit-account identifier after account-number, deposit-account, or bank-account anchors, but it does not require an account holder, BSB, balance, password, or transaction authority. Disclosure may assist social engineering, payment misdirection, or attempted direct-debit fraud when combined with routing, identity, and process information. The account owner faces bounded risk from the atomic reference, and successful financial harm requires several material companion facts and access to a payment workflow. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL therefore better fit what the detector establishes, while co-occurrence with an identifiable holder, BSB, mandate, or live payment instruction would raise the context toward SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to QGISCF OFFICIAL, PSPF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, OFFI, and Low because the detected unit is one account reference requiring substantial additional data for misuse. SENSITIVE is not met without holder identity, routing, authorization, transaction context, or a composite financial record.

generic.rationale: Low generic handling is appropriate for a standalone deposit-account reference with bounded correlation value. Composite statements, mandates, and payment instructions containing the identifier require their dedicated SENSITIVE controls.

patterns.name: Domestic and Family Violence Disclosure in Case Record
patterns.description: Detects client, tenant, patient or customer case records that record a disclosure of domestic and family violence (DFV): case notes, intake assessments, service referrals and payment applications that name or number an individual and state that they have disclosed, experienced, fled or are at risk of DFV, coercive control or intimate partner violence. Sector-neutral: the same shape appears in housing, human services, health, education, justice and Commonwealth support records (Leaving Violence Program, the legacy Escaping Violence Payment, and Crisis Payment for extreme circumstances family and domestic violence). Also covers information-sharing requests and disclosures under Part 5A of the Domestic and Family Violence Protection Act 2012 (Qld) - s 169D (assessing a domestic violence threat), s 169E (responding to a serious domestic violence threat) and s 169F (police referral to a specialist DFV service provider) - made or received by prescribed entities (for example state schools, Hospital and Health Services, housing, corrections and police) and specialist DFV service providers, when the record names the requesting or disclosing entity, the person at risk or the person using violence, the information shared, the reason and the date. The Department of Education's Part 5A Instrument of Authorisation, which quotes s 169D verbatim, and the DFV Information Sharing Guidelines are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a DFV disclosure statement regex (disclosed / reported / experiencing / fleeing / escaping / at risk of, followed within three words by domestic or family violence, DFV, FDV, intimate partner violence, coercive control or non-fatal strangulation) or a Leaving Violence Program / Escaping Violence Payment / FDV Crisis Payment reference. 75 tier requires a populated case-record field (client, tenant, patient, customer or participant name/ID, case/file/reference number, or date of birth with a non-placeholder value) within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires two distinct DFV response terms (safety plan, referral, specialist service, protection order, party roles, refuge) that are independent of the disclosure phrase. Part 5A route: the primary also matches an information sharing request/disclosure/referral, a Part 5A request/disclosure/referral, a request/disclosure/referral under s 169D/E/F, a Part 5A or s 169D/E/F citation of the DFVP Act, or "specialist DFV service provider". A second 75 tier requires a populated Part 5A party field (requesting/disclosing/receiving/providing/ referring entity, agency, organisation, service or officer with a value; person at risk, person using violence, aggrieved, respondent or victim-survivor with a two-word name) or a populated Part 5A detail field (information shared/disclosed/requested/provided with a value; date of request/disclosure/referral; risk level or reason for sharing/disclosure with a value; or a consent status). A second 85 tier requires a party field AND a detail field plus an independent Part 5A evidence term (serious threat, consent not obtained, without consent, reasonably believes, risk assessment, Level 2, CRASF, High Risk Team, safety plan, QPRIME, occurrence number). All enforce tiers exclude template/fixture text and Part 5A instrument/guidance text (Instrument of Authorisation, Column 4, Table of Authorised Officers, Domestic and Family Violence Information Sharing Guidelines, Example for paragraph). 65 is discovery-only (disclosure statement or Part 5A anchor alone), which will also surface policy, legislation and guidance text.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the disclosure phrase is common in policy, training and service guidance, so enforce tiers depend on a populated case-record field to distinguish an individual's record from general text. Free-text case notes without any structured identifier fall to the discovery-only tier. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies an individual's case record that records a disclosure of domestic and family violence. Such records reveal that a named or numbered person is a victim-survivor, often with the identity of the person using violence, children, current circumstances and support arrangements. Unauthorised disclosure can alert the person using violence, escalate risk, and expose highly personal information. Policy text, blank forms and statistics are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy; records that also reveal a refuge or concealed address are covered by au-dfv-confidential-address at a higher rating.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 fits PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because the record identifies a person as a DFV victim-survivor, often naming the person using violence and children, and disclosure can alert that person. PROTECTED is reserved for records that also reveal a refuge or concealed address, rated higher by au-dfv-confidential-address.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to a DFV disclosure recorded in a case file. High handling belongs to records that also expose a refuge or concealed location.

patterns.name: Domestic and Family Violence Refuge or Confidential Address
patterns.description: Detects records that disclose where a person at risk of domestic and family violence (DFV) is living or sheltering: refuge, shelter, safe house and crisis accommodation addresses, addresses flagged as confidential, suppressed or not to be disclosed, and silent elector entries. This is the highest-harm DFV disclosure, because it tells a person using violence where to find the victim-survivor. Sector-neutral: it applies to housing, human services, health, education, court, police, electoral and payroll records.
patterns.operation: Primary: a DFV refuge/shelter/safe house/crisis accommodation phrase, a refuge or safe house address/location label, a confidential/suppressed/withheld/not-to-be-disclosed address statement, a "do not disclose address/location/whereabouts" instruction, or "silent elector". 75 tier requires an Australian street address or suburb+state+postcode within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires a populated person or case field (name, client/tenant/elector, case or file number, or date of birth with a non-placeholder value). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases are strongly associated with concealed locations, but policy text that mentions a refuge address alongside an office address can reach the 75 tier. The 85 tier requires a person or case field, which policy text rarely carries. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

A silent elector record with a street address fires both at PROTECTED (this one PROTECTED Personal-Privacy, the electoral one PROTECTED Electoral Roll); an organisation deploying both should let the electoral policy take precedence for roll-derived records. The electoral classifier also covers name-plus-district and name-plus-DOB silent elector records without an address, which this classifier does not detect. Use this one for cross-sector confidential-address policies and the electoral one for electoral-roll policies; do not stack both in one rule if match counts matter.

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies a record that places a person at risk of domestic and family violence at a refuge, shelter, safe house, crisis accommodation, or an address that has been deliberately kept confidential, suppressed or silently enrolled. Disclosure can let a person using violence locate the victim-survivor and children, with a credible risk of serious injury or death, and can compromise the refuge for every other resident. This is the circumstance the DFV order classifiers reserve PROTECTED for. Risk 10 supports PROTECTED Personal-Privacy; review the classification against the agency's own harm assessment before enforcement.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to PSPF and QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED Personal-Privacy and High because a refuge, safe house or suppressed address tells a person using violence where the victim-survivor and children are, with credible risk of serious injury or death and exposure of other residents. Higher national-security levels are out of scope.

generic.rationale: High with High Personal-Privacy handling applies because disclosure can directly enable violence against the person being protected. No higher generic tier exists.

patterns.name: Domestic and Family Violence Criminal Offence Record
patterns.description: Detects charge sheets, court briefs, court lists, criminal histories and corrections records for domestic and family violence offences against an identified person: Queensland coercive control (Criminal Code s334C, from 26 May 2025) and engaging in domestic violence to aid a respondent (s179A); NSW abusive behaviour towards current or former intimate partners (Crimes Act s54D, from 1 July 2024); Tasmanian persistent family violence (Criminal Code s170A), economic abuse and emotional abuse or intimidation (Family Violence Act 2004 ss8-9); SA coercive control (Criminal Law Consolidation Act s20C, not yet proclaimed); contraventions of protection, intervention and restraining orders in every jurisdiction; and "domestic violence offence" notations (Qld Criminal Code s1 and Penalties and Sentences Act s12A; NSW Crimes (Domestic and Personal Violence) Act s12).
patterns.operation: Primary: any of two regexes — a DFV offence title or notation (abusive behaviour towards intimate partner, persistent family violence, emotional abuse or intimidation, engaging in domestic violence to aid a respondent, domestic violence offence / relevant domestic violence offence / recorded as a domestic violence offence, contravention or breach of a DV order, notice, direction, intervention or restraining order), or a section-anchored coercive control reference (coercive control with s334C or s20C; s54D with Crimes Act; s170A with Criminal Code; economic abuse with Family Violence Act). Bare "coercive control" is never a primary. 75 tier requires a populated accused/defendant/ offender/respondent name field within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires a populated charge-record field (charge, offence, count, plea, court date, date of offence, outcome, sentence, QPRIME QP + 10 digits, NSW H number, QP9 or Court Attendance Notice reference). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: offence titles and DV notations are distinctive but also appear in legislation, sentencing guides, police annual reports and media. Enforce tiers require a populated accused/defendant name; 85 adds a populated charge-record field. Section numbers are only used when paired with the offence name or Act, because 54D, 170A and 20C collide with other statutes. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: DFV incident language is common in police annual reports, media and procedures, so enforce tiers depend on a police reference or a populated party field. The L17 form code alone is ambiguous and is only a primary, never evidence. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

patterns.name: Australian Domestic and Family Violence Protection Order
patterns.description: Detects domestic and family violence protection orders, police-issued notices and directions, and applications for them, in every Australian jurisdiction, when the document names the parties. Covers Qld protection orders, temporary protection orders, Police Protection Notices and Police Protection Directions; NSW apprehended domestic violence orders (including provisional orders); Vic family violence intervention orders and family violence safety notices; WA family violence restraining orders; SA intervention orders; Tas police family violence orders and family violence orders; ACT family violence orders (interim and after-hours); NT domestic violence orders; and recognised DVOs under the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme. Complements the Queensland-specific domestic-violence-order-application classifier.
patterns.operation: Primary: any of two regexes — a case-insensitive order/notice name list across all jurisdictions, or a case-sensitive acronym list (DVO, TPO, PPN, PPD, ADVO, FVIO, FVSN, FVRO, PFVO, FVO). 75 tier requires a populated party field (aggrieved, respondent, protected person, person in need of protection, affected family member, affected person, applicant, defendant or named person, with a non-placeholder name) or a form-style name field (family name, given names, full name, as used under the party headings of court application forms) within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires an order condition (must not approach/contact/locate…, within N metres of, ouster or no-contact condition, weapons surrender, good behaviour) or a published court-form anchor (Qld Form DV1 and version footer, SPI #, NSW Police application number / Central Name Index / NOTICE TO DEFENDANT, Vic FVI01 / Include on Intervention Order, WA PERSON SEEKING TO BE PROTECTED, ACT AF form number, Court File Number). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: order names are published widely in legal information, court forms and statistics, so enforce tiers depend on a populated party field. "Intervention order" and "protection order" are also used outside DFV (for example personal safety intervention orders), which are equally sensitive. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.
regulations: Domestic and Family Violence Protection Act 2012 (Qld)

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies a domestic and family violence protection order, police notice or direction, or an application for one, that names the protected person and the respondent. These documents disclose allegations of violence, relationship and family details, children, exclusion zones and contact restrictions; unauthorised release can expose the protected person to retaliation and reveal untested allegations about the respondent. Legal explainers, blank forms and statistics are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Legal; documents that also reveal a refuge or concealed address are covered by au-dfv-confidential-address at PROTECTED.

PROTECTED is not met by the order itself; documents that also reveal a refuge or concealed address are classified PROTECTED by au-dfv-confidential-address.

generic.rationale: Medium Legal handling protects the parties to a DFV order from retaliation and the respondent from release of untested allegations.

patterns.name: Domestic and Family Violence Risk Assessment or Safety Plan
patterns.description: Detects completed domestic and family violence (DFV) risk assessments, safety plans and multi-agency risk meeting records for an identified person, across Australian frameworks: Qld Common Risk and Safety Framework (CRASF), QPS Domestic Violence Protective Assessment Framework (DV-PAF) and High Risk Teams; NSW Domestic Violence Safety Assessment Tool (DVSAT) and Safety Action Meetings; Vic MARAM; WA CRARMF; SA and NT Family Safety Framework meetings and Positive Action Plans; NT RAMF Common Risk Assessment Tool; and generic DFV risk assessments and safety plans.
patterns.operation: Primary: any of two regexes — a case-insensitive framework/tool/meeting/assessment phrase, or a case-sensitive framework acronym (CRASF, DVSAT, DV-PAF, MARAM, CRARMF). Ambiguous acronyms (SAM, HRT, FSM, RAST, CRAT) are deliberately excluded. 75 tier requires a populated risk level (serious threat, at threat, high, elevated, category 1/2 …) and a populated party field (victim-survivor, person using violence, aggrieved, respondent, client …) within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires an evidence-based risk indicator (strangulation, threats to kill, access to weapons, recent separation, pregnancy, stalking, sexual violence, coercive control, escalation, suicide threats, harm to animals). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: framework names appear heavily in guidance and training, and framework manuals contain example risk levels. Enforce tiers therefore need both a populated risk level and a populated party field; 85 adds a risk indicator. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.
regulations: Domestic and Family Violence Protection Act 2012 (Qld)

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies a completed DFV risk assessment, safety plan or multi-agency risk meeting record for identified people. These records hold the most detailed picture of the danger a victim-survivor faces — lethality indicators such as strangulation, threats to kill and weapon access, children, pregnancy, and the agencies' safety actions — and are shared under statutory information-sharing schemes. Disclosure to the person using violence can defeat the safety plan and escalate lethal risk. Guidance, blank forms and non-DFV clinical assessments are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy; assessments that also disclose a refuge or concealed address are covered by au-dfv-confidential-address at PROTECTED.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 and the Medium tier reflect lethality indicators such as strangulation, threats to kill and weapon access, plus safety actions that fail if the person using violence obtains them. Labels stay PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy; SENSITIVE rather than PROTECTED applies unless a refuge or concealed address is also disclosed.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling with tight need-to-know access applies to one assessment or safety plan. High handling is reserved for records that also expose a refuge or concealed address.

patterns.name: Australian Drug and Alcohol Test Result
patterns.description: Detects Australian workplace drug and alcohol testing records - screening and confirmatory results under AS/NZS 4308 (urine) and AS/NZS 4760 (oral fluid), laboratory result phrasing (non-negative, cut-off concentrations in ng/mL), and breath/blood alcohol readings recorded in fitness-for-work programs.
patterns.operation: The primary regex matches the Australian testing-standard anchors (AS/NZS 4308, AS/NZS 4760), explicit drug-and-alcohol test result phrasing, laboratory result language and recorded alcohol readings. On its own it is discovery only (65), because policies, procedures and training cite the same vocabulary. Tier 75 also requires one populated record structure: a donor / worker field or a populated test field (specimen or chain of custody number, collection date, or a stated result). Tier 85 requires a populated donor / worker field plus a second, distinct structure: a populated test field or a quantitative reading (BAC / breath alcohol value, ng/mL concentration, or a drug class with its result). Enforce tiers exclude template fixtures and policy / procedure wording.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium on the primary alone: the AS/NZS standard citations and non-negative / cut-off laboratory phrasing are distinctive of testing records, but the same standards are cited in workplace policies, procedures and training material that hold no individual result. The Purview tiers gate 75 on one populated record structure and 85 on a populated donor field plus a populated test field or quantitative reading, which separates individual results from program documents.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to an individual drug or alcohol test outcome. It is not High because the harm is employment and reputational damage within one worker's case.

patterns.name: NCCD Student Disability Adjustment Record
patterns.description: Nationally Consistent Collection of Data on School Students with Disability (NCCD) records for a named student: disability category, level of adjustment and the evidence of adjustments provided.
patterns.operation: Primary: NCCD Student Disability Adjustment Record anchors taken from published forms, statutes and procedures. 75 tier requires a populated record field (person, identifier or reference label with a non-placeholder value) within 300 characters. 85 tier requires two distinct populated record fields plus an independent corroborative term. All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface guidance, blank forms and statistics.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: primary anchors are distinctive form titles and statutory terms, but they also appear in guidance, blank forms and statistics, so enforce tiers require populated record structure. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic records laid out like the published forms.

customisation.note: Extend the record-structure evidence with the customer's Education Queensland student ID (EQ ID) format (see docs/identifiers.md#qld-eq-id). The public fallback is the documented labelled-field regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a nccd student disability adjustment record about an identified person, gated on populated record fields. Nationally Consistent Collection of Data on School Students with Disability (NCCD) records for a named student: disability category, level of adjustment and the evidence of adjustments provided. Unauthorised disclosure exposes highly personal circumstances and can cause harm, discrimination or retaliation. Guidance, blank forms and statistics are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a populated NCCD record states a named student's disability category, level of adjustment and the evidence behind it. PROTECTED is not met by one student's adjustment record, which exposes disability status without safety or bulk consequences.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to a child's disability classification and adjustment evidence. High is not met for an individual record.

patterns.name: Confidential University Research Invention Disclosure
patterns.description: Detects populated confidential university research invention disclosures: an invention disclosure / research commercialisation disclosure heading combined with labelled inventor, invention title or technical-description fields carrying real values. Phrase-only mentions (policy, process pages, news) stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex). Primary: research/university/confidential invention disclosure, invention disclosure form/record, research commercialisation disclosure, IP disclosure form. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated field - inventor/lead researcher/chief investigator name, invention or technology title, or novel feature/technical description/commercial application text. 85: primary plus two distinct field types (the four above plus disclosure number/date, faculty, funding source or grant number) plus confidentiality evidence (confidential invention, patent filing pending, provisional patent, prior art search, inventorship, IP ownership). Template/sample framing and guidance/news framing are excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers require labelled inventor, title or technical-description values beside the disclosure heading; blank forms (placeholder values) and guidance fail the placeholder guard and exclusion groups. Published patent abstracts share the field labels but lack the disclosure heading. Medium, not high, because internal research-office paperwork with the same headings can still match.
patterns.risk_description: A populated confidential university research invention disclosure can expose confidential education information. Classification is a package mapping, not a determination of every document's risk. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated record structure (labelled fields with real values, identifiers or data rows); phrase-only mentions in guidance, marketing, blank forms and news stay at 65 discovery.

references.title: IP Australia - What to consider before applying for a patent (public disclosure destroys novelty)

classification.rationale: Populated confidential university research invention disclosure maps to SENSITIVE InfoTech. The classifier requires record context and corroborating fields. The mapping does not determine the risk of every matched document.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling applies to the populated record. Synthetic checks establish local matching behavior, not tenant detection accuracy.

patterns.name: School-Held Student Court Order Record (Family Law and Domestic Violence Orders)
patterns.description: School records showing that a student is the subject of a current family law order or a domestic violence order: the completed "Court Orders" section of the Queensland state school Application for Student Enrolment Form (SEF-1 V8, approved under the Education (General Provisions) Act 2006) - "Family Court Orders" (orders made pursuant to the Family Law Act 1975 concerning the welfare, safety or parenting arrangements of the student) and "Other Court Orders" (such as a domestic violence order) with commencement and end dates - and school file notes recording a parenting or protection order held for a student and the person who may not collect or contact the student. The blank SEF-1 form contains every anchor phrase and is a decoy; enforce tiers need populated order dates and a named student or restricted person. Complements au-qld-student-enrolment-form (form detection) and au-education-guardian-collection-record (collection permissions), which do not tier on court-order content.
patterns.operation: Primary: a court-order phrase (Family Court Order(s), Other Court Order(s), orders made pursuant to the Family Law Act 1975, family law order, parenting order, domestic violence order, protection order, or court order(s) concerning the welfare, safety or parenting arrangements). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated order date (commencement, start, end, expiry, issue or made date followed by a dd/mm/yyyy date - the blank form's ___/___/_____ does not match) AND one of: a populated student field (student, prospective student, child or pupil name/ID/number, legal family or given name, EQ ID, OneSchool ID, or date of birth with a non-placeholder value) or a populated restriction field (restrained/restricted/named person or parent, respondent or aggrieved with a name, or "not permitted/authorised/allowed to collect/contact", "no contact with" or "do not release (the student) to" followed by a name). 85 tier requires the order date AND the student field AND the restriction field AND an independent school term (school, principal, enrolment, class teacher, office staff, deputy principal, guidance officer, year level). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (fact sheet, information for schools, guidelines for schools, Legal Aid Queensland, frequently asked questions). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface the blank SEF-1 form, the enrolment procedure and family-law guidance.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the "Family Court Orders" / "Other Court Orders" headings and the Family Law Act 1975 wording are taken from the published SEF-1 V8 form and are distinctive, but the blank form, the enrolment procedure and family-law guidance for schools contain the same words. Enforce tiers therefore need a filled order date plus a named student or restricted person, which the blank form does not carry. School-side note wording ("not permitted to collect", "do not release to") is not published as formal wording and is matched only as a generic populated-field shape. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: Domestic and Family Violence Protection Act 2012 (Qld)

false_positives.mitigation: Enforce tiers need a filled dd/mm/yyyy order date plus a populated student or restricted-person field; the blank form's ___/___/_____ and label-only fields do not match. Guidance exclusion group for fact sheets and information for schools.

false_positives.description: Protection orders and family-law documents held outside schools (courts, police, legal files) that carry a child's name and order dates.
false_positives.mitigation: Such documents can reach 75 through the student/child field. The 85 tier needs a school term. The documents themselves are covered by au-dfv-protection-order and the family-law classifiers.

false_positives.mitigation: No court-order primary, so no match; au-education-guardian-collection-record covers them.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a school record showing that a named student is the subject of a current family law parenting order or domestic violence order, with the order dates and the person who must not collect or contact the student. Disclosure to the restrained parent or another person using violence can reveal which school the child attends, the arrangements protecting them and the other parent's circumstances, with a credible risk of abduction or serious harm to a child. This is the child-safety equivalent of the DFV confidential-address harm that the au-dfv set treats as PROTECTED. Risk 10 supports PROTECTED Personal-Privacy; organisations that keep these notes in routine enrolment files may choose SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy after their own harm assessment.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to PSPF and QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED Personal-Privacy and High because a populated court-orders record names the student, order dates and the person barred from contact, revealing the child's school and protective arrangements. Credible risk of abduction or serious harm makes significant damage inherent; national-security levels are out of scope.

generic.rationale: High with High Personal-Privacy handling applies because disclosure to a restrained person can locate and endanger a child. No higher generic tier exists.

Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia - Schools and family law orders (decoy source, content not reviewed)

patterns.name: Australian Electricity Derivative / PPA Confirmation
patterns.description: Detects Australian OTC electricity derivative and power purchase agreement confirmation content - documentation under the June 2006 Australian Electricity Addendum and 2005 ISDA Commodity Definitions, electricity swap/cap/floor/swaption confirmations settled against the AEMO regional reference price, and PPA confirmation phrasing with $/MWh fixed prices.
patterns.operation: Matches distinctive documentation anchors (Australian Electricity Addendum, ISDA Commodity Definitions with electricity context), instrument-confirmation phrases (electricity swap confirmation, cap/floor/swaption on electricity), or fixed-price terms quoting $/MWh against a NEM regional reference. Confirmation documents are formulaic, making phrase anchors reliable.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the Addendum and ISDA anchors are highly specific to executed or drafted electricity derivative documentation; the price-term arm is looser and needs corroboration. Market convention discussion (AFMA guides) uses the same vocabulary without deal data.

should_match.description: Documentation anchor for an AU electricity derivative confirmation

should_match.description: Instrument confirmation with fixed $/MWh price

should_match.value: the cap strike is settled against the pool price as determined by AEMO under the 2005 ISDA Commodity Definitions for electricity transactions
should_match.description: ISDA Commodity Definitions with electricity context

should_match.value: power purchase agreement - executed confirmation attached for the wind farm offtake
should_match.description: PPA with confirmation phrasing

should_not_match.value: the swap meet is on Saturday and entry is $5
should_not_match.description: Generic prose with swap and a price

should_not_match.value: solar PPA explained - a power purchase agreement is a long-term contract
should_not_match.description: Educational PPA definition without confirmation context

should_not_match.value: electricity prices averaged $92/MWh in Q2 according to the AER report
should_not_match.description: Public market price commentary, not a fixed-price deal term

false_positives.description: AFMA conventions, ISDA templates, law-firm explainers and training material quote the same documentation anchors without live deal terms.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative deal keywords (counterparty, notional, strike); reject template/example framing from enforcing tiers.

patterns.risk_description: Executed derivative confirmations and PPAs reveal hedge book composition, counterparties, volumes and prices - among the most commercially sensitive records an energy market participant holds.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Financial and Medium because an executed swap, cap or PPA confirmation reveals counterparties, volumes, regional reference and $/MWh price, exposing part of a participant's hedge book. PROTECTED is not met because a single trade does not show the whole position or cause significant damage.

generic.rationale: Medium Financial handling applies to confidential trade terms between named counterparties. One confirmation falls short of High.

patterns.name: Beneficiary, Dependant or Next-of-Kin Nomination Record
patterns.description: Populated beneficiary and dependant nominations held by superannuation funds and employers: binding and non-binding (including lapsing and non-lapsing) death benefit nominations under Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Regulations 1994 reg 6.17A (made for SIS Act 1993 s 59(1A)), employer group life insurance beneficiary nominations, and HR dependant, next-of-kin and emergency contact records. Each record ties an identified member or employee to named family members, their relationship to the member and, on death benefit forms, the share each person receives, witness details and dates of birth. Bulk member extracts with TFNs and balances belong to superannuation-fund-member-statement-bulk, and super identifiers (USI, member number) on their own belong to global-top500-096-superannuation-identifiers.
patterns.operation: Primary: a nomination or dependant record phrase (binding / non-binding / lapsing / non-lapsing (death benefit) nomination, death benefit nomination, nomination of beneficiaries / dependants, beneficiary nomination / designation, preferred or reversionary beneficiary, life insurance / group life / death benefit beneficiary, dependant details / declaration / information / record / form, next of kin details / record / form / nomination, emergency contact details / information / record / form). 65 is discovery-only (phrase alone) and surfaces fund PDS text, blank forms and HR policies. 75 requires a populated member or employee field (member / employee / staff member / insured person / policy holder name or number, staff or payroll number, with a non-placeholder value; a "relationship to member" label does not count) AND a populated beneficiary or dependant entry that gives a name and a relationship (a beneficiary / nominee / dependant / next of kin / emergency contact field with a name followed within 120 characters by a relationship label or a bracketed or dashed relationship such as spouse, partner, child, parent or legal personal representative, or a pipe / tab table row of name then relationship). 85 additionally requires a nomination detail structure: a share, proportion or percentage value, a relationship cell followed by a percentage, a populated date of birth (beneficiary or member), a named witness, or a date witnessed. Every enforce tier excludes template/fixture text and PDS, guide, fact sheet, policy and legislation wording.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: nomination forms and dependant records are dense labelled forms, and the enforce tiers need a populated member field plus a named beneficiary with a relationship, which PDS text, policies and blank forms do not carry. patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies populated beneficiary, dependant and next-of-kin nominations: an identified member or employee linked to named family members, their relationships and, on death benefit forms, each person's share, dates of birth and witnesses. Breach evidence shows why this matters: the 2026 Oracle PeopleSoft HCM campaign exposed employee dependant and beneficiary details alongside payroll data, and the 2025 credential-stuffing attacks on Australian super fund member portals exposed beneficiary details used in fraudulent withdrawals. The records map family structures (including children and de facto or interdependency relationships), help an attacker impersonate a member or a nominated beneficiary, and reveal who benefits on the member's death. Risk 7 reflects personal and financial-fraud harm across a household; bulk member extracts with TFNs and balances stay at risk 9 under superannuation-fund-member-statement-bulk.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 fits PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a nomination maps a member's family, beneficiaries' dates of birth and death benefit shares, supporting impersonation and fraudulent withdrawals. Higher risk is not met; bulk member extracts with TFNs and balances sit at risk 9 under a separate pattern.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling protects household relationships and benefit shares for one member. High applies only to bulk member data carrying tax identifiers and balances.

patterns.name: Energy Retail Customer Hardship, Payment Plan or Concession Record
patterns.description: Energy retailer customer records about hardship, payment plans, concessions and vulnerability. The National Energy Retail Law requires each retailer to have a customer hardship policy (s 43) meeting minimum requirements (s 44), and National Energy Retail Rules Part 3 (rr 70A-75B) sets out hardship customer obligations: informing the customer of the policy (r 71), payment plans set by capacity to pay, arrears and expected consumption (r 72), waiver of late payment fees (r 73), Centrepay (r 74) and the AER Customer Hardship Policy Guideline (r 75A). Queensland Government energy concessions (Electricity Rebate, Reticulated Natural Gas Rebate, Home Energy Emergency Assistance Scheme, Medical Cooling and Heating Electricity Concession Scheme) are applied through the retailer on proof of a Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card, Veteran (DVA) Gold Card, Queensland Seniors Card or ImmiCard. Records tie an account holder, customer or account number, NMI/MIRN or supply address to hardship program status, arrears, concession card details, payment plan amounts and "personal circumstances" notes. The incident class is a retailer's outsourced call-centre compromise exposing customer circumstances notes and government concession numbers. Published hardship policies, the AER guideline, blank applications and news are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a hardship, concession or vulnerability phrase (hardship customer / program / plan / flag / status / team / assessment / application / arrangement / case / payment plan; energy, electricity or gas hardship, concession or rebate; customer, financial or energy hardship record / note / referral; Electricity Rebate; Reticulated Natural Gas Rebate; Home Energy Emergency Assistance (Scheme) / HEEAS; Medical Cooling and Heating Electricity Concession (Scheme) / MCHECS; concession card holder / details / number / type; concession eligibility or status; personal circumstances note / notes / flag; vulnerable or vulnerability customer / flag / indicator / marker / note). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated account field (NMI/MIRN label with an NMI-shaped value, customer or account number containing a digit, a named account holder, or a supply / service / property / premises / site address with a street number) AND a populated hardship or concession field (hardship program / status / flag / plan / customer / indicator of enrolled, active, approved, accepted, commenced, granted, entered or current; a concession or rebate type / applied / status / eligibility naming a scheme or approved / active / eligible; a concession card type naming the card; arrears, amount owing / overdue / outstanding, debt or balance owing with a dollar amount; late payment fees waived; a Centrepay deduction / reference / amount / arrangement; or a disconnection or de-energisation hold) OR a detail field (below). 85 tier requires the account field AND a hardship or concession field AND a detail field (payment plan, instalment, agreed payment or plan amount with a dollar value; a Pensioner Concession, pension, Health Care, DVA / Veteran Gold or Seniors card number with a CRN-shaped, DVA-file-shaped or alphanumeric value; a CRN / Centrelink customer reference number with a CRN-shaped value; a DVA file number; or a personal / customer / household circumstances, hardship reason or vulnerability note of several words) AND an independent energy-account term (electricity, gas, energy, retailer, bill, meter, kWh, tariff, NMI, MIRN). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a policy/guidance/news exclusion (this policy, our hardship policy, published on our website, Customer Hardship Policy Guideline, standardised statements, Australian Energy Regulator, National Energy Retail Law, National Energy Retail Rules, you may be eligible, told reporters, said in a statement). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface policies, concession pages and news.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: NERL/NERR hardship terms and the Queensland concession scheme names are distinctive, but every retailer must publish a hardship policy containing the AER guideline's standardised statements and concession pages list the same cards, so enforce tiers need a populated account field plus a populated hardship, concession or detail field, and policy, guideline and news wording is excluded. The CRN shape (nine digits and a letter) and DVA file number shape are reused from au-centrelink-crn and global-dva-file-number and have no checksum; retailer account numbers are organisation-defined, so account values are loose and placeholder-guarded. Water and council hardship records with the same fields can reach 75 here; the 85 tier needs energy-account evidence. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the populated-field evidence with the customer's utility customer account number format (see docs/identifiers.md#utility-account-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Energy Retailer Family Violence Affected Customer Record
patterns.description: Energy retailer account records that identify a customer as affected by family violence under Part 3A of the National Energy Retail Rules (rules 76A-76M): the account identification made under rule 76C, the preferred or safe method of communication the retailer must record under rule 76H(4), instructions not to disclose affected customer information (rule 76G) to a current or former joint account holder, and assistance notes such as fee or debt waivers, payment plans, hardship program entries and disconnection holds considered under rule 111(2A). Complements the sector-neutral au-dfv-* classifiers with energy account structure (NMI, MIRN, customer/account number, supply address).
patterns.operation: Primary: an affected-customer or family-violence account phrase (affected customer, customer affected by / experiencing family violence, family violence or DFV/FV flag, indicator, alert, marker, customer, account, note or case). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: an account field (NMI/MIRN label with an NMI-shaped value, a customer/account number containing a digit, an account holder name, or a supply/service/premises address with a street number) or a protection-action field (preferred/safe contact or communication method with a value, a "do not disclose/discuss ... to/with the joint account holder/former partner" instruction or a named joint account holder, a fee/debt waiver with an amount or status, a disconnection hold with a status or date, a payment plan with an amount, or a hardship program status). 85 tier requires an account field AND a protection-action field AND an independent energy-account term (electricity, gas, retailer, bill, meter, concession). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a policy/guidance exclusion (published on our website, this policy, National Energy Retail Rules, Australian Energy Regulator, Guidance for Energy Retailers, AEMC, rule change). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface published family violence policies and guidance.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "affected customer" is the defined Part 3A term, but every retailer must publish a family violence policy (rule 76A) and the AER and AEMC publish guidance using the same words, so enforce tiers need populated account or protection-action fields and a policy/guidance exclusion. Retailer CRM field labels (for example the wording of an internal family violence flag) are not published and are unverified, so the account and action fields are generic labelled-value shapes. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's utility customer account number format (see docs/identifiers.md#utility-account-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.description: Portfolio-level wholesale electricity hedge book and contract position reports held by a NEM generator, retailer or gentailer: contracted volumes aggregated by NEM region (QLD1, NSW1, VIC1, SA1, TAS1), product (swap, cap, floor, PPA, futures) and period, in MW or MWh, with strikes in $/MWh, counterparties, mark-to-market and the open or net position against forecast generation or load. patterns.operation: Primary: hedge book vocabulary (hedge book / position / cover / ratio / report / portfolio, contracted position, net open or net contracted position, open position, cap cover, swap volume, contract cover, position report). 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated position row: a NEM region ID followed on the same line by a MW or MWh volume. 85 requires two distinct position rows (min_count 2, unique) plus a $/MWh strike or price and an independent term (counterparty, mark-to-market / MtM, VaR, forecast generation, strike, hedge ratio). Every tier excludes template/fixture text and public reporting (AER State of the Market, ASX daily settlement prices, annual report / financial statement notes, media releases). 65 is discovery-only and will surface FX and securities position language.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases are shared with financial-markets position reporting, so enforcement requires NEM region IDs with MW/MWh volumes on the same line; forward curves (region plus $/MWh without volume) do not satisfy the row regex. patterns.name: Energy Retailer or Distributor Life Support Register Record
patterns.description: Life support equipment registration records kept by Australian energy retailers and distributors under Part 7 of the National Energy Retail Rules (rules 123A-126A): completed medical confirmation forms, register entries and deregistration records that tie a premises (NMI, MIRN or supply address) to a customer and to life support equipment from the rule 3 list (oxygen concentrator, intermittent peritoneal dialysis machine, kidney dialysis machine, chronic positive airways pressure respirator, Crigler-Najjar syndrome phototherapy equipment, ventilator for life support, or other certified equipment). Applies in Queensland (Energex, Ergon Energy and retailers) since 1 July 2015.
patterns.operation: Primary: a life support registration phrase (life support equipment/register/registration/deregistration/customer/premises/flag/status/user/program, medical confirmation form, confirmation reminder notice, deregistration notice). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: either a premises field (NMI/MIRN label followed by an NMI-shaped value, or a service/supply/property/premises address label followed by a street number and name) or a medical-confirmation field (equipment type from the rule 3 list, a provider number containing a digit, or a named medical practitioner) or a rule 126 register-date field (a filled date for when supply is required, medical confirmation received, registration or deregistration date, or a reason for deregistration). 85 tier requires a premises field AND a medical-confirmation or register-date field AND a populated customer field (customer/account holder/patient name, or a customer/account number). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a rules/guidance exclusion (National Energy Retail Rules, AEMC, fact sheet, rule change, Improving Life Support Processes). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface blank forms, fact sheets and the rules themselves.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases come straight from NERR Part 7 and retailer forms, but the same phrases fill the rules, blank forms, distributor eligibility pages and fact sheets, so enforce tiers need populated record fields. The NMI value is shape-checked only (no checksum validator), and provider-number format is unverified, so values are loose and placeholder-guarded. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic records laid out like the published form headings.

keywords: service address where equipment is located

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's utility customer account number format (see docs/identifiers.md#utility-account-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a life support register entry or completed medical confirmation that links an identified customer and premises (NMI or address) to a household member's dependence on medical equipment such as dialysis, oxygen or ventilation. The record is health information about a person tied to a physical location where a vulnerable person lives, and the register itself is the safeguard against planned interruption; disclosure exposes health status and location, and tampering or loss can put a life at risk during outages. Guidance, the Rules, blank forms and fact sheets are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 and the Medium tier reflect a record tying a premises and customer to a household member's dependence on dialysis, oxygen or ventilation, where loss or tampering can put a life at risk during outages. Labels remain PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy, not PROTECTED, because each entry covers one premises, not the whole register.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to health dependence linked to a physical address. A full register extract, rather than one entry, would warrant High handling.
