patterns.name: Enterprise Bargaining Position, Wage Offer Costing and Claims Matrix
patterns.description: Confidential employer-side enterprise bargaining material produced before an agreement is made: bargaining position papers, wage offer costings, costed claims matrices (management response to a union or employee log of claims) and negotiation strategy briefs that record the approved mandate, fallback positions and trade-offs. Bargaining is conducted under Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) Part 2-4 (s 172 making an enterprise agreement, s 173 notice of employee representational rights, s 228 good faith bargaining requirements, s 229 bargaining orders) and, for the Queensland public sector and local government, Industrial Relations Act 2016 (Qld) chapter 4 collective bargaining (s 169 notice of intention to bargain, s 173 parties must negotiate in good faith). Published enterprise agreements, Fair Work Commission approval decisions, union newsletters and news reports are decoys; au-enterprise-agreement-document covers agreement text.
patterns.operation: Primary: a bargaining position or costing phrase (bargaining position / strategy / parameters / brief / costing / offer / proposal / objectives / claims matrix; employer, management, agency, department, council or company bargaining or negotiating position or offer; claims matrix or claims costing; union, employee or bargaining claims log; log of claims costing; EA, EBA, EBn or enterprise agreement costing / bargaining position / wage offer / offer costing; cost of the union, employee or bargaining claims; wage offer costing). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated costing structure: an offer rate (Year 1-5 with a percentage, a percentage per annum / p.a. / per year / compounding / from 1 July, or a wage, pay or salary increase, offer or rise with a percentage) or a cost impact (cost of claim / offer / proposal / clause / increase, annual / total / full-year / recurrent / cumulative / incremental / additional / net cost, $ impact, cost impact, budget impact or on-costs followed by a dollar amount; a number of FTE; or an FTE count field). 85 tier additionally requires a mandate or negotiation-strategy marker (approved, endorsed, government, Cabinet, Board or wages policy mandate; mandate ceiling / limit / approved / parameters; within or outside the mandate; fallback or walk-away position; opening offer or position; bottom line; trade-off; concessions available or to trade; negotiation or negotiating strategy; not to be disclosed, shared or tabled to the union, bargaining representatives or employees). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a published-material exclusion (nominal expiry date, This Agreement will / shall, approved by the Fair Work Commission, FWCA, Deputy President, join your union, join the union, Authorised by, told reporters, said in a statement). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface union bargaining updates, HR explainers and news.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "bargaining position", "claims matrix" and costing wording are the ordinary vocabulary of employer bargaining files, but union bargaining updates, FWC decisions and news reports quote the employer's position and offer percentage too, so enforce tiers need a populated costing structure and exclude published-material and news wording, and 85 needs a mandate or strategy marker that only the employer's internal papers carry. Mandate and costing layouts are organisation-defined, so the structures are generic labelled shapes. Genuine internal papers that quote an FWC decision number (FWCA) or the nominal expiry date of the current agreement within the window are suppressed, which is an accepted false negative. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Family and Domestic Violence Leave and Workplace Support Record
patterns.description: Detects HR, payroll and timesheet records showing that a named or numbered employee has taken or requested family and domestic violence (FDV) leave, and employee DFV support and workplace safety plans. Under Fair Work Act 2009 ss106A-106E every national-system employee is entitled to 10 days of paid FDV leave, and Fair Work Regulations 2009 reg 3.48 prevents FDV leave from being shown on pay slips because the record itself discloses that the employee is experiencing violence. Queensland public sector and state-system employees have DFV leave under the Industrial Relations Act 2016 (Qld) ss 52-54, and Queensland public service employees have additional support under Public Service Commission Directive 03/20 "Support for employees affected by domestic and family violence": confidentiality of disclosures, risk assessment and safety planning, changes to work location, hours, email addresses and telephone numbers, removal of public contact details, secure parking, flexible working arrangements, and support to transfer or relocate. Enterprise agreements and other directives and policies use the same terms.
patterns.operation: Primary: a family and domestic violence / domestic and family violence / domestic violence / family violence leave phrase, the FDV leave / DFV leave / FDVL abbreviations, a workplace / DFV / FDV safety plan phrase, a DFV/FDV support plan, options, arrangement or request or workplace support or adjustment phrase, "employee(s) affected by domestic and family violence", "Directive 03/20", or a Fair Work Act 2009 s 106A-106E or Industrial Relations Act 2016 s 52-54 citation. 75 tier requires a populated employee field (employee/staff/worker name, number or ID with a non-placeholder value) within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires either a populated leave detail (leave dates, start/end date, days or hours taken) or a populated workplace-support structure (work location changed to a named place, a new or unlisted work email or phone with a value, hours/roster changed, security or reception alerted, a photo of the respondent held, a named respondent or perpetrator, a DVO naming the workplace, secure parking allocated, email blocking applied, online profile removed, flexible arrangements with a value, or a review date). All enforce tiers exclude template/fixture text and directive/policy text (This directive, this policy applies, Supersedes, QH-POL, information sheet, Workplace approach to employees who use violence). 65 is discovery-only and will surface policy, directive, enterprise agreement and payroll configuration text.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: FDV leave and DFV support terms are common in enterprise agreements, directives, HR policy and payroll setup, so enforce tiers require a populated employee field and exclude directive/policy text. Records that identify the employee only by name in free text, without a field label, fall to discovery. Workplace safety-plan field labels are not published by the directive, so the support structure is a generic populated-field shape built from the support options the directive lists. Whether Directive 03/20 has been replaced under the Public Sector Act 2022 was not verified; the anchor is kept because existing records cite it. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

terms: Workplace approach to employees who use violence

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies an HR, payroll or timesheet record showing that an identified employee has requested or taken family and domestic violence leave, or a workplace safety or support plan for an employee affected by DFV. The record discloses that the employee is experiencing violence and, often, when they are absent, where they now work, their new contact details and the identity of the respondent. If it reaches a person using violence who works in the same organisation, a shared payroll mailbox or a joint bank statement, it can escalate risk; this is why reg 3.48 keeps FDV leave off pay slips and Directive 03/20 requires disclosures to be kept confidential. Enterprise agreements, directives, policies and payroll configuration are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy; safety plans that record a relocated work location may warrant handling at the au-dfv-confidential-address level.

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies financial statements such as profit-and-loss reports, balance sheets, income statements, and statements of financial position containing revenue, costs, assets, liabilities, and profitability. Premature disclosure can reveal performance, liquidity, solvency, and business strategy to competitors, counterparties, investors, or fraudsters. The reporting entity, owners, employees, and creditors may face serious commercial and financial harm, but the normal statement concerns one entity and may later be publicly released. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Financial fit a non-public statement, while market-wide consequences, systemic insolvency, or protected government operations would be needed for PROTECTED.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps consistently to QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, SENSITIVE Financial, SENS_Fin, and Medium because non-public statements consolidate material financial position and performance. PROTECTED is not met by the normal single-entity statement because its scope is contained and disclosure does not create broad privileged compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium Financial handling is appropriate for non-public financial statements and supporting results. High handling requires systemic consequences, protected operations, or exceptional aggregate scale.

patterns.name: FOI Exemption Section References
patterns.description: Detects Freedom of Information Act exemption section references (sections 33-38 and 42-47) in Australian government documents. Requires FOI/freedom of information keyword context.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex (?i)\b(?:s(?:ection|ect)?\.?\s*(?:3[3-8]|4[2-7][A-Za-z]?))\b matches FOI Act section references in formats like s33, section 47F, sect.38, etc. for sections 33-38 and 42-47 (with optional letter suffix). The Purview engine uses Pattern_au_foi_section (same regex). Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires FOI terms + government context keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires FOI terms with source code exclusion; Low (65) requires legal context keywords. Evidence uses 3 keyword groups (10 FOI terms, 8 government context terms, 10 legal context terms) within 300-character proximity. Keyword lists: au-government-foi.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: section number references are somewhat specific to FOI contexts when combined with the s/section prefix and constrained number ranges. However, legislative section references appear in many legal contexts, so corroborative keywords improve accuracy.

should_match.description: FOI Act section 33 exemption
FOI Act section 47F personal privacy
FOI Act section 38 secrecy provisions

should_not_match.description: Section number below valid range (32 instead of 33-38)
Section number above valid range (39 instead of 33-38)
Section 41 not in valid range (42-47)

false_positives.description: Legislative section references in non-FOI contexts such as other acts, regulations, or legal documents that use sections 33-38 or 42-47.
false_positives.mitigation: Require proximity to FOI-specific keywords such as FOI, freedom of information, exemption, or right to information to confirm FOI context.

false_positives.description: Code snippets and configuration examples containing section-related keywords or numeric references in developer documentation.
false_positives.mitigation: Check for common source code patterns (function, import, class) and exclude technical contexts to reduce false positives.

patterns.risk_description: This regex finds Australian FOI exemption citations in sections 33-38 and 42-47, such as s33 or section 47F, when FOI, government, or legal context is nearby. The detector returns a public statutory reference, not the information withheld under that provision, although a citation can modestly hint at privacy, security, or deliberative concerns. Harm to an agency or applicant is low and correlation-dependent unless surrounding text reveals exempt facts, legal tactics, or an unreleased decision. Risk 4 OFFICIAL is appropriate for the citation; SENSITIVE is not met without substantive exempt material, identifiable case content, legal strategy, or a protected operational record.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, the OFFICIAL DLM, and Low because FOI section citations are public legal metadata with limited standalone meaning. SENSITIVE is not met without withheld facts, case details, legal strategy, or protected operations.

generic.rationale: Generic Low handling fits a public exemption citation whose consequence depends on confidential information in the surrounding decision or case record.

patterns.name: Fair Work Commission or QIRC Employment Application / Case File
patterns.description: Applications and employer case files for Fair Work Commission matters (Form F2 unfair dismissal application, Form F3 employer response, Form F8 general protections application involving dismissal; matter numbers such as U2024/1234) and Queensland Industrial Relations Commission (QIRC) applications and appeals, where the record names the applicant, respondent or employer and carries matter and dismissal/decision particulars. Published FWC/QIRC decisions are public and are treated as decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a tribunal or application phrase (Fair Work Commission, Queensland Industrial Relations Commission, QIRC, Form F2/F3/F8, unfair dismissal application/claim/remedy/matter, general protections application/dispute/claim/matter, application for an unfair dismissal remedy). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated party field (applicant, respondent, appellant, employer, employee, former employee, representative, lodged by, with a non-placeholder value). 85 tier requires the party field AND a matter field (an FWC unfair dismissal matter number U20YY/NNNN, or a matter/case/file number or reference label with a value containing a digit) AND a dismissal/decision field (date the dismissal took effect, date of dismissal/termination/decision, employment start/end date with a date; reasons for the dismissal with text; remedy/outcome/orders sought with a value) AND an independent corroborative term (Fair Work Act 2009, Industrial Relations Act 2016, conciliation, reinstatement, compensation, jurisdictional objection, notice of listing, appeal, conference). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a decision/guidance exclusion (a neutral citation such as [2026] FWC 1234 / FWCFB / QIRC, catchwords, appearances, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, practice note). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: tribunal names and form numbers are distinctive but saturate FWC/QIRC guidance and news, and published decisions carry the same parties, matter numbers and dismissal dates, so enforce tiers need populated party fields and a decision-citation exclusion. The U20YY/NNNN unfair dismissal matter number format is taken from published FWC decisions (secondary verification); QIRC matter numbers and form numbers were not verified, so QIRC records rely on labelled matter/file references. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's case / matter reference number format (see docs/identifiers.md#case-reference-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Australian Gas Supply or Transportation Agreement (Executed / Populated)
patterns.description: Executed or negotiated gas supply, gas sale and purchase, gas transportation and gas storage agreements between named parties, carrying the commercial terms that the Competition and Consumer (Gas Market Code) Regulations 2023 s 25(2) requires a covered supplier's agreement to specify - quantity and annual quantity, flexibility and load factor, supply period, delivery points, price or price structure including take-or-pay conditions - together with the industry terms that express them (Annual Contract Quantity / ACQ, Maximum Daily Quantity / MDQ, take-or-pay, swing). Published Gas Market Code text, model or template agreements, ACCC gas inquiry reports and law-firm commentary are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: agreement titles (gas supply / sale / sales / transportation / storage agreement, gas sale and purchase agreement, agreement for the supply of (regulated) gas). 75 requires, within 300 characters, either a populated quantity term (ACQ, MDQ, DCQ, MHQ, annual quantity, annual / daily contract quantity, take-or-pay quantity or percentage, swing, with a GJ / TJ / PJ value or percentage) or a populated party / delivery / price field (seller, buyer, supplier, shipper, delivery or receipt point, contract / base / commodity price, commencement or expiry date, or a $/GJ price). 85 requires both a quantity term and a party / delivery / price field plus an independent contract term (take or pay, load factor, major interruption, price review, nomination, shortfall, curtailment, force majeure, Gas Market Code). Every tier excludes template/fixture text, model and pro forma agreements, ACCC gas inquiry material, explanatory statements and media releases. 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: agreement titles appear in the Gas Market Code, ACCC reports and law-firm articles, so enforcement requires populated terms (quantities with GJ/TJ/PJ units, named parties, delivery points, $/GJ prices). ACQ, MDQ and take-or-pay are industry practice rather than statutory terms (s 25 uses "quantity", "annual quantity", "delivery points" and "take or pay conditions"), which is why they are evidence rather than primary anchors. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.
regulations: Competition and Consumer (Gas Market Code) Regulations 2023 (Cth)

patterns.risk_description: A populated gas supply or transportation agreement discloses who is buying gas from whom, the contracted volumes (ACQ, MDQ, swing), delivery points, price and price-review mechanics and take-or-pay exposure. These terms are commercially confidential between the parties; the Gas Market Code requires covered suppliers to keep and report agreements to the ACCC (ss 33, 38) precisely because the terms are not public. Disclosure lets competitors and counterparties price against the parties' positions in a concentrated east-coast market. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence (negotiated contract terms rather than a trading book).

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence and Medium because an executed agreement reveals parties, ACQ, MDQ, delivery points, pricing and take-or-pay exposure that the Gas Market Code keeps from the public. PROTECTED is not met by one negotiated contract, which lacks trading-book scale or broader market consequence.

generic.rationale: Medium Commercial-in-Confidence handling applies to negotiated volumes and prices between named parties. One contract does not reach High.

patterns.name: Healthcare Provider Identifier - Individual
patterns.description: Detects Healthcare Provider Identifier - Individual (HPI-I) patterns. The HPI-I is a 16-digit number starting with the prefix 800361. No checksum validation.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \b800361\d{10}\b matches 16-digit numbers starting with the fixed prefix 800361. The Purview engine uses Pattern_hpii (same regex). Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires HPI-I-specific terms + provider credential keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires HPI-I terms + provider role keywords; Low (65) requires HPI-I terms only. Evidence uses 3 keyword groups (11 HPI-I terms, 23 provider credential terms, 11 provider role terms) within 500-character proximity. Keyword lists: au-healthcare-identifiers, healthcare-identifiers.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the 800361 prefix provides strong structural specificity for a 16-digit identifier. However, corroborative keywords are recommended to distinguish from other long numeric sequences. The prefix significantly reduces false positives compared to generic patterns.

HPI-I with typical digit sequence
HPI-I upper range

should_not_match.description: Wrong prefix (800362 instead of 800361)
Too few trailing digits (9 instead of 10)
Too many trailing digits (11 instead of 10)

false_positives.description: Long numeric sequences in unrelated contexts (tracking numbers, serial codes) matching the Healthcare Provider Identifier - Individual format
false_positives.mitigation: Use corroborative keywords and, where available, checksum validation to filter false matches.

patterns.risk_description: The canonical HPI-I regex detects one 16-digit healthcare-provider identifier beginning 800361, with provider credential and role terms strengthening confidence. It can help correlate a practitioner across Australian health systems or support billing and impersonation pretexts when paired with name, workplace, and other credentials. The number alone exposes no patient's care, practitioner disciplinary history, system password, or billing authority. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL reflect bounded provider-identifier harm, while a linked credential package, claim, or protected workforce record sets the SENSITIVE threshold.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to OFFICIAL and Low tiers because one HPI-I is a provider-matching reference without patient information, account access, or independent billing capability. SENSITIVE is not met without linked authentication, employment, claim, or clinical data.

generic.rationale: A healthcare provider identifier is generically Low with Low DLM because meaningful misuse requires the practitioner identity and further credential or billing evidence.

patterns.name: Healthcare Provider Identifier - Organisation
patterns.description: Detects Healthcare Provider Identifier - Organisation (HPI-O) values. The HPI-O is one of the four healthcare identifiers assigned under the Healthcare Identifiers Act 2010 (Cth); it identifies a healthcare provider organisation such as a hospital, medical practice, pathology or imaging laboratory or pharmacy, and is used in My Health Record, secure messaging and NASH transactions. It is a 16-digit number starting with the prefix 800362; the official format carries a Luhn check digit (not enforced here, matching the sibling au-individual-healthcare-identifier and au-hpi-individual classifiers). Labelled HPI-O references inside provider directories without a value are left to global-top500-337-provider-identifier-records.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \b800362\d{10}\b matches 16-digit numbers starting with the fixed prefix 800362. Checksum: Luhn (NOT enforced in this regex-only pattern; structural detection only, as for IHI and HPI-I). 65 (discovery only): the bare 800362 value. 75: value plus an HPI-O term (HPI-O, HPIO, Healthcare Provider Identifier - Organisation, organisation identifier). 85: HPI-O term plus independent organisation / HI Service context (hospital, medical practice, pharmacy, pathology, diagnostic imaging, HI Service, HPOS, NASH, responsible officer, organisation maintenance officer, Healthcare Provider Directory, secure messaging, My Health Record). Template wording and non-health numeric context (invoice, tracking, serial, shipment) are excluded from enforce tiers.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the 800362 prefix gives strong structural specificity to a 16-digit number, but the Luhn check digit is not enforced, so other long numbers that happen to start 800362 surface at 65 until an HPI-O label is present.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier detects one 16-digit HPI-O value (prefix 800362) and enforces only with an HPI-O label, with 85 adding organisation or HI Service context. An HPI-O identifies a provider organisation, not a person: it is shared with every participating provider through the Healthcare Provider Directory and appears on secure messages and My Health Record uploads. Disclosure can help a pretext against a practice or support correlation of an organisation's digital health transactions, but the number gives no patient information, no NASH certificate or HPOS access, and no billing authority. Risk 4 and OFFICIAL reflect that bounded organisational exposure; a NASH certificate, HPOS credentials or linked patient records would set the SENSITIVE threshold and are covered by their own classifiers.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, the OFFICIAL DLM and the Low tier because an HPI-O is an organisational healthcare identifier distributed through the Healthcare Provider Directory, with no patient information, access secret or billing capability. SENSITIVE is not met without a linked NASH certificate, HPOS credential or patient record; the HPI-I sibling sits one step higher at risk 5 because it identifies an individual practitioner.

generic.rationale: Low with Low DLM suits an organisational provider identifier; meaningful misuse needs organisation credentials or patient data that this value does not carry.

patterns.name: HV Switching Sheet or Access / Test Permit
patterns.description: Completed high-voltage switching sheets (switching programs) and Access / Test Permits for electrical apparatus, in the form used by Queensland electricity entities under the Queensland Electricity Entity Standard for Safe Access to High Voltage Electrical Apparatus (SAHVEA, Nov 2023). SAHVEA cl 7.3 requires a switching sheet to carry a unique reference number, the apparatus, step-by-step switching to isolate, prove de-energised and earth, the completion time of each step, isolation points and DNOBs, Operator Earth locations, and the issue, surrender and cancellation of permits. SAHVEA cl 9.2 requires an Access / Test Permit to carry the associated Switching Sheet number, Work Area, issue and surrender times, the Switching Co-ordinator, Nearby Exposed Live HV/LV and an Abnormalities Section. Populated sheets expose isolation points, equipment identifiers, network configuration and work schedules. SAHVEA itself, ENA DOC 003, blank forms and training material are decoys. "Sanction for test" and "vicinity authority" are not SAHVEA terms and are not used as anchors.
patterns.operation: Primary: Switching Sheet, switching program(me), Access / Test Permit, Access Permit or Test Permit. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface SAHVEA, ENA guidelines, blank forms, training material and unrelated "access permits". 75 requires, within 300 characters, either (a) a populated switching step line (a step number, an optional time, then Open / Close / Apply / Remove / Earth / Isolate / Rack out / Rack in / Check open / Prove de-energised / Attach or Place DNOB, followed by an equipment token such as a kV value, CB, DNOB, isolator, earth switch, bus or busbar, feeder, circuit breaker or an alphanumeric plant label), or (b) a populated sheet or permit field (Switching Sheet / Permit / Access Permit / Test Permit No., Number or Ref; Recipient, Switching Co-ordinator, Switching Operator, Issued to/by, Received by or Surrendered by with a person name; Work Area or Isolation Point with a value; or an Issue / Surrender / Cancellation time with an hh:mm value) plus HV evidence (DNOB, Operator Earth, Working Earth, Isolation Point, Nearby Exposed Live, HV apparatus, substation, circuit breaker, earthed, de-energised). 85 requires two distinct step lines (min_count 2, unique) plus a populated sheet or permit field plus HV evidence. All tiers exclude template/fixture text. Enforce tiers also exclude SAHVEA, ENA DOC 003, "Safe Access to High Voltage", "authorised person" course material and "Shall include the following".
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: Switching Sheet and Access / Test Permit are SAHVEA defined terms, but "access permit" and "test permit" also appear in unrelated contexts (building access, vehicle testing). Enforcement therefore needs a populated switching step with an electrical equipment token, or a populated permit field together with HV isolation vocabulary. Sheet and permit number formats are not public (SAHVEA only requires them to be unique), so number fields are anchored on the label with a loose value. "Switching program" is general industry usage outside Queensland and is not a SAHVEA term. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: Queensland Electricity Entity Standard for Safe Access to High Voltage Electrical Apparatus (SAHVEA, Nov 2023) cl 7.3, 9.2

patterns.risk_description: A populated switching sheet or Access / Test Permit identifies specific HV apparatus, isolation and earthing points, feeder and circuit-breaker identifiers, crew members and the times when plant will be out of service. For a transmission or distribution network or a generator connection, this reveals network configuration and windows of reduced redundancy that could be used to target critical electricity assets. It also carries worker names and safety-critical isolation records. Standards, blank forms, training and news are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE InfoTech.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 matches PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a completed switching sheet or Access / Test Permit identifies HV apparatus, isolation and earthing points, crew names and when plant is out of service. generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling fits completed switching programs that reveal network configuration and reduced-redundancy windows. A single work package does not reach High.

patterns.operation: Capitalised two-to-four component name structure is the primary signal. patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: enforcement requires capitalised name structure, Australian dictionary evidence, and personal-record context. patterns.risk_description: The Australian Individual Name Record combines name-related dictionary terms with capitalised word structure, so it can identify an actual person's name rather than only a blank label. A matched name can support identity correlation, unwanted contact, or a more credible pretext when joined to an organisation, role, account, or case. Names are nevertheless routinely disclosed and the low-confidence construction can also match headings or ordinary title-cased text. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL recognise the potentially populated identity value without assuming the surrounding document is a sensitive personal dossier.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to OFFICIAL and Low tiers because the detector may return a real individual name but that name alone has limited confidentiality impact and uncertain precision. SENSITIVE is not met without additional private attributes, a vulnerable subject, or consequential operational context.

generic.rationale: An individual name record is generically Low with Low DLM because standalone names are commonly observable and require linked data for material misuse.

patterns.name: Australian Loan Agreement
patterns.description: Detects populated Australian loan agreements and credit contracts: a loan agreement / credit contract / loan facility phrase combined with named borrower or lender fields, a stated loan amount or repayment, or a loan/facility reference number. Phrase-only mentions stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex). Primary: (personal|business|commercial|consumer|secured|unsecured) loan agreement/contract/deed, credit contract, loan facility (agreement), line of credit agreement. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated field - named borrower/lender/credit provider/guarantor, loan amount/principal/facility limit/repayment with a dollar value (ranges such as '$5,000 to $50,000' excluded), or a loan/account/facility/contract number. 85: primary plus two distinct field types (the three above or a labelled interest/comparison rate) plus loan-term evidence (repayment schedule, default interest, events of default, drawdown, financial covenants, credit guide, NCCP). Template/sample framing and guidance/marketing framing are excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers need populated party, amount or reference fields next to the agreement phrase, so lender marketing, calculators and consumer guidance (which name the same terms without values) stay at 65. Medium because loan-application correspondence can carry the same fields.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

patterns.risk_description: The pattern identifies Australian loan agreements through borrower, lender, principal, interest, repayment, security, covenant, and default terms, so the unit is a legal facility record. Disclosure can expose a borrower's finances and obligations, reveal covenant pressure, or support impersonation and interference in drawdown, repayment, or settlement communications. The borrower, lender, guarantors, and secured parties may face serious legal, privacy, and financial harm within one facility, although execution and payment changes require separate verification. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Legal fit that composite contract, while privileged lending-system access or a bulk portfolio would be needed for PROTECTED. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated record structure (labelled fields with real values, identifiers or data rows); phrase-only mentions in guidance, marketing, blank forms and news stay at 65 discovery.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps consistently to QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, SENSITIVE Legal, SENS_Leg, and Medium because an executed loan agreement consolidates consequential obligations and personal financial context. PROTECTED is not met by the normal single agreement because affected parties and facility scope are bounded and disclosure does not itself authorize funds.

generic.rationale: Medium Legal handling is appropriate for executed loan contracts, covenants, and default provisions. High handling requires aggregated portfolios, privileged origination control, or exceptional protected-operation consequences.

patterns.name: Australian Marking - OFFICIAL
patterns.description: Detects the Australian Government OFFICIAL protective marking (PSPF / QGISCF) in both email forms ([SEC=OFFICIAL] subject markings, X-Protective-Marking headers) and visible document banners. Excludes UNOFFICIAL and OFFICIAL: Sensitive (handled by au-marking-sensitive). Regex logic ported from Microsoft's canonical PSPF SIT guidance; matched case-sensitively so the lowercase English word "official" does not trigger.
patterns.operation: A standalone uppercase OFFICIAL candidate, excluding OFFICIAL Sensitive variants, is discovery-only at 65. A formal SEC, classification, security-classification, protective-marking, or marking field raises it to 75; an explicit Australian or Queensland protective-security context can also corroborate a standalone banner at 75. The 85 tier requires a complete X-Protective-Marking header with VER, NS=gov.au, and SEC=OFFICIAL fields. Enforcing tiers reject public marking guides, training, templates, and examples.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: case-sensitive uppercase OFFICIAL plus the structured SEC= form make this a reliable marking detector. The English word "official" (lowercase) is excluded by case.

should_match.description: Discovery probe (65) - bare page-footer banner with no formal marking field or government context
Medium-tier probe - formal classification field without a complete header

High-tier probe - complete Australian protective-marking header

false_positives.description: Uppercase use of OFFICIAL in non-marking contexts (e.g. "OFFICIAL OPENING").
false_positives.mitigation: Explicit PSPF/QGISCF government context or a structured marking field is required above discovery; the complete header remains the strict 85 path.

false_positives.description: ALL-CAPS prose (legal boilerplate, headers, or documents rendered entirely in capitals) defeats the case-sensitivity signal the bare OFFICIAL banner relies on — any all-caps rendering of the word can fire with no protective-marking intent.
false_positives.mitigation: Treat discovery-only banner hits as inventory; the structured field and government-corroborated paths at 75 are the balanced enforcement signals.

patterns.risk_description: The detector recognises the Australian Government OFFICIAL marking in structured email headers, subject tags, or an uppercase document banner, while excluding OFFICIAL: Sensitive. A true match normally indicates routine government business whose unauthorised release may cause administrative inconvenience, minor reputational effects, or a handling breach but not material security damage. Bare all-caps uses such as an official opening can still collide, and the marking says nothing about a hidden higher-risk record. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL fit the stated level; SENSITIVE would require an OFFICIAL: Sensitive caveat or substantive non-public personal, legal, commercial, or operational content.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, and Low tiers because the marking denotes routine official business with bounded harm. SENSITIVE is not met without a sensitive caveat or materially harmful underlying content.

generic.rationale: An Australian OFFICIAL marking is generically Low with Low DLM because it denotes routine government information rather than a protected operation or sensitive record.

changelog.description: Move the SEC= formal-label evidence term into a string-style group. As a word-style term it could not match "[SEC=...]" subject markings in Purview, because a letter follows the "=" (tenant gating claim 9), so the 75 tier never fired on them.

patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: case-sensitive uppercase PROTECTED plus the structured SEC= form make this a reliable marking detector. The English word "protected" (lowercase) is excluded by case.

generic.rationale: An Australian PROTECTED marking is generically High with High Government DLM because it explicitly denotes information requiring significant-damage controls.

patterns.name: Medical Certificate or Fitness-for-Work Clearance
patterns.description: Populated medical certificates and fitness-for-work clearances held by employers: practitioner certificates given as evidence for personal / sick leave (Fair Work Act 2009 s 107(3) lets an employer require evidence that would satisfy a reasonable person), certificates of fitness or capacity issued outside a workers' compensation claim, fitness-for-duty assessments, pre-employment medical clearances and return-to-work clearances. The records name the employee or patient, state a practitioner's opinion that the person is unfit, or fit for normal, restricted or modified duties over a stated period, and often carry a diagnosis, work restrictions and the practitioner's name and provider or registration number. Boundary: workers' compensation claim records, Form 132M work capacity certificates and Comcare certificates of capacity belong to au-qld-workers-compensation-claim; statutory WHS health monitoring reports (Schedule 14 chemicals, lead, asbestos, audiometry) belong to au-whs-health-monitoring-record. Both are excluded from this classifier's enforce tiers.
patterns.operation: Primary: medical certificate, certificate of fitness / illness / incapacity / capacity, fitness for work / duty or return to work certificate or clearance, medical clearance, fitness for duty assessment, pre-employment medical certificate / clearance / declaration, or practitioner certification wording ("unfit for work / duty", "fit for normal / restricted / modified / light / alternative duties"). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces leave policies, blank certificates and Fair Work guidance. 75 requires a populated employee / patient field (patient, employee, worker, staff member, candidate or applicant name or number with a non-placeholder value, or "this is to certify that" / "I have examined" followed by a person's name) AND a dated fitness outcome: unfit / fit / unable for work or duties from a date (to a date), a period of incapacity or absence as a date range, a condition preventing work between two dates, or a labelled outcome (fit, unfit, fit with restrictions, cleared) followed by a date. 85 additionally requires a medical detail or practitioner structure: a populated diagnosis / condition / restrictions / treatment field, a concrete restriction (no lifting, no driving, no work at heights, maximum kg or hours), a named treating / examining doctor or practitioner, a provider / AHPRA / registration number by label, or a populated practice or clinic name. Every enforce tier excludes template/fixture text, workers' compensation and WHS health monitoring context, Fair Work Ombudsman guidance, legislation and policy wording.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: certificate wording is standardised and the enforce tiers need a named employee or patient plus a dated fitness outcome, which leave policies, guidance and blank certificates do not carry. Provider and registration numbers are matched by label only (no public-format validation), and clinic letters or rehabilitation notes that follow the same layout will also match. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic certificates laid out like GP certificates and employer return-to-work clearances.

customisation.note: Extend the populated-field evidence with the customer's employee ID / payroll number format (see docs/identifiers.md#employee-id). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies medical certificates and fitness-for-work clearances about a named employee or patient, gated on a dated fitness outcome, with 85 also requiring diagnosis, restriction or practitioner detail. These are health information under the Privacy Act and IPA 2009: they reveal illness, injury, mental health or pregnancy-related absences and work restrictions, and they sit in HR inboxes, leave systems and manager folders well outside clinical systems. Breach evidence points to occupational health records as a target: the claimed 2026 PeopleSoft intrusion listed occupational health (Medlink) records, and the 2025 Western Sydney University incident exposed staff health and disability information. Leakage can drive discrimination in rostering, promotion and termination decisions. Workers' compensation certificates and WHS health monitoring reports are handled by their own classifiers. Risk 8 matches au-whs-health-monitoring-record and au-drug-alcohol-test-result.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a dated fitness outcome, often with diagnosis and restrictions, reveals illness, injury, mental health or pregnancy-related absence for a named employee. PROTECTED is not met for one certificate; the harm is discrimination in rostering or termination.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to an individual's health evidence held in HR inboxes and leave systems. It is not High because the record covers one person's leave or duties decision.

changelog.description: Classification reasoning drafted 2026-09-25 for owner review (SIT-Reference had an auto-populated placeholder, no generic classification, no tier).

Initial release - medical certificates, certificates of fitness / capacity outside a workers' compensation claim, fitness-for-duty assessments, pre-employment medical clearances and return-to-work clearances. 65 phrase only; 75 needs a populated employee / patient field and a dated fitness outcome; 85 adds diagnosis / restriction or practitioner detail. Workers' compensation and WHS health monitoring context excluded (handled by au-qld-workers-compensation-claim and au-whs-health-monitoring-record). Provider and registration numbers matched by label only.

patterns.name: Australia Medicare Card Identifier
patterns.description: Identifies Australian Medicare card numbers (10-11 digits, first digit 2-6). Filters same-digit sequences. Requires corroborative health-scheme keywords for reliable detection.
patterns.operation: Detection of a 10-11 digit Medicare card number (first digit 2-6) with an inline Checksum validator (Weights 1,3,7,9,1,3,7,9,0,0,0 / Mod 10 / CheckDigit 9 — weighted sum of digits 1-8 mod 10 must equal digit 9), AllDigitsSameFilter, and health-scheme corroborative keywords. Note: Func_australian_medical_account_number is a Purview detection function, not a usable validator (it is not on Microsoft's validator-function list), but the generic Checksum validator now enforces the Medicare checksum in the exported SIT. Corroborative evidence: 3 tiers with health-scheme-specific and broad health keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: 10-11 digit numbers are common in the wild. The Medicare checksum validator and health-scheme keywords significantly improve accuracy. AllDigitsSameFilter removes trivial matches.

should_match.description: Ten-digit Medicare card number (first digit 2-6), passes mod-10 checksum
Ten-digit Medicare card with display spacing, passes mod-10 checksum
Eleven-digit Medicare card with IRN, passes mod-10 checksum

should_not_match.description: First digit 1, not a valid Medicare prefix (2-6)
Too short for a Medicare card number
Twelve digits, too long
fails mod-10 checksum (single-digit perturbation of valid value 2270 19324 8)
fails mod-10 checksum (single-digit perturbation of valid value 4851 93897 0)

false_positives.description: Generic 10-11 digit reference numbers in non-health contexts.
false_positives.mitigation: Require health-scheme keywords in proximity. The Medicare checksum validator and AllDigitsSameFilter remove non-conforming and trivial matches.

patterns.risk_description: The Australia Medicare Card Identifier regex detects a 10- or 11-digit card number beginning 2 through 6, supported by health-scheme keywords. A disclosed value can assist beneficiary correlation, fraudulent billing enquiries, or a Medicare-themed identity pretext when combined with the holder's name and other details. The exported detector does not enforce the intended checksum, and the card number alone reveals no diagnosis, service, claim, payment, or portal credential. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy (owner decision 2026-09-25): a national health or health-insurance identifier is health information about an identifiable person and links them to their health-service and entitlement records, so it is treated as SENSITIVE even when found alone; PROTECTED requires a linked clinical record, claim, credential, or bulk patient register.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy (owner decision 2026-09-25): a national health or health-insurance identifier is health information about an identifiable person and links them to their health-service and entitlement records, so it is treated as SENSITIVE even when found alone; PROTECTED requires a linked clinical record, claim, credential, or bulk patient register.

generic.rationale: A Medicare card identifier is generically Low with Low DLM because meaningful misuse requires the beneficiary identity and additional claim or account evidence.

patterns.name: Australian Medicare Number
patterns.description: Detects Australian Medicare card numbers, which are issued to Australian citizens and permanent residents for access to subsidised healthcare under the Medicare system. The number consists of 10 digits: the first digit is between 2 and 6, followed by 8 additional digits and a single check digit. Numbers are commonly formatted as groups of 4-5-1 digits separated by spaces or hyphens.
patterns.operation: Checksum: Mod 10 with weights [1,3,7,9,1,3,7,9] on digits 1-8 compared against digit 9 — now enforced in the exported SIT by the inline generic Checksum validator Validator_au_medicare_number_checksum (Weights 1,3,7,9,1,3,7,9,0,0 / Modulo 10 / CheckDigit 9; Func_australian_medical_account_number remains genuinely absent from Microsoft's validator-function list, so the generic Checksum validator is used instead — see docs/checksum-validator-semantics.md). Reference: https://clearwater.com.au/code/medicare/, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-defn-australia-medical-account-number Corroborative evidence: 6 keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: au-health-scheme-terms, au-healthcare-identifiers, pii-civic-credentials.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence when corroborative evidence keywords are present. The leading digit constraint (2-6) and fixed 10-digit length reduce false positives compared to generic digit sequences. Combined with proximity keywords like "medicare" or "health insurance", this pattern reliably identifies Medicare numbers.

patterns.name: Medicare Provider Number
patterns.description: Detects Medicare Provider Number patterns. An 8-character code consisting of 6 digits, a location character, and a check character. Validated by location and check character sets.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \b\d{6}[0-9A-HJKLMNPQRTUVWXY][ABFHJKLTWXY]\b matches 6 digits followed by a location character (0-9, A-H, J-L, M, N, P, Q, R, T-W, X, Y) and a check character (A, B, F, H, J, K, L, T, W, X, Y). The Purview engine uses Pattern_au_medicare_provider (same regex) with a TextMatchFilter excluding known test values. Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires Medicare provider terms + medical context keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires Medicare provider terms; Low (65) requires medical context keywords only. Evidence uses 2 keyword groups (6 Medicare provider terms, 10 medical context terms) within 500-character proximity. Keyword lists: au-healthcare-identifiers, healthcare-identifiers.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the constrained character sets for location and check positions provide moderate specificity. Corroborative keywords are recommended to reduce false positives from 8-character alphanumeric strings.

should_match.description: Medicare provider number with valid location and check chars
Low-range provider number
High-range provider number

should_not_match.description: Only 5 digits instead of 6
Invalid check character (I not in valid set ABFHJKLTWXY)
Invalid check character (S not in valid set ABFHJKLTWXY)

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords within the proximity window to confirm sensitive data context rather than general discussion.

false_positives.description: In Australian English, similar terminology used in formal or administrative contexts (education, professional documentation) that does not constitute sensitive data collection.
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with additional contextual signals such as structured identifiers, form fields, or database column headers to distinguish sensitive records from general references.

patterns.risk_description: This regex recognizes an eight-character Medicare provider number shape with constrained location and check-character sets and nearby provider or medical terms. A real value identifies a clinician at a practice location and may help construct plausible referrals or billing submissions, but it is an administrative identifier rather than a secret, patient diagnosis, or login credential. Direct fraud requires practitioner identity, patient information, service details, and access to a claims channel, while legitimate numbers commonly appear on routine healthcare documents. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL are proportionate; a credential set, signed prescription authority, or bulk provider billing record would raise the context to SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, and Low for one professional administrative identifier. SENSITIVE is not met because the number supplies neither patient information nor authenticated prescribing or claiming capability.

generic.rationale: Low classification and Low DLM reflect the limited independent misuse of a provider-location reference without practitioner authority, patient details, or billing access.

Abbreviated tenement codes (ML/EPC/MDL) are deliberately excluded - bare "ML 123" collides with millilitre notation.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: blast-design parameters and geotechnical stability phrasing are near-exclusive to operational mining engineering documents, which is the security-sensitive core of this pattern. The JORC arms are equally distinctive but JORC-compliant statements are routinely published in ASX announcements and annual reports, so enforcing tiers need corroboration and public-release framing rejection.

patterns.description: Detects populated Australian mortgage documents (mortgage deeds, home loan contracts, registered mortgages, discharges): the mortgage phrase combined with named mortgagor/mortgagee fields, a security property or title reference, or a secured loan amount. Phrase-only mentions stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: keyword_proximity evaluated through purview tiers. Primary: mortgage deed/agreement/contract/document/instrument, home loan agreement/contract, secured loan agreement/deed, residential/registered mortgage, discharge of mortgage, memorandum of common provisions. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated field - named mortgagor/mortgagee/borrower/lender, security property/property address/title reference/lot on plan with a numbered value, or loan amount/principal/secured amount with a dollar value. 85: primary plus two distinct field types (the three above or a dealing/registration/loan account number) plus mortgage-term evidence (LVR, LMI, offset account, redraw, break costs, power of sale, event of default, discharge authority, Land Title Act). patterns.risk_description: This classifier identifies mortgage deeds and related records through mortgagor, mortgagee, property security, title, LVR, discharge, and consent terms. Disclosure can reveal a borrower's address, secured property, debt position, equity, lender relationship, and settlement details that support fraud, coercion, or targeted impersonation. The borrower, household, lender, and property stakeholders may face serious financial, legal, and privacy harm within one mortgage, while title changes and fund movements still require formal verification. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Legal fit that composite security record, while a bulk mortgage portfolio or privileged land and lending-system access would be needed for PROTECTED. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated record structure (labelled fields with real values, identifiers or data rows); phrase-only mentions in guidance, marketing, blank forms and news stay at 65 discovery.

PROTECTED is not met by the normal single mortgage because the affected property and parties are bounded and separate legal controls prevent direct alteration.

generic.rationale: Medium Legal handling is appropriate for mortgage deeds, discharges, and property-security terms. High handling requires bulk portfolios, privileged registry control, or exceptional protected-service consequences.

Boundary: hospital discharge summaries and referral letters belong to au-qld-health-discharge-summary-referral and general medical records to au-qld-health-medical-record; a bare IHI value is au-individual-healthcare-identifier.
patterns.operation: Primary: shared health summary, event summary, specialist letter, eReferral / e-referral, pharmacist shared medicines list, advance care planning document, Prescription and Dispense view, Medicines (Information) view. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus a populated patient field (patient name, DOB, IHI, Medicare, DVA by label, or a bare 800360 IHI value) plus My Health Record provenance (My Health Record, MHR, Australian Digital Health Agency, national digital health record). 85: the 75 evidence plus a populated document content or authorship field (medications, adverse reactions, medical history, immunisations, diagnoses / interventions, clinical synopsis, recommendations, document author, authoring organisation, HPI-I / HPI-O, document ID). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and Agency / PHN guidance, webinar, fact sheet and training framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the document type names are fixed by the My Health Record system and enforce tiers need a populated patient field plus explicit My Health Record provenance. "Event summary" also appears in IT and security reporting, which lacks the provenance and stays at 65. Copies with the provenance header stripped will be missed at 75/85.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier recognises My Health Record clinical document types and enforces only when a populated patient field (IHI, name, DOB, Medicare) sits with explicit My Health Record provenance, with 85 also needing document content or authorship. A shared health summary or event summary condenses a patient's medicines, adverse reactions, medical history, immunisations and treating providers; together with the IHI it links the person to their national health record. Unauthorised use or disclosure of health information in the system is a civil penalty matter under the My Health Records Act 2012 (Cth). The normal unit is one patient's document, so the harm is serious but contained. Risk 8 matches the other single-patient clinical record classifiers.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a populated My Health Record document discloses one patient's medicines, adverse reactions, history and IHI. PROTECTED is not met: one document does not give bulk access to the national system, and system credentials such as NASH certificates are handled by other classifiers.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling protects a single patient's national health summary. High would need bulk extracts or access credentials for the national system.

patterns.name: Nationality and National Origin (Australia)
patterns.description: Detects references to nationality/citizenship/immigration-status disclosure in Australian documents: nationality fields, national origin, citizenship status, visa status, and naturalization records. Not framed as an Art-9-style special category (Australia has no equivalent regime) — sensitivity here rests on immigration-status/visa risk under the Migration Act 1958 (Cth) and on the "national origin" limb of the Racial Discrimination Act 1975 (Cth), distinct from that Act's race/ethnicity limb covered by the sibling au-racial-ethnic-origin pattern. Topic-grade detector, low confidence by design.
patterns.operation: Phrase regex matching indicative nationality/citizenship/immigration-status disclosure terminology (nationality field, national origin, citizenship status, immigration status, visa status, country of citizenship, dual citizenship, naturalization status, non-citizen status). Detects the presence of nationality/immigration subject matter in a disclosure/record context; not a structured-token detector. Pair with corroborative keywords to raise precision. The Purview export is a single 65 discovery_only tier built from this phrase regex verbatim — inventory only, no enforcement; populated-field 75/85 enforcement awaits a separately reviewed EDM/ML design.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low by design. Nationality/immigration status has no fixed format, so it is detected purely by topic vocabulary. The bare word "national" appears constantly in unrelated contexts (National Bank, nationally recognized, national holiday); the regex is scoped to full disclosure phrases only, and hits should be paired with corroborative keywords (citizenship, visa, immigration) to raise precision.

should_match.description: Naturalization status phrase present

should_not_match.description: Near-miss proper noun ("National Bank"), no nationality disclosure

false_positives.description: The word "national"/"nationally" appears in unrelated contexts (proper nouns like National Bank, adverbial "nationally recognized", "national holiday") that have nothing to do with a person's nationality or citizenship.
false_positives.mitigation: The regex targets full disclosure phrases ("national origin", "citizenship status", "visa status") rather than the bare word "national"; require corroborative keywords (citizenship, visa, immigration, passport) for confidence.

patterns.risk_description: Nationality and immigration status carry discrimination and safety risk under the Racial Discrimination Act 1975 (Cth)'s national-origin limb; disclosure of visa/citizenship status can expose individuals to targeted harassment or immigration enforcement risk.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because disclosed visa, citizenship or national origin can expose a person to discrimination, harassment or immigration enforcement risk. Higher risk is not met: this is a low-confidence topic detector and does not treat nationality as a special category.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling reflects discrimination and immigration-status risk for an identified person. It is not High because a nationality or visa field alone lacks enforcement or safety detail.

patterns.name: NDIS Participant Number
patterns.description: Detects NDIS Participant Number patterns. A 9-digit number starting with the prefix 43.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \b43\d{7}\b matches 9-digit numbers starting with prefix 43. The Purview engine uses two regexes: Pattern_ndis_labeled (labeled format with NDIS/NDIA/participant prefix + 43 + digits) and Pattern_au_ndis (bare 43 + 7 digits format). Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires NDIS label + NDIS context keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires NDIS label keywords; Low (65) requires NDIS label keywords only (minimum context). Evidence uses 2 keyword groups (6 NDIS label terms, 9 NDIS context terms) within 300-character proximity. Keyword lists: au-identity-ndis, au-government-services-australia.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low confidence: a 9-digit number starting with 43 is a relatively short pattern that can match phone numbers and other numeric sequences. Corroborative evidence keywords such as NDIS, NDIA, or participant number are essential for reliable detection.

should_not_match.description: Wrong prefix (44 instead of 43)

false_positives.mitigation: Layer with additional contextual signals such as structured identifiers, form fields, or database column headers to distinguish sensitive records from general references.

patterns.risk_description: The low-confidence regex recognises a nine-digit 43-prefix NDIS participant number near programme labels. A genuine value may imply programme participation or help correlate a record, but it contains no disability details, plan, service history, or authentication data. The normal affected unit is one participant and serious misuse requires identity or a linked NDIS file. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy (owner decision 2026-09-25): an NDIS participant number reveals disability scheme participation, which is health and disability information about an identifiable person, so it is treated as SENSITIVE even when found alone; PROTECTED requires a linked plan, service history, credential, or bulk participant register.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy (owner decision 2026-09-25): an NDIS participant number reveals disability scheme participation, which is health and disability information about an identifiable person, so it is treated as SENSITIVE even when found alone; PROTECTED requires a linked plan, service history, credential, or bulk participant register.

generic.rationale: Low generic classification reflects a programme identifier whose material privacy impact arises only when joined to identity or support records.

patterns.description: Detects AEMO NEM dispatch bid/offer submission artefacts - the MMS bidding table vocabulary (BIDDAYOFFER, BIDOFFERPERIOD, BIDOFFERFILETRK, MNSP day-offer tables), the Dispatch Bid/Offer Submissions JSON payload fields (energyBids, fcasBids, mnspBids, rebidExplanation), and the participant FTP bid filename convention (<PARTICIPANTID>_<x>BID<x>_<timestamp>.zip/.json). patterns.operation: Matches distinctive AEMO bidding tokens: MMS data-model bidding table names, the NEM Dispatch Bidding API JSON member names, or a bid submission filename. Corroborative rebid/trading keywords and absence of documentation framing raise precision; enforcement should target pre-publication submissions, not the public archive.

patterns.name: NEM Dispatchable Unit Identifier (DUID) Context
patterns.description: Detects AEMO Dispatchable Unit Identifiers (DUIDs) when labelled as such. DUIDs are short (max 8 character) unit codes - modern IDs are alphanumeric, legacy IDs may contain '#', '/' or '-' (e.g. BARRON-1, W/HOE#1, ER01, LOYYB1). IMPORTANT: DUIDs are fully PUBLIC identifiers (published in the AEMO NEM Registration and Exemption List and in five-minute NEMWEB dispatch data). This pattern is a discovery-only context marker and corroborative building block for sensitive-content patterns (bids, availability, curves) - it must never enforce on its own. A bare DUID token is indistinguishable from ordinary text, so the pattern requires the DUID label (or dispatchable-unit phrasing) immediately before the code.
patterns.operation: Matches 'DUID' (or 'dispatchable unit id/identifier') followed within a few characters by a plausible DUID token of 3-8 chars from the DUID charset (the token must contain a digit, '#', '/' or '-', which excludes ordinary following words and covers virtually all registered DUIDs). Deploy alongside a keyword dictionary of actual registered DUIDs generated from the AEMO NEM Registration and Exemption List ('PU and Scheduled Loads' tab) for participant-specific precision.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low confidence by design: the identifier itself is public, so a match carries no sensitivity on its own - DUIDs appear throughout public AEMO dispatch data, market commentary and analyst material. The pattern exists for discovery and as an AND-condition/corroborative element beside sensitive-content patterns (au-nem-bid-file, au-forward-curve-artefact) and participant-specific DUID dictionaries.
regulations: National Electricity Rules Ch 2 (registration) and cl 3.8 (dispatch)

customisation.note: For participant-specific precision, replace the full-market DUID dictionary with the subset registered to your organisation (deployment overlay). Without the overlay this pattern stays a generic market-context discovery marker.

patterns.name: NEM Generating Unit Outage / Maintenance Plan (Internal)
patterns.description: Internal generating-unit outage and maintenance plans held by a NEM generator before (or in more detail than) the public PASA submission: planned outage schedules and overhaul programmes listing the unit or DUID, outage start and finish dates, MW deratings, unit states, work scope and return-to-service (RTS) dates or unit recall times. The unit-level PASA availability and unit-state codes AEMO publishes under NER cl 3.7.2(f)(5) (NEMweb MTPASA_DUIDAvailability / STPASA_DUIDAvailability) are public and treated as decoys; the plan detail behind them (scope, work orders, exact dates, reason narrative, drafts not yet submitted) is not published.
patterns.operation: Primary: outage-plan vocabulary (planned / unit / major / minor outage plan, schedule, programme or window, outage plan revision, planned or maintenance outage, overhaul plan or schedule, return to service, RTS date, unit recall time). 75 requires, within 300 characters, either a populated schedule row (a date range on one line followed by a MW figure or an NER unit-state token such as OUTAGEPLANBASIC or DERATINGPLANEXTEND, or "derated to/by NNN MW") or a populated plan field (DUID, unit, outage start / finish / type / reference, RTS date, recall time, work order, work scope with a non-placeholder value). 85 requires both a schedule row and a plan field plus an independent internal-plan term (draft, not yet submitted, work order, scope of work, tube leak, overhaul, boiler inspection, turbine, PASA submission). Every tier excludes template/fixture text, AEMO public-file markers (",AEMO,PUBLIC,", PUBLIC_MTPASA / PUBLIC_STPASA, I,MTPASA,DUIDAVAILABILITY, the PASAAVAILABILITY,PASAUNITSTATE header), ESOO and market notices. 65 is discovery-only and will surface IT and network outage notices.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "planned outage" and "return to service" are generic (IT, network and fleet maintenance use them), so enforce tiers require generator-specific structure: a dated schedule row carrying MW or an NER unit-state token, or a populated DUID / outage / RTS field. Public AEMO PASA CSVs are excluded on their header markers. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's generator outage work order / reference format (see docs/identifiers.md#generator-outage-work-order). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: An internal generating-unit outage plan discloses when and for how long specific units will be unavailable or derated, the work scope and the return-to-service dates, ahead of or in more detail than AEMO's public unit-level PASA data. In the NEM this is market-sensitive: advance knowledge of a competitor's capacity withdrawal informs bidding and contract pricing, and outage windows also reveal plant condition and periods of reduced resilience for critical infrastructure. Unit-level PASA availability itself is public, so the risk sits in the plan detail and timing. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence and Medium because internal outage scope, dates and return-to-service timing inform competitors' bidding and reveal windows of reduced resilience. PROTECTED is not met because unit-level PASA availability is already public and the detail concerns planned, bounded outages.

generic.rationale: Medium Commercial-in-Confidence handling protects outage timing and scope beyond the published PASA data. It is not High because the core availability is public.

patterns.name: NEM Rebid Log Book Entry or Late-Rebid Contemporaneous Record
patterns.description: Internal NEM trading-desk rebid records: trading log / log book entries and the late-rebid contemporaneous record that a Generator must make under NER cl 3.8.22(ca). These entries carry the material conditions behind a rebid, the event, aware and decision times (AER Rebidding and Technical Parameters Guideline s 3.4 fields eventTime, awareTime, decisionTime), the P/A/F/E rebid category and the fuller narrative behind a published "SL" / "see log" rebid reason. Distinct from au-nem-bid-file, which detects AEMO MMS bid tables, Dispatch Bidding API JSON keys and bid filenames; this classifier covers the trader's reasoning record, which is never published.
patterns.operation: Primary: rebid log vocabulary (rebid log / reason / record, late rebid or late rebidding period, contemporaneous record, trading log, log book entry, see log, bidding or offer strategy). 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated log structure: an event / aware / decision time field with a clock value (e.g. "Aware time: 14:02"), a rebid reason line in the HHMM~category~ form, or a "Category: P|A|F|E" field. 85 requires two distinct populated time fields (min_count 2, unique) plus an independent trading term (DUID, price band, pre-dispatch, RRP, dispatch or trading interval, MAXAVAIL). Every tier excludes template/fixture text, the AER guideline title, AER reports and media releases, and AEMO public-file markers (",AEMO,PUBLIC,", PUBLIC_BIDMOVE, I,BID,BIDDAYOFFER_D). 65 is discovery-only and will surface guidance and training text.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the phrases come from NER cl 3.8.22(ca) and the AER guideline and also appear in that guideline, AER enforcement material and training decks, so enforce tiers require populated log fields (clock-valued event/aware/decision times or the published HHMM~category~ reason form). The HHMM~category~ form also appears in next-day public bid data, which is excluded only when the AEMO PUBLIC header or bid table marker is within the window, so extracts pasted without headers can reach 75. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.
regulations: AER Rebidding and Technical Parameters Guideline (October 2024)

patterns.risk_description: A rebid log or late-rebid contemporaneous record reveals a generator's real-time trading reasoning: what the desk knew and when (aware and decision times), plant conditions, price-band movements and the commercial trigger for each rebid. Before AEMO's next-day publication it is market-sensitive, and the fuller log narrative is never published; it is also the primary evidence in AER inquiries under NER cl 3.8.22A. Disclosure would expose trading strategy to competitors and prejudice regulatory processes. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence (commercial trading reasoning rather than financial statements; au-nem-bid-file carries SENSITIVE Financial for the bid prices themselves).

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence and Medium because rebid logs record aware and decision times, plant conditions and the commercial trigger behind each rebid, and are primary AER evidence. PROTECTED is not met because exposure is confined to one participant's trading reasoning and a regulatory process.

generic.rationale: Medium Commercial-in-Confidence handling applies to unpublished trading-desk reasoning that competitors or investigators could exploit.

patterns.name: NEM System Restart Plan or Local Black System Procedure
patterns.description: Completed system restart material for a named National Electricity Market generating system or network: local black system procedures (LBSPs) that generators, integrated resource providers and network service providers must prepare and submit to AEMO for approval under NER cl 4.8.12(d)-(g), and extracts of the AEMO system restart plan, which NER cl 4.8.12(b) makes confidential information. Such a record holds plant and unit data, units that can restart without external supply, dead-bus synchronisation and trip-to-house-load (TTHL) capability, minimum load and transformer energisation limits, step-by-step restart switching, and approver and contact blocks. The blank AEMO Generator LBSP template, the SRAS Guideline, the System Restart Standard and news about restart tests contain the same headings without values, so they stay at 65 discovery.
patterns.operation: Primary: local black system procedure(s) / LBSP, system restart plan, black start (capability), system restart ancillary services / SRAS, or trip to house load / TTHL. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface the NER, the AEMO SRAS Guideline, the blank LBSP template and news. 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated restart structure. That can be a technical value from the AEMO LBSP template items: number of units with a digit, unit or station capacity in MW, minimum load in MW, largest transformer in MVA, or dead-bus synchronisation answered Yes/No. It can also be a restart step line (Step N: Open / Close / Start / Energise / Synchronise / Isolate / Transfer / Block load ... followed by a kV, CB, bus, breaker, MW or Unit N token), or a populated version/contact field (Approver, Release Date, Primary or Secondary Contact, Name of the generation facility, Name of Registered Participant) with a non-placeholder value. 85 requires two distinct structure hits (min_count 2, unique) plus independent restart evidence such as energy support agreement, ancillary services agreement, dead bus, auxiliary supply, restart path, electrical sub-network, diesel generator, TNSP or confidential information. All tiers exclude template/fixture text. Enforce tiers also exclude guidance and consultation text: System Restart Standard, SRAS Guideline, Guidelines for Preparing Local Black System Procedures, Reliability Panel, the WEM Local Black Start Procedure Guideline, issues or consultation papers, draft or final determinations, media releases and aemc.gov.au.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary terms are NER defined terms (cl 4.8.12, 3.11.7-3.11.10) and AEMO LBSP template headings. They dominate the Rules, the SRAS Guideline, Reliability Panel papers and the blank template, so enforce tiers depend on populated values (MW, MVA, unit counts, Yes/No answers, restart step lines, approver and contact fields). The item codes and headings come from the AEMO Generator LBSP template (final stage, 2019). Step-line wording (Open, Close, Energise and similar) is ordinary switching language, not a mandated AEMO format. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
