patterns.risk_description: A populated system restart plan extract or local black system procedure sets out how a named NEM generating system or network restarts after a black system: which units can start without external supply, restart switching steps, dead-bus and house-load capability, loading limits and who to call. NER cl 4.8.12(b) makes the system restart plan confidential information, and this material is system-security sensitive for critical electricity assets under the SOCI Act. Disclosure would help anyone planning to disrupt or delay power system restoration. The NER, guidelines, the blank template and news are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports PROTECTED InfoTech because one procedure is enough to plan the disruption or delay of power system restoration.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 maps to PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED InfoTech (PROT_IT) and the High tier because a populated LBSP or restart plan extract shows which units can black start, the restart switching sequence and who to call, and NER cl 4.8.12(b) makes the system restart plan confidential. One procedure is enough to plan the disruption or delay of power system restoration, the same harm as grid dispatch plans, which are PROTECTED InfoTech at risk 9. The NER, guidelines, the blank template and news stay out of enforce tiers.

generic.rationale: High InfoTech handling applies because one plant's restart procedure gives anyone seeking to delay restoration the switching sequence and contacts they need. Access should be limited to the operators and engineers responsible for restart.

patterns.name: NGER Emissions and Energy Report Working Papers (Pre-Lodgement) and Safeguard Working Papers
patterns.description: Working and draft National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting (NGER) material before it is lodged with, or published by, the Clean Energy Regulator: section 19 reports being prepared in EERS (the Emissions and Energy Reporting System), facility details under NGER Regulations reg 4.04A (facility name, address, facility identification number, industry sector), facility-level Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions in t CO2-e, energy production and consumption in GJ / MWh, fuel activity data, method selections, NGER Act s 23 audit information (audit team leader, assurance findings), and Safeguard Mechanism working papers (responsible emitter, covered emissions, baseline emissions number, net position number, SMC / ACCU surrender planning, declared multi-year periods). The CER's own published data (corporate and electricity sector CSVs released by 28 February, the Safeguard baselines and emissions table released by 15 April) is public and is excluded from enforce tiers.
patterns.operation: Primary: NGER / National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting, "section 19 report", EERS / Emissions and Energy Reporting System, Safeguard Mechanism / Safeguard facility / Safeguard baseline, "baseline emissions number", "safeguard mechanism credit unit", "declared multi-year period", "multi-year monitoring period" or "designated large facility". 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface CER guidance, legislation and published data. 75 requires one populated structure within 300 characters: a labelled NGER field with a non-placeholder value (facility name, facility identification number, controlling / reporting / registered corporation, responsible emitter, reporting year, facility address, latitude / longitude, industry sector, ANZSIC, audit team leader, production variable, monitoring period) or an emissions / energy quantity line (Scope 1/2, covered emissions, net emissions number, gas species, energy produced / consumed, electricity produced, fuel type followed by a number with t CO2-e, GJ, TJ, PJ, MWh, GWh, kL, ML, kg or t, or a label-colon value for the Safeguard quantities such as net position number, ACCUs surrendered, SMCs issued or borrowing adjustment). 85 requires a labelled field plus a quantity line, or two distinct quantity lines, plus independent evidence: an NGER working term (section 19, operational control, Method 1-4, uncertainty, s 23 audit information, reasonable / limited assurance, EERS submission, draft / not yet submitted / working paper, Measurement Determination) or a public-format ACCU serial range or ERF project ID, which are supporting evidence only. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude CER published data signals (the exact CSV column headings, cer.gov.au / cleanenergyregulator.gov.au / legislation.gov.au URLs, compilation headers, "Civil penalty:", guide and fact-sheet framing).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary terms are statutory and distinctive, but CER guides, the NGER Act and Regulations and the CER's published data all use them, and the NGER facility identification number and reporter ID formats are not public, so there is no identifier to anchor on. Enforce tiers depend on populated facility fields and quantity lines with NGER units, and published-data column headings are excluded. A generator's facility-level totals become public after 28 February, so the classifier is aimed at the working detail and pre-lodgement drafts. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act 2007 (Cth)
National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Regulations 2008 (Cth)
National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting (Safeguard Mechanism) Rule 2015 (Cth)

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's nger facility identification number format (see docs/identifiers.md#nger-facility-id). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies an entity's own NGER and Safeguard working material before lodgement or publication: draft section 19 reports, facility details, per-source fuel and energy quantities, method selections, s 23 audit information and Safeguard surrender planning, gated on populated fields and quantity lines. Facility and group totals for generators are published by the Clean Energy Regulator after 28 February and Safeguard data by 15 April, but the working detail is never published and is protected information in the CER's hands (CER Act s 43). Before release it can be market-sensitive for listed and trading entities (production, fuel mix, unit surrender liabilities) and it carries compliance exposure under the NGER Act. Published CER data, legislation and guidance are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence and Medium because pre-lodgement NGER and Safeguard working papers expose per-source fuel data, method choices, audit findings and surrender planning that are never published. PROTECTED is not met because totals are later released by the CER and the harm is commercial and compliance-related.

generic.rationale: Medium Commercial-in-Confidence handling protects facility-level working detail before lodgement. Later publication of totals keeps it below High.

patterns.description: Detects New South Wales driver licence numbers in the established eight-digit or four-digit-plus-two-letter shapes. Enforceable tiers require an explicit driver-licence-number label and NSW context; the strict tier additionally requires Transport for NSW, Service NSW, or a legacy NSW road authority.
patterns.operation: The bare NSW-shaped value is discovery-only at 65. A labelled value with NSW context reaches 75. A labelled value with NSW context and issuing-authority evidence reaches 85. Template/example language is excluded at every tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the candidate shapes collide with routine identifiers, while a nearby licence-number label and NSW context materially improve precision. Authority evidence supports high-confidence classification.

patterns.risk_description: A confirmed NSW driver licence number can support identity correlation and licence-themed impersonation, especially when paired with the holder's name or date of birth. The number alone is not a licence image, card number, driving history, or authenticator. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL reflect the bounded harm of one atomic government identifier.

classification.rationale: A labelled NSW licence number with NSW context is one government identifier, so risk 5, PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM and Low tier apply. Paired with name or date of birth it aids impersonation, but SENSITIVE is not met because the match exposes no licence image, card number, driving history or authenticator.

generic.rationale: Low with Low handling suits one NSW licence number; a full identity bundle with card number and date of birth is what would justify Medium.

patterns.description: Detects five implemented Australian standard number-plate shapes for NSW, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, and Western Australia. It does not validate issuance and excludes personalised plate formats; registration and transport-agency evidence controls enforcement.

patterns.risk_description: The low-confidence TestPattern regex detects several Australian state number-plate formats, with stronger tiers requiring registration, transport-agency, and vehicle context. A genuine plate identifies a publicly displayed vehicle and can support tracking only when combined with sightings, timestamps, owner attribution, or access to registration records. Serial codes, policy documents, and template values can match the broad structural patterns. Risk 4 OFFICIAL reflects low standalone harm; SENSITIVE requires a protected person, concealed movement history, active threat, or an aggregated identified tracking dataset.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, OFFI, and Low handling for one low-confidence vehicle plate. The next SENSITIVE level is not met because owner attribution, movement history, protected-person status, and safety consequences are not established.

generic.rationale: Generic Low handling suits a public vehicle marker whose privacy impact depends on repeated location evidence, reliable attribution, or protected-person context.

patterns.name: Pay Slip or Time and Wages Record
patterns.description: Populated employee pay slips and payroll wage records: the Fair Work pay slip (employer name and ABN, employee name, pay period, date of payment, gross and net amounts, deductions, superannuation contributions, hourly rate or annual salary, loadings and allowances - Fair Work Regulations 2009 regs 3.45-3.46) and the Queensland time and wages record kept by state and local government and other state-system employers (Industrial Relations Act 2016 (Qld) ss 339-340).
patterns.operation: Primary: a pay slip or payroll record phrase (pay slip / payslip, pay advice, earnings statement, salary or wage slip, payroll statement / advice / record / register, wages record / book / sheet, time and wages record). 65 is discovery-only (phrase alone) and surfaces guidance, award pay guides, marketing and blank forms. 75 requires the phrase plus a gross/net/total amount field with a dollar value, plus either a pay period / pay date / week-ending field with a date or an earnings line with a dollar value. 85 requires the phrase, the gross/net amount, an earnings line (ordinary hours, hourly rate, overtime, allowance, leave loading, base pay, annual salary with a dollar value), a deduction or superannuation line with a dollar value (PAYG / tax withheld, salary sacrifice, union fees, super guarantee), and a populated employee identity field (employee name, employee / staff / payroll number, TFN). Every enforce tier excludes template/fixture text and pay-slip guidance, pay guide and payroll software marketing wording.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: a pay slip is a dense labelled form, and the enforce tiers need dollar values against gross/net, earnings and deduction labels, which guidance, pay guides and blank forms do not carry. Payroll journals, costing spreadsheets and bank remittance advices can carry the same labels and amounts and may reach 75 when a pay slip phrase is nearby. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; tests are synthetic records laid out like FW and Qld wage records.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's employee / staff id format (see docs/identifiers.md#employee-id). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: A populated pay slip or time and wages record ties a named employee to their income, hourly rate or salary, tax withheld, salary sacrifice, union fees, child support deductions and super fund, and often to leave types that reveal health or family circumstances. It is one person's data per slip; bulk payroll files with TFNs and bank details are covered at higher risk by payroll-master-file-with-tax-file-numbers. Risk 6 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a pay slip ties a named employee to pay, tax withheld, union fees and child support deductions, enabling payroll fraud and false income evidence. Higher risk is not met for one slip; bulk payroll files with TFNs and bank details are rated higher elsewhere.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling fits a single employee's income and deduction detail. High is reserved for bulk payroll files carrying tax and bank identifiers.

patterns.name: PBS Prescriber Number
patterns.description: Detects PBS Prescriber Number patterns. A 7-digit number whose check digit uses weights [0,5,8,4,2,1], mod 11 (checksum NOT enforced in this regex-only pattern; structural detection only).
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \b\d{7}\b matches any 7-digit number. Checksum: weights [0,5,8,4,2,1], mod 11 (NOT enforced in this regex-only pattern; structural detection only). The Purview engine uses two regexes: Pattern_pbs_labeled (labeled format with prescriber/PBS prefix + 7 digits) and Pattern_pbs_prescriber (bare 7-digit format). Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires PBS label + healthcare/pharmacy keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires PBS label keywords; Low (65) requires PBS label keywords only (minimum context). Evidence uses 2 keyword groups (6 PBS label terms, 11 healthcare/pharmacy terms) within 300-character proximity. Keyword lists: au-healthcare-identifiers, au-healthcare-medications. Adds label-context matching and exclusion logic for sample/template/test placeholders.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low confidence: a bare 7-digit number is extremely common and will match phone numbers, postcodes, reference codes, and many other numeric sequences. Corroborative evidence keywords such as PBS, prescriber, or pharmaceutical are essential for reliable detection. Context label evidence plus explicit template/example exclusion improves precision for high-risk identifiers.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords within the proximity window to confirm sensitive data context rather than general discussion.

false_positives.description: In Australian English, similar terminology used in formal or administrative contexts (education, professional documentation) that does not constitute sensitive data collection.
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with additional contextual signals such as structured identifiers, form fields, or database column headers to distinguish sensitive records from general references.

patterns.risk_description: This SIT detects any seven-digit sequence as a possible PBS prescriber number, with stronger tiers relying on PBS, prescriber, pharmacy, or healthcare labels because the checksum is not enforced. A genuine number identifies a prescribing professional for administrative claims and may assist forged paperwork or billing reconnaissance, but it does not reveal a patient's medicines and is not itself prescribing authority or system access. Common seven-digit phone and reference values create substantial false-positive exposure, while practical fraud needs practitioner identity, prescription details, patient data, and an authenticated channel. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL are justified; linked prescriptions, signing credentials, or a bulk prescriber-claim dataset would meet SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 corresponds to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, and Low for one prescriber administrative number. SENSITIVE is not met because the value lacks patient medication facts, authenticated authority, and independent claiming capability.

generic.rationale: Low and Low DLM reflect bounded misuse of a professional billing reference without a prescription, patient identity, signature, or access credential.

patterns.name: Australian Person-Linked Residential Address
patterns.description: Detects a populated Australian residential street address linked to a labelled person. Bare address structure is available for discovery, the balanced tier requires person and residential context plus Australian geography, and the strict tier requires state and postcode corroboration. A parallel household-utility path treats a utility supply/service address linked to a labelled account holder as a person-linked residence. Absorbs the former au-top500-041-home-address and au-top500-054-home-utility-account-addresses classifiers.
patterns.operation: Pattern_au_person_linked_street_address matches a populated street number, street name, and Australian road type. The 65 tier is discovery-only. The 75 tier requires a labelled person, an explicit residence relationship, and at least one state, locality, or postcode signal, where locality evidence draws on the consolidated 15,829-entry Australian suburbs and localities registry. The 85 tier requires the same person and residence relationship plus an explicit residential-address label, an Australian state or territory, a postcode, and registry or major-locality evidence. The utility path mirrors this: 75 requires a labelled account holder, utility-service context (electricity/gas/water account, supply or service address), independent account/metering context (account number, NMI, MIRN, meter number), and one geographic signal; 85 adds a supply/service/connection-address field label, state, locality, and postcode. Company account-holder suffixes veto the utility path. Unattributed home addresses stay discovery-only. Template and example content is excluded from the enforcing tiers.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: enforcement requires a populated Australian street structure, a labelled person, an explicit residential relationship, and geographic corroboration. The high tier additionally requires complete state/postcode evidence, while bare structures remain discovery-only.

patterns.risk_description: A true enforcing match links an identified person to a populated Australian residence. Disclosure can enable unwanted contact, residence verification, targeted social engineering, or physical targeting, although a single ordinary record does not establish vulnerability, a safety threat, or a protected location. Risk 6 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy treatment; protected-person and safety-critical residences require stronger controls.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because an enforcing match links an identified person to an Australian residence, supporting unwanted contact, social engineering or physical targeting. Higher risk is not met: an ordinary address does not establish vulnerability or a protected location.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to a person-linked home address. It is not High unless the address belongs to a protected person or a safety-critical residence.

patterns.name: Psychosocial Hazard Risk Register or Risk Assessment
patterns.description: Psychosocial hazard registers and risk assessments kept by a person conducting a business or undertaking under the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) Part 3.2 Division 11 (s 55A meaning of psychosocial hazard, s 55B meaning of psychosocial risk, s 55C duty to manage psychosocial risks, s 55D determining control measures) and the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 (in force 1 April 2023). Register rows record a hazard (job demands, low job control, poor support, aggression from customers, remote or isolated work), a risk rating, controls and an owner for a team or work area. Most rows are aggregate; the higher tier is reserved for rows that identify an affected worker or link a complaint, grievance or claim. The Code's own text and example register, blank registers and training material are decoys. Complements au-workplace-harassment-psychosocial-complaint, which covers individual complaints.
patterns.operation: Primary: a psychosocial register phrase (psychosocial hazard / risk / safety / health and safety register, (risk) assessment, identification, log, matrix, profile, or action / management / control plan; or a WHS, risk or hazard register headed psychosocial). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated hazard-row structure: a risk rating field (inherent / residual / current / overall / target risk rating, level, score or ranking, likelihood, consequence or severity with a rating word, number or matrix cell) AND either a populated hazard field (hazard, hazard type / category / description / identified with at least two words) or a populated control / owner field (existing, current, proposed or additional controls, control measures, treatments or actions with at least three words; a risk, action, control or hazard owner or responsible person with a value; or a review, due, target or completion date). 85 tier additionally requires an individual worker field: an affected, impacted, exposed, injured or named worker / employee / staff member / officer, worker or employee name, complainant, reported by or raised by with a two-part name; an employee, staff, worker or payroll number with a digit; or a complaint, grievance, case, incident or (WorkCover) claim reference with a digit. All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance/training exclusion (this Code, this Code of Practice, example risk register, case study, learning outcomes, facilitator notes, training module, workshop activity). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface the Code, WorkSafe guidance and news.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the WHS Regulation Division 11 terms and the Code of Practice vocabulary are distinctive, and a populated rating plus hazard or control field separates a working register from guidance, but the Code itself publishes an example risk register with the same columns and training decks reproduce it, so guidance and training wording is excluded and blank fields are placeholder-guarded. Most registers are aggregate (team or work-area level), so 85 is reserved for rows that identify a worker or link a complaint, grievance or claim. Employee and complaint number formats are organisation-defined and loosely shaped. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 (Qld)

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a working psychosocial hazard register or risk assessment: hazards such as aggression, excessive job demands or poor change management rated and assigned to owners for a team or work area, and at 85 rows that name or number an affected worker or link a complaint, grievance or claim. Aggregate rows expose internal WHS risk and potential non-compliance with the s 55C duty; identified rows add a worker's exposure to bullying, aggression or distress, which is sensitive personal and potentially health information. The Code, blank registers and training material are excluded. Risk 6 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because register rows expose internal WHS risk and possible s 55C non-compliance, and identified rows add a worker's exposure to bullying or aggression. Higher risk is not met because most rows are aggregate team hazards, not a worker's health or complaint file.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling fits hazard ratings and, at the strict tier, identified worker exposure. It is not High because the register is not itself a complaint or medical record.

patterns.name: QLD Ambulance Service Patient Care Record
patterns.description: Populated Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) patient care records: electronic Ambulance Report Forms (eARF, earlier ePARF), paper ambulance report forms and paramedic patient care records or reports. They record the patient, the case or incident, chief complaint and mechanism of injury, vital-sign observations, treatment and medicines given, and the transport destination or hospital handover. Copies are requested by hospitals, police, insurers, lawyers and coroners, and travel outside the QAS clinical system. Boundary: hospital clinical handover sheets belong to au-qld-health-clinical-handover; police incident reports to qps-incident-report.
patterns.operation: Primary: eARF / ePARF / e-ARF, (electronic) ambulance report form, patient care record, ambulance (patient) (care) record or report, paramedic (patient) (care) record or report. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus a populated patient field (patient name, DOB, age, Medicare, URN, address) plus a populated clinical field (chief complaint, presenting problem, mechanism of injury, observations, vital signs, GCS, BP, heart / pulse / respiratory rate, SpO2, BGL, pain score, treatment, drugs or medications administered, provisional diagnosis, clinical assessment, triage category, transport destination, transported to, destination hospital, handover). 85: the 75 evidence plus either a populated case field (case, incident, job, CAD or event number, dispatch / call / at-scene time) or explicit QAS provenance (Queensland Ambulance Service, QAS, Triple Zero call, Ambulance Service Act). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and Clinical Practice Manual, guideline, training, news and patient-information framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: eARF and ambulance report form wording is specific, and enforce tiers need a populated patient and a populated clinical field. "Patient care record" is also used by aged care and hospital systems; those records reach 75 when they carry observations or treatment, which is health information about a person, and only reach 85 with a case number or QAS provenance.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier recognises QAS eARF and ambulance patient care records and enforces only when a populated patient field sits with a populated clinical field (complaint, observations, treatment, destination), with 85 also needing a case number or QAS provenance. These records are routinely requested by police, insurers, lawyers and coroners, so copies circulate outside the clinical system. Disclosure can expose stigmatised conditions or the circumstances of an assault or accident. patterns.name: Queensland Council Cat and Dog Registration Record
patterns.description: Council dog and cat registration forms, registration notices, renewals and registry records that identify the owner. Dog registration is statutory under the Animal Management (Cats and Dogs) Act 2008. Under s 47 the registration form must state the owner's name, residential address, contact telephone number and email address, and the dog's age, breed, colour, sex, distinguishing marks, address, PPID number, desexing and regulated status. The council gives the owner a registration notice (s 49) and keeps it in the dog registry (ss 177-178). Cat registration, where required, is imposed by local law, which s 6 permits. The dog registry is open to public inspection, but owner information in the registration notice is excluded (s 179(2)), and s 39 restricts the release of identifying information. The owner block is therefore the sensitive part of the record. Declarations, attacks and destruction orders are covered by au-qld-regulated-dog-declaration-attack-record.
patterns.operation: Primary: dog / cat / animal / pet registration [form / notice / record / renewal / application / details / certificate], dog / cat / animal registry, registration notice for the / your dog or cat, lifetime dog or cat registration. Owner field values must be on the same line as the label and are placeholder-guarded (withheld, not, none, nil, excluded, redacted, suppressed, blank lines, brackets). 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated owner field: owner, owner's [full] name, registered owner, owner's address, residential or postal address, contact / owner telephone or phone, mobile or email, followed by a name of two or more capitalised words, a street address, an Australian phone number or an email address. 85 requires two distinct owner field values (min_count 2, unique) plus a populated animal field (breed, colour, sex, desexed, age, animal / dog's / cat's name, microchip or PPID number, registration or tag number). Animal fields alone never reach 75, which keeps public registry extracts at 65. All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (open to inspection, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, how to register). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. The registration phrases are common on council web pages and renewal reminders, so enforce tiers need populated owner fields. Registration and tag numbers are council-defined and are matched only as labelled loose values. Microchip (PPID) numbers are matched only as a labelled loose value. The ISO 11784 15-digit structure was not verified from a primary source for this build and is not relied on. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's council animal registration number / tag format (see docs/identifiers.md#animal-registration-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a council dog or cat registration record that names the owner with a residential address, phone or email alongside the animal. The Act withholds owner details from the public dog registry (s 179(2)) and restricts the release of identifying information (s 39). Pet registers have been misused to locate people, including people with DFV confidential addresses, and bulk extracts expose many households' contact details. Legislation, council web pages, blank forms and owner-less registry extracts are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 5 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy for owner-identified records.

patterns.name: Queensland Workplace Asbestos Register, Management Plan or Removal Record
patterns.description: Populated workplace asbestos records under the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) chapter 8: asbestos registers (s 425 - date identified, location, type and condition of asbestos or ACM), asbestos management plans (s 429, reviewed at least every 5 years under s 430), asbestos removal control plans (s 464), regulator notification of licensed removal (s 466), clearance inspections and clearance certificates (ss 473-474, including the less than 0.01 asbestos fibres/mL air-monitoring statement), air monitoring (s 482) and class A / class B removal licence details (ss 485, 487). The target is a record for a real site with filled location, material, friable status, condition, sample result or removalist fields. Worker asbestos health monitoring reports (ss 435-444) are covered by au-whs-health-monitoring-record and are not targeted here.
patterns.operation: Primary: asbestos register, asbestos management plan, asbestos removal control plan, clearance inspection, clearance certificate, asbestos air monitoring (report or results) or asbestos removal notification. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces the Regulation, the Code of Practice, SWA guidance and blank templates. 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated register or plan field (location, room, area, building, material, ACM or asbestos type, friable status, condition, sample number, result, date identified, removalist, licence number, assessor, clearance date, quantity or extent) whose value is not blank, bracketed, n/a, tbc or another placeholder. 85 requires two distinct populated fields plus an analysis or monitoring result (a named asbestos fibre type detected or not detected, "no asbestos detected", or a labelled fibre reading in fibres/mL) plus independent corroboration (Regulation section references, class A or B licence, licensed asbestos assessor, competent person, NATA, encapsulation, enclosure, decontamination, WorkSafe notification). All tiers exclude template/fixture text and legislation or awareness-training text (maximum penalty, penalty units, asbestos awareness, fact sheet, media release, public register).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases are statutory record names that also appear throughout the Regulation, the Code of Practice and guidance, so they are discovery-only on their own. Enforcement depends on populated labelled fields, which guidance and blank templates do not carry, but an informal register written without "label: value" fields (for example a table pasted without column headers) will stay at 65. The Queensland Code of Practice Appendix D/E register column names could not be read at source and are unverified, so the field list uses the legislated fields (s 425 date, location, type, condition) plus common industry labels rather than a template's exact headings. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's asbestos removal licence number format (see docs/identifiers.md#asbestos-removal-licence-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's asbestos sample reference format (see docs/identifiers.md#asbestos-sample-reference). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: A populated asbestos register, management plan or removal record says where asbestos-containing material is in a named building or plant, whether it is friable and in poor condition, what laboratory results showed and whether removal was cleared. It is not a public record, but it is shared with workers and contractors (s 427), so it is internal-sensitive rather than secret. Unauthorised disclosure creates WHS and environmental liability exposure (evidence of known, unremediated friable asbestos), regulatory scrutiny and reputational harm, and can affect property transactions. It does not carry personal health information; worker health monitoring is handled by a separate classifier. Risk 7 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 fits PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Government because a populated asbestos register or removal record shows where friable ACM sits in a named building, its condition and lab results, creating WHS liability. PROTECTED is not met: the record is shared with workers and contractors under s 427 and carries no personal health data.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling fits a site asbestos register or clearance record that evidences known hazards and liability. It is not High because it is routinely shared with workers and contractors.

A completed application can combine identity, contact details, employment or volunteering context, criminal-history screening, and a suitability decision, exposing the applicant to stigma, fraud, and loss of opportunity. The normal unit is one safeguarding application rather than a whole child-protection database, and non-child-related blue-card references are excluded by context. classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy, and Medium because a Blue Card application combines identity and consequential screening information. patterns.name: Queensland Council Building, Plumbing or Planning Enforcement Complaint and Investigation File
patterns.description: Complainant and investigation content in Queensland council building, plumbing and planning compliance files: complaint intake records, complainant details, site inspection and investigation notes, and officer recommendations that lead to a show cause or enforcement notice. The notices themselves are largely public. Building Act 1975 s 247 (show cause), s 248 (enforcement notices) and s 251 (register of notices given); Plumbing and Drainage Act 2018 ss 143-146 (enforcement and show cause notices) with Plumbing and Drainage Regulation 2019 s 115 (register of show cause and enforcement notices) and s 116 (register open to inspection free of charge); Planning Act 2016 s 167 (show cause), s 168 (enforcement notices) and s 170 (notifying about them). The private part is who complained, often a neighbour, and what officers recorded during the investigation. This classifier targets that content, not the notice or the public register entry.
patterns.operation: Primary: show cause notice, enforcement notice, development offence / offense, unlawful building / plumbing / drainage work, unlawful use or development, non-compliant / illegal / unapproved plumbing, drainage, building work, structure or development, building / plumbing / planning / development compliance or enforcement complaint / investigation / request / file / matter / case, and building / plumbing / planning / development complaint. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces notices, public register extracts, legislation and guidance. 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated private structure and independent context. The structure is either a complainant field (complainant [name / details / address / contact / phone / mobile / email], name of complainant, reported by, informant, person making the complaint, customer name, requester / requestor, followed by a name of two or more capitalised words, a street address, an Australian phone number or an email address) or an investigation field (investigation / inspection / site inspection / site visit / officer / file / case notes, findings, observations or outcome; details / nature / summary / description of the complaint or allegation; complaint details / summary; allegation; investigating officer; action taken; recommended action; officer recommendation; evidence obtained, followed by at least 10 characters of text). The context is a council or statute term (council, local government, Building Act 1975, Plumbing and Drainage Act 2018, Planning Act 2016, building certifier, plumbing inspector, compliance officer, enforcement authority, Development Tribunal, Planning and Environment Court, site inspection) or a labelled complaint / case / request / CRM reference, property / assessment number or application number. 85 requires the complainant field AND the investigation field AND the same context. Field values must be on the same line as the label and are placeholder-guarded (anonymous, withheld, not, none, nil, redacted, suppressed, blank lines, brackets). Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (fact sheet, frequently asked questions, how to make / lodge a complaint, annual report).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Show cause and enforcement notice vocabulary is statutory and distinctive, but the notices and registers are public, so enforce tiers ignore the notice and need a populated complainant or investigation field with council or statute context. Complaint and CRM reference formats are council-specific, so they are loose label-anchored values used only as context. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's case / matter reference number format (see docs/identifiers.md#case-reference-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's council property / rates assessment number format (see docs/identifiers.md#council-property-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's development application number format (see docs/identifiers.md#council-development-application-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Council CCTV Footage Access Request and Release Record
patterns.description: Council records of requests for CCTV footage and of footage released: request forms from residents, insurers and businesses, police requests, and release registers or logs recording the camera, the footage period, the incident or Queensland Police Service (QPS) reference, and who received the footage. No Queensland statute deals specifically with council CCTV. Councils handle footage as personal information under the Information Privacy Act 2009 and their CCTV policy. A disclosure to a law enforcement agency relies on QPP 6.2(e) (disclosure reasonably necessary for enforcement-related activities), and QPP 6.5 requires the agency to make a written note of that disclosure. That note is the basis of the release register. Council CCTV policies, published camera location lists, legislation and news are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: CCTV / camera / video / surveillance / security camera footage request(s), access request(s), release, disclosure, application, register or log; request(s) for / to view / to access / to obtain (CCTV / camera / video) footage; footage request(s) / release / disclosure (form / register / log / record); CCTV request(s) / release / disclosure / access (form / register / log / record); release of (CCTV / camera / video) footage. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone). 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure and independent context. The structure is a footage field (camera [ID / no. / number / name / location / site / reference], recording date / time / period, footage date / time / period / timeframe / duration / start / end, date / time (and time) of footage / recording / incident, time range / period / window, start time, end time, timestamp, period requested), a requester or recipient field (requested by, requester / requestor, applicant (name), released / provided to, recipient, requesting officer, QPS / police officer, officer name / collecting, collected by, person depicted / identified / of interest, insurer, followed by a name, street address, phone number or email) or a labelled QPS / police / QPRIME / occurrence / incident / event / job reference or number with a digit-bearing value. The context is QPS, Queensland Police Service, police, Information Privacy Act, QPP 6, law enforcement, council, insurance claim, incident or offence. 85 requires the footage field AND either the requester / recipient field or the incident reference AND the same context. Field values are on the same line as the label and placeholder-guarded. Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a policy exclusion (this policy / procedure / guideline / fact sheet, frequently asked questions, how to request / apply, annual report, camera locations, CCTV network map, legislation.qld.gov.au).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Footage request and release wording is distinctive, but council CCTV policies and web pages use the same words. Enforce tiers therefore need populated camera, footage-period, requester or incident-reference fields. Camera IDs and QPS occurrence numbers have no verified public format, so they are loose label-anchored values. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's qps occurrence / police reference number format (see docs/identifiers.md#qps-occurrence-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Cemetery Burial, Cremation and Exhumation Record
patterns.description: Council cemetery and crematorium records about a deceased person and the people arranging the disposal of the remains: burial and interment applications and bookings, rights (grants) of burial or interment, ashes and niche placements, exhumation applications and approvals, and cremation records. Cremation records follow the Cremations Act 2003 (Qld): an application for a permission to cremate by a close relative, personal representative or their agent (s 6), accompanied by a cause of death certificate and a cremation risk certificate, and the crematorium's record of particulars and permissions kept for 15 years (s 14). A populated record names the deceased (name, date of death, age, cause or place of death), the applicant, next of kin, right holder or funeral director and their relationship to the deceased, and the plot, niche or right number and burial, cremation or exhumation date. Published burial search and grave locator listings, fee schedules, cemetery policies and the statute text are decoys. The statutory basis for burial and exhumation records is council local law and is not asserted here.
patterns.operation: Primary: (application for a) permission to cremate; cremation risk certificate / application / permit / register / record; right or grant of burial or interment; interment right / application / record / register / order / authority; burial register / record / application / permit / booking / authority; exhumation application / permit / licence / order / approval / record / request; application to or for exhume / exhumation; or ashes / niche / columbarium placement or interment application or record. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone). 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a deceased field (deceased / name of deceased / deceased person's full name with a two-word name, a date of death, an age at death, or a cause or place of death with a word value), a kin field (applicant, next of kin, close relative, personal representative, executor, holder of the right or grant, right holder, grantee, funeral director or contact person with a two-word name, or relationship to the deceased with a word value) or a plot field (plot, grave, allotment, niche, row, section, site or wall reference containing a digit; a dated burial, interment, cremation, exhumation, funeral or reinterment date; or a right / grant / licence number containing a digit). 85 requires a kin field AND a deceased or plot field AND an independent corroborative term (cemetery, crematorium, funeral director, headstone, memorial, Cremations Act 2003, independent doctor, coroner, reinterment, cause of death certificate and similar). Blank lines, bracket placeholders, n/a/tbc and "Yes / No" prompts are rejected. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude public listing and guidance wording (burial / grave / cemetery / deceased search, locator or finder, search results, family history, genealogy, maximum penalty, penalty units, in this section, fees and charges, this guide/fact sheet/policy/procedure, frequently asked questions, legislation.qld.gov.au).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: permission to cremate and cremation risk certificate are Cremations Act 2003 terms and the burial and exhumation anchors are distinctive, but the same words fill council cemetery pages, fee schedules, local laws and public burial search tools, so enforce tiers need populated deceased, kin or plot fields and exclude listing and guidance wording. Right-of-interment, plot and approved-form numbers are council-specific and unverified, so values are loose and digit-gated. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's cemetery interment right / plot reference format (see docs/identifiers.md#cemetery-interment-right-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

false_positives.description: Cemetery fee schedules, local laws, policies and the Cremations Act text.
false_positives.mitigation: A guidance/statute exclusion suppresses fee schedules, penalty wording, the legislation site and policy wording; these also lack populated fields.

false_positives.mitigation: A death notice with no record primary stays below 65; a funeral director's cremation application file is in scope.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a cemetery, crematorium or exhumation record that links a deceased person to the family members, executors and funeral directors arranging the burial, cremation or exhumation, often with cause of death, relationship details and reasons for exhumation. Disclosure can inflame next-of-kin disputes, expose health information about the deceased, breach cultural protocols for First Nations remains and reveal contact details of bereaved families. Burial locations themselves are often published, so public search listings, fee schedules, policies and the statute text are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 6 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because the record links a deceased person's cause of death to next of kin, executors and exhumation reasons, and can breach First Nations cultural protocols. Higher risk is not met because burial locations are often published.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling covers cause of death and bereaved families' contact details. It is not High because the record concerns one interment and much burial data is public.

patterns.name: Queensland Contaminated Land Site Investigation or Management Record
patterns.description: Unpublished contaminated land records under the Environmental Protection Act 1994 (Qld) chapter 7 part 8: site investigation reports and validation reports (s 381), site management plans (s 383), site suitability statements, auditor reports, and working papers about land on the environmental management register (EMR, s 371 - a notifiable activity has been carried out, or the land is contaminated) or the contaminated land register (CLR, s 372). Notifiable activities include Schedule 3 item 8 (operating a coal fired power station) and item 13 (manufacturing, repairing or disposing of electrical transformers). The target is a document for a real site with filled lot on plan / site / contaminant fields and sampling or laboratory content, such as soil and groundwater results in mg/kg or ug/L. Bare EMR/CLR search extracts are fee-based public records (s 542) and are deliberately held at discovery unless they carry investigation content.
patterns.operation: Primary: environmental management register, contaminated land register, site investigation report, site suitability statement, contaminated land investigation document, contaminated land auditor, notifiable activity, or site management plan when a contamination term or s 383 follows within 80 characters. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces the Act, DETSI guidance, public search results and title notations. 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated site field (lot on plan, lot/plan, real property description, title reference, site address, site, notifiable activity, contaminant or contaminant of concern, sample or borehole ID, monitoring well, depth, consultant, auditor, landowner or occupier) whose value is not blank, bracketed or a placeholder, AND either a laboratory result row or investigation-work vocabulary (sampling, borehole, groundwater, soil samples, exceedance, laboratory, NATA, remediation, investigation level, HIL, EIL, conceptual site model). 85 requires two distinct populated site fields, a laboratory result row (a named contaminant such as TRH, PAH, BTEX, PFAS, PFOS, benzo(a)pyrene, PCBs, arsenic, lead, chromium or mercury followed within 60 characters by a concentration in mg/kg, ug/L, mg/L or ng/L) and investigation-work vocabulary. Lot on plan is matched as a labelled loose value because the exact register field format is unverified. All tiers exclude template/fixture text and legislation, guidance and public-search text (maximum penalty, penalty units, fact sheet, media release, search fee).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the register and report names are statutory and appear in the Act, DETSI guidance and every public search result, so they are discovery-only alone. Enforcement needs populated site fields plus sampling or laboratory content, which guidance and bare register extracts lack. Guidance tables of investigation levels can carry contaminant-plus-concentration rows, so a guidance document that also has filled site fields could reach 75. Lot on plan is matched as a labelled loose value (format unverified), and "contaminated land auditor" is a legacy phrase whose current statutory wording is "auditor" (used only at 65). 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's queensland lot on plan / real property description format (see docs/identifiers.md#qld-lot-on-plan). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: Unpublished site investigation and validation reports, draft site management plans, sampling data and pre-sale due diligence describe contamination on identified land (lot on plan, address) with concentrations against investigation levels before the regulator or a buyer has seen them. Disclosure creates environmental liability and remediation cost exposure, affects land value and transactions, invites regulatory action and damages reputation. Register listings themselves are fee-based public records (s 542), so bare extracts are not the target. Risk 7 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 matches PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Government because unpublished investigation reports give contaminant concentrations for identified land before the regulator or a buyer sees them, affecting liability and land value. PROTECTED is not met: the harm is financial and regulatory for one site, and EMR/CLR listings are public.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling protects unpublished contamination data tied to a lot on plan, which affects liability and sale value. One site's investigation does not warrant High.

patterns.name: Queensland Council Local Law Infringement Notice or SPER Referral Record
patterns.description: Council-issued infringement notices for local law and animal management offences, and the default certificates and referral records that send unpaid notices to the State Penalties Enforcement Registry (SPER). Under State Penalties Enforcement Act 1999 s 15, an infringement notice must state a unique number for the notice, its date, the alleged offender's full name and address, the offence particulars (place, time and date, and identifying particulars for any animal or vehicle), and the fine. s 22 and s 23 set out payment, court election and instalments within 28 days. When the alleged offender defaults, the administering authority may give SPER a default certificate (s 33), and SPER may then issue an enforcement order (s 38). Council compliance and remedial notices (Local Government Act 2009 s 138AA) often precede the infringement. Local law registers are public, but individual notices and SPER referral batches are not.
patterns.operation: Primary: [penalty] infringement notice, default certificate, State Penalties Enforcement Registry, referred / referral / lodged / registered to or with SPER, SPER referral / registration / lodgement / debt, remedial notice, compliance notice. Every enforce tier also needs a council or local-law context term within 300 characters (local law, council, regional / city / shire council, Local Government Act 2009, Animal Management (Cats and Dogs) Act, authorised person, unregistered dog, wandering, animal at large, overgrown, unsightly, remedial notice). This context requirement keeps traffic-camera notices at 65. 75 requires context plus either a populated alleged-offender field (alleged offender, offender, person served, recipient, full name, name, or residential / postal address, followed by a name of two or more capitalised words or a street address) or a labelled infringement notice number (the infringement-notice-number fallback: notice label followed by a value of at least 7 characters containing a digit). 85 requires context plus an alleged-offender field, a labelled notice number and a populated offence or penalty field (offence [description / details / code / provision / location / date], nature of offence, provision contravened, place or date of offence, fine, penalty [amount], amount payable / due / owing / outstanding, due date, pay by). Field values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded. All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (frequently asked questions, fact sheet, State Penalties Enforcement Regulation, infringement notice offence means, annual report). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Infringement and SPER vocabulary is shared with traffic, transport and other state agencies, so enforce tiers need a council / local-law context term and populated fields. Infringement notice number formats are unpublished, so the notice number is the registry's label-anchored fallback (infringement-notice-number). 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's infringement notice number format (see docs/identifiers.md#infringement-notice-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Council Rates Arrears and Sale of Land for Overdue Rates Record
patterns.description: Queensland local government records about overdue rates and charges and the sale of land to recover them under Local Government Regulation 2012 ch 4 pt 12: arrears ledgers and debt recovery referrals (s 132 overdue rates, s 133 interest on overdue rates), and notices of intention to sell land for overdue rates or charges (s 140), which must state the resolution date and terms, the land as shown in the land record, the overdue amount including the period unpaid, and the interest owing. Sale procedures follow in ss 141-146. These records tie a named owner, a rates assessment or property number and a land description to that owner's arrears. The auction notice that s 142 requires councils to publish is public and is a decoy.
patterns.operation: Primary: an overdue-rates or sale-of-land phrase (overdue / unpaid / outstanding rates (and charges), rates arrears, arrears of rates, notice of intention to sell (land), sale of land for overdue rates, rates debt recovery). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a property/owner field (assessment, property, rates account or valuation number with a value containing a digit; a lot on plan, land description or title reference with a value; a Qld lot-on-plan string such as Lot 14 on RP812334; a named registered owner, owner or ratepayer; or a property/land address with a street number) or an arrears field (amount overdue, arrears balance, total owing or interest owing/charged with a dollar amount; unpaid/overdue/in arrears since a date or year; a filled period unpaid; or a notice or resolution date). 85 tier requires a property/owner field AND an arrears field AND an independent council term (council, local government, ratepayer, rate notice, general rates, land record, chief executive officer, interested parties, mortgagee). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a public-notice/policy exclusion (auction notice, offered for sale, bidders, auctioneer, conditions of sale, this policy, revenue statement, statutory "This section applies if" text). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface the Regulation, revenue policies and news.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "notice of intention to sell land for overdue rates or charges" is the verified s 140 heading and "overdue rates or charges" is the statutory term, but the same words fill the Regulation, council revenue statements, debt recovery policies and the auction notices councils must publish (s 142(4)). Enforce tiers therefore need populated owner, property and arrears fields and a public-notice exclusion. Assessment and property number formats differ by council and are unverified, so values are loose and placeholder-guarded. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's council property / rates assessment number format (see docs/identifiers.md#council-property-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Council Rates Concession or Hardship Application
patterns.description: Individual applications, assessments and decisions for rates concessions made by Queensland local governments under Local Government Regulation 2012 ch 4 pt 10. Covers pensioner rebates (s 120(1)(a) land owned or occupied by a pensioner; s 123 rebate for land occupied by pensioners; sch 8 defines a pensioner as a holder of a pensioner concession card), hardship concessions (s 120(1)(d) payment will cause hardship to the land owner) and agreements to defer rates (ss 121(b), 125). A concession for a stated ratepayer can be granted only after that ratepayer applies (s 122(3)). These records link a named applicant and property to Centrelink or DVA concession status, income, household circumstances and the council's decision. Council concession policies, revenue statements and class resolutions are public and are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a rates concession phrase (pensioner (rates) concession / rebate / remission / subsidy / discount; rates or rating concession, rebate, remission, relief or deferral; rates (financial) hardship; hardship application / assistance / concession for rates; deferral of rates; application or agreement to defer rates; concession for or on rates). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: an applicant/property field (named applicant, ratepayer, owner, pensioner or occupier; a property or assessment number containing a digit; or a property address with a street number), an eligibility field (pensioner concession / health care / DVA / gold card number, a Centrelink CRN, a DVA file number, a card expiry date, or a filled pension or payment type), a hardship field (filled reason for hardship or circumstances, an income amount, a number of dependants, or a rent / mortgage / living expense amount) or a decision field (decision / outcome / recommendation of approved, declined, granted or deferral approved, or a rebate, concession, remission or deferral granted with an amount, percentage or status). 85 tier requires an applicant/property field AND an eligibility, hardship or decision field AND an independent council or Centrelink term (council, local government, ratepayer, rate notice, Centrelink, Services Australia, Department of Veterans' Affairs). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a policy exclusion (this policy, policy statement, revenue statement, to be eligible, how to apply, you may be eligible, frequently asked questions). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface concession policies, budget resolutions and the Regulation.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the concession, rebate, hardship and deferral terms come from LGR ss 119-126, but councils also use them in public concession policies, revenue statements and budget resolutions, so enforce tiers need populated applicant, eligibility, hardship or decision fields and a policy exclusion. The Centrelink CRN shape (9 digits and a letter) is reused from au-centrelink-crn; concession card and rates assessment formats are unverified, so those values are loose and placeholder-guarded. The State Government pensioner rate subsidy form's field names were not verified and are not used as anchors. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's council property / rates assessment number format (see docs/identifiers.md#council-property-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Council CEO and Senior Executive Register of Interests
patterns.description: Register of interests entries and lodgement forms for a Queensland local government's chief executive officer, senior executive employees, councillor advisors and persons related to them (spouse or dependent), kept under Local Government Regulation 2012 (Qld) ss 289-291 and schedule 5 (shareholdings and controlling interests, executive officer roles, trusts, self managed superannuation funds, land, liabilities, gifts, sponsored travel and other particulars). Unlike a councillor's register, which may be inspected by the public (s 293(1)) and is published as an extract (s 295), these registers are open only to councillors, the CEO and persons permitted by law (s 293(2)-(3)); access must be applied for in writing and logged (s 294), and disclosure outside those persons is an offence (s 297(2)). The public councillor register, its published extracts and councillor declarations in minutes are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a register of interests phrase (register/registers of interests, interests register, register of financial interests, statement of interests). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, BOTH a restricted-role field (position/role/designation/category/register type/capacity/relevant person/relationship label whose value is chief executive officer, CEO, deputy CEO, senior executive employee, senior executive, general manager, executive director, director, councillor advisor, spouse, dependent, related person or person related to) AND a populated schedule 5 interest field (shareholding, corporation, company, trust, self managed superannuation fund, real property, land, liabilities, gifts, sponsored travel, hospitality, investments, executive officer, directorships, memberships, donations, other income, financial institution, debts, partnerships followed by a non-placeholder value; nil/none values do not count). 85 tier requires the role field, two distinct interest fields (min_count 2, unique results) AND an independent corroborative term (section 290/291/294/297, schedule 5, related person, spouse, dependent, mayor, restricted, confidential, access log). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a public-register/guidance exclusion (councillor register of interests, register of interests of a councillor, register of councillor interests, extract of the register, published extract, may be inspected by the public, fact sheet, guideline, frequently asked questions). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface councillor registers, guidance and legislation.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "register of interests" is shared by the public councillor register, state parliament registers and guidance, so enforce tiers need a restricted-role value (CEO, senior executive employee, councillor advisor or related person) and populated schedule 5 interest fields. The approved form layouts vary by council and were not verified, so field labels follow schedule 5 particulars. A councillor's spouse register (restricted under s 293(2)(d)) that is labelled only with councillor wording can fall to 65. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Council Rates or Water Account Domestic and Family Violence Affected Customer Record
patterns.description: Rates and water account records held by Queensland councils and water service providers that flag a ratepayer or water customer as affected by domestic and family violence and record the protective steps taken: a safe or preferred contact method, a suppressed or confidential postal or residential address, instructions not to disclose account details to a co-owner, joint account holder or former partner, account separation, redirected rate notices, and payment arrangements, interest waivers or holds on recovery or restriction action. Unlike energy (National Energy Retail Rules Part 3A) there is no verified Queensland statute that sets out these steps for councils or water providers; they come from council and utility hardship and DFV policies, with the Local Government Regulation 2012 s 120(1)(d) hardship concession and Information Privacy Act 2009 obligations in the background. Modelled on au-energy-family-violence-customer-record. Published council and utility DFV and hardship policies are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a DFV-affected customer phrase (affected by / experiencing / impacted by / fleeing / escaping / victim(-survivor) of domestic (and family) or family violence; domestic or family violence flag, indicator, alert, marker, customer, ratepayer, account, note, case or hardship; DFV, DV or FV flag / indicator / alert / marker / customer / ratepayer / account / note / case / hardship / affected). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: an account field (property, assessment, rates account, water account, customer or account number with a value containing a digit; a named account holder, ratepayer, registered owner, owner, co-owner, customer or applicant; a property, service, supply, premises or rateable land address with a street number; or a water meter number) or a protection-action field, split across a contact/disclosure regex and an account-arrangement regex (preferred or safe contact method with a value; "do not disclose / discuss / release / share / provide / send ... to / with the joint, former, other or co- owner, account holder, partner or ratepayer"; a postal, residential, mailing, contact or notice address suppressed, withheld, confidential or protected; address or contact details suppression, or a suppressed / silent address, record or account, with yes / active / applied / approved; rate, rates or water notices redirected or sent to a stated place; account separation / split with a status; a payment plan or arrangement amount; interest, fees or penalties waived, remitted or suspended; or recovery, debt recovery, collection or restriction action suspended or on hold). 85 tier requires an account field AND a protection-action field AND an independent council or water term (council, local government, rate notice, rates notice, rates, ratepayer, water, sewerage, meter, Urban Utilities, Unitywater). patterns.name: Queensland Development Application Submission Submitter Details (Redaction Aid)
patterns.description: Submitter names and contact details in submissions about Queensland development applications, submission summaries in assessment reports, and decision notices that list principal submitters. Under the Planning Act 2016 sch 2, a properly made submission must state the name and residential or business address of all submission-makers and one postal or electronic address for service. Section 63(2)(h) requires the decision notice to state the name, residential or business address and electronic address of each principal submitter. Planning Regulation 2017 sch 22 s 5(1)(d) requires the assessment manager to keep any properly made submission available for inspection and purchase. These documents are public by law. Many councils redact submitters' contact details before publishing online, but that is council practice, not a verified statutory requirement. This is a discovery-only redaction aid. It surfaces documents that carry submitter details so they can be reviewed before publication. It is not a blocking classifier.
patterns.operation: Discovery only (65). Primary: properly made submission(s), submitter(s) / principal submitter(s), submission-maker(s), submission(s) about / on / regarding / in relation to / objecting to / in support of / against / for the (proposed) development (application), application or DA, objection(s) to the (proposed) development (application), application or DA, and development application submission(s). The 65 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated submitter field and planning context. The submitter field is a submitter / principal submitter / submission-maker / objector [name / address / details / email / phone / mobile / contact] label, name of (the) (principal) submitter, submission (made) by, your (full) name, or an unqualified name, full name, residential / postal / business / home / electronic address, address (for service), email, phone, mobile or telephone label (the unqualified labels must not follow another word, so Applicant name and Owner address do not count). The value must be a name of two or more capitalised words, a street address, an Australian phone number or an email address, on the same line as the label. Placeholder values are rejected (withheld, not, none, nil, redacted, suppressed, blank lines, brackets). Planning context is development application, Planning Act 2016, Planning Regulation 2017, assessment manager, public notification, material change of use, reconfiguring a lot, planning scheme, decision notice or council. The tier ANDs NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (how to make / making a submission, fact sheet, frequently asked questions). There are no 75 or 85 tiers, because the documents are public.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Submission and submitter wording plus a populated name or contact field and planning context is a reliable signal for submitter details. However, the documents are public by law, so the classifier only flags them for redaction review at 65. The recommended confidence is 65 and there are no enforce tiers. 65 is a heuristic evidence tier, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Queensland Council Disaster Vulnerable Persons Register Record
patterns.description: Completed registrations and entries in a Queensland council or Local Disaster Management Group vulnerable persons register (VPR), also called a special needs register or a register of persons requiring special assistance in a disaster or evacuation. A populated entry ties a named person and home address to disability, mobility or medical dependency (oxygen, dialysis, life sustaining equipment), a carer or emergency contact, and evacuation or transport needs. The Disaster Management Act 2003 does not create or name these registers. Councils keep them under the state framework "People with vulnerabilities in disasters: A framework for an effective local response" (2016) and their own local disaster management arrangements. Information acquired while performing a function under the Act is covered by the s 139 confidentiality offence. The Local Disaster Management Plan is public (s 60) but the register is not.
patterns.operation: Primary: a register or form title (vulnerable persons register [registration / form / entry / record], VPR registration / entry / record / form, persons requiring special assistance in a disaster, special needs registration [form], people with vulnerabilities in disasters). Field regexes use same-line values only, so a blank form's stacked labels (Name: / Address:) never count, and values are placeholder-guarded. 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated field: a person or address field (name, full name, registrant, resident or client followed by a capitalised name of two or more words; address, residential address or location followed by a street number and name), a needs field (description of special requirements, special needs, assistance required, evacuation needs, life sustaining equipment, medical condition / equipment / dependency, mobility aid, support aid or assistance animal, medication or disability followed by a value that is not none, nil or no), or a carer / contact field (contact person, carer, next of kin, emergency contact, support person, relationship to the person being registered, followed by a value). 85 requires all three field types together: person or address, needs, and carer or contact. All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (framework for an effective local response, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, how to register, who can register). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone). It will surface council VPR web pages, blank forms, the state framework and news.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. The register titles are distinctive but not statutory. "Vulnerable Persons Register" and the form title "Registration - Persons Requiring Special Assistance in a Disaster/Evacuation" come from a Queensland council page and form (Central Highlands Regional Council, Annexure 3-C). Other councils word their forms differently, and recall on differently titled registers is lower. The needs, contact and person field labels follow that form: person being registered, contact person who can provide special assistance, description of special requirements, support aid animal, life sustaining equipment, relationship to the person being registered. Framework vocabulary adds oxygen dependent, reliant on medical equipment and medication, and carers. Field values are loose and placeholder-guarded. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.
