patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a completed vulnerable persons register entry or special-assistance registration. The entry ties a named person and home address to disability, mobility limits or dependence on medical equipment such as oxygen or dialysis, along with carers and evacuation needs. It is health information tied to the location of a person who may not be able to self-evacuate. Disclosure exposes health status and makes the person identifiable as someone living alone or dependent on others, which carries risks of targeting and exploitation. Loss or corruption of the register can delay evacuation. Information acquired under the Disaster Management Act 2003 is subject to the s 139 confidentiality offence. Council web pages, the state framework, LDMPs and blank forms are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 and the Medium tier reflect an entry tying a named person and home address to disability or oxygen or dialysis dependence, flagging someone who may not self-evacuate. Labels stay PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy; SENSITIVE rather than PROTECTED applies to a single entry, though register loss can delay evacuation.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to one person's health status and location, backed by the s 139 confidentiality offence. A full register extract would justify High handling.

patterns.name: Queensland Drinking Water Incident Notification Record
patterns.description: Working records of a drinking water service provider's notifications to the drinking water regulator under Water Supply (Safety and Reliability) Act 2008 (Qld) s 102 (notice of noncompliance with water quality criteria) and s 102A (notice of prescribed incident): the immediate notification and the follow-up notice in the approved form covering the noncompliance or incident, the circumstances, the action taken or to be taken, and the measures to prevent recurrence. Includes internal boil water notice decision and incident logs that carry the scheme, incident reference, notification times, parameter exceedances (E. coli, total coliforms, turbidity NTU, chlorine mg/L) and corrective actions. Distinct from au-water-quality-data-reference, which covers routine measured water quality data: this classifier needs the incident or notification structure. Public boil water notices, media releases and published DWQMP annual or water quality reports are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: an incident/notification phrase (notice of noncompliance with water quality criteria, notice of prescribed incident, prescribed incident, water quality incident/noncompliance/non-compliance, drinking water incident/noncompliance, noncompliance with the water quality criteria, boil water notice/advisory/alert, do not drink/consume notice). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated incident-administration field: scheme or scheme name, service provider or SPID, incident number/reference/ID/date/type, date and time of detection/incident/notification, time regulator notified or informed, notified to regulator, or sampling point / sample location, each with a non-placeholder value. 85 tier requires that field AND a second distinct structure (a parameter exceedance such as E. coli, total or thermotolerant coliforms, turbidity, free/total chlorine, chlorine residual, monochloramine, fluoride, nitrate, manganese, Naegleria or trihalomethanes followed within 25 characters by a number with NTU, mg/L, ug/L, MPN/100mL, cfu/100mL or orgs/100mL; or a populated action field of at least three words: action taken/proposed/to be taken, corrective or immediate actions, root cause, circumstances, measures to prevent recurrence) AND an independent corroborative term (regulator, section 102/102A, water quality criteria, DWQMP, drinking water quality management plan, Queensland Health, public health unit, ADWG, exceedance, detection, reasonable excuse). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a public-notice/publication exclusion (rolling boil, residents are advised, until further notice, media release, we apologise for the inconvenience, annual report, water quality report, fact sheet, frequently asked questions). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface public boil water notices, legislation and guidance.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the s 102/102A notice titles and "prescribed incident" are statutory and distinctive, but boil water notice wording is widely published, so enforce tiers require populated incident-administration fields and a public-notice exclusion. Parameter values are unit-checked only. The approved form's own field headings were not available to the research, so field labels follow the s 102(3)/102A(3) content list (noncompliance or incident, circumstances, action taken, preventive measures) and common incident-log labels. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's case / matter reference number format (see docs/identifiers.md#case-reference-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a drinking water service provider's s 102 or s 102A notification working record or incident log: the affected scheme, the contamination or treatment failure (E. coli, turbidity, disinfection loss), when it was detected and notified, and the corrective actions. Before a public notice is issued, disclosure can cause panic or misinformation, and the circumstances and root-cause detail reveal treatment-plant weaknesses in a critical infrastructure asset and potential regulatory offences; afterwards the record still carries enforcement-relevant admissions. It rarely identifies private individuals. Public boil water notices, published DWQMP annual reports, legislation and blank forms are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 7 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE Government.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 fits PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Government because a s 102 or s 102A notification record reveals a scheme's contamination or treatment failure, root cause and corrective action before public notice. PROTECTED is not met: it rarely identifies individuals and the incident itself is usually made public.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling protects pre-publication water quality incident records and treatment weaknesses at a named scheme. It is not High because the substance is typically released through a public notice.

patterns.name: Queensland Elector Participation Data (Who Voted, How and Where)
patterns.description: Post-election elector participation data ("election and elector information") that the Electoral Commission of Queensland releases on request to registered political parties, independent members and, for council elections, councillors: for each elector who voted, their name and address, whether they voted in person, by post or in another way, and the polling booth location (Electoral Act 1992 s 133A; LG Fact Sheet 04). Also marked-roll extracts that record which electors voted. The data may be used only for an election-related purpose (s 133A(6), maximum 200 penalty units) and never includes silent electors (s 133A(5)). Booth-level results, turnout statistics, results by vote type and the fact sheet are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: election and elector information, elector (participation) information or data, voter / elector participation, marked (electoral / voters / certified) roll or list, voted in person / by post / (in an)other way, vote / voting method or type, how (the elector) voted, or section / s 133A. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces results, turnout statistics and the fact sheet. 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated elector name: a delimited surname and given names followed by a street address, or a labelled elector / voter / name / surname / family name field with a non-placeholder value. 85 requires a delimited elector row with a street address AND a vote-method value (in person, by post, postal, pre-poll, early vote, ordinary or other way, either in a column after the address or as a labelled vote method / how voted / voted field) AND a polling booth value (a labelled polling booth / place / voting centre field, or a column value ending State School, Community / Civic / Early Voting / Pre-poll Centre, Hall, PCYC, Library or Uniting Church), plus an independent electoral context term. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude fact-sheet / FAQ / legislation-site wording and results wording (formal / informal votes, two-candidate preferred, first preferences).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the s 133A wording is distinctive, but vote-method and polling-place vocabulary is shared with published results, turnout statistics and the ECQ fact sheet, so enforce tiers need populated elector names and 85 needs name-and-address rows with per-elector vote method and booth values. The column layout of ECQ's s 133A release is not published, so the row shapes are generic. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Queensland Electoral Roll Extract or Copy
patterns.description: Extracts and copies of the Queensland electoral roll or a council voters roll: the certified copies and electronic roll data that the Electoral Commission of Queensland (ECQ) must give candidates, registered political parties, members of the Legislative Assembly and local governments (Electoral Act 1992 s 61; Local Government Electoral Act 2011 s 21), and AEC Electoral Roll Access (ERA) data files. The roll holds each elector's surname, given names, address, sex, occupation, date of birth, identifying number and enrolment date (s 58(3); Electoral Regulation 2024 s 3). Only name and address are in the publicly available part (sch 1; Regulation s 5), so a copy that carries date of birth, sex, occupation, enrolment date or an elector ID is restricted information whose misuse is an offence (s 177; Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 s 91B). Enrolment figures, public inspection guidance, party and candidate registers and fact sheets are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: electoral / voters / council voters roll, roll extract / data / changes / copy / download, certified copy or list of the roll or of voters, elector ID / identifying number, electoral district / division, or ERA extract / download / data file. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces guidance, fact sheets and enrolment statistics. 75 requires, within 300 characters, at least two different elector rows: a delimited surname and given names followed by a street address (tab, comma, pipe, semicolon or a run of spaces between columns, as in a printed or exported roll). 85 additionally requires a populated non-public field, either on an elector row (a date of birth or enrolment date, or a single-letter sex code, in a column after the address) or as a labelled field (date of birth, enrolment date, sex / gender, occupation or elector ID with a non-placeholder value), or an AEC ERA data-file name (EX<nn>_C<nnnn>_<8 digits>_<STATE>_<DIVISION>.txt/.zip), plus an independent electoral context term. The elector ID has no published format, so it is a loose digit-bearing label value. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude fact-sheet, FAQ, legislation-site and "how to enrol / check your enrolment / you can inspect" guidance wording.

patterns.name: Queensland Serious Electrical Incident or Dangerous Electrical Event Notification
patterns.description: Completed notifications and internal records of a serious electrical incident or dangerous electrical event under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld). Serious electrical incident (s 11) covers a person killed by electricity or receiving a shock or injury treated by or under a doctor, or at high voltage. Dangerous electrical event (s 12) covers unsafe proximity to HV equipment, significant property damage caused by electricity, and unlicensed or unsafe electrical work. A business or undertaking must notify the regulator immediately (Electrical Safety Regulation 2013 s 265, with written notice within 48 hours if required and records kept 5 years). A distribution entity must give written notice in the approved form received within 24 hours (s 266). Section numbers are taken from the 27 Sep 2024 version of the Regulation; the current version could not be retrieved. Records name the injured or involved person, date, time and location, the equipment and voltage, the injury and treatment, and the notification to the Electrical Safety Office. The Act and Regulation, ESO safety alerts and prosecution summaries, toolbox talks and blank forms are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: serious electrical incident, dangerous electrical event, Electrical Safety Office, or electrical incident notification / report. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface the Act and Regulation, safety alerts, toolbox talks and blank forms. 75 requires, within 300 characters, either a populated incident field (date or time of the incident or event with a date/time value; location, site or address of the incident with a value; injured / involved person or worker with a name; equipment involved or voltage with a value) or an injury and treatment narrative (received or sustained an electric shock, burns or injury followed by treated, doctor, hospital, ambulance or first aid, or "treated by a doctor" / "admitted to hospital" / "transported to ... Hospital"). 85 requires two distinct populated incident fields (two when/where fields, two who/what fields, each min_count 2 unique, or one of each) plus a notification structure (notified, reported or advised to the ESO, Electrical Safety Office, WHSQ or the regulator with a time or date, or an ESO / notification / incident reference number with a value). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. Enforce tiers also exclude legislation and publication text (Maximum penalty, penalty units, legislation.qld.gov.au, safety alert, toolbox talk, prosecution and fine reporting, "you must notify").
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: serious electrical incident and dangerous electrical event are defined terms in ss 11-12 of the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) and appear in almost every ESO publication, so enforcement depends on populated incident fields and injury or notification detail. The approved form's field headings could not be verified (the PDF download was blocked), so field labels are common incident-report labels, not the form's exact wording. Electrical licence numbers have no published format and are not used. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

keywords: person conducting a business or undertaking

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's electrical safety office notification reference format (see docs/identifiers.md#eso-incident-notification-reference). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Electoral Enrolment Application or Update Record
patterns.description: Completed electoral enrolment and update-of-enrolment forms, and the enrolment transaction records that ECQ and the AEC hold under the joint roll arrangement (Electoral Act 1992 (Qld) s 62). A claim for enrolment carries the elector's name, date of birth, residential, postal and previous addresses, and evidence of identity: an Australian driver's licence number, an Australian passport number, Medicare card details or a citizenship certificate number (Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 ss 98, 98AA; AEC form ER022ESw_QLD Q2, Q3, Q6 and Q7). Queensland enrolment and provisional enrolment of 16 and 17 year olds run under Electoral Act 1992 ss 65 and 66. Date of birth, sex, occupation and enrolment date are restricted information that is never in the publicly available part of the roll (Electoral Regulation 2024 s 5), and Electoral Act s 33 makes the information confidential in the hands of anyone administering the Act. The "Enrol or update your enrolment" guidance, blank forms and published enrolment figures are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: enrolment application / form / claim / record / details / update / change / transaction, application or claim for enrolment, update / change / transfer of enrolment, provisional enrolment, re-enrolment, electoral enrolment, enrol to vote, enrol or update, or the ER022 heading "registration as a silent elector and/or enrolment". Every enforce tier also needs an electoral context term within 300 characters (electoral roll, elector, Electoral Commission of Queensland, ECQ, AEC, electoral district or division, electorate, Electoral Act 1992, Commonwealth Electoral Act, enrolled address, general postal voter, silent elector). This keeps school and training enrolment forms at 65. 75 requires context plus a populated date of birth field (date of birth, birth date or DOB followed by a date on the same line) and a populated address field (residential, postal, enrolled, previous, home or street address followed by a street number and name or a PO Box). 85 requires context plus a populated date of birth field and a populated evidence-of-identity number field (driver's licence, licence, passport, Medicare card or citizenship certificate number followed by a value of 6 to 16 characters containing a digit). Values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded, so blank forms stay at 65. All tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary; enforce tiers also exclude published figures and guidance (total State enrolment, weighted enrolment, enrolment statistics or figures, frequently asked questions, fact sheet, legislation.qld.gov.au). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Enrolment wording is shared with school, TAFE and course enrolment, so enforce tiers need an electoral context term and populated fields. The identity fields are label-anchored because the classifier does not validate licence, passport or Medicare formats; the elector identifying number (Electoral Act s 58(3)(d)) has no published format and is not used. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Queensland Environmental Harm Notification or Environmental Authority Incident Report
patterns.description: Populated environmental incident records under the Environmental Protection Act 1994 (Qld): duty-to-notify reports of serious or material environmental harm (s 320B employee to employer and s 320D employer written notice to the administering authority, each within 24 hours; s 320DA owner, occupier or auditor), transitional environmental program (TEP) documents (ss 330-344E), environmental authority (EA) non-compliance and incident reports, and incidents at regulated structures such as ash dams and tailings or process-water dams (assessed by consequence category). The target is an internal incident notification, investigation or compliance report with a filled incident date, location, contaminant, release quantity or EA field. Lodged EA conditions, the EA public register and published monitoring results (s 540 public register) are public and are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: notice or notification of (serious or material) environmental harm, serious or material environmental harm, section 320B/320C/320D/320DA, transitional environmental program, regulated structure, consequence category, environmental incident notification or report, or EA non-compliance / incident notification or report. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces the Act, EA conditions, guidance and the public register. 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated incident field (date or date/time of incident, release, discharge, event, spill or exceedance; incident date, time or location; location of release; release or discharge point; receiving environment or waters; contaminant; substance released; quantity or volume released; EA number or reference; environmental authority; condition breached; notified by; reported by; duration) whose value is not blank, bracketed or a placeholder. 85 requires two distinct populated incident fields, a release or exceedance measurement (a release, discharge, spill, overflow, seepage, exceedance, limit, concentration or volume term followed within 40 characters by a value in kL, ML, m3, litres, tonnes, mg/L, ug/L, mg/m3 or NTU) and independent evidence: notification-duty vocabulary (administering authority, 24 hours, Pollution Hotline, containment, clean-up, root cause, corrective action, ash dam, seepage) or a public-format EA number (EPPR, EPSX, EPSL, EPVX, EPVL or EPPG plus 8 digits, P-EA- plus 9 digits, EA plus 7 digits), used only as supporting evidence. All tiers exclude template/fixture text and legislation, public-register and media text (maximum penalty, penalty units, public register, permit holder, media release, fact sheet).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the duty-to-notify, TEP and regulated-structure terms are statutory and appear in the Act, EA conditions and guidance, so they are discovery-only alone. Enforcement needs populated incident fields (and at 85 a release or exceedance measurement), which legislation, EA conditions and the public register lack. EA numbers are public formats and never drive a tier on their own. Published monitoring reports lodged under EA conditions can carry filled fields and measurements; "public register" wording is excluded, but a lodged report copied without that wording can still match. "Design storage allowance", "mandatory reporting level" and "register of regulated structures" are unverified and not used. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's environmental incident / notification reference format (see docs/identifiers.md#environmental-incident-reference). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: Internal environmental harm notifications, EA non-compliance and incident investigations, and regulated-structure (ash dam, process-water dam) incident records describe releases of contaminants from an identified site - what, where, when, how much and against which licence condition - before or beyond what is lodged on the public register. patterns.name: Queensland Food Business Licence Application or Inspection and Improvement Notice Record
patterns.description: Council food business licence applications, food premises inspection reports and improvement notices under the Food Act 2006 (Qld). A person must hold a licence to carry on a licensable food business (s 49). The application is made to the local government (s 52) in the approved form, which must provide for the applicant's contact details (s 85). It must state the applicant's name and address, or for a corporation its directors, the premises, the business, and details of any conviction for a relevant offence (s 53). Council decides suitability, including convictions and previous refusal, suspension or cancellation (s 57). An authorised person may give an improvement notice stating the provision believed to be contravened, how it is contravened and the period to remedy it (s 209). Information gained in administering the Act about a person's affairs is confidential (s 272). The chief executive's register of mobile-premises food businesses (ss 264-266), council lists of licensed businesses and published conviction or "name and shame" registers are public and are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: food business licence [application / renewal / restoration / amendment / number / certificate / conditions], licence to carry on a licensable food business, licensable food business, food safety / food premises / food business inspection [report / record / checklist / findings], routine / follow-up / compliance inspection report, improvement notice, food safety supervisor notification or details, accredited food safety program. Every enforce tier needs a food context term within 300 characters (Food Act 2006, food business, food premises, food safety, Food Standards Code, food handler, food handling, environmental health officer). Field values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded. 75 requires context plus one populated structure, either a licensee / person field (licensee, applicant, proprietor, director, food safety supervisor, contact person, person in charge, operator, residential / home / postal address, phone, mobile, email or date of birth, followed by a name of two or more capitalised words, a street address, an Australian phone number, an email address or a date) or an inspection / suitability field (non-compliance, finding, observation, contravention, provision contravened, relevant provision, action required, corrective action, remedy by, period to remedy, compliance or re-inspection date, inspection outcome / result, convictions, relevant offence, details of the offence, previously refused / cancelled / suspended). 85 requires context plus both a person field and an inspection / suitability field. All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a public-register / guidance exclusion (name and shame, register of food businesses, public register, published register, register of auditors, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, how to apply, Work Health and Safety Act). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Licence and inspection vocabulary is statutory (Food Act 2006 ss 49, 52-53, 57, 209), but it also fills council web pages, the Act and public licence lists, and "improvement notice" is shared with work health and safety law. Enforce tiers therefore need food context and populated same-line fields, and public registers are excluded by phrase. Licence and inspection numbers are council-defined and are not relied on. A company licensee name matches the person field, so an unlabelled public list that names companies with phone numbers can still reach 75. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a council food business licence application, inspection report or improvement notice that names the licensee or applicant with private contact details, or records inspection findings, contraventions or conviction details. Food Act s 272 makes information about a person's affairs gained in administering the Act confidential, and licence applications carry convictions, previous refusals and directors' details (ss 53, 57). Most sole-trader licensees are identifiable individuals. Legislation, blank forms, public registers of food businesses, published conviction registers and WHS notices are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 4 supports OFFICIAL with privacy handling.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 supports PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL DLM with privacy handling for a council food licence application, inspection report or improvement notice naming a licensee or recording contraventions, kept confidential by Food Act s 272. SENSITIVE is not met because the usual record concerns one business's compliance, and public registers are excluded.

generic.rationale: Low with Low handling fits routine licensing and inspection records for one food business; conviction details on an application would justify Medium.

patterns.risk_description: The keyword pattern identifies Queensland tender packages and evaluation records containing selection criteria, procurement submissions, pricing schedules, value-for-money analysis, or standing-offer details. Premature disclosure can help a supplier optimize against confidential scoring, undercut rivals, coordinate bids, or challenge a process using information unavailable to competitors. The agency, evaluators, bidders, and public procurement outcome may suffer serious but procurement-bounded financial and integrity harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Government fit that non-public package, while protected operational requirements or government-wide strategic damage would be needed for PROTECTED.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, SENSITIVE Government, SENS_Gov, and Medium because confidential evaluation and pricing can materially distort a tender. PROTECTED is not met by the normal package because consequences remain bounded to one procurement and do not establish significant protected-government damage.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling is appropriate for tender submissions, scoring, evaluations, and non-public pricing. High handling requires protected requirements or consequences extending beyond the individual procurement.

patterns.risk_description: The keyword classifier identifies Queensland Health handovers containing ISBAR language, patient status, current medicines, observations, clinical notes, and treatment plans rather than a generic project handover. A genuine handover consolidates current condition, immediate risks, therapies, and care responsibilities, so disclosure can expose intimate health facts, enable impersonation, or disrupt safe continuity of care. The normal unit is one patient's shift or transfer record, creating serious privacy and operational harm without assuming a ward-wide census. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE are appropriate; PROTECTED would require a bulk handover repository, critical incident coordination, or compromise that creates significant patient-safety damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, the Personal-Privacy DLM, and Medium for a current clinical handover. PROTECTED is not met because the normal record concerns one patient and does not establish broad or severe safety compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium classification and Medium Personal-Privacy DLM protect the combined current status, medication, observation, and treatment information in one handover.

patterns.name: QLD Health Clinical Incident or Patient Safety Report
patterns.description: Populated clinical incident and patient safety records from Queensland Hospital and Health Services: RiskMan and PRIME CI clinical incident notifications, patient safety incident reports, severity assessment code (SAC) ratings, sentinel event notifications, clinical reviews and root cause analysis (RCA) reports under the Hospital and Health Boards Act 2011 (Qld). They identify the patient harmed or at risk, the incident and its SAC or harm rating, and often the staff involved, contributing factors and open disclosure. Boundary: pharmacovigilance and trial adverse event reports belong to global-top500-339-adverse-event-reports; aged care SIRS notifications to au-aged-care-serious-incident-notification; NDIS reportable incidents to au-ndis-reportable-incident.
patterns.operation: Primary: clinical incident (report, notification, record, form, review, analysis), patient safety incident or event (report), RiskMan, PRIME CI, sentinel event, root cause analysis, severity assessment code. 65 (discovery only): primary alone, which surfaces policies, statistics and IT root cause analyses. 75: primary plus a populated patient field (patient name, DOB, URN / UR number, MRN, Medicare, IHI) plus a populated incident field (incident number / ID / reference, incident date or time, date of incident, location of incident, incident type or category, SAC rating / score, harm level or rating, severity, outcome for patient). 85: the 75 evidence plus independent review context (contributing factors, open disclosure, clinical review panel, review team, commissioning authority, learning review, human factors, recommendations, findings, Hospital and Health Boards Act). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and guideline, policy, training, statistics and media framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: clinical incident, RiskMan, PRIME CI and SAC wording is specific to health incident management, and enforce tiers need a populated patient field and a populated incident field. Root cause analysis and incident numbers also appear in IT and WHS reporting, which lack a patient field and stay at 65. Staff-only incidents without a patient are not covered.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier recognises clinical incident, RiskMan / PRIME CI, SAC and root cause analysis records and enforces only when a populated patient field sits with a populated incident field, with 85 also needing review context such as contributing factors or open disclosure. A genuine record links a named patient to an adverse outcome (fall, medication error, missed deterioration, death) and often names the staff involved and the failures found. Disclosure can harm the patient and family, prejudice open disclosure, coronial or litigation processes, and expose clinicians; RCA reports also carry statutory confidentiality under the Hospital and Health Boards Act 2011 (Qld). The normal unit is one incident, so risk 8 and SENSITIVE apply.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a populated clinical incident record links a named patient to an adverse outcome and can name staff and failures. PROTECTED is not met for one incident: it does not expose a child protection matter, a whistleblower or bulk incident data, and serious harm still depends on a single patient episode.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling protects the patient's harm event and the review findings for one incident. High would need bulk incident extracts or a register of SAC 1 events.

patterns.name: QLD Health Clinical Credentialing and Scope of Practice Record
patterns.description: Populated credentialing and scope of clinical practice records for named practitioners, as produced under the Queensland Health directive on credentialing and defining the scope of clinical practice: credentialing committee decisions and minutes, credentialing applications and recredentialing files, scope of clinical practice approvals, clinical privileges, conditions and supervision requirements, and referee reports. They name the practitioner with their registration details and record the scope granted, declined or restricted, conditions or undertakings on their Ahpra registration, and referees' frank assessments. Boundary: practitioner directories and lists of labelled provider identifiers belong to global-top500-337-provider-identifier-records; a bare Ahpra registration number to global-ahpra-registration; public sector discipline outcomes to au-qld-public-sector-discipline-record.
patterns.operation: Primary: (re)credentialing committee / decision / application / outcome / file / record / review / panel (including "credentialing and scope of clinical practice committee"), scope of clinical practice, scope of practice decision / approval / review / application / outcome, clinical privileges. 65 (discovery only): primary alone, which surfaces the directive, committee terms of reference and by-laws. 75: primary plus a populated practitioner field (practitioner, applicant, medical officer, doctor or nurse name, Ahpra / registration number, profession, specialty, position, facility) plus a populated decision field (decision, outcome, recommendation, scope granted / approved / requested / declined, privileges granted, conditions, restrictions, supervision requirements, review date, period of appointment, effective date). 85: the 75 evidence plus independent regulatory or assessment context (referee report, conditions on registration, undertakings, notification to Ahpra, Medical Board, Nursing and Midwifery Board, Office of the Health Ombudsman, peer review, performance concerns, supervised practice, Health Practitioner Regulation National Law). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and directive, terms-of-reference, by-law, guideline, training and media framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: credentialing and scope of clinical practice wording is specific to health workforce governance, and enforce tiers need a populated practitioner field and a populated decision field, which the directive, committee terms of reference and by-laws lack. Committee minutes that list several practitioners in a table without labels may be missed at 75.
regulations: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law Act 2009 (Qld)

patterns.name: QLD Health Discharge Summary or Referral Letter
patterns.description: Populated clinician-to-clinician transfer documents: hospital discharge summaries, discharge letters, transfer of care summaries, GP and specialist referral letters and requests for specialist consultation. They carry patient identifiers together with the structure of a handover between treating teams: admission and discharge dates, discharge destination, referring, receiving or usual GP, and clinical content such as principal diagnosis, medications on discharge, reason for referral and follow-up arrangements. Boundary: au-qld-health-medical-record covers medical records generally and fires on the bare phrase "discharge summary" plus a patient identifier; this classifier enforces only when discharge or referral structure (dates, referring or receiving clinician) is also populated. Shift handover sheets belong to au-qld-health-clinical-handover; My Health Record documents to au-my-health-record-clinical-document.
patterns.operation: Primary: discharge summary / letter / referral, transfer of care summary or letter, GP / specialist / medical / outpatient / clinical referral (letter), referral letter, letter of referral, request for specialist consultation or opinion. 65 (discovery only): primary alone, which surfaces guidelines, patient leaflets and blank forms. 75: primary plus a populated patient identifier field (patient name, DOB, URN / UR number, MRN, Medicare, IHI, DVA, hospital or episode number) plus a populated discharge / referral structure field (admission, discharge or referral date, length of stay, discharge destination, referring / receiving / discharging / admitting / usual doctor, GP, consultant or facility, referred to / by). 85: the 75 evidence plus a populated clinical content field (principal / discharge / secondary diagnosis, procedures performed, medications on discharge, medication changes, reason for referral or admission, presenting complaint, clinical summary, follow-up plan, recommendations, investigations, allergies). Enforce tiers exclude the shared template dictionary and guidance, patient-information, training and news framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the document titles are standard across Queensland Health, private hospitals and general practice, and enforce tiers need populated patient and handover-structure fields, which guidelines, leaflets and blank forms lack. Field labels are matched by wording only, so a clinic letter that uses the same labels without the title stays at 65 and an unusual layout with unlabelled fields may be missed. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

These documents travel by fax, secure messaging, email and patient portals between hospitals, GPs and specialists, so they are among the most frequently misdirected health records. One document exposes identity, diagnosis, treatment, medications and the patient's treating clinicians, enabling discrimination, coercion or fraud. The ordinary unit is one patient episode, so the harm is serious but contained. Risk 8 matches au-qld-health-medical-record and au-qld-health-clinical-handover.

The normal document is routine transport administration and does not itself identify cargo, a protected movement, or critical logistics. Risk 5 OFFICIAL captures the bounded operational value; SENSITIVE is not met without sensitive cargo, precise live movement schedules, protected routes, or critical-supply consequences.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, the OFFICIAL DLM, and Low because an ordinary permit has limited route and operator value. SENSITIVE is not met without sensitive cargo, live protected movements, or critical-logistics consequences.

generic.rationale: Generic Low handling is appropriate for routine heavy-vehicle permit administration, with stronger controls driven by cargo sensitivity and live route timing.

A completed record can expose financial hardship, household composition, disability or support needs, past tenancies, and housing insecurity that may enable stigma, fraud, or coercive targeting. patterns.name: Queensland Local Disaster Management Group Contact List or Activation Roster
patterns.description: Contact lists, call-out lists and activation rosters for a Queensland council's Local Disaster Management Group (LDMG) that hold members' private after-hours mobiles, home phone numbers, home addresses or personal email addresses. Every local government must establish a Local Disaster Management Group (Disaster Management Act 2003 s 29), whose chairperson appoints a local disaster coordinator (s 35). The council gives written notice of the group's members to the police commissioner and the district group each year (s 37). The local disaster management plan must be available for inspection and on the council website (s 60), so published LDMG membership that lists roles and office numbers is public and is a decoy. Information acquired in performing a function under the Act must not be disclosed (s 139). Vulnerable persons registers are covered by au-qld-disaster-vulnerable-persons-register.
patterns.operation: Primary: Local Disaster Management Group, LDMG, [deputy] local disaster coordinator, optionally followed by contact list / details / directory / register, contacts, phone list, membership [list], member list, activation roster / list / contacts, roster, call-out list or on-call roster. 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated private contact field: an after-hours / AH / home / private / personal / mobile / cell phone label followed by an Australian phone number, a home / residential / private address followed by a street address, a personal / private / home email followed by an email address, or an Australian mobile followed by (AH), (after hours), (home), (private) or (personal). Office, switchboard and enquiries numbers do not count. 85 requires two distinct private contact values (min_count 2, unique) plus a named member entry (name, member, chair[person], deputy chair[person], [deputy] local disaster coordinator / LDC, delegate, proxy, contact / duty / on-call / liaison officer, followed by a name of two or more capitalised words that is not a role word such as Mayor or Chief Executive Officer) plus a roster / activation evidence term (activation, activated, stood up, stand up, lean forward, on call, on-call, roster, after hours, call-out, phone tree, contact list). Values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded. All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (available for inspection, public version, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, media release). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium-low. The group and coordinator names are statutory (Disaster Management Act 2003 ss 29, 35), but they also fill public disaster plans, council web pages and news, and contact lists are usually tables where labels are sparse. Enforce tiers therefore need a private contact value (an after-hours / home / private / mobile label, a home address, a personal email, or a mobile marked AH / home). A plain "Mobile:" label counts, so a published media or duty mobile next to LDMG text can reach 75. Contact lists with no labels and no AH markers stay at 65; generic phone classifiers catch those. Roster and activation terms are council practice, not statutory, and are used only as 85 evidence. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies an LDMG contact list or activation roster that ties named disaster management officials, councillors and agency representatives to private after-hours mobiles, home phone numbers, home addresses or personal email addresses. Disclosure exposes those people to unwanted contact and harassment during and after emergencies, and to targeting of the people who coordinate a response; s 139 of the Disaster Management Act 2003 restricts disclosure of information acquired under the Act. The published plan and role-only membership lists are public and are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 4 supports OFFICIAL with privacy handling.

classification.rationale: Risk 4, PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL DLM with privacy handling fit an LDMG roster tying named members to private mobiles, home addresses or personal emails, which s 139 of the Disaster Management Act restricts. SENSITIVE is not met because harm is bounded to harassment or unwanted contact of a small group; role-only membership lists are public.

generic.rationale: Low with Low handling fits one council's private contact roster; misuse is nuisance or targeted contact rather than compromise of the disaster response itself.

patterns.name: Queensland Public Library Member and Borrowing Record
patterns.description: Public library member (borrower, patron) records held by Queensland councils, which may run library facilities as a local government function under the Libraries Act 1988 s 54: membership applications and registrations, member profiles and exports from the library management system, junior member records with parent or guardian consent, borrowing and loan histories, holds and reservations, and overdue notices. The Libraries Act has no member-privacy provision; confidentiality rests on the Information Privacy Act 2009 and council policy. Reading history can reveal political, religious, health and sexuality interests, and junior member records hold children's data. Library policies, conditions of membership, catalogue records and news are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: library member / membership / borrower / patron / card / account (optionally followed by record, details, profile, application, registration, form, number, ID, history, list, report or export); borrower record / details / profile / history / number / ID / barcode; patron record / details / history / barcode / ID; loan, borrowing or circulation history; items on loan, overdue or borrowed; or overdue items / notice / loans. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces policies and help pages. 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a member field (member / borrower / patron / cardholder / account holder name with a two-word value, a library card / member / borrower / patron / card number, ID or barcode containing a digit, or a parent / guardian name for a junior member), a contact field (address with a street number and name, an email address, or an Australian phone or mobile number) or a loan field (dated due, borrowed, checked out, issued, renewed or returned date; an item title; an item barcode; fines or charges owing with a dollar amount; or counts of holds, reservations or items on loan). 85 requires a member field AND a contact or loan field AND an independent corroborative term (branch, overdue, renewal, holds, reservation, junior member, fines, due date, loans and similar). Library card numbers have no public format (vendor and council specific), so the value is a loose, digit-bearing label value. Blank lines, bracket placeholders and n/a/tbc are rejected. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude catalogue and policy wording (call number, place a hold, copies available, catalogue record, this policy/procedure/guide/fact sheet, conditions of membership or use, frequently asked questions, members are/must, legislation.qld.gov.au).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: library member, borrower and loan-history wording is distinctive for library systems, but the same phrases appear in library policies, help pages and membership conditions, and library card number formats are vendor-specific (commonly 14-digit Codabar barcodes, unverified), so enforce tiers need populated member plus contact or loan fields. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's library card / member number format (see docs/identifiers.md#library-card-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a library member or borrowing record that ties a named borrower (card number, home address, phone or email) to their loans, holds and fines. Borrowing history can reveal health conditions, religious or political views, sexuality and family violence circumstances, and junior member records hold children's details and a guardian's contact information. Library policies, catalogue records, blank forms and news are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 5 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

patterns.name: Queensland Major Hazard Facility Safety Case or Hazardous Chemicals Manifest
patterns.description: Queensland major hazard facility (MHF) safety case outlines and safety cases under the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) chapter 9 (ss 551-561, Schedule 18: facility description, process flow drawings, general layout drawings locating major incident hazards and initiators, security arrangements), and manifests of hazardous chemicals under s 347 and Schedule 12 (UN number, proper shipping name, class and division, container and storage area identification, after-hours contacts). Populated versions give a hostile reader a map of what is stored where and how the site is protected.
patterns.operation: Primary: MHF / safety case outline / manifest of hazardous chemicals anchors from WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) ch 7 and ch 9. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface the Regulation, Safe Work guidance, local community information and blank manifest templates. 75 requires, within 300 characters, either a populated Schedule 12 / Schedule 18 field (UN number, proper shipping name, class and division, container or storage area ID, tank ID, drawing number, site address, after-hours contact, security zone or gate with a non-placeholder value) or a manifest table row (UN number followed by an upper-case proper shipping name and a class). 85 requires two distinct populated fields plus independent security or major-incident content (security arrangements, unsupervised access, key register, CCTV, intruder alarm, major incident hazard or initiator, process flow or general layout drawing). All tiers exclude template/fixture text and the pattern-specific exclusion group (local community information, fact sheets, safety data sheet transport sections, media releases).

patterns.risk_description: A populated MHF safety case or hazardous chemicals manifest tells a reader which Schedule 15 chemicals are held, in what quantities and containers, where they sit on the site layout, which events can initiate a major incident and how the site is secured. That is targeting information for sabotage or theft at a facility whose failure can harm the surrounding community. The Regulation gives no confidentiality regime beyond the operator's right to withhold security-exposing information from other facilities (s 562(3)) and the community (s 572(3)), so these documents rely on the operator's own handling. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE; PROTECTED is not justified for a single facility's documents.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 matches PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Government because a populated MHF safety case or Schedule 12 manifest shows which hazardous chemicals are held, where and how the site is secured, which is targeting information. PROTECTED is not met for one facility's documents; it would need aggregation across sites or national-level consequence.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling protects site layouts, chemical inventories and security arrangements that could aid sabotage or theft. A single facility's safety case stays below High.

patterns.name: Queensland Mandatory Notification of Data Breach (MNDB) Statement, Notice or Register Entry
patterns.description: Completed records under the Queensland Mandatory Notification of Data Breach (MNDB) scheme in chapter 3A of the Information Privacy Act 2009 (Qld), as inserted by the Information Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2023: the s 51 statement to the Information Commissioner, the s 53 notice to affected individuals, s 52 further information, and entries in the s 72 register of eligible data breaches. The scheme has applied to Queensland government agencies since 1 July 2025 and to local government since 1 July 2026. A populated record names the agency and gives the date of the breach, the type of eligible data breach (unauthorised access, unauthorised disclosure or loss, s 47), the kinds of personal information involved, the number of individuals affected or notified, and the containment and mitigation steps. OIC guidance, the Act, published MNDB statistics and blank templates are decoys. Overlaps with au-data-breach-report, which is framed around the Commonwealth Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC); Commonwealth NDB signals are excluded from this classifier's enforce tiers.
patterns.operation: Primary: "eligible data breach", "mandatory notification of data breach(es)", "MNDB", "register of eligible data breaches", "data breach register", "Information Privacy Act 2009", a s 51/53/72 statement/notice/register reference, or "statement to the Information Commissioner". 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces OIC guidance, the Act, policies and statistics. 75 requires one populated record field within 300 characters: agency name, a dated breach/discovery/containment/statement/notification field, a count of individuals affected or notified, a selected breach type (unauthorised access / unauthorised disclosure / loss), the kind of personal information involved, or a containment/mitigation step. Blank lines, bracket placeholders and n/a/tbc are rejected. 85 requires two distinct populated fields plus an independent corroborative term (serious harm, mitigate, OIC, privacy complaint, s 166A, phishing, misdirected, ransomware and similar). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude guidance/legislation signals and Commonwealth NDB signals (OAIC, Notifiable Data Breaches, Privacy Act 1988, s 26WK/26WL).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "eligible data breach" and the chapter 3A section references are specific statutory terms, but OIC guidance, agency data breach policies (s 73) and training repeat them, and the Commonwealth NDB scheme uses the same "eligible data breach" phrase. Enforce tiers therefore require populated s 51/53/72 fields and exclude Commonwealth NDB signals. There is no public MNDB reference number format. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: Information Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2023 (Qld)

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's case / matter reference number format (see docs/identifiers.md#case-reference-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a completed Queensland MNDB statement, notice or register entry, gated on populated fields. Before containment, a notification is a roadmap to the exposed data and the control weakness; it also names the agency, the kinds of personal information and the affected cohort, and register entries aggregate incidents and remediation gaps across the agency. Guidance, legislation, statistics and blank templates are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a completed MNDB statement or notice describes the exposed personal information, affected cohort and control weakness, forming a roadmap before containment. PROTECTED is not met because the record describes the breach rather than holding the breached data.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to breach statements and register entries naming data kinds and remediation gaps. High is not met because the notice does not carry the compromised records.

patterns.risk_description: The detector finds Queensland vessel registration, boat-licence, Maritime Safety Queensland, commercial-vessel survey, and hull-identification registration material. A populated record can connect an owner or operator to a vessel and regulatory status, supporting nuisance, low-level fraud, or location correlation when combined with other information. Registration is routine administration and much of the vessel reference data is observable or registry-facing; the pattern does not require a live voyage, valuable cargo, or protected maritime operation. Risk 5 OFFICIAL reflects bounded harm; SENSITIVE is not met without attributed financial data, precise movement, protected ownership, or operational-security context.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, the OFFICIAL DLM, and Low because routine vessel registration has limited standalone misuse value. SENSITIVE is not met without protected ownership, live movements, financial data, or maritime-security consequences.

generic.rationale: Generic Low handling suits ordinary vessel registration and licensing data whose sensitivity rises only with protected parties, finances, or live operational context.

patterns.name: Queensland Mining and Petroleum Royalty Return
patterns.description: Royalty returns, assessments and calculation worksheets for coal, minerals and petroleum (including coal seam gas) lodged with the Queensland Revenue Office by resource authority holders under the Mineral Resources Act 1989, the Mineral Resources (Royalty) Regulation 2025 and the Petroleum and Gas (Production and Safety) Act 2004. A return covers a return period and states the mining lease, petroleum lease or other tenement, the quantity of coal, mineral or petroleum sold, disposed of or used (tonnes, ounces, gigajoules), its value and permitted deductions, the royalty rate and the royalty payable. The figures are a producer's unpublished production, sales value and cost position for each tenement. Intellectual property and music royalty statements (global-top500-177-license-and-royalty-agreements) are a different subject; this SIT needs mining or petroleum context.
patterns.operation: Primary: [mineral / minerals / coal / petroleum / gas / mining] royalty return / assessment / lodgement / calculation / worksheet / statement. Every enforce tier needs resources context within 300 characters (Mineral Resources Act 1989, Mineral Resources (Royalty) Regulation, Petroleum and Gas (Production and Safety) Act, Queensland Revenue Office, Commissioner of State Revenue, QRO, mining lease, petroleum lease, mineral development licence, mining tenement, tenement holder, resource authority, run-of-mine, ROM, saleable coal, thermal / metallurgical / coking coal, coal seam gas, wellhead, free on board, FOB, private royalty, mine site). 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus context plus one of a tenement number (ML, MDL, EPM, EPC, PL, PPL, ATP, MLA with digits, mining / petroleum lease number, labelled tenement), a production quantity (a number with tonnes, kt, Mt, dmt, wmt, oz, GJ, TJ, PJ or bbl, or labelled tonnes / quantity / volume sold / produced / disposed of / mined / used) or a royalty amount (royalty payable / due / amount / rate, total royalty, amount payable, value of coal / mineral / petroleum / gas, gross value, wellhead value, deductions claimed, sale value with a dollar amount or percentage). 85: primary plus context plus any two of tenement, return period (return / royalty / reporting period, period / quarter / month ending with a date or month), quantity and amount. Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (public ruling, fact sheet, QRO Online guide, frequently asked questions, annual report, media release, budget paper, learn more).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Royalty return wording also appears in QRO rulings and guides and in intellectual property or music royalty statements, so enforce tiers need resources context and populated return fields, and guidance framing is excluded. Tenement prefixes are short, so they count only as one field among several. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.
regulations: Petroleum and Gas (Production and Safety) Act 2004 (Qld)

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a Queensland coal, mineral or petroleum royalty return or worksheet with resources context and populated return fields: tenement, return period, quantity sold or produced, value and royalty payable. It exposes a producer's unpublished production volumes, realised prices, deductions and royalty liability for each tenement, which competitors, counterparties and traders can exploit, and it is confidential taxpayer information held by the Queensland Revenue Office. Rulings, guides, budget commentary, blank forms and music or IP royalty statements are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence; PROTECTED is not met for a single return, though consolidated returns across a producer's portfolio sit at the upper end of this band.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence and Medium because a royalty return discloses a producer's unpublished production, sale value and royalty liability per tenement. PROTECTED is not met for a single return; consolidated portfolio returns sit at the upper end of this band.

generic.rationale: Medium Commercial-in-Confidence handling fits a producer's confidential production and royalty figures; consolidated portfolio returns deserve stricter handling within the same level.

patterns.name: QLD Monitored Medicines and Schedule 8 Record
patterns.description: Populated Queensland monitored-medicine records under the Medicines and Poisons Act 2019 (Qld): QScript patient history reports and alerts, Schedule 8 (S8) and other monitored-medicine prescriptions and dispensing records, controlled drug register entries, substance authorities (prescribing approvals for S8 medicines) and Queensland Opioid Treatment Program records. They name a patient and the monitored medicine prescribed or supplied, and often show dispensing history, multiple-prescriber alerts or treatment for drug dependence. Boundary: general medication histories and medication lists without a monitored-medicine frame belong to global-top500-324-medication-histories; the PBS prescriber number alone is au-pbs-prescriber-number.
patterns.operation: Primary: QScript, monitored medicine(s), Schedule 8 / S8 medicine, drug, poison, prescription or register, controlled drug prescription or register, drug of dependence, substance authority, (Queensland) Opioid Treatment Program, QOTP. 65 (discovery only): primary alone, which surfaces prescriber guidance, the monitored-medicines list and QScript training. 75: primary plus a populated patient field (patient name, DOB, address, Medicare, IHI, URN / MRN) plus a populated medicine record field (medicine / drug / item, strength, form, quantity, repeats, dose, directions, date prescribed / dispensed / supplied, prescriber, dispensing pharmacy, indication). 85: the 75 evidence plus independent monitoring or approval context (patient history, dispensing or prescription history, multiple prescribers or pharmacies, early supply, high-risk, drug-dependent person, approval / authority number, approval granted, opioid replacement, Medicines and Poisons Act). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and guidance, user-guide, training and reference-list framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: QScript, Schedule 8 and substance authority wording is specific to monitored medicines and the enforce tiers need a populated patient and a populated medicine field, which guidance, the published monitored-medicines list and training material lack. Pharmacy and GP systems that print S8 dispensing labels with a patient name will match at 75; that is health information about a person and is an accepted match.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier recognises QScript, Schedule 8, substance authority and opioid treatment records and enforces only when a populated patient field sits with a populated medicine field, with 85 also needing monitoring or approval context such as dispensing history, multiple-prescriber alerts or an approval number. A genuine record shows that a named person is prescribed opioids, stimulants or benzodiazepines, may be treated for drug dependence, or has been flagged for high-risk use. Disclosure can drive stigma, discrimination in employment and insurance, and targeting for diversion or theft of medicines. The normal unit is one patient's record, so the harm is serious but contained. Risk 8 matches global-top500-330-substance-use-treatment-records and global-top500-324-medication-histories.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a populated monitored-medicine record reveals a named patient's opioid, stimulant or benzodiazepine treatment and possible drug dependence. PROTECTED is not met for one patient's record; a bulk QScript extract or the prescriber and pharmacy access credentials for the system would be needed.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling protects one patient's controlled-medicine treatment and dependence history. High is not met unless monitoring data is extracted in bulk.

patterns.name: Queensland Apparent Non-Voter Notice, Response or Infringement Record
patterns.description: Elector-level records from ECQ's compulsory voting enforcement process: apparent failure to vote notices issued after a State or local government election (Electoral Act 1992 (Qld) s 134), elector responses giving a valid and sufficient reason for not voting or saying that they did vote and giving the details, payment records (s 135), infringement notices for failing to vote (s 186; LGEA 2011 ss 165, 166, 168), and referrals of unpaid notices to the State Penalties Enforcement Registry (SPER). ECQ's published process is apparent failure to vote notice, then infringement notice, then SPER referral. Excuses often disclose health conditions, hospital admissions, disability, bereavement, travel, religious duty (s 186(2)) or family circumstances. The "Do I have to vote?" page, penalty unit value statements, aggregate non-voter statistics and blank response forms are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: apparent failure to vote, failure / failed / failing to vote, non-voter(s) / nonvoter(s), valid and sufficient reason or excuse, or reason / excuse for not voting. 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated elector name field (elector, voter, name, full name, recipient, addressee or name of elector followed by a name of two or more capitalised words, or surname / family name followed by a capitalised word) AND one apparent-failure-to-vote structure: a labelled notice number (the infringement-notice-number fallback: infringement notice, offence notice or notice followed by no. / number / ref and a value of at least 7 characters containing a digit), a populated reason, excuse or payment field, or a populated address field (street number and name or PO Box). 85 requires a name field AND a labelled notice number AND a populated reason, excuse or payment field (reason [for not voting / given], excuse, explanation, elector's response, response, outcome, decision, I did vote, voted at, polling place attended, amount paid / payable / due / owing / outstanding, penalty amount, payment [received / amount / date / reference / status], paid, fine [amount], due date, pay by, status). Values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded. All tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary; enforce tiers also exclude guidance and statistics wording (do I have to vote, frequently asked questions, fact sheet, value of a penalty unit, penalty unit value, annual report, legislation.qld.gov.au). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Failure-to-vote wording is distinctive to compulsory voting enforcement, but ECQ and AEC guidance, penalty statements and annual reports use the same phrases, so enforce tiers need a populated elector name plus a notice number, excuse, payment or address field. The ECQ notice number format is unpublished, so the notice number is the registry's label-anchored infringement-notice-number fallback. The "Apparent Failure to Vote" notice title and the response wording come from the ECQ "Do I have to vote?" page. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the populated-field evidence with the customer's infringement notice number format (see docs/identifiers.md#infringement-notice-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies an elector-level apparent failure to vote notice, the elector's response, a failure-to-vote infringement notice or a SPER referral that names the elector with an address, a notice number and the excuse or payment position. Excuses routinely disclose health conditions, hospital admissions, disability, pregnancy, bereavement, travel, religious duty and family or domestic circumstances, which is why the label is SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy rather than the roll-derived SENSITIVE Electoral Roll: the harm is the personal circumstances, not the roll entry. Once a notice becomes an infringement notice or SPER referral it also carries enforcement character; an organisation that wants SENSITIVE Legal for that stage should co-deploy au-qld-council-infringement-sper-record, which fires on failure-to-vote infringement notices only when council or local-law context (for example a named city or regional council in a local government election notice) sits within 300 characters. Guidance, penalty unit statements, statistics and blank forms are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 6 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because an elector's excuse routinely discloses health, hospital admission, disability, bereavement or family circumstances with name and address. Higher risk is not met: the notice is one elector's penalty position, and infringement stages can add SENSITIVE Legal separately.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling reflects the personal circumstances in an excuse, not the roll entry. It is not High because the record is one elector's compliance matter.

patterns.description: Detects Queensland notifiable condition reports - notifiable condition or disease notifications, communicable disease reports and public health notifications made under the Public Health Act 2005 (Qld) - when the phrase sits with populated case identifiers and notification fields.
patterns.operation: Primary: notifiable condition/disease report or notification, communicable disease report, public health notification, disease notification or surveillance, reportable condition/disease. 65 (discovery only): phrase alone. 75: phrase plus a populated patient/case identifier field. 85: identifier field plus a populated notification field (condition, organism, onset date, specimen/collection date, test result, notifying doctor or laboratory, vaccination status, occupation, setting) plus independent public-health response evidence (contact tracing, case investigation, outbreak, public health unit, Public Health Act 2005, close contacts, exclusion period). Template and guidance/training framing excluded from 75/85. Converted from keyword_list to regex.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: enforce tiers need a populated case identifier; 85 also needs a notification field and public-health response evidence. Surveillance dashboards, guidelines and news carry the phrases without a case and stay at 65.

patterns.risk_description: The detector recognises Queensland notifiable condition and disease notification language and enforces only when populated case identifier fields sit nearby; phrase-only text stays at 65 discovery. A genuine report can identify an infected person, diagnosis, exposure contacts, locations, and public-health action, enabling stigma, retaliation, evasion of controls, or harm to an active investigation. The ordinary case is bounded to one notification or cluster rather than the full surveillance system, but its disclosure still creates serious individual and operational consequences. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE are justified; PROTECTED would require a major outbreak operation, protected source intelligence, or disclosure causing significant population-safety damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, the Personal-Privacy DLM, and Medium for a notifiable-condition case report. PROTECTED is not met because an ordinary notification lacks major outbreak-command scale and significant population-safety damage.

generic.rationale: Medium classification and Medium Personal-Privacy DLM protect diagnosis, contact, exposure, and surveillance details within one public-health notification.

patterns.name: QLD Perinatal Data Collection or Termination of Pregnancy Record
patterns.description: Populated pregnancy-outcome records about an identified person: Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (QPDC) and Perinatal Online birth records submitted under the Public Health Act 2005 (Qld), and termination of pregnancy records under the Termination of Pregnancy Act 2018 (Qld) - medical (MS-2 Step) and surgical termination clinic notes, referrals, consent and procedure records. They name the patient and carry pregnancy fields such as gestation, LMP, gravida and parity, mode of birth, birthweight, method of termination and medicines given. Termination of pregnancy data is among the most sensitive health information held and can expose a person to stigma, coercion, family violence or legal jeopardy outside Queensland. Boundary: topic mentions of pregnancy, abortion and contraception without a populated record belong to global-reproductive-health-data; cancer notifications to au-qld-cancer-register-notification.
patterns.operation: Primary: (Queensland) Perinatal Data Collection, QPDC, Perinatal Online, perinatal (data) form / record / notification, (medical / surgical) termination of pregnancy, MS-2 Step, abortion record / procedure / referral. 65 (discovery only): primary alone, which surfaces the QPDC manual, patient information and statistics. 75: primary plus a populated patient field (patient or mother's name, DOB, URN / UR number, MRN, Medicare, IHI) plus a populated pregnancy field (gestation, gestational age, EDD, LMP, gravida, parity, plurality, onset of labour, mode of birth or delivery, birthweight, Apgar, outcome of pregnancy, baby's sex, method of termination, procedure date, indication). 85: the 75 evidence plus independent obstetric or statutory context (antenatal, postnatal, obstetric, maternity, birth suite, neonatal, midwife, ultrasound dating, anti-D, consulting or second medical practitioner, Public Health Act). Enforce tiers exclude template wording and manual, guideline, patient-information, training, statistics and media framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: QPDC, Perinatal Online and termination of pregnancy wording is specific, and enforce tiers need a populated patient field and a populated pregnancy field, which manuals, patient information and statistics lack. Maternity records that do not use these titles (antenatal cards, birth suite notes) are not covered unless the title appears.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier recognises Queensland Perinatal Data Collection and termination of pregnancy records and enforces only when a populated patient field sits with a populated pregnancy field, with 85 also needing obstetric or statutory context. A genuine record reveals that a named person was pregnant and how the pregnancy ended: birth details including the baby, or a termination with its gestation and method. Termination of pregnancy information is among the most sensitive health data held: disclosure can lead to stigma, family or community coercion, domestic and family violence, and legal exposure where the person travels to or lives in a jurisdiction that criminalises abortion. Risk 9 reflects that severity for a single record. The SIT-QUALITY-BAR PROTECTED triggers for risk 9 (critical system, child, whistleblower, bulk suppressed addresses) are not met by an ordinary adult record, so the label stays SENSITIVE; a record about a minor or a bulk extract would justify PROTECTED.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium, as for involuntary mental health records, because one perinatal or termination of pregnancy record exposes a named person's pregnancy outcome with severe stigma, coercion and legal risk. PROTECTED is not met: the SIT-QUALITY-BAR risk-9 triggers (critical system attack, exposing a child, a whistleblower, bulk suppressed addresses) do not apply to an ordinary adult record; a minor's record or a bulk extract would meet them. Owner review requested.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling with tightly restricted access applies to one person's pregnancy outcome record. High is warranted for bulk perinatal or termination data or records about minors.
