patterns.name: Queensland Pool Immersion Incident Record
patterns.description: Records of a pool immersion incident involving a young child (under 5) in Queensland under the Building Act 1975: the hospital notice to the chief executive (health) under s 245G (name and date of birth of the young child, day of the examination, address of the child's parents, address where the incident happened), the onward notice to QBCC, the local government and the Family and Child Commissioner under s 245I, and the council's follow-up pool inspection under s 246ADA, together with council drowning and near-drowning incident files. Pool immersion information may be disclosed only as allowed by s 257A. Public pool safety certificate and regulated pools register entries, pool fencing guidance, the statute text and drowning statistics are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: pool immersion incident/notice/information/notification/report, (child) immersion incident, (non-fatal) drowning incident or notification, near-drowning, or a reference to Building Act s 245G, s 245I or s 246ADA. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone). 75 requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a child field (young child / child / name of child / patient / person involved with a two-word name, a date of birth, or an age in years or months), a location field (address where the immersion incident happened, incident / pool / property / premises address or location, address of the child's parents, or home address, followed by a street number and name) or an incident field (dated date of incident, immersion, examination, admission or presentation; or outcome, condition, treatment, injuries, how the child accessed the pool, barrier condition or gate condition with a word value). 85 requires a child field AND a location or incident field AND an independent corroborative term (hospital, emergency department, ambulance, CPR, resuscitation, QBCC, pool fence, pool gate, pool barrier, regulated pool, pool safety inspector, coroner and similar). Blank lines, bracket placeholders, n/a/tbc and "Yes / No" prompts are rejected. Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude statute and guidance wording (maximum penalty, penalty units, this section applies, in this section, legislation.qld.gov.au, this guide/fact sheet/policy/campaign, frequently asked questions, National Drowning Report).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "pool immersion incident" and the s 245G notice fields come straight from the Building Act 1975, but the statute, QBCC and Queensland Health guidance and water-safety campaigns repeat them, so enforce tiers need populated child, location or incident fields. Pool safety certificate and form numbers are not used because their formats and form numbers are unverified. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a pool immersion incident record that names a young child, gives the child's date of birth, the family's address and the address of the pool, and records the clinical outcome, which may be death or brain injury. It is health information about a child that the Building Act restricts (s 257A) and that can feed coronial and child-safety processes; disclosure causes serious distress to families and can prejudice investigations. Statute text, guidance, public pool register entries, blank forms and drowning statistics are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a populated s 245G or s 245I notice names a young child with date of birth, family and pool addresses and an outcome that may be death or brain injury. PROTECTED is not met because one incident record lacks bulk scale or significant-damage consequences.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling fits a child's identity, home address and immersion outcome, which Building Act s 257A restricts. It is not High because one incident notice does not carry population-scale or life-safety exposure.

patterns.name: Queensland Postal Vote Application or Declaration Envelope Record
patterns.description: Elector-level postal and declaration voting records held by ECQ and returning officers: postal vote applications (Electoral Act 1992 (Qld) s 119, which require the address to which ballot papers are to be sent), the record of posted voting papers (s 119(7)), declaration envelope records that are signed and witnessed (ss 117, 119(8)), declaration envelopes for uncertain identity (s 121), the register of special postal voters (s 68; grounds in s 114(2)), and late-vote registers. Silent electors are automatically special postal voters (s 114(2)(b)), so the special postal voter register and dispatch lists hold silent-elector addresses. Declaration envelopes are stored for at least a year (s 136). Local government elections have parallel provisions (LGEA 2011 ss 21A, 79, 81, 82). The ECQ postal voting web page, the declaration envelope count procedure, postal vote statistics and blank forms are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: postal vote / votes / voting / voter / voters (optionally followed by application, request, register, record, pack, papers, certificate or status), application for a postal vote, declaration envelope(s), declaration vote(s), special or general postal voter(s), register of special postal voters, posted voting papers, or late vote(s). 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated elector name field (elector, voter, applicant, name, full name or name of elector followed by a name of two or more capitalised words, or surname / family name followed by a capitalised word) AND one application or declaration structure: a populated address field (residential, postal, enrolled, home, mailing, dispatch, overseas or temporary address, or the address to which ballot papers are to be sent, followed by a street number and name or a PO Box), a populated declaration field (witness name, a signed / witnessed / declaration / envelope status such as signed, witnessed, accepted, rejected or admitted, a special postal voter status, or a special postal voter ground), or the silent-elector corroborator (silent elector, silent enrolment). 85 requires a name field AND an address field AND a declaration field or the silent-elector corroborator AND a populated date field (date received, signed, witnessed, sent, dispatched, issued, posted, returned, processed or registered, followed by a date). Values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded. All tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary; enforce tiers also exclude guidance wording (frequently asked questions, fact sheet, how to apply for a postal vote, you can apply for a postal vote, legislation.qld.gov.au). 65 is discovery-only. The silent-elector corroborator does not raise the label here; au-qld-silent-elector-record carries the PROTECTED label and should be deployed alongside so a silent elector's postal record is escalated.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Postal and declaration vote wording is common in ECQ and AEC guidance, count procedures and statistics, so enforce tiers need a populated elector name plus a populated address, declaration or silent-elector structure. The ECQ postal vote application form field labels are UNVERIFIED (the AEC EF048 form is an image), so the field regexes use general labels plus the verified s 119(3)(c) wording. Elector identifying numbers have no published format and are not used. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies an elector-level postal vote application, declaration envelope record, special postal voter register entry or late-vote register line that ties a named elector to a residential or dispatch address, witness details and dates. The records reveal where an elector is (often a temporary, remote or overseas address), why they cannot attend a polling booth (distance, illness, infirmity, religious belief, detention) and whether and when their vote arrived. Silent electors are automatically special postal voters (Electoral Act s 114(2)(b)), so the special postal voter register and dispatch lists hold suppressed addresses; when the silent-elector wording co-occurs with an address, au-qld-silent-elector-record carries the PROTECTED Personal-Privacy label and should take precedence. Guidance, count procedures, statistics and blank forms are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 7 supports the roll-derived SENSITIVE Electoral Roll label.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Electoral Roll and Medium because the record ties an elector to a dispatch address, witness and the reason they cannot attend, such as illness or detention. PROTECTED is not met for ordinary postal voters; special postal voter entries that expose silent electors escalate to the silent elector pattern.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to an elector's temporary address and absence reason. High applies where a silent elector's address is exposed.

patterns.name: Queensland Public Sector Discipline Record (Show Cause Notice, Allegations, Disciplinary Finding)
patterns.description: Discipline records about an identified public sector employee under the Public Sector Act 2022 (Qld) and the Discipline Directive 05/23 (made under ss 100 and 222): show cause notices on disciplinary finding (allegation, particulars, the disciplinary ground under section 91 and the evidence, 14 days to respond), show cause notices on proposed disciplinary action (7 days), suspension notices, disciplinary findings and decision letters. Council and university discipline letters that use the same wording (show cause, allegation, particulars, disciplinary finding) are also caught. Overlaps global-top500-063-disciplinary-records (generic, being rebuilt separately); this classifier is the Qld-anchored, populated-record version.
patterns.operation: Primary: a discipline phrase (show cause notice/letter/process, show cause notice on disciplinary finding or on proposed disciplinary action, notice to show cause, Discipline Directive, Directive 05/23, disciplinary ground/finding/decision, proposed or serious disciplinary action, grounds for discipline, section 91(1)). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated employee field (employee/subject employee/staff member/officer name, employee or payroll number, position number or title, work unit, classification with a non-placeholder value) OR a populated allegation field (Allegation N: / Particulars: followed by at least three words, or "it is alleged that ..."). 85 tier requires the employee field AND the allegation field AND a decision/response structure (response due or respond-by date, notice/decision/suspension date, suspended with effect from a date, a finding of substantiated / not substantiated, proposed disciplinary action or penalty with an action word, or "within 14/7 days of receiving this notice") AND an independent corroborative term (natural justice, procedural fairness, Public Sector Act 2022, section 91, misconduct, delegate, Code of Conduct, respond in writing). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a directive/guidance/decision exclusion (this directive, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, catchwords, case study, hypothetical, training module). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface the directive, guidance and blank notices.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the notice names and the section 91 ground come straight from Directive 05/23 and the Act, but the same words fill the directive, agency guidance, training and published appeal decisions, so enforce tiers need populated employee and allegation fields and 85 also needs a response-date or finding structure. Employee and position numbers are agency-defined, so values are label-anchored and placeholder-guarded rather than shape-checked. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic notices laid out like the directive's required content.

patterns.name: Queensland Public Sector Selection Report and Candidate Assessment
patterns.description: Recruitment and selection records under the Recruitment and Selection Directive 07/23 (Public Sector Act 2022 (Qld) ss 46 and 222): selection panel reports, comparative and merit assessments documenting why the proposed successful applicant is "best suited", candidate scoring and ranking sheets, referee checks and panel recommendations for a named candidate and position. Council and university selection reports with the same structure are also caught. Overlaps global-top500-074-interview-evaluation-notes (generic phrase classifier being rebuilt separately).
patterns.operation: Primary: a selection phrase (selection report, selection panel report, selection panel, recruitment and selection report/outcome/decision, comparative assessment, merit assessment/ranking, best suited, referee report/check/comments, panel chair, Directive 07/23). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, a populated candidate field (applicant, candidate, preferred/recommended/successful applicant or candidate, referee, interviewee, with a non-placeholder value) OR a populated position field (position number/title/ID, vacancy or job reference, classification, work unit). 85 tier requires the candidate field AND a score/ranking field (score, rating, ranking or rank with a numeric value such as 44/50, 85%, rank 1, or a suitability rating such as highly suitable / not suitable) AND a recommendation/panel field (recommendation, recommended for appointment, panel chair/members/recommendation, delegate approval, approved by, reasons best suited, with at least two words) AND an independent corroborative term (merit, appointment, interview, shortlist, key capabilities, role description, conflict of interest). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a job-advertisement/guidance exclusion (how to apply, applications close, about the role, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, training module, case study, this directive applies). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: selection report, comparative assessment and best suited are the directive's own terms, but they also fill the directive, recruitment guidance and job advertisements (which carry position numbers and classifications), so a job-ad exclusion is applied and 85 needs candidate, score and recommendation structures together. Position numbers and job references are agency-defined and are label-anchored only. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic selection records.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's position number format (see docs/identifiers.md#position-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Treasury Corporation Client Loan or Facility Agreement
patterns.description: Loan, facility and client agreements between Queensland Treasury Corporation (QTC) and its borrowing clients (government departments, statutory bodies, government owned corporations, local governments and universities), with their facility offers and confirmations, drawdown notices, debt pool and loan statements and repayment schedules. QTC is the State's central financing authority under the Queensland Treasury Corporation Act 1988 and lends to statutory bodies under the Statutory Bodies Financial Arrangements Act 1982 with Treasurer's borrowing approval. A client agreement states the client number, loan or facility number, facility limit or principal, interest rate or margin, fees, maturity and repayment schedule. These terms are the borrower's unpublished debt position and pricing. state-borrowing-and-debt-issuance-strategy covers QTC's own market borrowing and issuance strategy; this SIT covers the client-side lending documents.
patterns.operation: Primary: [fixed rate / floating rate / working capital / term] loan agreement / offer / confirmation / schedule / statement, [master] [loan] facility agreement / offer / letter / confirmation / schedule, master client / lending agreement, client service agreement, repayment schedule, debt pool / facility statement, drawdown notice / request / confirmation. Every enforce tier needs QTC context within 300 characters (Queensland Treasury Corporation, QTC, Queensland Treasury Corporation Act 1988, Statutory Bodies Financial Arrangements Act 1982, SBFA, generic debt pool, Treasurer's approval, borrowing approval). 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus context plus one of a labelled client / loan / facility / deal / borrower number, a facility amount (facility limit / amount, loan amount / principal, principal, approved borrowing / limit / amount, borrowing limit, drawdown amount, amount drawn, outstanding balance / principal, book / market value with a dollar amount) or loan terms (interest / fixed rate, margin, administration or competitive neutrality fee, maturity date, repayment amount / date / frequency, instalment amount, loan term with a value, or a dated repayment row with two amounts). 85: primary plus context plus any two of reference, amount, terms and a populated borrower field (borrower, client [name], entity [name]). Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a publication / guidance exclusion (annual report, investor booklet, investor book, offering circular, information memorandum, media release, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, borrowing program). Field values are placeholder-guarded.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Loan and facility agreement wording is used by every lender, so enforce tiers need QTC context plus populated loan fields, and QTC's public investor and annual reporting is excluded. Client and facility number formats are unpublished, so references are label-anchored. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Queensland Referable Dam Emergency Action Plan - Unredacted Notification List or Population at Risk Detail
patterns.description: Unredacted working copies of Queensland referable dam emergency action plans (EAPs) under the Water Supply (Safety and Reliability) Act 2008 s 352H, and failure impact assessments, that contain the warning and notification lists (named individuals with mobile numbers, in order of priority) or property-level population at risk (PAR) detail (street addresses with occupant or PAR counts). Approved EAPs are published by design on the s 352M register with individuals' names, addresses and contact details removed, so the published plan is not the target; the personal detail stripped from it is.
patterns.operation: Primary: referable dam, dam emergency action plan, emergency action plan for a named dam or weir, failure impact assessment or rating, population at risk (PAR). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface every published EAP, the Act and the Business Queensland EAP list. 75 requires, within 300 characters, either an unredacted contact row (a two-word personal name followed within 40 non-digit characters by an Australian mobile number; role, agency and place words are rejected as names) or a property-level PAR row (a street address or Qld lot-on-plan followed by a PAR, occupant, resident or person count). 85 requires both a contact row and a PAR row plus independent EAP operating content (Dam Duty Officer, Lean Forward, Stand Up, Stand Down, controlled copy, warning list, notification list, order of priority, inundation, spillway). All tiers exclude template/fixture text and a pattern-specific exclusion group (media releases, public register and Business Queensland listing text, have your say).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the EAP and referable dam terms are statutory and appear in every published plan, so they only drive discovery. Enforcement rests on personal contact rows and property-level PAR rows, which the published s 352M copies remove. Name-plus-mobile matching can still catch an agency role number where the role words are not in the rejection list, and mobile-only matching misses individuals listed with landlines. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic rows using ACMA fictional mobile numbers.

patterns.name: Queensland Regulated Dog Declaration or Dog Attack Record
patterns.description: Queensland council animal management enforcement records under the Animal Management (Cats and Dogs) Act 2008. Covers proposed declaration notices (s 90: breed, colour, sex, distinguishing marks, reasons, written representations within at least 14 days), regulated dog declarations (s 89 and s 94: declared dangerous or declared menacing dog), information notices (s 95), destruction orders (s 127A) and dog attack investigation or complaint records (attack offences ss 194-195). These records name the owner, the dog, the address and, for attacks, the victim and their injuries. The state regulated dog register may be inspected only by officers, owners and similar persons (s 173). The council dog registry is open to inspection, but owner information is excluded (s 179(2)), so a registry extract without owner details is not matched at enforce tiers. Restricted dog provisions survive only as transitional permits after the 2024 amendments (Act No. 17 of 2024), which introduced prohibited dogs (s 127).
patterns.operation: Primary: proposed declaration notice, notice of proposed declaration, regulated dog declaration, dangerous or menacing dog declaration, declared dangerous or menacing dog, dog attack [investigation / report / complaint / incident / record], destruction order, prohibited dog, restricted dog. Field values must be on the same line as their label and are placeholder-guarded (withheld, not, none, nil, excluded, redacted, suppressed, blank lines, brackets). 75 requires, within 300 characters, either an owner field (owner, dog owner, registered owner, owner's name, responsible person, relevant person, owner's address, followed by a name of two or more capitalised words or a street address) or an incident / victim field (date or location of attack or incident, victim or victim's name, person or animal attacked, injuries sustained, nature of injuries, complainant, witness, veterinary report or treatment, followed by a value). Dog-description fields alone (breed, colour, sex, microchip or PPID number, registration or tag number) never reach 75, which keeps registry extracts without owner details at 65. 85 requires an owner field, a dog-description or incident / victim field, and an independent corroborative term (written representations, information notice, authorised person, impounded, seized, bitten, bodily harm, veterinary surgeon, compliance notice, Animal Management (Cats and Dogs) Act). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (fact sheet, frequently asked questions, open to inspection, how to report). 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. The primary phrases are the Act's own terms (ss 89-95, 127, 127A), but they also appear in the Act, council fact sheets, QCAT decisions and news. Enforce tiers therefore need a populated owner or victim / incident field. PPID microchip numbers are matched only as a labelled loose value (9-15 characters after a microchip / PPID label). The ISO 11784 15-digit structure was not verified from a primary source for this build and is not relied on. Registration and tag numbers are council-defined. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's council animal registration number / tag format (see docs/identifiers.md#animal-registration-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

These are enforcement and possible prosecution records. They carry health information about attack victims, and neighbour-dispute and complainant details that are often contested. The state regulated dog register is not public (s 173), and owner details are withheld from the public council registry (s 179(2)). Legislation, fact sheets, news and owner-less registry extracts are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Legal.

patterns.name: Queensland Reportable Conduct Scheme Notification or Report (QFCC)
patterns.description: Completed notifications and reports under the Queensland Reportable Conduct Scheme in the Child Safe Organisations Act 2024 (Qld), which commenced on 1 July 2026 and is regulated by the Queensland Family and Child Commission (QFCC). The head of an entity must give QFCC an initial notification within 3 business days of becoming aware of a reportable allegation or conviction, an interim report within 30 business days and a final report with the investigation findings. A populated record names the worker (name, date of birth, role, Blue Card or exemption notice number), the child, the head of entity or delegate, the type of reportable conduct (child sexual offence, sexual misconduct, ill-treatment, significant neglect, physical violence, or behaviour causing significant emotional or psychological harm), dates, and risk-management steps. The scheme page, the QFCC guideline, the Act and blank forms are decoys. Reportable conduct records from other states' schemes (NSW, Vic, ACT) that use the same labels can also reach 75; the Queensland-specific corroborative terms mostly lift only Queensland records to 85.
patterns.operation: Primary: "reportable conduct (scheme)", "reportable allegation", "reportable conviction", "Child Safe Organisations Act 2024", or "initial notification / interim report / final report to QFCC / the Commission". 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces QFCC guidance, the Act and policies. 75 requires one populated record field within 300 characters: worker / child / young person / student / head of entity / delegate / notifier name, date of birth, role or position, Blue Card or exemption notice number, a dated conduct/awareness field, or a selected type of reportable conduct from the verified list. Blank lines, bracket placeholders and n/a/tbc are rejected. 85 requires two distinct populated fields plus an independent corroborative term (QFCC, Blue Card, stood down, police, 3 / 30 business days, risk assessment, supervision and similar). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude guidance/legislation signals.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the scheme vocabulary is specific, but QFCC guidance, sector policies and training repeat it and the other states' reportable conduct schemes use similar terms. Enforce tiers require populated worker/child/entity fields; the Blue Card number format is not used as a value pattern (label only). 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's blue card / exemption card number format (see docs/identifiers.md#qld-blue-card-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a completed reportable conduct notification or report, gated on populated worker, child or entity fields. These records carry unproven allegations of child sexual offences, sexual misconduct, ill-treatment, neglect or violence against a named worker, together with details of the child. Disclosure can harm the child, prejudice the investigation or any police matter, and defame a worker whose allegation is not substantiated. Guidance, legislation, policies and blank forms are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports PROTECTED Personal-Privacy because a single record exposes a child.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 maps to PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED Personal-Privacy (PROT_Pvc) and the High tier because a QFCC reportable conduct notification names a child alongside unproven allegations of sexual offences, ill-treatment or neglect by a named worker with Blue Card details. Disclosure can harm the child, prejudice the investigation or a police matter and defame the worker. A single record exposes a child, the same harm as child protection case files, which are PROTECTED Personal-Privacy at risk 9.

generic.rationale: High Personal-Privacy handling applies because the record ties an identified child to alleged abuse and names the worker under allegation. Access should be limited to the people handling the notification.

patterns.name: Queensland Revenue Office Notice of Assessment (Transfer Duty, Land Tax, Payroll Tax)
patterns.description: Notices of assessment and reassessment issued by the Queensland Revenue Office (QRO, the Commissioner of State Revenue) for transfer duty and other duties, land tax and payroll tax, including annual payroll tax reconciliation assessments. A notice names the taxpayer (purchaser / transferee, land owner or employer), carries a client, assessment or transaction number and a payment reference, states the amount assessed, interest and due date, and identifies the basis: the property (Queensland lot on plan such as Lot 12 on SP298765, or a title reference) with its dutiable or taxable land value, or the employer's taxable wages. Information obtained under a tax law is confidential under the Taxation Administration Act 2001 (Qld) Part 8. Commonwealth (ATO) notices of assessment use the same title; this SIT needs Queensland revenue context, and global-top500-083-employer-payroll-tax-filings covers generic payroll tax filings.
patterns.operation: Primary: notice of [re]assessment, [re]assessment notice, land tax [re]assessment, [transfer / landholder / vehicle registration] duty [re]assessment, payroll tax [re]assessment, annual [payroll tax] reconciliation return / assessment, statement of land tax / duty assessed. Every enforce tier needs Queensland revenue context within 300 characters (Queensland Revenue Office, Office of State Revenue, Commissioner of State Revenue, QRO, OSR, QRO Online, qro.qld.gov.au, Taxation Administration Act 2001, Duties Act 2001, Land Tax Act 2010, Payroll Tax Act 1971). 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus context plus one of a labelled client / assessment / transaction / lodgement / employer / taxpayer number or payment / duties reference, a labelled amount (amount payable / due / assessed / owing, duty / land tax / payroll tax / tax payable, balance due, unpaid tax interest, penalty tax, amount to pay), an assessment basis (lot on plan, title reference, or taxable / land / site / unimproved / dutiable value, consideration or taxable wages with a dollar amount) or a populated taxpayer field (taxpayer, client name, [registered] owner, transferee, purchaser, employer [name], entity name). 85: primary plus context plus any two of those four. Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (frequently asked questions, fact sheet, public ruling, calculator, media release, annual report, how to, learn more, you may be eligible). Field values are placeholder-guarded.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Assessment titles are shared with the ATO and with QRO's own guidance, so enforce tiers need Queensland revenue context plus a populated assessment field, and guidance framing is excluded. QRO client and assessment number formats are unpublished, so references are label-anchored. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Financial; PROTECTED is not met for a single taxpayer's notice, though bulk assessment extracts sit at the upper end of this band.

generic.rationale: Medium Financial handling fits confidential state tax assessment information for an identified taxpayer; bulk extracts deserve stricter handling within the same level.

patterns.name: Queensland Right to Information Access Application, Consultation or Decision
patterns.description: Case records for access applications under the Right to Information Act 2009 (Qld): the s 24 access application (including the combined Right to Information and Information Privacy Access Application form), s 37 consultation with a relevant third party, and the s 54 decision notice giving reasons, with refusal grounds under s 47(3) - exempt information (s 48, schedule 3) and contrary to public interest information (s 49, schedule 4) - plus internal review (s 80) and external review by the Information Commissioner (s 85). A populated record carries the applicant's name, the application reference, dates received/decided, the documents sought, page counts, third parties consulted, the decision maker and the outcome. Published disclosure logs (s 78A) are public and treated as decoys, as are the Act, OIC/RTI guidance and blank forms. Overlaps with au-foi-exemption-references, which matches Commonwealth FOI Act exemption section references (ss 33-47) and does not cover Queensland schedule 3/4 grounds. India's Right to Information Act 2005 applications are excluded.
patterns.operation: Primary: "Right to Information Act (2009)", "RTI Act", "RTI (access) application", "Right to Information (access) application", "Information Privacy Access Application", "RTI reference/decision/application number", or a Queensland schedule 3 / schedule 4 ground reference (e.g. "schedule 3, section 10", "sch 4 pt 3"). Bare "Right to Information" (a Queensland government website footer link) is not a primary. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces guidance, the Act and disclosure logs. 75 requires one populated field within 300 characters: applicant / third party / decision maker name, application or RTI reference containing a digit, a dated application/decision field, the documents sought or scope, a page/document count, or a selected decision outcome (full/partial access, access refused, refuse to deal, deferred access). 85 requires two distinct populated fields plus an independent corroborative term (contrary to the public interest, exempt information, internal/external review, Information Commissioner, section 37, processing period, evidence of identity and similar). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude guidance/legislation signals, published disclosure log framing and Indian RTI Act 2005 signals.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the RTI Act titles, form name and schedule 3/4 references are Queensland-specific, but guidance, the Act, training and published disclosure logs repeat them, and RTI application reference formats vary by agency (none is used as a value pattern). Enforce tiers require populated case fields and exclude disclosure-log framing. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's rti / ip application reference format (see docs/identifiers.md#qld-rti-application-reference). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Queensland Silent Elector Record
patterns.description: Records that identify a silent elector: completed AEC silent elector registrations (form ER022ESw_QLD, used for Queensland enrolment under the joint roll arrangement), silent elector registers, roll entries flagged silent, silent enrolment confirmations and special postal voter register entries for silent electors. A silent elector is a person whose address the Electoral Commission of Queensland has kept off the public roll because showing it would put the personal safety of the person or their family at risk (Electoral Act 1992 s 58(5) and sch 1; Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 s 104, backed by a statutory declaration). Silent electors are automatically special postal voters (s 114(2)(b)), and council voters rolls must omit their address (LGEA s 19(2)). Nomination form guidance, fact sheets, AEC guidance, blank forms, legislation and news are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: silent elector(s), silent enrolment, registration as a silent elector, the ER022ESw form code, or the ER022 declaration wording (residential address shown on any / the publicly available roll places the personal safety ... at risk). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone). 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated name field (elector, name, full / current / family / given name, surname or applicant, with a non-placeholder value) plus one of: a populated electoral district / division / electorate / ward field (or "Division n" / "Ward n"), a residential street address, or a date of birth. 85 requires the populated name field plus a residential street address or a populated date of birth, plus an independent electoral context term (enrolled, enrolment, roll, special postal voter, personal safety, statutory declaration, AEC, ECQ and similar). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude the candidate nomination form instruction ("please do not insert your address details here"), fact sheet / FAQ / legislation-site wording, "addresses of silent electors are not released" style disclosure notes and the s 133A(5) wording. The pattern carries PROTECTED Electoral Roll for records with an address; name-only records at 75 carry the lower SENSITIVE Electoral Roll sensitivity (see risk_description).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "silent elector" is a specific statutory term, but it appears in every ECQ candidate nomination form, fact sheet and AEC guidance page, so enforce tiers need a populated name field plus a district, address or DOB, and nomination and fact-sheet wording is excluded. The exact silent marker or column in ECQ internal extracts is not published, so roll-extract rows flagged "S" without the words "silent elector" are not detected. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

A silent elector record with an address fires both, at PROTECTED (this one PROTECTED Electoral Roll, the DFV one PROTECTED Personal-Privacy); an organisation deploying both should let the electoral policy take precedence for roll-derived records. This classifier adds the name-plus-district and name-plus-DOB records (no address) that the DFV classifier does not detect, plus the ER022 form code and silent enrolment wording. patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a record that names a silent elector: a person whose address the Electoral Commission has withheld from the public roll because showing it would put the personal safety of the person or their family at risk, a status granted on a statutory declaration (Electoral Act 1992 s 58(5); CEA s 104). Silent electors are frequently people escaping domestic and family violence, stalking or threats. A record that pairs a silent elector's name with their residential address (ER022 registration, special postal voter register, internal roll entry) defeats the protection and can let the person posing the risk find them, so the pattern-level label is PROTECTED Electoral Roll (risk 10), the PROTECTED mirror of SENSITIVE Electoral Roll. Owner decision on the split: a record that names a silent elector with only their district or date of birth and no residential address (the name-only 75 tier) carries the lower SENSITIVE Electoral Roll sensitivity; deploy the 75 tier under a SENSITIVE Electoral Roll rule and the 85 tier with an address under PROTECTED where the policy engine allows per-tier labels. Nomination forms, fact sheets, guidance, blank forms and news are excluded from enforce tiers.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to PSPF and QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED Electoral Roll and High because pairing a silent elector's name with their residential address defeats a safety protection often granted to people escaping violence or stalking. patterns.name: Queensland SPER Enforcement and State Fine Debt Record
patterns.description: State Penalties Enforcement Registry (SPER) enforcement-stage records for fines issued by Queensland state agencies and courts: enforcement orders, fine collection notices, SPER debt statements and instalment or payment plans, enforcement warrants, seizure and sale orders, redirection orders, fine option orders and driver licence suspension notices. SPER, part of the Queensland Revenue Office, collects unpaid infringement notices referred by the Queensland Police Service, Transport and Main Roads, Translink, Queensland Rail and other state agencies, plus court-ordered fines. Under the State Penalties Enforcement Act 1999 the registrar may make an enforcement order for an unpaid amount and enforcement fee and take enforcement action (licence suspension, redirection of earnings or bank accounts, seizure and sale). The record names the debtor with an address, a SPER reference, the issuing agency and the amount owing. This SIT is the state and SPER-stage counterpart of au-qld-council-infringement-sper-record (council local law notices and their referral to SPER) and traffic-camera-record (camera-detected offence notices); local-law context is excluded here so council notices stay with the council SIT.
patterns.operation: Primary (enforcement-stage vocabulary): SPER debt(s) / debtor / enforcement order / enforcement action / referral / registration / instalment plan / payment plan, enforcement order, fine collection notice, enforcement warrant, seizure and sale order / warrant, fine option order, arrest and imprisonment warrant, redirection order, [driver] licence suspension notice. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus a populated debtor field (debtor, alleged offender, offender, customer / client name, full name, name, residential / postal address followed by a name or street address) or a labelled SPER / client / customer / debtor reference or order / notice / warrant number, plus state context within 300 characters (State Penalties Enforcement Registry, State Penalties Enforcement Act, Queensland Revenue Office, Queensland Police Service, Transport and Main Roads, Translink, Queensland Rail, camera detected offence, Magistrates Court, issuing / referring agency, enforcement fee and other state issuers). 85: primary plus debtor field, reference and a populated amount field (amount owing / outstanding / payable / due, total debt, balance, enforcement fee, unpaid amount, fine amount, instalment amount, due date, pay by) plus state context. Field values must be on the label's line and are placeholder-guarded. Enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary, a guidance exclusion (FAQ, fact sheet, State Penalties Enforcement Regulation, annual report, media release, if you do not pay) and a local-law exclusion (local law, Animal Management (Cats and Dogs) Act, unregistered dog, overgrown allotment, unsightly, remedial notice).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium. Enforcement-order vocabulary also appears in planning and court contexts and in SPER's own public guidance, so enforce tiers need a populated debtor field or SPER reference plus state context, and guidance framing is excluded. SPER reference formats are unpublished, so the reference is label-anchored. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy. Test values are synthetic.

SSAN is prescribed as a security sensitive explosive because of its use in improvised explosive devices; the plan is a direct guide to diverting it and a list of people who could be coerced. Risk 9 supports PROTECTED Government because one plan is enough to divert IED precursors or to target the people it names.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 maps to PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED Government (PROT_Gov) and the High tier because an SSAN or explosives security plan names the people with unsupervised access, the authorised receivers and the magazine and store locations, and sets out the controls that detect access and trace custody. One holder's plan is a guide to diverting IED precursors and a list of people who could be coerced, which is serious harm rather than limited damage, so PROTECTED does not depend on a national aggregation of sites.

generic.rationale: High Government handling applies because one plan exposes explosives custody controls and the people who could be targeted to defeat them. Access should be limited to the holder's security officers and the regulator.

patterns.name: Queensland Trade Waste Approval and Compliance Record
patterns.description: Trade waste and seepage water approvals issued by a Queensland sewerage service provider (council or water utility) under Water Supply (Safety and Reliability) Act 2008 (Qld) ch 2 pt 6 (s 180 approvals, s 181 conditions such as maximum daily quantity and limits for suspended solids and biochemical oxygen demand, ss 182-184 suspension and cancellation, s 185 amendment), and the compliance records that follow them: sampling results against discharge limits, grease arrestor and pre-treatment inspections, and breach or non-compliance notices. The records carry the approval holder's business, premises, approval number, process chemistry and non-compliance history. Published trade waste guidance, acceptance criteria tables, fact sheets and blank application forms are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a trade waste record phrase (trade waste approval/permit/licence/agreement/application/category/generator/discharge/plan/customer/inspection, seepage water approval). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated record field: an approval/permit/licence/agreement number label with a digit-bearing value, or an approval holder/permit holder/business/trading name/generator/occupier/premises/site address field with a non-placeholder value. 85 tier requires one of those fields AND a discharge limit or sampling result structure (a trade waste parameter such as BOD, COD, suspended solids, FOG, oil and grease, total nitrogen/phosphorus, ammonia, sulphate, metals, or daily discharge volume/flow followed within 25 characters by a number with a mg/L, g/m3, kL/day, kL, L/s, L/day or m3/day unit) AND an independent corroborative term (sampling, exceedance, breach, non-compliance, grease arrestor, pre-treatment, suspension, cancellation, show cause, conditions of approval, sewerage, sewer). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a guidance exclusion (fact sheet, information sheet, frequently asked questions, how to apply, application guide, acceptance criteria, media release). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface guidance, blank forms and policy text.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "trade waste approval" and "seepage water approval" are statutory terms (WSSR Act s 180) and uncommon outside the record type, but they fill council trade waste policies, fact sheets and application forms, so enforce tiers require populated approval or premises fields. Approval numbers are council-defined with no published format, so values are label-anchored, digit-bearing and placeholder-guarded. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's trade waste approval number format (see docs/identifiers.md#trade-waste-approval-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a trade waste or seepage water approval, amendment or compliance record that ties a named business and premises to its approval number, discharge conditions, process chemistry, sampling results and breach history. Disclosure exposes commercially sensitive process and volume information and an operator's non-compliance record before any enforcement outcome, and gives insight into sewerage treatment loadings; it rarely identifies private individuals beyond business contacts. Guidance, acceptance criteria tables, legislation and blank forms are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 5 supports OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE Commercial-in-Confidence.

PROTECTED is not met: harm is commercial and reputational to one operator.

generic.rationale: Medium Commercial-in-Confidence handling protects a business's process and non-compliance detail before any enforcement outcome. High is not met for one operator's approval.

patterns.name: Victim Assist Queensland Financial Assistance Application
patterns.description: Completed applications for financial assistance under the Victims of Crime Assistance Act 2009 (Qld) ss 51-52, made on the Victim Assist Queensland "Financial Assistance Application Form: Primary victim" (Form 1, Version 5, effective 14 September 2023) or recorded in Victim Assist case files: the primary victim's name and date of birth, the act of violence (what happened, key dates, offender name), police report details (reference number, station, investigating officer) or special primary victim report details (for example a domestic violence worker), injuries, recognition payment (special assistance) and recovery expense claims, and safe contact arrangements. Acts of violence include domestic and family violence, sexual offences and child abuse. The blank form, qld.gov.au application guidance and media coverage are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a Victim Assist anchor (Victim Assist Queensland, Financial Assistance Application Form: Primary victim, Victims of Crime Assistance Act 2009, primary victim application, special primary victim / special primary victim report, or recognition payment (special assistance)). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: an applicant field (the victim's / your / applicant / primary victim's full name, other names used, date of birth or offender's name, with an optional form hint in brackets, followed by a non-placeholder value) or a crime field (a police or claim reference number containing a digit, a police station or investigating officer with a name, "date the report was made" or "when did it start/end/happen" with a date). 85 tier requires an applicant field AND a crime field AND an independent act-of-violence or claim term (assault, domestic violence, sexual, injury, counselling, offender, recovery expenses, loss of earnings, medical). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a media/guidance exclusion (media statement, ministerial statement, annual report, how to apply). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface the blank form and application guidance.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the form title, Act name and "special primary victim" are distinctive Victim Assist Queensland terms taken from Form 1 Version 5, but the blank form, qld.gov.au guidance and news use them too. Enforce tiers therefore need populated applicant or crime fields; the blank form's labels have no colon-delimited values. Victim Assist internal case-file labels and the claim reference number format are not published, so they are matched as labelled values containing a digit. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Queensland Water Customer Hardship, Payment Plan or Supply Restriction Record
patterns.description: Water and sewerage customer account records held by Queensland councils and water service providers about financial hardship, payment plans and restriction of supply for non-payment. Water Supply (Safety and Reliability) Act 2008 s 169 lets a service provider reduce the domestic water supply of an owner or occupier who does not pay after notice "to the minimum level necessary for the health and sanitation purposes", but not shut it off completely. In South East Queensland the Customer Water and Wastewater Code (made under the South-East Queensland Water (Distribution and Retail Restructuring) Act 2009) covers financial hardship, including Centrepay, and when supply can be restricted for non-payment; Urban Utilities' Residential Customer Charter describes payment plans and a Financial Hardship Policy. Records combine an account holder, water account or customer number, property or service address, arrears and the hardship, payment plan or flow-restriction action. Published charters, hardship policies, the Code and drought restriction notices are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a water hardship or restriction phrase (water / flow / supply restriction device, valve, disc, washer or notice; restricted / restricting / restriction of the (domestic) water supply; water supply restricted / restriction / limitation / reduced; water, sewerage or water and sewerage bill / account / charges hardship, payment plan, arrangement, assistance, arrears or overdue; water or sewerage (financial) hardship; hardship program / policy / assistance / application for water or sewerage; minimum level necessary for (the) health and sanitation). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: an account field (customer, account or water account number with a value containing a digit; a named account holder, customer, owner, occupier or tenant; a service, supply, property, premises, site or connection address with a street number; a property or assessment number; or a water meter number) or an action field (arrears, amount overdue, outstanding balance or debt with a dollar amount; a payment plan or instalment amount; a Centrepay deduction, reference or amount; a restriction device fitted / installed / applied / removed / lifted with a status or date; a restriction, final, reminder, overdue or disconnection warning notice issued with a date; or a hardship program / status / plan / flag / application of enrolled, active, approved, accepted, commenced or granted). 85 tier requires an account field AND an action field AND an independent water-account term (meter, meter read, sewerage, consumption, kilolitres, kL, water usage, Centrepay, Urban Utilities, Unitywater, distributor-retailer, council). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a policy/guidance exclusion (this policy, published on our website, Customer Water and Wastewater Code, customer charter, dam levels, water conservation measures, drought, This section applies if, must not completely shut off). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface charters, policies, legislation and drought restriction news.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: WSSR Act s 169 wording is verified and the hardship, Centrepay and restriction-for-non-payment topics of the SEQ Customer Water and Wastewater Code are confirmed by the Queensland Government business portal, but the Code's clause numbers and exact wording could not be retrieved (the PDF was not accessible), so no Code clause text is used as an anchor. "Water restriction" also means drought restrictions (WSSR s 41), so enforce tiers need populated account and action fields and a drought/policy exclusion. Water account and meter number formats are provider-specific and unverified, so values are loose and placeholder-guarded. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: South-East Queensland Water (Distribution and Retail Restructuring) Act 2009 (Qld)

patterns.name: Queensland Water Special Needs (Medical) Supply Register Record
patterns.description: Register entries and customer records kept by Queensland water service providers and councils for "special needs" customers and properties whose occupants need a continued, uninterrupted and unrestricted water supply for life support or other medical needs, most often home haemodialysis. The basis is customer-charter and code practice, not a statutory register: the Water Supply (Safety and Reliability) Act 2008 contains no special-needs or dialysis provision; the SEQ Customer Water and Wastewater Code covers "customers and tenants with special needs for an uninterrupted supply of water" (clause wording not retrieved); and the Urban Utilities Residential Customer Charter defines a special needs residential property as one where an occupant needs such supply as confirmed by a registered medical specialist, treating hospital or dialysis centre, and commits to at least four business days' notice of planned interruptions to those properties. Modelled on au-energy-life-support-register. Charters, glossaries and eligibility pages are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: a special-needs supply phrase (special needs customer / residential property / property / register / registration / flag / premises / occupant; uninterrupted (and unrestricted) (water) supply for life support or (special) medical needs; home haemodialysis, hemodialysis or home dialysis customer / register / registration / flag / patient; medical or dialysis priority register / customer / flag). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a premises field (service, supply, property or premises address with a street number; a property or assessment number; or a water meter number), a medical field (medical need / requirement / condition / equipment, equipment or treatment type, reason for registration or special need filled with (home) haemodialysis, dialysis, life support, oxygen, ventilator or tracheostomy; confirmed or certified by a named person; a named treating specialist, nephrologist, doctor, hospital, renal unit, dialysis centre or medical specialist; or a medical confirmation date) or a priority field (notification / contact / customer priority of high, urgent, critical or 1-3; a notice period or notice required of N (business) days; a filled alternate or emergency supply arrangement; a restriction, disconnection or shut-off exemption / hold of yes, applied or active; or a registration or review date). 85 tier requires a premises field AND a medical or priority field AND a customer field (named customer, account holder, occupant, tenant, patient or resident; or a customer, account or water account number) AND an independent water-operations term (interruption, shutdown, shut-off, water main, water meter, water account, sewerage, planned works, mains break, Urban Utilities, Unitywater). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a charter/guidance exclusion (customer charter, Customer Water and Wastewater Code, published on our website, this policy, fact sheet, frequently asked questions, glossary, is a property where, how to register, National Energy Retail Rules). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone).
patterns.confidence_justification: Low: there is no statutory water special-needs register in Queensland. The anchors come from one verified provider charter (Urban Utilities: special needs customer, special needs residential property, home haemodialysis, confirmed by a registered medical specialist, treating hospital or dialysis centre, four business days' notice) and the Code's topic as described by the Queensland Government; other providers' register names and fields are unverified. "Special needs customer" is also used outside water (transport, disability services), so enforce tiers need populated premises, medical or priority fields and 85 needs water-operations evidence. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: South-East Queensland Water (Distribution and Retail Restructuring) Act 2009 (Qld)

patterns.name: Queensland Workers' Compensation Claim or Work Capacity Record
patterns.description: Workers' compensation claim records for an identified worker under the Workers' Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2003 (Qld): the application for compensation, work capacity certificates (WorkCover / WorkSafe Form 132M, and the Comcare certificate of capacity equivalent), rehabilitation and return to work plans and suitable duties plans (WCRA ss 220, 226, 228), and claim decisions. Claim records combine health information (injury, diagnosis, capacity, restrictions, treating practitioner) with a claim, and WCRA s 572A prohibits obtaining or using such documents for employment purposes such as pre-employment checks. The WorkCover claim number format is not public, so it is matched only by its label.
patterns.operation: Primary: workers' compensation claim / application / claim form, "application for compensation", "work capacity certificate", "Form 132M", "certificate of capacity", "(rehabilitation and) return to work plan / coordinator", "suitable duties plan / program", "WorkCover (Queensland) claim", "Comcare claim" or RRTWC. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface WorkSafe / WorkCover guidance, blank certificates, policies and news. 75 requires one populated field within 300 characters: either a worker / claim field (worker or claimant name, employee, claim number by label, date of injury or birth, employer, insurer, case manager, policy number) or an injury / medical field (injury description, nature of injury, diagnosis, mechanism of injury, body part, capacity, restrictions, suitable duties, treating practitioner, review date) with a non-placeholder value, or a capacity statement ("fit for suitable duties", "no capacity for any work"). 85 requires a populated worker / claim field AND a populated injury / medical field plus an independent claim / insurer context term (insurer, self-insurer, weekly compensation, claim accepted / rejected, statutory claim, WCRA 2003, AHPRA). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude legislation text, fact sheets / guides, "how to make a claim" explainers and job ads.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the form titles and statutory phrases are specific, but they also appear throughout WorkSafe / WorkCover guidance, HR policies and blank certificates, and the claim number has no public format. Enforce tiers therefore require populated worker, claim or medical fields. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic records laid out like Form 132M and a typical RRTW plan.

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's workers compensation claim number format (see docs/identifiers.md#workcover-claim-number). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.risk_description: The detector targets an entity's own SOCI/AESCSF compliance or maturity assessment results for critical infrastructure assets. Disclosure can reveal unimplemented practices, maturity gaps and remediation status that help an attacker prioritise weaknesses in an essential service. Such material is typically SOCI "protected information" handled under the Act's own disclosure rules, which is not the same as a PSPF PROTECTED security classification; the normal unit is a bounded assessment rather than a full operational blueprint. Risk 8 with OFFICIAL: Sensitive / SENSITIVE InfoTech fits; a higher marking needs asset-level exploit paths or a national-significance designation established by the content.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 fits PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE InfoTech because an entity's own AESCSF or SOCI assessment reveals unimplemented practices, maturity gaps and remediation status that help an attacker prioritise. PROTECTED is not met: SOCI protected information is not a PSPF classification, and a bounded assessment lacks asset-level exploit paths.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling protects maturity scores and compliance gaps for critical infrastructure assets. It stays below High unless the content gives asset-level exploit paths.

patterns.name: SOCI Mandatory Cyber Security Incident Report or Ransomware Payment Report
patterns.description: Completed regulatory cyber incident reports made to the Australian Signals Directorate: mandatory cyber security incident reports under the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 (s 30BC critical incidents, 12 hours, written record within 84 hours of an oral report; s 30BD other incidents, 72 hours, written record within 48 hours), content entered in the ASD/ACSC "Report a cyber security incident" form (organisation, ABN, contact number, date and time the incident was identified, whether it is ongoing, incident type, Home Affairs consent), and ransomware payment reports under s 27 of the Cyber Security Act 2024. Distinct from global-security-incident-report and the OT cyber incident report classifiers, which cover internal incident and forensic reports; this one requires the regulatory reporting frame plus populated ASD form fields.
patterns.operation: Primary: "cyber security incident report/notification" (optionally "critical"), "mandatory cyber (security) incident report(ing)", "ransomware payment report", "critical cyber security incident", s 30BC / 30BD, "Cyber Security Act 2024" or "reported to ASD/ACSC/Australian Signals Directorate". 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface cyber.gov.au and CISC guidance and commentary. 75 requires one populated structure within 300 characters: a verified ASD form question with an answer ("Date and time the incident was identified" + date, "Is the incident ongoing?" + a single Yes/No, the Home Affairs consent question + a single Yes/No), an organisation/reporting entity name, ABN, Australian contact number, a selected incident type from the form's list, a dated oral report, or a ransomware payment amount/date. Blank forms that print "Yes / No" are rejected. 85 requires two distinct structure hits plus an independent corroborative term (significant/relevant impact, OT/IT/customer data impact, NOCS, ASD, Home Affairs, ransom demand, threat actor). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude guidance and legislation signals.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the statutory terms and ASD form labels are specific, but cyber.gov.au, CISC and law-firm guidance repeat the deadlines, section numbers and form questions. Enforce tiers require answered form fields rather than the questions alone, and there is no public report identifier. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a completed mandatory cyber security incident report or ransomware payment report made to ASD, gated on answered form fields. These reports are SOCI "relevant information" (s 5A: reports under s 30BC or 30BD) and describe a live compromise of a critical infrastructure asset: affected IT/OT systems, timing, whether the attacker still has access, and for ransomware reports the payment made. Disclosure can aid the attacker or copycats and prejudice the asset's security; unauthorised disclosure of protected information is an offence under SOCI s 45. Guidance, blank forms and commentary are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports PROTECTED InfoTech because the report describes a weakness in a critical asset that may still be open.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 maps to PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED InfoTech (PROT_IT) and the High tier because a completed s 30BC or s 30BD report describes a live compromise of a critical asset: the affected IT and OT systems, whether the attacker still has access, and any ransomware payment. That is a security vulnerability of a critical system that the attacker or copycats can use, the same harm as OT security assessments (PROTECTED, risk 10). The label rests on that harm; SOCI s 45 adds a disclosure offence but is not a PSPF marking.

generic.rationale: High InfoTech handling applies, with SOCI disclosure restrictions on top, because the report shows where a critical asset was compromised and may still be exposed. Access should be limited to the incident response team and the officers who report to ASD.

patterns.name: SOCI Act Relevant Information Record (CIRMP, Asset Register, SoNS Obligations)
patterns.description: Documents that are "relevant information" under s 5A of the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 (Cth): a critical infrastructure risk management program (CIRMP, s 30AC) and the annual CIRMP report (s 30AG: up-to-date statement for a financial year, board or governing body approval, hazards with a significant relevant impact; LIN 23/006 and LIN 26/075 terms), Register of Critical Infrastructure Assets submissions (s 6 interest and control information, s 7 operational information), and Systems of National Significance enhanced cyber security obligation documents (incident response plan s 30CD, cyber security exercise evaluation reports s 30CQ / 30CR, vulnerability assessment report s 30CZ, system information reporting notices s 30DB / 30DC). There is no statutory marking for this material, so the classifier does not anchor on "PROTECTED" or any other label.
patterns.operation: Primary: CIRMP / "critical infrastructure risk management program", "Register of Critical Infrastructure Assets", "system(s) of national significance", "enhanced cyber security obligations" or a SOCI section reference (s 30AC, 30AG, 30AQ, 30CD, 30CH, 30CQ, 30CR, 30CZ, 30DB, 30DC). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface CISC guidance, legislation and law-firm articles. 75 requires one populated record structure within 300 characters: a labelled entity/asset/hazard/interest field with a non-placeholder value, a financial-year field, an ABN value, an s 30AG statement that the program was (not) up to date for a named financial year, a type-and-level-of-interest percentage, or a dated board/governing-body approval. 85 requires two distinct structure hits plus an independent corroborative term (significant relevant impact, LIN 26/075 defined terms, CISC, relevant Commonwealth regulator). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude legislation and guidance signals (cisc.gov.au, legislation.gov.au, "Civil penalty:", compilation headers, law-firm disclaimers).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary terms are statutory and distinctive, but CISC guidance, the legislation and law-firm commentary use every one of them, and there is no statutory marking or public identifier for CIRMPs, register entries or SoNS reports. Enforce tiers therefore depend on populated record fields laid out like register submissions and annual reports. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.name: Australian Superannuation Fund Number
patterns.description: Detects Australian Superannuation Fund Number (RSE) patterns. An R prefix followed by 7 digits, registered with APRA.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \bR\d{7}\b matches an uppercase R followed by exactly 7 digits. The Purview engine uses two regexes: Pattern_super_labeled (labeled format with RSE/fund/APRA/superannuation prefix + R + digits) and Pattern_au_super_fund (bare R + 7 digits format). Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires superannuation terms + payroll/retirement keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires superannuation terms; Low (65) requires superannuation terms only (minimum context). Evidence uses 2 keyword groups (9 superannuation terms, 9 payroll/retirement terms) within 300-character proximity. Keyword lists: financial-deposit-terms, industry-hr.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low confidence: an R followed by 7 digits is a relatively short pattern that can match reference codes, part numbers, and other alphanumeric sequences. Corroborative evidence keywords such as superannuation, APRA, or RSE are essential for reliable detection.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

Low-range fund number

should_not_match.description: Wrong prefix letter (S instead of R)

false_positives.description: Financial terminology appearing in published reports, accounting textbooks, regulatory guidance, or template documents without actual transaction data.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords within the proximity window. Cross-reference with structured financial identifiers to confirm actual sensitive data.

false_positives.description: In Australian English, standard business terminology overlapping with financial detection keywords in routine correspondence and documentation.
false_positives.mitigation: Increase confidence threshold when scanning business correspondence. Layer with transaction-specific patterns for higher precision.

patterns.risk_description: The regex finds an uppercase R followed by seven digits, with stronger tiers adding RSE, fund, APRA, payroll, or retirement context. That value identifies a regulated superannuation fund rather than an individual member, balance, login, or authority to transact. Misuse is therefore mainly misrouting, impersonation, or correlation against a fund, and the bare format can also collide with unrelated reference numbers. Risk 4 OFFICIAL reflects low and reversible harm from the atomic fund identifier; SENSITIVE would require linkage to a member account, contribution transaction, or authentication material.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 is consistent with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, and Low tier because an RSE fund number is an organisational routing identifier and does not expose a person's superannuation holding. SENSITIVE is not met without member-level or transactional data that the detector does not capture.

generic.rationale: Low generic handling is suitable for a fund identifier whose harmful use depends on additional member, payment, or access information. Medium handling becomes appropriate only when the number is embedded in a private contribution or account record.

patterns.name: Telco Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence Affected Person Record
patterns.description: Telecommunications provider account records that identify a customer or end-user as an "affected person" under the Telecommunications (Domestic, Family and Sexual Violence Consumer Protections) Industry Standard 2025 (F2025L00664). Covers the agreed communication method recorded under s 10, the privacy, safety and security protections put on the account under ss 11-12 (PIN or password, verification code to a safe number or email, a new account not linked to the perpetrator), holds on and urgent reversal of a service limiting action under s 13, non-disclosure instructions under ss 25 and 27, privacy breach notifications to the affected person and the ACMA under s 29, and the record of the type of evidence sought, provided and sighted under ss 14 and 30-31. Most of the Standard commenced on 1 January 2026 (1 April 2026 for small providers); some provisions commenced on 1 July 2025. This is the telco counterpart of au-energy-family-violence-customer-record, with telco account structure (account or customer number, service or mobile number, MSISDN).
patterns.operation: Primary: an affected-person or DFV account phrase (affected person, customer/consumer affected by or experiencing domestic, family or sexual violence, a DFV/DFSV/FV or domestic/family violence flag, indicator, alert, marker, account, note or case, or "service limiting action"). 75 tier requires, within 300 characters, one populated structure: a telco account field (an account, customer or service number or ID containing a digit, a labelled mobile/service/phone number or MSISDN with an Australian mobile value, or an account holder name) or a protection-action field (an agreed, preferred or safe communication or contact method with a value, a safe number or email with a value, a PIN, password or verification code added or set, a restriction, suspension, disconnection or barring reversed or lifted, a disconnection, suspension, credit-management or collections hold with a status or date, a new account not linked to the perpetrator, an authorised representative removed, a "do not disclose/discuss ... to/with" the account holder, authorised representative, former partner or perpetrator, a populated "evidence sought/provided/sighted" field, or an "ACMA notified" / "affected person notified" entry with a date). 85 tier requires an account field AND a protection-action field AND an independent telco term (mobile, SIM, nbn, carriage service, telco, prepaid, postpaid, handset, porting, plan, bill). All enforce tiers AND NOT the shared template-exclusion dictionary and a standard/policy exclusion (this industry standard, a provider must, DFV statement, our DFV policy, published on our website, Communications Alliance, Action on telco consumer protections). 65 is discovery-only (primary phrase alone) and will surface the Standard, ACMA guidance and published telco DFV statements.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: "affected person", "agreed communication method" and "service limiting action" are the defined terms of F2025L00664, but the Standard, ACMA guidance and every provider's published DFV statement (s 17) use the same words, and "affected person" is also used outside DFV. Enforce tiers therefore need a populated telco account or protection-action field, and a standard/policy exclusion. Provider CRM field labels (for example the wording of a DFV flag) are not published and are unverified, so the account and action fields are generic labelled-value shapes. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a telco account record that marks a customer or end-user as affected by domestic, family or sexual violence and carries the account, service or mobile number together with how the provider may safely contact them, what must be withheld from an account holder, authorised representative or former partner, security protections, reconnection or collections holds, the evidence type sighted, and any privacy breach. The Standard (ss 25 and 27) prohibits disclosing information that could identify or locate an affected person, including the fact that they are an affected person. Disclosure to a person using violence can reveal a victim-survivor's number, whereabouts and new account, with a credible risk of serious harm. This is the same harm the au-dfv-confidential-address and au-energy-family-violence-customer-record classifiers treat as PROTECTED. Risk 10 supports PROTECTED Personal-Privacy; review against the organisation's own harm assessment before enforcement.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to PSPF and QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED Personal-Privacy and High because the record exposes an affected person's service number, new account, safe contact and security protections, which the Standard (ss 25, 27) bars disclosing. A person using violence could use it to locate or contact them, so serious harm is inherent; higher levels are out of scope.

generic.rationale: High with High Personal-Privacy handling applies because the record can reveal a victim-survivor's number and whereabouts. No higher generic tier exists.
