should_not_match.description: ALL-CAPS prose containing SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL and EU but not the EUCI bilingual marking — fails at the regex level

false_positives.description: ALL-CAPS prose (headings, legal boilerplate, or fully-capitalised documents) can defeat the case-sensitivity signal, but only if it reproduces the exact bilingual "<FR-LEVEL> UE/EU <EN-LEVEL>" (or the French "<FR-LEVEL> UE") construction — which is itself the marking, so residual collision is very low.
false_positives.mitigation: The dual-form tier (85) is structurally near-unique; treat single-language French-component hits (75) as lower confidence in all-caps context. Corroborative EU/EUCI keywords within 300 characters reinforce genuine marking context.

false_positives.description: The single-language ENGLISH halves (EU RESTRICTED, EU CONFIDENTIAL, EU SECRET, EU TOP SECRET) are real components of the verified markings but are not shipped as a standalone tier: an "EU " prefix on common English classification words (especially EU RESTRICTED / EU SECRET) carries a materially higher false-positive surface than the French components, whose classification words (RESTREINT, CONFIDENTIEL) do not occur in ordinary English text.
false_positives.mitigation: Documented as a deliberate scoping decision rather than shipped. The English halves are still detected whenever they appear as part of the canonical dual marking (tier 85).

false_positives.description: This SIT's SECRET / CONFIDENTIAL / TOP SECRET vocabulary overlaps with the US/UK/NZ/AU marking families, but the mandatory UE/EU bilingual construction (85) and the trailing UE marker (75) mean a genuine EUCI marking is structurally distinct from those nations' bare-word tiers; a document carrying both an EUCI marking and a national marking is expected to fire both SITs as corroborating signals.
false_positives.mitigation: No mitigation needed — the bilingual/UE structure makes the EUCI forms distinct from national bare-word markings.

patterns.risk_description: The detector recognises the full EUCI ladder, from RESTREINT UE/EU RESTRICTED through CONFIDENTIAL, SECRET, and TOP SECRET bilingual markings, plus lower-tier French halves. A genuine hit denotes classified EU information, but the normal match may be the lowest restricted rung rather than a strategic TOP SECRET asset. Disclosure can breach Council handling rules and cause diplomatic, operational, or security harm whose scale depends on the exact level and underlying record. Risk 8 preserves SENSITIVE as the broad-ladder baseline; PROTECTED would require a high rung or contents capable of significant strategic, safety, protected-operation, or system-scale damage.

sensitivity_labels.euci: RESTREINT UE/EU RESTRICTED / CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL / SECRET UE/EU SECRET / TRÈS SECRET UE/EU TOP SECRET
sensitivity_labels.ca_gov: Protected B / Confidential / Secret / Top Secret

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to SENSITIVE and Medium tiers because the detector spans RESTREINT through TOP SECRET and an unspecified hit does not establish the highest consequence. PROTECTED is not met without a high branch or credible significant strategic, safety, or operational damage.

generic.rationale: A mixed EUCI ladder match is generically Medium with Medium Government DLM until the exact marking and contents establish a High consequence.

patterns.name: EU NIS2 Cybersecurity Risk-Management Measures
patterns.description: Detects NIS2 Article 21 cybersecurity risk-management measures documentation from essential and important entities — gap assessments, board approval papers, and the policies implementing the Article 21(2)(a)-(j) measures (incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, cyber hygiene, cryptography, access control, multi-factor authentication). These documents catalogue an entity's security posture and unremediated gaps.
patterns.operation: Keyword proximity: primary topic phrase (cybersecurity risk-management measures — the Article 21 term of art) within 300 characters of Article 21 vocabulary (all-hazards approach, Directive (EU) 2022/2555, essential entity, incident handling, supply chain security, cyber hygiene, multi-factor authentication). Negative keyword exclusion for news, consultancy, and training material. Concept classifier: matches the topic, not identifier-grade evidence.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: honest topic matcher. 'Cybersecurity risk-management measures' is the NIS2 Article 21 term of art and the only primary; 'all-hazards approach' is also a ubiquitous FEMA/civil-protection term of art, so it corroborates but never fires alone. The 85 tier additionally requires the directive's measure vocabulary (essential/important entity, incident handling, supply chain security, cyber hygiene). The individual Article 21(2) measure names are generic security vocabulary, so they corroborate but never trigger alone; consultancy and academic material is suppressed only by noise exclusions.

patterns.risk_description: The NIS2 Article 21 concept regex covers incident handling, supply-chain security, continuity, cryptography, access control, multifactor authentication, and related board or gap-assessment language, while excluding obvious public samples. Directives, guidance, and templates have little standalone sensitivity, but an organisation-specific assessment can catalogue unremediated weaknesses and accepted residual risks that support attack planning. The normal topic match does not identify an entity, live control gap, or reachable system and therefore creates limited harm. Risk 4 and OFFICIAL suit the public or unattributed branch; SENSITIVE requires a current internal assessment that names exploitable deficiencies, affected services, or unresolved control failures.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, OFFI, and Low because the concept detector can match public Article 21 guidance, generic security policies, consultancy material, and templates without identifying an organisation or live deficiency. SENSITIVE requires a current entity-specific gap assessment, board risk acceptance, or implementing record that names affected services, unremediated control failures, or exploitable security weaknesses.

generic.rationale: Low generic handling follows the accepted concept-level outcome, with stronger treatment necessary when evidence confirms current internal control weaknesses or residual-risk decisions.

patterns.description: Detects NIS2 Article 23 significant-incident notifications from essential and important entities — the 24-hour early warning, 72-hour incident notification, intermediate report, final report, and progress report submitted to the CSIRT or competent authority. patterns.operation: Keyword proximity: primary topic phrase (significant incident — the Article 23 defined trigger) within 300 characters of Article 23 vocabulary (early warning, incident notification, CSIRT, competent authority, Directive (EU) 2022/2555, severe operational disruption, indicators of compromise, final report). 'Significant incident' is the Article 23 defined trigger term and the only primary; the stage names 'early warning' and 'incident notification' are ubiquitous outside NIS2 (meteorology, PagerDuty-style ops tooling) so they corroborate but never fire alone. 'Significant incident' still occurs in generic incident-management prose at the 75/65 tiers; the 85 tier, which requires NIS2-specific vocabulary (CSIRT, Directive (EU) 2022/2555, severe operational disruption, indicators of compromise), approaches document-class precision.

patterns.name: EU VAT Identification Number - All Member States
patterns.description: Detects EU VAT identification numbers for all 27 member states in a single consolidated pattern, built branch-by-branch from the per-country structures published in the European Commission VIES FAQ (Q11). Covers the Greek quirk (Greece prefixes with EL, not GR) and Northern Ireland's XI prefix, which remains checkable in VIES for goods traders under the Windsor Framework — XI is included with the UK 9-digit, 12-digit and GD/HA government/health-authority forms; plain GB numbers are NOT included because Great Britain left the VIES scheme after Brexit. This pattern is a superset alongside the existing per-country detectors (at/be/de/fr/hu/it-vat-number), which stay untouched for deployed-GUID stability — the same document may fire both, following the global-iban / eu-iban precedent.
patterns.operation: Structural detection via a bounded per-country alternation (no generic alphanumeric collapse). Per-country check digits (e.g. IT Luhn, HR ISO 7064 MOD 11-10, SK divisible-by-11) are not expressible in a single regex and no Purview validator function covers VAT, so checksums are not enforced. Reference: European Commission VIES FAQ Q11 per-country format table, corroborated row-by-row against secondary mirrors. Spaced presentations are accepted only where the VIES format table itself renders them: DK (4 blocks of 2 digits), FR (2-character key, space, 9-digit SIREN) and XI (UK 3-4-2 blocks, optional 3-digit branch-trader block) — bounded literal-space classes only, never free whitespace. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: vat-numbers.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: every branch requires the exact two-letter member-state prefix followed by that state's verified digit/letter structure, which is distinctive in business documents; this matches the confidence of the existing per-country VAT detectors. The short Romanian branch (RO + 2-10 digits, no leading zero) is the loosest row and is the main reason the bare structural tier stays discovery-only.

France with the SIREN split into triplets — VIES prints the SIREN as a single 9-digit block after the key
Northern Ireland wrong grouping — VIES prints 3-4-2 digit blocks, not 3-2-4
Germany spaced — the VIES DE row is a single 9-digit block; no spacing is documented

false_positives.description: Deliberate overlap with the existing per-country detectors (at/be/de/fr/hu/it-vat-number): the same VAT number can fire both this consolidated pattern and a per-country pattern. This mirrors the accepted global-iban / eu-iban superset precedent.
false_positives.mitigation: Deploy either the consolidated pattern or the per-country patterns, or de-duplicate at the reporting layer if both are enabled.

false_positives.description: Two capital letters followed by digits occur in other identifier schemes (order codes, national IDs, IBAN fragments); the short Bulgarian/Czech/Romanian digit bodies are the most collision-prone rows, and no checksum can be enforced in the exported SIT.
false_positives.mitigation: Every branch is bounded to the exact per-country structure (no generic 8-12 alphanumeric collapse); the reporting tier requires VAT keywords within the proximity window and the bare structural tier is discovery-only.

patterns.risk_description: This consolidated pattern recognizes country-specific VAT structures for all EU member states plus the VIES-eligible XI forms, using exact prefix branches and VAT context rather than a generic alphanumeric rule. A matched value identifies a business for registration and invoice validation and is generally intended for exchange or registry checking, not personal authentication. Reuse can aid false supplier records or invoice fraud, but the actor still needs company details, payment instructions, and access to a commercial process; overlap with deployed country-specific VAT detectors is expected. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL fit the bounded entity-level harm, while confidential returns, bank changes, or a coordinated payment-fraud record would raise the context toward SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, and Low for a public-facing EU VAT identifier. SENSITIVE is not met because even a structurally credible match provides no confidential fiscal result, credential, or payment authority.

generic.rationale: Low classification and Low DLM reflect routine cross-border business disclosure and limited standalone confidentiality. Fraud risk depends on invoice, supplier, banking, or account-process data that this identifier does not establish.

patterns.name: French Phone Number
patterns.description: Detects French national telephone numbers per ARCEP's numbering plan: 10-digit numbers in the "0X XX XX XX XX" form covering geographic (01-05), mobile/personal (06-07), and polyvalent (09) leading digits, plus the +33 international form (10-digit domestic number with the leading 0 dropped, per ARCEP convention), including the widespread "+33 (0)6 39 98 45 67" letterhead rendering (a common-but-nonstandard practice — ITU-T E.123 advises against the parenthesised trunk digit in international notation, but it is ubiquitous on French letterheads and email signatures, so it is matched for detection purposes). The 09 polyvalent range is in scope because it is predominantly personal PII in practice: 09 is the standard residential VoIP home-line range, auto-issued with consumer internet boxes to millions of French households; only the small 0937-0939 sub-range carries ARCEP's newer "technical platform" category (app-to-driver ephemeral numbers and similar). Numbers beginning 08 (value-added services) remain intentionally out of scope — organizational/service numbers rather than personal PII, mirroring how uk-phone-number scopes out non-geographic service ranges.
patterns.operation: Validation: none (French numbers have no checksum). Reference: ARCEP, La numérotation, https://www.arcep.fr/la-regulation/grands-dossiers-thematiques-transverses/la-numerotation.html; ARCEP Décision n° 2021-0532 du 8 avril 2021 (établissant le plan national de numérotation et ses règles de gestion), https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000043910234. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: phone-context. Both the domestic and international (+33) sub-regexes are evidence-gated at every tier — no tier fires without positive corroborative evidence, per the phone-family convention — see confidence_justification.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the leading-digit constraint (01-07 and 09 domestic, restricting to geographic, mobile/personal, and polyvalent ranges) and the fixed 10-digit length narrow the format, but French numbers carry no checksum and a 10-digit sequence with those leading digits is still a high digit-collision format. Per the phone-family convention (every tier requires positive corroborative evidence; a +CC prefix alone is insufficient gating; there is no 65 rung), both the domestic and +33 international sub-regexes are evidence-gated at every tier: 75 requires generic phone-context evidence and 85 requires country-specific phone keywords with template/noise exclusion. The literal +33 prefix improves precision when present but is not by itself sufficient gating.

should_match.description: ARCEP-reserved fictional root for audiovisual works (Décision n° 2021-0532, §2.5.12), mobile 06 range, space-separated
ARCEP-reserved fictional root, geographic 01 (Paris-region-style) range
ARCEP-reserved fictional root, geographic 02 range, dot-separated
International +33 form of the mobile fictional root, leading 0 dropped
Widespread "+CC (0)" letterhead rendering — nonstandard per E.123 but ubiquitous on French letterheads
Domestic mobile written without separators
Polyvalent 09 residential VoIP home-line range, illustrative synthetic value (ARCEP's audiovisual-works fictional roots include no 09 root)

should_not_match.description: Leading digit 8 is a value-added-service number, out of scope for this personal-communications pattern

Second digit 0 — "00" is the international call prefix, not a subscriber-number category (the plan's subscriber categories are 01-09; this pattern covers 01-07 and 09, with 08 value-added services deliberately out of scope)
Only 8 digits total, two short of the required 10
Valid-shaped digit run embedded inside a longer reference number, rejected by digit boundaries

Australian mobile in 4-3-3 grouping (signature block, 2026-10-16 boilerplate run). 04 is a valid French geographic prefix, so only the grouping tells them apart; the domestic sub-regex needs French pairs or no separators.
Australian landline in 2-4-4 grouping; not French pair grouping

false_positives.description: Australian numbers share the 10-digit trunk-0 shape (04 mobiles, 02/03/07/08 landlines), and 04 and 07 are valid French prefixes, so an Australian signature-block number next to "Mobile:" reached 75.
false_positives.mitigation: The domestic sub-regex accepts only the French written forms: ten digits with no separators, or a separator before every pair ("06 39 98 45 67", "06.39.98.45.67"). Australian 4-3-3 mobiles and 2-4-4 landlines no longer match. An Australian number written without separators ("0412555019") is still indistinguishable and relies on the phone-context gating.

false_positives.description: A 10-digit sequence with a 01-07 or 09 leading digit can still coincidentally match invoice numbers, order numbers, or other structured identifiers of the same length and leading-digit distribution.
false_positives.mitigation: Every tier — for both the domestic and +33 international sub-regexes — requires positive phone-context or country-specific evidence within 300 characters; no zero-evidence tier exists, so a bare digit run without corroborating context never fires at any confidence level.

false_positives.description: Since January 2023, geographic numbers (01-05) are no longer tied to a physical department, so the leading digit alone does not confirm a caller's actual location — this pattern detects the number format only, not geographic attribution.
false_positives.mitigation: Rely on surrounding document context (postal addresses, entity names) rather than the leading digit for any geographic-attribution use case.

false_positives.description: Within the 09 range, the 0937-0939 sub-range carries ARCEP's "technical platform" category (organizational platform-to-customer communication numbers, e.g. app-to-driver ephemeral numbers) rather than personal home lines — the regex cannot distinguish this sub-range from the residential VoIP majority of the 09 block.
false_positives.mitigation: Accepted trade-off: the 09 block outside 0937-0939 is predominantly personal residential lines, and a platform number matched in error is a low-harm false positive; evidence gating still applies at every tier.

patterns.risk_description: The French phone pattern finds domestic and +33 numbers in geographic 01-05, mobile 06-07, and 09 polyvalent ranges, including the common parenthesised trunk rendering; 08 service numbers are excluded. Disclosure permits calling, smishing, vishing, and correlation, but the number alone does not show who controls it or whether a 09 value is a household line or technical platform endpoint. A routine match affects one contact point and may also be a business line or structured numeric reference. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL fit that bounded exposure; SENSITIVE would require linkage to protected communications, credentials, precise location, or a vulnerable person's private identity context.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to OFFICIAL because a French number enables contact and social engineering but does not itself authenticate the subscriber or reveal a sensitive relationship. SENSITIVE is not met without credentials, private communications, vulnerable-person context, or linked identity and location information.

generic.rationale: Generic Low handling reflects one French-format contact route whose ownership, geography, and personal-versus-platform status are not established by the value alone.

references.title: Légifrance: Décision n° 2021-0532 du 8 avril 2021 (plan national de numérotation), incl. §2.5.12 Numéros pour œuvres audiovisuelles

ITU-T Recommendation E.123: Notation for national and international telephone numbers — the international "(0)" trunk-digit form is documented as common practice that E.123 advises against

changelog.description: French grouping (2026-10-16 boilerplate run): the domestic sub-regex fired at 75 on an Australian mobile ("Mobile: 0412 555 019") because it allowed a separator between any two digits. The domestic sub-regex and its top-level copy now accept only ten unseparated digits or five pairs with a separator before each pair, the way French numbers are written. Australian 4-3-3 mobiles and 2-4-4 landlines are added as should_not_match, and the unseparated form as a should_match. The +33 international sub-regex is unchanged.

patterns.name: Mobile Advertising ID (IDFA / GAID / AAID)
patterns.description: Detects mobile advertising identifiers - Apple's IDFA and Google's Advertising ID (GAID, also called AAID) - when they appear labelled with an advertising-ID keyword. These IDs are UUIDs in the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form. Although resettable, advertising IDs are persistent cross-app device identifiers treated as personal data under GDPR and CCPA/CPRA, and their disclosure enables cross-context tracking and re-identification.
patterns.operation: A labelled IDFA, GAID, AAID, advertising-ID, or ad-ID UUID candidate is discovery-only at 65. Explicit iOS, Android, Apple-IDFA, Google-Advertising-ID, or mobile-ad-SDK context raises it to 75. The 85 tier additionally requires an attribution, consent, campaign-event, device-profile, install, or audience-segment record. Enforcing tiers reject public documentation, templates, and examples.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the UUID body is generic (any v4 UUID matches the hex layout), so detection relies on an explicit advertising-ID label adjacent to the value. The label requirement keeps false positives low, but unlabelled IDFA or GAID values are intentionally not matched.

should_not_match.description: Template contains otherwise high-tier evidence

false_positives.description: Other UUIDs (session tokens, request IDs, correlation IDs) that happen to sit next to the word 'ad' or 'id'.
false_positives.mitigation: The pattern requires a specific advertising-ID label; tighten the label list further if generic 'ad id' collides in your corpus.

patterns.risk_description: The detector finds a canonical UUID only when labelled as an IDFA, GAID, AAID, advertising ID, or equivalent mobile advertising identifier. A real value can support cross-app device correlation and re-identification when an advertising platform or data broker also holds behavioural records. By itself it is resettable, does not name the user, and contains no location, browsing history, or device-access secret, while unrelated UUIDs remain a documented collision risk. Risk 5 OFFICIAL reflects bounded tracking potential; SENSITIVE would require a person-level identity link, behavioural profile, precise location history, or a substantial cross-context dataset.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, the OFFICIAL DLM, OFFI, and Low tier for one labelled but resettable advertising identifier. The next SENSITIVE level is not met because the match lacks identity resolution, behaviour, location, or a consequential advertising profile.

generic.rationale: Generic Low and Low handling fit a resettable advertising identifier whose privacy impact becomes material only after linkage to identity or behavioural datasets.

patterns.name: Auth0 Token
patterns.description: Detects Auth0 client secrets. Auth0 issues an unprefixed 64-character base64url-style client secret, indistinguishable from other long random strings, so this pattern requires an adjacent Auth0 label plus an assignment separator to structurally qualify a match. A leaked client secret lets an attacker mint tokens as the application and impersonate it against every API it is authorized for.
patterns.operation: An Auth0 label (auth0 / AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET) followed within a short gap by an assignment separator (= or :) and a 64-character (bounded to 100 for longer variants) base64url-charset value. Both production detectors that cover Auth0 client secrets (TruffleHog auth0oauth, Kingfisher auth0.2) use a label-gated 64-plus-character [A-Za-z0-9_-] body; neither fires value-only, and neither does this pattern. Auth0 Management API tokens are JWTs with no Auth0-specific visible marker and are deliberately out of scope (covered generically by the JWT pattern). Auth0 client IDs (32-character identifiers) are public identifiers, not secrets, and are structurally excluded by the 64-character floor. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: Auth0's own documentation does not publish the client secret's visible format. TruffleHog's production detector pins a 64-plus-character [a-zA-Z0-9_-] body paired with Auth0 context, and Kingfisher's production rule independently pins the same label-gated 64-plus-character body -- converging secret-scanning-ecosystem evidence, but for an unprefixed opaque string. Without an adjacent Auth0 label the value is indistinguishable from any other 64-character token, so this pattern requires the labelled assignment and offers no value-only tier. Auth0 is not a GitHub secret-scanning partner and gitleaks has no Auth0 rule, consistent with the format's inherent ambiguity.

should_match.description: Auth0 client secret in the canonical env var (label + assignment + 64-char body)
Auth0 label with colon separator and a 64-char base64url-charset body
Quoted Auth0 secret in a config assignment
Two distinct Auth0 Token values in one file; the 85 tier needs two distinct tokens (one token, or the same token repeated, stays below 85)

should_not_match.value: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789AB with no vendor context
should_not_match.description: Bare 64-char value with no Auth0 label anywhere (could be any hash or token)

should_not_match.value: AUTH0_CLIENT_ID=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345
should_not_match.description: Auth0 client ID (32-char public identifier, not a secret; below the 64-char floor)

should_not_match.value: auth0 secret too short: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP0123
should_not_match.description: Auth0 label present but value far too short (20 chars, not 64)

should_not_match.value: rotate the auth0 client secret in the application settings
should_not_match.description: Prose mention without a token value

should_not_match.value: template example placeholder record identifier
should_not_match.description: Template/sample context should be excluded even when anchor words are present

false_positives.description: A 64-character hash (for example a SHA-256 hex digest) or unrelated token appearing in a labelled assignment near the word "auth0" in configuration or logs.
false_positives.mitigation: The regex requires label adjacency plus an assignment separator and never fires value-only; corroborative keywords and placeholder checks add further gating.

false_positives.description: Auth0 Management API access tokens are JWTs (eyJ...) with no Auth0-specific visible marker and are not matched by this pattern.
false_positives.mitigation: Documented as a deliberate scope decision; generic JWT detection covers that shape, and pairing it with Auth0 tenant domains is left to log-analysis tooling.

false_positives.mitigation: Check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx, 0000) and documentation file types to reduce false positives.

patterns.risk_description: The medium-confidence identifier pattern finds an Auth0-labelled 64-to-100-character client secret assignment and deliberately excludes public client IDs and generic JWTs. A live client secret can let an attacker impersonate the application, mint or obtain tokens through allowed flows, and call APIs within the client's configured grants. Harm normally affects one Auth0 application and its authorized APIs and users, with grant type, audience, scope, and rotation containing impact. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained identity-platform compromise, while a broadly privileged tenant-management application would raise the classification.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Auth0 client secret can authorize material application impersonation within configured grants. PROTECTED is not met because the detector does not establish tenant-wide management privilege, broad API scope, or significant cross-application compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium InfoTech handling fit Auth0 client secrets because they can compromise a bounded application identity while grants, audience, and revocation normally contain the result.

patterns.name: Binance API Key
patterns.description: Detects Binance API keys, which are 64-character case-sensitive alphanumeric strings with no distinctive prefix. Because a bare 64-char alphanumeric token is generic (it collides with any random token of that length), this pattern is context-gated: it requires a nearby Binance label and an assignment (= or :) before the value. A leaked key grants API access to the account (trading and, if enabled, withdrawal).
patterns.operation: A Binance label followed within a short gap by an assignment (= or :) and a 64-character alphanumeric value. Ed25519/RSA/HMAC refer to the secret signing-key type; the API key identifier itself is always the 64-char alphanumeric string. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: credentials.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: a 64-char alphanumeric string has no distinctive prefix and is indistinguishable from any other 64-char token, so detection relies on an adjacent Binance label plus an assignment. Binance has no standalone secret scanner (e.g. no TruffleHog detector) precisely because the bare value is not self-identifying.

patterns.risk_description: The medium-confidence detector finds a Binance-labelled 64-character API key value, using vendor context because the token has no distinctive prefix. Disclosure can identify an enabled trading credential and, when combined with its signing secret or a workflow that accepts the key, support unauthorized account queries, orders, or other permitted API activity. The affected party is one Binance account, with key permissions, IP restrictions, signing requirements, withdrawal settings, and revocation containing harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained financial and account risk, while a complete unrestricted credential pair with high-value withdrawal authority would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 supports QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Binance API key is part of an operational financial credential and can expose or enable material account activity within its permissions. PROTECTED is not met because the match does not establish the signing secret, unrestricted withdrawal rights, high balance, or severe irreversible loss.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification with Medium InfoTech handling is appropriate for Binance API keys because financial misuse can be serious while signing, permission, balance, and restriction controls normally bound the outcome.

patterns.description: Detects biometric data about an identified person - biometric templates, identifiers and records, fingerprint scans or templates, facial recognition, iris/retina scans, voiceprints and palm prints - when the biometric phrase sits with a populated person identifier and biometric enrolment/capture fields.
patterns.operation: The primary regex matches biometric data phrases (biometric data/template/identifier/scan/record, fingerprint scan/data/template, facial recognition, iris or retina scan, voiceprint, palm print, liveness detection). 65 (discovery only): phrase alone - policy, guidance, news and survey-design text naming the category stays here. 75: phrase plus a populated identified-person field (name, DOB, employee/member/customer/patient/participant number or ID, data subject). 85: person field plus a populated biometric record field (enrolment/capture/sensor ID, date or type, match or quality score, finger position, modality, liveness result, capture device) plus independent record evidence (enrolled, minutiae, false match rate, matched against, access control, time and attendance, identity verification). Template framing and guidance/policy/public-aggregate framing are excluded from 75/85. Converted from keyword_list to regex so the tier logic decides matches.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low by design: the attribute has no fixed format. Enforce tiers now require the attribute to be tied to an identified person record (a populated name/DOB/ID field), and 85 also requires a populated biometric record field plus independent record evidence, so policy text, surveys-in-design and news naming the category stay at 65 discovery.

patterns.name: Encoded Biometric Template
patterns.description: Detects encoded biometric template artifacts rather than the word "fingerprint". Matches the ISO/IEC 19794 family modality magic markers (FMR\0 finger minutiae, FIR\0 finger image, FAC\0 face, IIR\0 iris — also the ANSI/INCITS 378 FMR header) and base64 blobs explicitly labelled as a biometric / fingerprint / iris / face template. Real biometric exfiltration moves as encoded templates, not plaintext.
patterns.operation: Two branches. (1) Magic-marker: a 3-character ISO/IEC 19794 modality code (FMR/FIR/FAC/IIR) immediately followed by a NUL byte, the file signature of an encoded biometric record. (2) Labelled-base64: a biometric-template label within a short gap of a substantial base64 blob. Corroborative evidence keywords within 300 characters raise confidence.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence. The FMR/FIR/FAC/IIR + NUL signature is a standards-defined biometric record header that does not occur in ordinary text, and the labelled-base64 branch requires an explicit biometric-template label adjacent to a long base64 blob. False positives are unlikely outside documentation that deliberately quotes these markers.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative keywords (minutiae, enrollment, ISO 19794) within the proximity window and treat hits inside obvious documentation/spec text as informational.

patterns.risk_description: This high-confidence detector targets encoded biometric artifacts: ISO modality magic markers or substantial base64 blobs explicitly labelled as fingerprint, face, iris, or biometric templates. A genuine template can be copied, replayed, or analysed to attack biometric matching, exposing the enrolled person to durable identity harm because the underlying trait cannot be reissued like a password. The normal true positive is an encoded reusable biometric artifact. Copying or replay can compromise biometric authentication permanently because the underlying trait cannot be reset. Once corroborated as an actual Encoded Biometric Template record, risk 9 and PROTECTED Personal-Privacy are proportionate to the significant damage disclosure can cause.

classification.rationale: The global TestPattern classifier is assessed on its confirmed substantive record rather than an uncorroborated topic hit. The normal true positive is an encoded reusable biometric artifact. Copying or replay can compromise biometric authentication permanently because the underlying trait cannot be reset. The major consequence supports risk 9 and a consistent PROTECTED crosswalk using PROTECTED Personal-Privacy, PROT_Pvc and High handling.

generic.rationale: A reusable encoded biometric template is High Personal-Privacy information because compromise creates a persistent authentication and tracking risk that cannot be remedied by reissuing the trait. The global TestPattern classifier carries High Personal-Privacy handling when its substantive match is confirmed.

patterns.name: BIP-39 Crypto Wallet Seed Phrase
patterns.description: Detects a BIP-39 mnemonic (crypto wallet recovery / seed phrase): a run of 11-24 space-separated lowercase words. Because the full 2048-word BIP-39 list cannot be embedded in a single regex, detection fires either when the word run is explicitly labelled as a seed/mnemonic/recovery phrase, or when the run contains one of a set of distinctive BIP-39 anchor words. A leaked seed phrase grants full, irreversible control of the wallet's funds.
patterns.operation: Two paths. (1) Labelled: a seed/mnemonic/recovery-phrase/wallet-backup label followed by a run of 11-24 lowercase words of 3-8 letters each. (2) Anchor: a run of 11-24 lowercase 3-8 letter words that includes a distinctive BIP-39 anchor word (abandon, ability, zoo, zone, etc.). LIMITATION: cannot fully validate that every word is in the BIP-39 list, so the labelled path is the precise one and the anchor path is a heuristic. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence when labelled, because the explicit seed/mnemonic/recovery-phrase label adjacent to a long lowercase word run is highly specific. The anchor path is more heuristic but still requires a long run of short lowercase words containing a distinctive BIP-39 word, which is uncommon in ordinary prose.

false_positives.description: Long runs of short lowercase words (e.g. word-game text or tokenized prose) that happen to contain a BIP-39 anchor word.
false_positives.mitigation: Prefer the labelled path; require corroborative wallet/crypto keywords for the anchor path and optionally validate words against the full BIP-39 list downstream.

patterns.risk_description: This regex detects an 11-to-24-word crypto-wallet recovery phrase when labelled as a seed, mnemonic, recovery phrase, or wallet backup, with a second heuristic path using distinctive BIP-39 anchor words. A valid complete phrase grants direct and normally irreversible control of the associated wallet, enabling immediate transfer and permanent loss of its assets. The normal true-positive is one credential, but the regex does not validate every word and establishes neither the wallet balance nor wider operational impact. Risk 8 SENSITIVE InfoTech captures the credential's exceptional exploitability; PROTECTED is not justified without evidence that the wallet value or connected function reaches significant-damage scale.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, and Medium because a valid seed phrase confers full, irreversible wallet authority. The next higher PROTECTED classification is not met because the detector proves neither wallet value nor a protected operation or consequence capable of significant damage.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium InfoTech controls fit a directly exploitable recovery secret whose compromise can transfer all assets in one wallet but whose value is unknown.

patterns.name: Braintree Access Token
patterns.description: Detects Braintree (PayPal) OAuth access tokens, which use a distinctive literal dollar-delimited structure: access_token$<environment>$<merchant-id>$<token>. A leaked token allows payment processing and transaction-history access on the connected merchant's behalf.
patterns.operation: Literal prefix access_token followed by three $-delimited segments: environment (production or sandbox, Braintree's two documented environments), a lowercase alphanumeric merchant ID (bounded 8-32 chars), and a lowercase alphanumeric token (bounded 16-64 chars). The structure (access_token prefix, $ delimiter, environment segment, merchant-id segment) is confirmed by Braintree's own SDK credential parser. The exact segment lengths are NOT vendor-published: the only concrete observation (16-char merchant id, 32-char token) comes from the Semgrep secrets registry rule -- which self-declares LOW confidence and traces to a legacy third-party regex list -- loosely corroborated by TruffleHog's separate legacy-credential shapes (16-char merchant id, 32-char private key). Bounded ranges around those observations are used so real tokens with different segment lengths are not missed; the literal access_token$env$ lead-in carries the distinctiveness. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the literal "access_token$production$"/"access_token$sandbox$" lead-in is self-describing and essentially cannot occur by accident, and the $-delimited structure is confirmed by Braintree's own SDK source (CredentialsParser splits on $ and requires the access_token prefix). The segment lengths are deliberately bounded ranges rather than exact pins because the only exact-length evidence (16/32) is a single low-confidence community rule; the confidence rests on the literal prefix and structure, not on segment lengths.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative Braintree keywords and check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx).

false_positives.description: Braintree legacy gateway credentials (merchant ID, public key, private key) are unprefixed opaque strings (GitGuardian lists them as non-prefixed) and are not matched by this pattern; nor are the client_id$/client_secret$ OAuth app credentials, whose segment shapes are not published.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex identifies a Braintree OAuth bearer token in the distinctive access_token$environment$merchant-id$token structure. A live production or sandbox token can authorize payment operations and reveal transaction history for the connected merchant within the token's grants. The affected scale is one merchant integration and its customers and transactions, with environment, permissions, revocation, and merchant controls limiting harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained payment-platform compromise, while a production token with broad high-value settlement authority would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because the detected Braintree bearer token can directly authorize material merchant and transaction activity. PROTECTED is not met because the normal token is bounded to one integration and the detector does not establish high-value settlement control or severe irreversible financial loss.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium InfoTech handling fit Braintree access tokens because they provide direct payment-platform access while merchant scope, environment, grants, and revocation contain the damage.

patterns.name: Candidate Application Pack (Resume / CV, Cover Letter, Selection Criteria Response)
patterns.description: A job applicant's own documents as held by recruiters, recruitment platforms and HR: a resume / CV, a cover letter with a selection criteria response, or a completed application form. Detected from CV section headings (employment history, work experience, education, referees, key skills, career objective), a populated candidate contact block (name with phone or email), employment date ranges and populated referee details. The panel's side of recruitment (interview notes, selection reports) and recommendation letters are covered by separate classifiers.
patterns.operation: Primary: a CV / application section heading followed by a colon or line break (employment / work / career history, work / professional experience, career objective / summary / profile, professional summary, education, qualifications, referees, key / core / technical skills, core competencies, personal details, licences and certifications, selection criteria response, response to the selection criteria). 65 is discovery-only (one heading) and surfaces job ads, position descriptions and CV guides. 75 requires at least 2 distinct headings plus, within 300 characters, a populated contact field: a phone or email label with a real phone number or email address, or a name followed by a separator and a phone number or email address. There are two 85 tiers, both built on the 75 evidence. 85a adds 2 or more distinct employment date ranges (Mar 2019 - Present, 2016 - 2019, 03/2014 - 11/2018). 85b adds populated referee details (a referee label or heading followed by a name and, within 140 characters, a phone number or email address). Every enforce tier excludes template/fixture text and job-advertisement, CV-writing-guide and staff-profile wording.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: CV headings are shared with job ads, position descriptions, CV writing guides and published staff profiles, so enforcement needs a populated phone or email contact with two distinct headings, and 85 needs a run of employment date ranges or a referee with contact details. Job-ad, CV-guide and staff-profile wording is excluded. CVs laid out as images or with headings the extractor merges into body text fall to 65 or below, and a published profile that avoids the excluded wording can reach 75. The 85/75 tiers are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; tests are synthetic documents.

patterns.name: Card Verification Value (Labelled)
patterns.description: Detects a labelled card verification value: a CVV / CVV2 / CVC / CVC2 / CID / CSC keyword (or the spelled-out "card verification value/code" / "card security code") immediately followed by a 3 or 4 digit value. The CVV is sensitive authentication data that PCI DSS 4.0 Requirement 3.3.1 prohibits storing after authorization.
patterns.operation: A CVV-family label (CVV, CVV2, CVC, CVC2, CID, CSC, or the full phrase) followed by up to 8 separator characters and a 3 or 4 digit code, bounded so it does not match inside a longer number. The label requirement keeps confidence reasonable because a bare 3-4 digit number is otherwise indistinguishable from ordinary data. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the value itself (3-4 digits) is generic, but requiring an adjacent CVV/CVC/CID-family label substantially reduces false positives. Not high because the label-plus-short-number structure can still appear in forms and test fixtures.

patterns.risk_description: This regex identifies a CVV, CVC, CID, CSC, or equivalent full label followed by a bounded three- or four-digit value. patterns.name: Cardano Address
patterns.description: Detects Cardano Shelley-era payment addresses: bech32-encoded with the mainnet human-readable prefix "addr1" (CIP-19 / CIP-5). The bech32 body varies with address type — enterprise (payment only) ~53 body chars, base (payment + stake) ~98 body chars, pointer in between — so the total ranges roughly 58-103 characters. The distinctive "addr1" prefix plus a long bech32 body is strong structure, gated at 85. Legacy Byron base58 (Ae2.../DdzFF...) and reward "stake1" addresses are not implemented (see report). Prefix/lengths verified against the CIP-19 test vectors.
patterns.operation: Single tier at confidence 85. The distinctive "addr1" bech32 HRP plus a 50-100 char bech32 body is matched, then AND-gated by cryptocurrency/wallet domain context (crypto-wallet-context dict) within proximity plus a template/sample noise NOT-group (never a bare high tier). Case-sensitive bech32 body (charset a c-h j-n p-z 0 2-9; the bech32 checksum is not expressible in a Purview-safe regex).
patterns.confidence_justification: Gated 85: the fixed "addr1" mainnet HRP combined with a long bech32 body (roughly 58-103 chars) is highly distinctive and unlikely to occur by chance, so it earns the high tier — but only when AND-gated by cryptocurrency/wallet domain context plus the noise exclusion. The bech32 checksum cannot be validated in a Purview-safe regex, so context gating is retained rather than exporting a bare tier.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

patterns.description: Detects Cloudflare API tokens - 40-character tokens that authenticate to the Cloudflare API. Because the raw token has no distinctive prefix, this pattern gates on nearby Cloudflare context to keep false positives low.

patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the 40-character token body is generic, so detection requires an adjacent Cloudflare context label. This cuts false positives at the cost of missing unlabelled tokens.

patterns.risk_description: This detector finds a 40-character Cloudflare API token only when an adjacent Cloudflare or CF token label supplies context, because the raw value has no distinctive prefix. A usable token can change DNS, firewall, Worker, or zone settings according to its configured permissions, enabling interception or service disruption. The impact is serious for the zones granted to one token, but token scope is configurable and the match does not prove full-account control. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE InfoTech fit the normal unit; PROTECTED requires demonstrated broad or critical-service authority.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps coherently to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, and SENS_IT for a Cloudflare token capable of direct configuration changes. PROTECTED is not met because the detector does not establish unrestricted account scope or critical infrastructure impact.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling reflects bounded but serious control over DNS and edge services. High handling requires verified global account privilege or major public-service consequences beyond the token shape.

patterns.name: Coinbase API Key
patterns.description: Detects Coinbase Developer Platform (CDP) API key names, which use the distinctive resource-path form organizations/{org-uuid}/apiKeys/{key-uuid}. This key name is paired with an EC/ECDSA (or Ed25519) signing secret and is used to mint ES256 JWTs for the Coinbase API. A leaked CDP key can grant programmatic access to accounts, trading and funds. The associated EC PRIVATE KEY PEM secret is detected separately by global-ec-private.
patterns.operation: Literal path organizations/ + a 36-char UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex) + /apiKeys/ + a second UUID. The full two-UUID Coinbase resource path is highly distinctive, so the value alone is strong evidence. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: credentials.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the literal organizations/.../apiKeys/... path carrying two UUIDs is a Coinbase-specific structure that does not collide with ordinary identifiers, so the value is reliable on its own; corroborative Coinbase/credential keywords further raise precision.

should_match.description: CDP key name with zero-entropy placeholder UUIDs (org + apiKey)
Labelled CDP key name in an assignment, repeated-letter and sequential filler UUIDs
Quoted CDP key name with sequential-hex filler UUIDs
Two distinct Coinbase API Key values in one file with context; the 85 tier needs two distinct tokens (one token, or the same token repeated, stays below 85)

should_not_match.description: Wrong path segment (keys instead of apiKeys)
Malformed org UUID (4 hex in first group instead of 8)

should_not_match.value: create a coinbase cdp api key under your organizations settings
should_not_match.description: Prose mention with the word organizations but no key-name value

false_positives.description: The literal word organizations followed by unrelated UUIDs (e.g. an unrelated resource path) could in principle resemble the structure.
false_positives.mitigation: The pattern requires the exact organizations/.../apiKeys/... two-UUID path; require corroborative Coinbase/credential keywords for the highest-precision alerting.

false_positives.description: Documentation or examples showing placeholder organizations/.../apiKeys/... strings.
false_positives.mitigation: Check for placeholder markers (example, 0000, xxxx) and require Coinbase context.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex identifies a Coinbase Developer Platform API key name in the organizations/{UUID}/apiKeys/{UUID} resource-path format, not the EC, ECDSA, or Ed25519 private signing key. Disclosure can reveal an organization and key identifier and help correlate other configuration, but it cannot mint the required JWT or authorize trading and fund access by itself. The affected Coinbase customer faces low, reversible confidentiality harm unless the associated private key or another bearer credential is also exposed. Risk 4 and OFFICIAL fit the standalone key name, while a name-private-key pair would require SENSITIVE treatment and broad financial authority could raise it further.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 supports QGISCF OFFICIAL, PSPF OFFICIAL, and the OFFICIAL DLM because the detected Coinbase resource path is a key identifier that requires the separate private signing key to authenticate. SENSITIVE is not met by the normal match because it cannot independently mint JWTs, access accounts, trade, or move funds.

generic.rationale: Low generic classification and Low DLM are appropriate for a standalone Coinbase API key name because direct misuse depends on the undisclosed private signing key and account context.

patterns.name: Credential Combolist / Stealer-Log Line
patterns.description: Detects credential combolist / infostealer-log lines: email:password pairs and host-or-url:user:pass triples, the format in which stolen credentials are aggregated and traded after info-stealer infections. These dumps fuel credential stuffing and account-takeover attacks. A lone email/password candidate is discovery-only; service-bound triples and multi-row dump structure support enforcement.
patterns.operation: Pattern_combolist_line recognizes a bounded email:password candidate or a host/URL:user:password record. The 65 tier inventories one line. The 75 tier requires either a service-bound host/URL triple or explicit combolist/stealer-log context around an email pair. patterns.name: Discord Bot Token
patterns.description: Detects Discord bot tokens: three dot-separated base64url segments where the first segment is the bot's numeric snowflake ID base64-encoded (always starting M, N, or O because it encodes an ASCII digit), the second is a 6-character timestamp, and the third is an HMAC of 27 to 38 characters. A leaked bot token grants full control of the bot account, including reading every channel the bot can see and sending messages as the bot.
patterns.operation: Structured triplet [MNO] + 23-27 base64url chars, dot, 6 chars, dot, 27-38 chars. Discord does not publish the format; the structure is multiply attested across the detector ecosystem -- TruffleHog (24.6.27), Kingfisher ([MNO]24.6.27), detect-secrets ([MNO]{23,25}.6.27), and community regex databases ([MNO]{23,25}.6.{27,38}) -- and derives from Discord's own client-side token parsing (the python-discord moderation bot's operationally-validated triplet, taken from discord-developers). Third-segment evidence split, disclosed honestly: the three production scanners all pin exactly 27, while a self-labeled-approximate community database extends to 38; no announcement or changelog documents an HMAC length change, so the 27-38 range is a recall-protective envelope over both attestations, not a documented format history. The first-segment range is bounded 24-28 total characters (attested 24-26 plus headroom for snowflake ID growth); the discontinued mfa.-prefixed user-token format (dead since May 2022) is out of scope. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the triplet structure is rigid (three exact-charset segments with tight length bounds and a structurally-derived [MNO] first character -- base64 of an ASCII digit always starts M, N, or O) and is independently attested by four detector ecosystems plus Discord's GitHub secret-scanning partnership (push protection enabled) and GitGuardian's prefixed high-recall detector. Kingfisher and GitHub's push protection fire on the bare shape in production, supporting a value-only discovery tier; TruffleHog label-gates the same regex as part of its standard PrefixRegex convention (no FP-motivated comment), the same divergence this corpus documents for other structurally-distinctive formats. The third-segment 27-38 range is a recall-protective envelope: 27 is pinned exactly by the production scanners, 38 comes only from a community regex database, and no vendor announcement documents a length change -- the envelope covers both attestations rather than asserting an unverified format timeline.

should_not_match.description: Third segment far too short (16 chars, below the 27-char floor)

should_not_match.description: Middle timestamp segment wrong length (10 chars, not 6)

false_positives.description: Three-part dotted base64url runs inside longer chains (for example JWT fragments or minified code) that happen to satisfy the segment lengths.
false_positives.mitigation: The rigid 6-character middle segment and [MNO] first character make coincidental matches rare; corroborative Discord keywords gate the recommended confidence tier, and boundary lookarounds reject runs glued into longer identifiers.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative Discord keywords and check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx).

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence pattern identifies a Discord bot token as three bounded base64url segments encoding the bot identity, timestamp component, and authentication HMAC. A live token lets an attacker operate as the bot, read channels visible to it, send messages, alter automated workflows, and abuse the bot's assigned permissions. The affected scale is the bot account and every server or channel it can access, with role permissions, token rotation, and moderation controls containing harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained collaboration-platform compromise, while a highly privileged bot spanning protected operational communities would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a Discord bot token is a complete bearer credential that can control the bot across its authorized channels. PROTECTED is not met because the normal token is limited by one bot's roles and does not establish broad privileged compromise or significant critical-service damage.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium InfoTech handling fit Discord bot tokens because they confer direct service control while bot permissions and community scope normally bound the harm.

patterns.name: Dogecoin Address
patterns.description: Detects Dogecoin mainnet addresses: Base58Check encoded, 34 characters long. Pay-to-Public-Key-Hash (P2PKH) addresses use version byte 0x1E and start with "D"; Pay-to-Script-Hash (P2SH) addresses use version byte 0x16 (22) and start with "A" (leading "9" is also possible for that version byte). A single leading letter is weak structure, so detection is context-gated. Prefix/version/length verified against libdogecoin and Dogecoin address-type docs.
patterns.operation: A leading D/A/9 plus a base58 body is discovery-only at 65. Explicit Dogecoin context enables 75 enforcement, while 85 additionally requires transfer-destination language. Template/sample text is excluded; the Base58Check checksum is not expressible in a Purview-safe regex.
patterns.confidence_justification: Gated 75, not high: a single leading D/A/9 plus a base58 run is weak structure with no regex-expressible checksum, so it collides with other similarly-prefixed base58 tokens (notably other coins' base58 addresses). Precision comes from the mandatory cryptocurrency/wallet domain-context gate plus the noise exclusion.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

patterns.name: DVA File Number
patterns.description: Detects Department of Veterans' Affairs (DVA) file numbers used to identify Australian veterans and eligible dependants for health and support services.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern using universal engine. The top-level regex \b[NVQSWATD][XKVGTASBM]?\s?\d{5,7}\b matches a state letter (N, V, Q, S, W, A, T, D) optionally followed by a card-type letter (X, K, V, G, T, A, S, B, M), an optional space, then 5-7 digits. The Purview engine uses Pattern_dva_file (same regex). Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires DVA-specific terms + card type keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires DVA-specific terms; Low (65) requires veteran context keywords. Evidence uses 3 keyword groups (7 DVA-specific terms, 9 card type terms, 10 veteran context terms) within 300-character proximity.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the constrained state-letter prefix and optional card-type letter provide moderate specificity. Corroborative keywords such as DVA, veteran, or defence service are recommended to reduce false positives from short alphanumeric codes.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

patterns.risk_description: The regex identifies a DVA file number built from a state prefix, optional card-type letter, and five to seven digits, with veteran or Department of Veterans' Affairs context used for corroboration. A valid number can link a veteran or eligible dependant to benefits, health, and support administration and can assist targeted enquiries or impersonation when paired with identity data. It does not by itself reveal service history, diagnosis, claim outcome, payment detail, or account access, and non-DVA reference codes can resemble the structure. classification.rationale: Risk 6 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because a DVA file number attributes a veteran-services relationship and can assist impersonation when paired with identity data. PROTECTED is not met because the number alone reveals no service history, diagnosis, claim outcome or account access.

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies the exact PEM header for an elliptic-curve private key, which is a marker that normally precedes key material rather than the cryptographic body itself. In a genuine key file, disclosure of the following private bytes can enable signing, impersonation, or decryption for the certificate or system bound to that key. The affected scale is one key pair and its relying service or identity, while header-only documentation, examples, and encrypted key bodies need separate validation. Risk 8 SENSITIVE is appropriate for the strong indication of a private key exposure; PROTECTED requires proof that the adjacent key is usable and controls critical, broad, or protected operations.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because an EC private-key header in a document commonly signals serious adjacent credential material. PROTECTED is not met by the header match alone because the detector does not verify the key body, encryption state, validity, usage, or operational criticality.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls for a private-key marker, requiring inspection of the surrounding PEM block and key revocation when confirmed. High is reserved for a validated usable key whose trust role or service scope could cause significant damage.

patterns.name: Electronic Mail Address
patterns.description: Identifies electronic mail addresses in local-part@domain.tld form using a pragmatic RFC 5322 / WHATWG HTML Living Standard subset: bounded local-part (64 characters, per RFC 5321) and domain-label quantifiers, not the full RFC 5322 address-list grammar (no quoted-string local parts, comments, or domain literals). Unlike the WHATWG "valid e-mail address" definition, a dotted domain ending in an alphabetic (or xn-- punycode) top-level label is required, so dotless intranet values such as user@localhost are deliberately excluded. Retina image asset names (logo@2x.png) are rejected in the primary. Absorbs the former global-email-address classifier.
patterns.operation: Validation: none (email addresses have no universal checksum). Reference: RFC 5322 section 3.4.1 (addr-spec), RFC 5321 section 4.5.3.1.1 (64-octet local-part limit), WHATWG HTML Living Standard "valid e-mail address". The bare address is discovery-only at 65, an explicit email or correspondence label enforces at 75, and a labelled address in an independent customer, contact-record, directory, account-holder, or communication record context reaches 85. Explicit templates and published public-contact context (public website, public directory, published contact, media enquiries, generic mailbox) are excluded from the enforcing tiers.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the bounded local-part@domain.tld structure with an alphabetic top-level label is distinctive to email addresses, and Retina asset names (logo@2x.png) are rejected in the primary. Residual collisions (package@1.2.build-style version tokens) stay at the discovery-only 65 tier unless an email label is present.

Medium-tier probe - email with an explicit correspondence label
High-tier probe - labelled email in an independent customer-record context

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex finds RFC-shaped electronic mail addresses with a valid multi-character top-level domain, rather than generic text containing an at sign. A genuine address can enable phishing, spam, account discovery, or unwanted contact against its mailbox owner, especially when the local part reveals a name or role. The address alone provides no mailbox content, password, token, or proof of a sensitive affiliation, and many business addresses are deliberately public. Risk 5 OFFICIAL reflects bounded direct contact risk; SENSITIVE would require authentication material, confidential correspondence, a protected identity, or a sensitive address roster.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 reconciles to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, the OFFICIAL DLM, OFFI, and Low tier because an email address enables contact but not mailbox access. generic.rationale: Generic Low and Low handling suit an email address that enables targeting and correlation but does not disclose mailbox contents or authentication material.

patterns.name: Employment/HR Sensitive Data
patterns.description: Detects sensitive employment case records about an identified worker: workplace investigations, disciplinary action and show cause notices, grievance and harassment complaints, workers compensation and return to work plans, termination and redundancy notices.
patterns.operation: Primary: an HR case phrase (disciplinary action, workplace investigation/bullying/misconduct, termination letter/notice, unfair dismissal, workers compensation, grievance or harassment complaint, return to work plan, redundancy notice, show cause notice, work capacity certificate). 75 tier requires a populated person field (employee/staff name or number, position number or title, work unit, worker, claimant, complainant, respondent or subject employee) with a non-placeholder value within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires a populated case detail (numbered allegation, incident/injury/termination date, claim/case/matter number, substantiated/upheld finding, or suitable duties from a date) and an independent corroborative term (witness, medical certificate, procedural fairness, support person, natural justice). All tiers exclude template/fixture text (template-exclusion); enforce tiers also exclude guidance, policy, training and media-release framing. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface policies, guidance, blank forms and statistics.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases also appear in policies, guidance, blank forms and news, so enforce tiers require a populated person field and 85 adds a record-specific populated detail plus independent corroboration. Person values are customer-defined (employee IDs, position numbers), so the field regexes use labelled loose values with a placeholder guard. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

patterns.risk_description: The pattern recognizes a Google API key beginning with AIza and the fixed 35-character suffix, making the match an API credential bound to a Google Cloud project or service configuration. An unrestricted live key can be used to consume enabled APIs, incur quota or billing, and in some configurations access project data exposed to key authentication. The direct scale is one key and its configured API restrictions, with application restrictions, disabled keys, examples, and unrelated test material limiting actual harm. Risk 8 SENSITIVE is retained for serious contained abuse of an active unrestricted key; PROTECTED would require demonstrated broad privileged access or significant protected-resource impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Google API key can authorize billable or data-bearing API activity within its configured project scope. PROTECTED is not met because the detector does not establish validity, API enablement, restrictions, privilege level, or critical data access.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls because Google API keys should be restricted, monitored, and rotated after unintended disclosure. High classification requires evidence that the key bypasses effective restrictions and enables significant compromise rather than ordinary bounded API usage.

patterns.risk_description: This broad regex captures a value of six or more non-space characters assigned to labels such as password, passwd, pwd, or pass. generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling reflects serious source and CI access within one account's authority. High handling requires administrator scope or demonstrated major downstream compromise.

patterns.name: Geographic Coordinates (Decimal Degrees, DMS, MGRS)
patterns.description: Detects geographic coordinates as a decimal-degree latitude/longitude pair (e.g. -33.8688, 151.2093), as a degrees-minutes-seconds (DMS) value with a hemisphere letter (e.g. 40° 26' 46" N), or as a Military Grid Reference System (MGRS) reference (e.g. 4QFJ 12345 67890). The slug predates the DMS and MGRS scope, which was absorbed from the former global-gps-coordinates-dms classifier.
patterns.operation: Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_coordinate_conversion. Decimal pairs are bounded to latitude -90..90 and longitude -180..180 with at least four decimal places. DMS values use hemisphere-bounded ranges (N/S 0-90, E/W 0-180, minutes/seconds 0-59, zero subdivisions at the 90/180 endpoints) with degree/minute/second marks and a hemisphere letter. Decimal and DMS primaries share the same tiers: 65 discovery-only, 75 with geolocation context, 85 with an explicit coordinate label plus an operational location-record term. MGRS references (grid zone + 100 km square + easting/northing) collide more easily with part numbers, so their 75/85 tiers require coordinate-system notation (MGRS, grid reference, latitude, longitude, coordinate) rather than generic location words. Template and public-map context are excluded from all tiers.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the decimal and DMS shapes are geographically bounded and the DMS form requires degree/minute/second marks and a hemisphere letter, but bare numbers can still be non-location data and the MGRS shape can collide with part numbers. Enforcing tiers require location context, and MGRS enforcement requires explicit coordinate-system notation.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords within the proximity window to confirm sensitive data context rather than general discussion.

false_positives.description: In English (as the primary international business language), similar terminology used in formal or administrative contexts (education, professional documentation) that does not constitute sensitive data collection.
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with additional contextual signals such as structured identifiers, form fields, or database column headers to distinguish sensitive records from general references.

false_positives.mitigation: MGRS enforcement tiers require coordinate-system notation (MGRS, grid reference, latitude, longitude, coordinate) rather than generic location words.

false_positives.description: Temperature or angle values written with a degree mark but no minutes/seconds or hemisphere.
false_positives.mitigation: The DMS primary requires minutes, seconds and a hemisphere letter, excluding bare degree values.

patterns.risk_description: The rule detects one geographic point written as a decimal-degree latitude/longitude pair, a degrees-minutes-seconds value, or an MGRS grid reference. The coordinate can aid surveillance or targeting only when it is current and linked to a person, protected facility, or sensitive activity. A normal isolated point may describe a public place, map example, survey location, or asset with no confidential association. Risk 4 OFFICIAL reflects low standalone harm; SENSITIVE requires attributable movement, protected-site, or operational context.

classification.rationale: An unattributed geographic point has low, reversible impact and fits risk 4 OFFICIAL. SENSITIVE is not met because the detector establishes neither a subject, current movement, nor a protected location.

generic.rationale: Low generic handling is appropriate for public geographic coordinates that become sensitive only through identity, time, or protected-asset linkage.

MGRS reference with explicit coordinate-system notation

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence detector finds a GroqCloud API credential through the distinctive gsk_ prefix and a bounded alphanumeric body. A live key can authorize billed inference, consume account quota, and expose prompts, outputs, or application data sent through the associated Groq project. The affected scale is one API account or project, with quota, permissions, monitoring, and rotation limiting damage. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained service and information exposure, while a shared production key carrying protected workloads across many systems would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 supports QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Groq key directly enables unauthorized billed API use within a material project. PROTECTED is not met because the detector does not establish broad privileged reach, protected prompt data, or significant compromise of a critical service.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification with Medium InfoTech handling suits Groq keys because they grant direct project access while quotas, project scope, and revocation contain the outcome.

patterns.name: Guarantor Agreement
patterns.description: Detects populated guarantee and indemnity instruments (personal/corporate/continuing guarantees, deeds of guarantee, guarantor agreements) that name the guarantor or borrower, state a guaranteed amount or limit, or carry an ABN/ACN. Phrase-only mentions stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: keyword proximity evaluated through purview tiers. Primary: personal/corporate/unlimited/limited/continuing guarantee, guarantee agreement/deed, deed of guarantee, guarantor agreement/undertaking. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated field - named guarantor/borrower/debtor/lender/creditor, guaranteed amount/guarantee limit/limit of liability/loan amount with a dollar value (ranges excluded), or an ABN/ACN. 85: primary plus two distinct field types (the three above or a labelled deed/execution date) plus guarantee-obligation evidence (indemnity, joint and several, secured obligations, payment on demand, continuing security, independent legal advice, principal debtor). Template/sample and guidance/marketing framing excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers require populated party, amount or company-number fields beside the guarantee phrase; product guarantees, marketing and consumer guidance stay at 65. Medium because credit-application correspondence can carry the same fields.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

patterns.risk_description: This concept classifier identifies guarantor agreements and deeds containing a named guarantor, personal guarantee, indemnity, joint liability, secured obligation, and continuing or unlimited exposure. Disclosure can reveal an individual's contingent debts, assets at risk, relationships, and negotiation pressure points, enabling fraud, coercion, or targeted financial exploitation. The guarantor, borrower, lender, and related household may face serious personal, legal, and financial harm within one facility, while enforcement still requires a valid underlying obligation and legal process. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Legal fit that composite commitment, while a broad portfolio of guarantees or privileged lending-system access would be needed for PROTECTED. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated record structure (labelled fields with real values, identifiers or data rows); phrase-only mentions in guidance, marketing, blank forms and news stay at 65 discovery.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 supports PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Legal and Medium because a populated guarantee names the guarantor, the guaranteed amount and contingent liabilities, exposing assets at risk and pressure points for coercion. PROTECTED is not met because the exposure is bounded to one facility and enforcement still needs legal process.

generic.rationale: Medium Legal handling protects a named guarantor's contingent debt and household exposure. A portfolio of guarantees would warrant more.

patterns.description: Detects HashiCorp Vault service tokens (hvs. prefix) and batch tokens (hvb. prefix). These tokens authenticate to a Vault server and can read secrets, keys and credentials. patterns.risk_description: This detector matches HashiCorp Vault service or batch tokens with the hvs or hvb prefix and a long constrained body. A live token can read the secrets, keys, certificates, and credentials allowed by its Vault policy, enabling further access and lateral movement. The normal unit is one policy-scoped token whose permissions may be narrow or broad, so serious harm is clear without assuming enterprise-wide compromise. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE InfoTech fit direct policy-bound secret access; PROTECTED requires a root-like policy, a broad credential cascade, or significant impact on critical protected operations.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps coherently to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, and SENS_IT because a Vault token directly exposes policy-authorised secrets. PROTECTED is not met because token policy and resulting blast radius are not known from the identifier alone.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling fits direct access to a bounded set of Vault secrets. High handling requires a verified root-like policy, broad credential cascade, or protected operational impact.

false_positives.description: Medical terminology in health education materials, research publications, clinical guidelines, or public health documents without patient-specific data.
