patterns.name: PuTTY Private Key (PPK)
patterns.description: Detects the header line of a PuTTY private key file (.ppk), as produced by PuTTYgen. The header begins with 'PuTTY-User-Key-File-' followed by the format version (2 or 3) and the SSH key algorithm. A leaked .ppk grants SSH access to whatever hosts trust the corresponding public key. Header-only candidates are discovery-only; ordered PPK metadata and the first public-blob line support enforcement.
patterns.operation: The 65 tier matches a version 2/3 PPK marker. The 75 tier requires a supported SSH algorithm followed by the normal Encryption, Comment, and non-zero Public-Lines fields. The 85 tier additionally requires the first Base64 public blob line. These fields occur at the start of normal PPK files, so enforcement does not depend on Private-Lines or Private-MAC after a long public section.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the 'PuTTY-User-Key-File-' prefix with a version digit and colon is a fixed, distinctive marker of a private key file and almost never appears outside of an actual .ppk file.

patterns.risk_description: This high-confidence detector matches a PuTTY PPK version 2 or 3 header and supported SSH key algorithm rather than a generic key reference. When the private body follows, the file can authenticate to hosts that trust the corresponding public key, enabling account access, persistence, and lateral movement. The normal unit is one key whose trusted hosts and passphrase protection are unknown, so the harm is serious but not automatically infrastructure-wide. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE InfoTech fit a genuine PPK with an unknown trust scope; PROTECTED requires confirmed privileged trust across critical systems or comparably significant compromise.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, and SENS_IT for a genuine SSH private key file. PROTECTED is not met because trusted-host count, privilege, encryption, and operational criticality are not established by the header.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling fits direct SSH authentication within one key's unknown trust scope. High handling requires evidence of widespread privileged trust or critical-system access.

patterns.name: Racial or Ethnic Origin
patterns.description: Detects racial or ethnic origin information in person-linked demographic, workforce, intake, census, application, and case records. The detector recognises explicit racial/ethnic-origin phrases and structured race or ethnicity fields, then raises confidence only when the same span contains a data-subject record and a populated attribution. Racial or ethnic origin is protected under GDPR Article 9 and Australian anti-discrimination and privacy law. Topic-grade detector, low confidence by design.
patterns.operation: The primary regex matches explicit racial/ethnic-origin phrases and structured race or ethnicity fields. 65 (discovery only): phrase alone - policy, guidance, news and survey-design text naming the category stays here. 75: phrase plus a populated identified-person field (name, DOB, employee/member/customer/patient/participant number or ID, data subject). 85: person field plus a second populated demographic field (country of birth, ancestry, cultural background, language spoken at home, interpreter required, Indigenous status) plus independent record evidence (self-described, selected category, diversity survey response, intake interview, equal employment opportunity data). Template framing and guidance/policy/public-aggregate framing are excluded from 75/85. Converted from keyword_list to regex so the tier logic decides matches.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low by design: the attribute has no fixed format. Enforce tiers now require the attribute to be tied to an identified person record (a populated name/DOB/ID field), and 85 also requires a second populated demographic field plus independent record evidence, so policy text, surveys-in-design and news naming the category stay at 65 discovery.

Disclosure can enable discrimination, profiling, harassment, or exclusion, while the normal single-person record does not by itself establish the scale or severe consequence required for PROTECTED. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy are appropriate.

The topic-only 65 branch is discovery-only. PROTECTED is not met by the normal individual record without bulk exposure, a credible severe threat, or significant damage.

generic.rationale: A confirmed person-linked racial or ethnic origin record is generically Medium Personal-Privacy because disclosure can enable discrimination, profiling, harassment, or exclusion. High handling requires a high-consequence population register, coercive targeting, or comparable severe harm.

A red-team / purple-team / adversary-simulation / threat-emulation title is discovery-only; enforcement requires attack-technique, ATT&CK technique ID, offensive-tool, or populated finding-record evidence, and high confidence requires a populated finding record (finding ID, severity, affected host) plus independent attack-path/TTP evidence.

The 85 tier requires a populated finding field plus an independent attack-technique phrase (attack path, initial access, lateral movement, persistence, exfiltration, C2), ATT&CK ID, or offensive-tool hit. Enforcing tiers reject templates and examples.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling protects demonstrated attack paths and blind spots until remediated. It is not High unless the findings show enterprise-wide administrative control.

false_positives.description: Authentication-related terminology in software documentation, security training materials, or system architecture descriptions without actual credentials.
false_positives.mitigation: Require proximity to credential-specific patterns (API keys, connection strings, tokens) rather than general security terminology.

false_positives.description: Code snippets and configuration examples containing credential-related keywords or placeholder values in developer documentation.

patterns.risk_description: This detector captures a redis URI with password, host, and port, reflecting Redis deployments where password-only authentication may be sufficient. A person with network reach can use a live value to read or modify cached data, sessions, queues, or configuration permitted by that Redis account. The usual impact is one cache or datastore instance and its dependent applications, while inaccessible internal hosts, test services, examples, and rotated passwords reduce harm. Risk 8 SENSITIVE is retained for serious application and data compromise; PROTECTED requires evidence of critical shared infrastructure or significant protected content.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because the Redis URI can contain the complete password-based access path to one service. PROTECTED is not met because reachability, validity, ACL privileges, persistence, instance sharing, and data criticality are unverified.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls because exposed Redis passwords can compromise application state and should be rotated promptly. High depends on proof that the instance is broadly shared, privileged, or critical rather than assumed from one connection string.

patterns.name: Religious or Philosophical Beliefs
patterns.description: Detects religious or philosophical belief information in person-linked membership, patient, workforce, census, pastoral-care, and accommodation records. The detector recognises explicit belief, affiliation, observance, denomination, and structured religion-field terminology, then raises confidence only for person records and populated belief or accommodation statements. Religious or philosophical beliefs are protected under GDPR Article 9 and Australian anti-discrimination and privacy law. Topic-grade detector, low confidence by design.
patterns.operation: The primary regex matches explicit religious/philosophical-belief phrases and structured religion, faith or denomination labels. 65 (discovery only): phrase alone - policy, guidance, news and survey-design text naming the category stays here. 75: phrase plus a populated identified-person field (name, DOB, employee/member/customer/patient/participant number or ID, data subject). 85: person field plus a named religion or denomination value (Catholic, Anglican, Muslim, Hindu, Sikh, Jewish, Buddhist, no religion ...) plus independent record evidence (chaplaincy, pastoral care, congregation, prayer, halal/kosher, Sabbath, Ramadan, religious leave). Template framing and guidance/policy/public-aggregate framing are excluded from 75/85. Converted from keyword_list to regex so the tier logic decides matches.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low by design: the attribute has no fixed format. Enforce tiers now require the attribute to be tied to an identified person record (a populated name/DOB/ID field), and 85 also requires a named religion or denomination value plus independent record evidence, so policy text, surveys-in-design and news naming the category stay at 65 discovery.

patterns.risk_description: A true positive attributes a religious or philosophical belief, affiliation, observance, or accommodation need to a person. Disclosure can enable discrimination, coercion, exclusion, harassment, or safety harm where minority status carries legal or social risk. The normal single-person record does not by itself establish the scale or severe consequence required for PROTECTED. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy are appropriate.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy because the enforcing tiers require explicit religious or philosophical belief terminology in a person-linked record; the 85 tier also requires a populated belief, denomination, observance, conversion, or accommodation statement. The topic-only 65 branch is discovery-only. PROTECTED is not met without a protected population, credible severe threat, or significant damage.

generic.rationale: A confirmed person-linked belief, affiliation, observance, or religious accommodation record is generically Medium Personal-Privacy because disclosure can enable discrimination, coercion, exclusion, harassment, or safety harm. High handling requires a severe threat or broad high-consequence holding.

patterns.name: Replicate API Key
patterns.description: Detects Replicate API tokens, which use a distinctive r8_ prefix followed by a fixed-length body of alphanumerics, underscores, and hyphens. A leaked token grants unauthorized, billed access to Replicate's hosted model inference API and any prompts, images, or data routed through it.
patterns.operation: A broad r8_ candidate is retained at 65 for discovery. The 75 tier requires the documented 37-character [0-9A-Za-z_-] body and rejects explicit template context. The 85 tier additionally requires a Replicate label or endpoint nearby. Replicate documents the 40-character total length, and TruffleHog corroborates the body charset.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the r8_ prefix and exact 40-character total token length are explicitly documented on Replicate's own security/API-tokens page, the body charset ([0-9A-Za-z_-]) is confirmed by TruffleHog's production detector, and Replicate is a confirmed GitHub secret-scanning partner. The exact format enforces at medium confidence; an explicit Replicate label is required for the maximum-rejection high tier.

should_match.description: Low-tier probe - plausible prefixed candidate with a noncanonical body length
Medium-tier probe - exact Replicate token structure without nearby vendor context
High-tier probe - exact token with an unambiguous Replicate label
Replicate brand mention followed by a token value
Token body containing underscores and hyphens (full documented charset)

should_not_match.value: r9_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijk
should_not_match.description: Wrong prefix (r9_ instead of r8_)

should_not_match.value: r8_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghij
should_not_match.description: Body too short (36 chars, below the fixed 37-char length)

should_not_match.value: remember to rotate the replicate api token before deploying
should_not_match.description: Prose mention without a token value

should_not_match.value: Documentation example: REPLICATE_API_TOKEN=r8_zZyYxXwWvVuUtTsSrRqQpPoOnNmMlLkKjJiIh
should_not_match.description: Exact but explicitly documented example must not enforce

false_positives.description: Documentation or examples showing placeholder r8_ strings.
false_positives.mitigation: Suppress explicit template/example framing; treat an exact bare token as medium and require an unambiguous Replicate label for high confidence.

false_positives.description: The common English verb "replicate" (e.g. "replicate this dataset") appearing in text near an unrelated token or hash of similar length.
false_positives.mitigation: The brand-name keyword term is case-sensitive (Replicate, capitalised) and additional unambiguous terms (replicate.com, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN) disambiguate from the generic verb.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence pattern identifies a Replicate API token through the distinctive r8_ prefix and exact 37-character body. A live token can authorize billed model execution and expose prompts, images, outputs, or other data submitted through the associated Replicate account or project. The affected scale is one account or workflow, with quota, project access, monitoring, and revocation limiting harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained AI-service exposure, while a shared production token carrying protected data across many systems would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 supports QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Replicate token directly enables unauthorized billed inference and access to a material workflow. PROTECTED is not met because the normal token is bounded to one account or project and does not establish protected content or broad critical-service compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification with Medium InfoTech handling suits Replicate tokens because they grant direct workflow access while quota, project scope, and rotation contain the outcome.

patterns.name: Reproductive & Sexual Health Data
patterns.description: Detects references to reproductive and sexual-health data: pregnancy, abortion, contraception, fertility treatment, gender-affirming care and STI/HIV status. Washington's My Health My Data Act (and a wave of post-Dobbs state consumer-health-data laws) treat this as protected consumer health data. Topic-grade vocabulary detector.
patterns.operation: The primary regex matches reproductive and sexual-health vocabulary (pregnancy, abortion, miscarriage, contraception, fertility treatment/IVF, mifepristone/misoprostol, emergency contraception, gender-affirming care, hormone therapy, STI/HIV status, prenatal care, postpartum). 65 (discovery only): term alone - policy, guidance, news and figurative uses stay here. 75: term plus a populated patient identifier field (name, DOB, URN/MRN, Medicare, patient number). 85: patient field plus a populated clinical field (gestation, EDD, LMP, gravida/parity, procedure, medication, diagnosis, test result, contraceptive method, cycle day, embryos transferred) plus independent clinical evidence (obstetrician, gynaecologist, midwife, ultrasound, beta hCG, antenatal, sexual health clinic, embryo transfer). Template and guidance/training framing excluded from 75/85. Converted from keyword_list to regex so the tier logic decides matches.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low by design: the vocabulary is common in policy, news and figurative prose. Enforce tiers now require a populated patient identifier, and 85 also requires a clinical field and independent clinical evidence.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative clinical keywords (patient, clinic, diagnosis, provider, record) within the proximity window; treat isolated colloquial hits as low confidence.

patterns.risk_description: The low-confidence detector finds reproductive and sexual-health terms (pregnancy, contraception, abortion medicines, fertility treatment, gender-affirming care, STI or HIV status) and enforces only when they sit with a populated patient identifier. When linked to a person, such material can expose intimate care choices and create stigma, discrimination, family conflict, or legal targeting. Isolated terms also appear in legislation, public-health guidance, agricultural fertility discussion, marketing, and colloquial uses, so identity and clinical context are material to the harm. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE preserve protection for real consumer-health data, while risk 8 or PROTECTED requires a named patient, diagnosis or treatment record, reproductive case file, bulk holding, or severe safety context.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, Personal-Privacy DLM, and Medium because identifiable reproductive or sexual-health information has credible direct personal consequences. Risk 8 and PROTECTED are not inherent in an unlinked topic term without patient, clinical, legal, or safety context.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium Personal-Privacy appropriately protect identifiable reproductive and sexual-health content while recognising topic-only alerts need corroboration. High handling is reserved for consequential records, aggregation, or acute safety exposure.

patterns.name: Residential Tenancy Agreement
patterns.description: Detects populated residential tenancy agreements (including Queensland Form 18a general tenancy agreements): the tenancy-agreement phrase combined with named tenant/lessor fields, a numbered premises address, a stated rent or bond amount, or a bond number. Phrase-only mentions stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: keyword proximity evaluated through purview tiers. Primary: residential tenancy agreement/act, Residential Tenancies Authority, (general) tenancy agreement, Form 18a, standard tenancy/rental agreement, lease agreement. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated field - named tenant/lessor/landlord/property manager, a numbered premises/property address, rent with a dollar value, or bond amount / bond number. 85: primary plus two distinct field types (the four above or a start/end date) plus tenancy-process evidence (entry condition report, breach notice, notice to vacate/leave, periodic/fixed term agreement, bond lodgement, RTA, routine inspection). Template/sample and guidance/news framing excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers require populated party, premises, rent or bond fields beside the tenancy phrase; renting guides, RTA fact sheets, rent statistics and blank Form 18a copies stay at 65. Medium because property-management correspondence can carry the same fields.

patterns.risk_description: The pattern identifies residential tenancy agreements containing named parties, premises, rent, bond, condition reports, authority notices, entry rights, and breach terms. Disclosure can expose a person's home address, occupancy, financial obligations, property condition, and dispute history, enabling privacy intrusion, targeted scams, or pressure in a tenancy dispute. The tenant, household, landlord, and agent may face moderate legal, personal, and financial harm within one lease, while the agreement does not itself authorize entry or payment. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Legal fit a populated agreement, while a bulk tenancy register, severe safety context, or privileged housing-system access would be needed for PROTECTED. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated record structure (labelled fields with real values, identifiers or data rows); phrase-only mentions in guidance, marketing, blank forms and news stay at 65 discovery.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Legal and Medium for a populated lease tying a tenant to a home address, rent, bond and dispute history, which enables scams or pressure in a tenancy dispute. PROTECTED is not met without a bulk tenancy register, severe safety context or privileged housing-system access.

generic.rationale: Medium Legal handling protects one lease's parties, premises and financial obligations. It is not High because harm stays within a single tenancy and the agreement does not itself authorise entry or payment.

patterns.name: Risk Register
patterns.description: Identifies populated risk registers, risk matrices and enterprise risk reports: risk IDs, rated likelihood/consequence/residual values and named risk owners. Titles alone are discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Regex_risk_register (risk register, risk (assessment) matrix, risk heat map, enterprise risk (management) report, KRI dashboard/report) is discovery-only at 65. 75 requires one populated structure: a labelled risk ID, a likelihood/consequence/inherent/residual rating with a value, or a named risk/treatment/control owner. 85 requires two distinct structures plus treatment/control wording. Enforcing tiers reject template/fixture wording (shared template-exclusion dictionary) and guidance, policy, training and news framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: titles are discovery-only; enforcement requires risk IDs, rated values or named owners, and 85 adds a second structure and treatment context.

patterns.risk_description: The concept pattern identifies risk registers and treatment records containing likelihood, consequence, inherent or residual ratings, owners, tolerances, and mitigation plans rather than generic discussion of risk. A substantive register can expose known vulnerabilities, control gaps, accepted residual risks, accountable teams, and remediation priorities that an attacker, competitor, or litigant could exploit. The affected scale may span several business functions, but an ordinary organisational register still produces serious contained harm rather than automatic critical-service compromise. Risk 8 SENSITIVE Government is appropriate; PROTECTED is not met without critical-infrastructure weaknesses, protected operations, or credible significant damage at strategic or system scale.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 fits PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Government because a populated register lists known risks, residual ratings, owners and treatment gaps that an attacker, competitor or litigant could prioritise against. PROTECTED is not met for an ordinary organisational register without critical-infrastructure weaknesses or strategic-scale consequences.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling protects rated risks, accepted residual exposure and treatment plans. It is not High unless the register maps critical-service weaknesses.

patterns.name: RSA Private Key Header
patterns.description: Detects PKCS#1 RSA private-key armor. A BEGIN line is discovery-only, the first DER-like Base64 line supports medium confidence, and several normally wrapped body lines near the header support high confidence.
patterns.operation: Regex_rsa_private matches the PKCS#1 BEGIN marker. The 75 tier requires a plausible first DER Base64 line beginning MII. The 85 tier additionally requires three consecutive 64-character armor lines, all within 300 characters of the header. It therefore classifies normal full keys without relying on a distant END marker. Header-only candidates remain discovery-only at 65.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: structurally constrained pattern with corroborative keyword support reduces false positive rates significantly. Added context gating and exclusion rules improve precision and reduce incidental matches.

Medium-tier probe - realistic first PKCS#1 DER armor line

false_positives.description: PEM-encoded certificates or public keys that use similar header formats
false_positives.mitigation: The pattern specifically matches the private key header text, but verify the full PEM block contains actual key material.

patterns.risk_description: The pattern identifies the exact PEM header for an RSA private key, a strong format marker that does not by itself include or validate the following key bytes. If a usable RSA key follows, disclosure can enable signing, TLS or account impersonation, or decryption according to how the key is deployed. The normal affected scale is one key and its relying certificate, host, or application, while documentation, incomplete blocks, passphrase protection, and revocation constrain misuse. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious potential from confirmed adjacent key material; PROTECTED requires evidence of a broad trust anchor, critical service, or other significant operational consequence.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because an RSA private-key marker commonly indicates credential material capable of serious impersonation. PROTECTED is not met by the header alone because key body, usability, passphrase state, trust role, deployment breadth, and criticality are unknown.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls for an RSA private-key marker, requiring full-block confirmation and key replacement when valid. High is reserved for verified keys serving broad signing, certificate-authority, or critical administrative roles.

patterns.name: RubyGems API Key
patterns.description: Detects RubyGems.org API keys (rubygems_ prefix), used to push gems. A leaked key lets an attacker publish or yank gems under the owner's account.
patterns.operation: Prefixed token format rubygems_ followed by 48 hex characters. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the rubygems_ prefix with a fixed 48-character hexadecimal body is highly specific to RubyGems.org API keys.

should_match.description: Exact 65 probe - prefixed hexadecimal key without independent gem context
Exact 75 probe - key with RubyGems publish context
Exact 85 probe - RubyGems.org context plus canonical key assignment

should_not_match.value: rubygems_abcdef0123456789abcdef
should_not_match.description: Too short to be a valid RubyGems key

should_not_match.value: rubygems_ghijkl0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
should_not_match.description: Non-hex characters in body (g-l are not hex)

should_not_match.value: NPM_TOKEN=rubygems_abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
should_not_match.description: Sibling package-registry label does not corroborate a RubyGems key

should_not_match.value: Documentation example: RubyGems.org package RUBYGEMS_API_KEY=rubygems_abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
should_not_match.description: Documentation example containing a valid-shaped key is excluded

should_not_match.value: run gem push after setting your rubygems.org api key
should_not_match.description: Prose mention without a token value

false_positives.description: Documentation or examples showing placeholder rubygems_ strings.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative keywords and check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx).

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies a RubyGems API key by its rubygems_ prefix and fixed 48-character hexadecimal body, with nearby credential context used as corroboration. A live key can let an attacker publish malicious gem versions, yank legitimate releases, or inspect resources permitted by the key scope, creating direct account and software-supply-chain harm. The normal unit is one revocable repository credential, and documentation placeholders or deliberately masked examples can produce non-actionable matches. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious but bounded misuse of the affected RubyGems account; PROTECTED would require evidence of unusually broad package ownership, major downstream impact, or another path to significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, SENS_IT, and the Medium tier because a valid RubyGems key provides immediately usable publishing authority but is normally scoped to one account and can be revoked. The structured token alone does not establish the widespread supply-chain consequences or significant organisational damage needed for PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium InfoTech handling is appropriate for a service credential whose unauthorised use can materially affect package integrity within its granted scope. Generic High is not inherent because the detector does not show tenant-wide privilege, irreplaceable key material, or realised large-scale compromise.

patterns.name: SCADA/ICS System Documentation and Network Diagrams
patterns.description: Identifies substantive SCADA and industrial-control-system documentation, including SCADA/ICS/OT network diagrams and topologies. Topic phrases are retained for discovery; enforcement requires point, tag, I/O, alarm, HMI, RTU, protocol-map, polling, or control-logic configuration content, or OT network-diagram structure (IP schema / addressing tables, PLC/RTU lists, Purdue levels, zones and conduits, control zones, trust boundaries, field networks), and high confidence also requires a populated asset, node, address, subnet, VLAN, register, or outstation detail.
patterns.operation: Regex_scada_ics_documentation recognises SCADA/ICS system, configuration, network, and architecture documentation topics and SCADA/ICS/OT/control-system network diagram and topology topics. The topic alone is discovery-only at 65. Concrete configuration content (Evidence_scada_configuration_content) or OT network-diagram structure (Evidence_ot_network_structure) raises it to 75; either of those plus a populated PLC/RTU/HMI/DCS node, IPv4 address or subnet, VLAN number, Modbus register, or DNP3 outstation (Evidence_scada_live_detail) reaches 85. Enforcing tiers reject explicit templates and training examples.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence requires substantive control-system configuration content or OT network-diagram structure. High confidence adds a deployable asset, node, address, subnet, VLAN, protocol register, or outstation value.

false_positives.description: Vendor manuals, standards, and engineering courses discuss SCADA, PLCs, HMIs, RTUs, and OT protocols without exposing a live system configuration.
false_positives.mitigation: Keep document topics discovery-only and require point, tag, I/O, alarm, HMI, RTU, polling, protocol-map, or control-logic content for enforcement.

false_positives.description: Training labs can include realistic asset IDs, IP addresses, register numbers, tags, and node names.
false_positives.mitigation: Reject explicit template, demo, tutorial, sample-data, and training-example framing from enforcing tiers.

false_positives.description: Vendor reference architectures, IEC 62443 and Purdue-model courseware, and OT security standards describe zones and conduits, Purdue levels, DMZs, and remote sites without exposing a live topology.
false_positives.mitigation: Diagram structure alone reaches 75 only alongside a SCADA/ICS/OT network-diagram topic; 85 additionally requires a populated node, address, subnet, VLAN, register, or outstation value, and template/training framing is excluded.

patterns.risk_description: This TestPattern identifies SCADA and industrial-control documentation through control-system names, PLC or HMI terms, and OT protocol evidence. An attacker could apply the documented architecture or configuration to manipulate field devices, evade safeguards, or disrupt physical processes. The composite record may affect the operator, essential-service customers, assets, and public safety rather than a single technical identifier. Risk 10 and PROTECTED InfoTech are justified, and no higher QGISCF tier exists.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to PSPF and QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED InfoTech and High because populated SCADA configuration, PLC/RTU lists, addressing and Purdue-zone diagrams let an attacker manipulate field devices or evade safeguards. The consequence extends to essential services and public safety, meeting significant damage; no higher QGISCF tier exists.

generic.rationale: High with High InfoTech handling applies to detailed OT architecture and configuration that enables physical-process attacks.

patterns.name: SCADA Point List / Register Map
patterns.description: SCADA and telemetry point lists and register maps for a live system: Modbus register maps (rows pairing an address with a holding register, input register, coil or discrete input type, plus function codes), DNP3 Device Profile XML data-point lists (binaryInputPoints / analogInputPoints with populated index and name), and OPC UA NodeId lists (ns=n;i= / s= / g= / b= identifiers). Enforcement requires repetition of the row or point structure so tutorials and specifications that show one or two examples do not fire.
patterns.operation: Proximity 1000 characters. Modbus - 85: a register row (address + register type, either order) repeated at least 10 times with distinct values + a function-code value (FC03, function code 16, 0x10...) + site evidence (IPv4 address or an RTU / outstation / slave ID / unit ID / pump station / substation term); 75: register row repeated at least 5 times + a function code or a register-map heading (Register Address, Register Type, Modbus Address, Slave ID, Unit ID). DNP3 - 85: a DNP3 point-section element (binaryInputPoints, analogInputPoints...) + at least 5 distinct populated points (index + non-spare name) + analog scaling (scaleFactor or units) + site evidence; 75: point section + at least 3 distinct populated points. OPC UA - 85: at least 10 distinct NodeIds + an opc.tcp:// endpoint + site evidence; 75: at least 10 distinct NodeIds. 65 (discovery-only): a register-map / point-list phrase, the DNP3 Device Profile root or namespace, a point section, a single register row or NodeId. All enforce tiers exclude template/noise text and protocol specification framing (Modbus Application Protocol, OPC 10000-6).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the DNP3 Device Profile XML elements and OPC UA NodeId grammar are verified machine formats, but register rows and NodeIds are short shapes that tutorials and SDK docs also show, so enforce tiers depend on repetition (min_count with unique results) and 85 adds a distinct structure plus site evidence. The 4xxxx/3xxxx Modicon notation is a convention, not the Modbus specification, so it is not relied on. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

false_positives.mitigation: Enforce tiers need repeated distinct rows or NodeIds (min_count 5 or 10 with unique results); specification titles and tutorial / template wording are excluded.

patterns.risk_description: A populated point list or register map is the address book of a control system: which register or point index reads or writes each pump, breaker, valve, setpoint and alarm at a named site, often with the RTU address or endpoint. With network access, an attacker can use it to issue writes (setpoints, coil commands, breaker operations) to the right addresses without reverse engineering, with consequences for supply and safety. Point lists for critical infrastructure assets can be SOCI protected information. Specifications, tutorials, templates and marketing are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 9 supports PROTECTED InfoTech because one list tells an attacker which address to write.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 maps to PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED InfoTech (PROT_IT) and the High tier because a populated register map or point list tells an attacker which address writes each pump, breaker, valve or setpoint at a named site, removing the reverse-engineering step. Network access is still needed to act on it, as it is for distributed control system configurations and SCADA documentation, which are PROTECTED InfoTech at risk 9 and 10. Specifications, tutorials, templates and marketing stay out of enforce tiers.

generic.rationale: High InfoTech handling applies because a site-specific point list is the address book for control-system writes. Access should be limited to the operators, engineers and integrators responsible for that site.

patterns.name: Security Audit Report
patterns.description: Detects populated security audit and assurance reports (SOC 2 Type I/II, ISO/IEC 27001 audits, SSAE 18, IRAP and security control assessments) that carry finding/exception references, severity ratings, technical evidence (hosts, IPs, CVEs) or audit scope details. Phrase-only mentions stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex. Primary: SOC 2 Type I/II (report), ISO/IEC 27001 audit/assessment, SSAE 18, (information/cyber) security audit/control report or assessment, IRAP assessment. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated structure - finding/exception/nonconformity reference with a digit, rating/severity value, technical evidence (IPv4, CVE ID, internal hostname, host/asset ID field), or audit scope field (audited entity, service organisation, audit period, report date, lead auditor). 85: primary plus two distinct structures (the four above or a control reference such as A.8.2, CC6.1, ISM-1234) plus assurance evidence (control objective/activity, trust services criteria, Statement of Applicability, exception noted, qualified opinion, operating effectiveness, CUECs, nonconformity). Template/sample and guidance framing excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers require populated finding, rating, technical or scope fields beside the audit-report phrase; vendor assurance pages, SOC 2 explainers and certification news stay at 65. Medium because redacted public trust-centre summaries can still carry scope fields. Removed clearance-vetting terms (NV1/NV2/AGSVA) that did not relate to audit reports.

patterns.risk_description: The keyword list identifies a security audit report by combining SOC 2, ISO 27001, IRAP, control-assessment, and audit-finding language; physical-security or home-security reviews are excluded. A genuine report can expose failed controls, exceptions, and remediation priorities that help an attacker select weak points or undermine assurance activity. The usual unit is a bounded assurance report whose findings may be process or compliance oriented rather than directly exploitable. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE InfoTech fit that serious organisational exposure; PROTECTED requires attack-ready weaknesses, critical-system scope, or significant operational damage. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated record structure (labelled fields with real values, identifiers or data rows); phrase-only mentions in guidance, marketing, blank forms and news stay at 65 discovery.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech and Medium because a populated SOC 2, ISO 27001 or IRAP report exposes failed controls, exceptions and remediation priorities. PROTECTED is not met because findings are often process or compliance gaps rather than attack-ready weaknesses in critical systems.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling protects audit findings and control exceptions that show where an organisation is weak. It is not High unless the report scopes critical systems with directly exploitable findings.

patterns.name: Security Clearance Reference
patterns.description: Detects references to Australian Government security clearances and personnel vetting status.
patterns.operation: Keyword-only pattern using Purview regex engine. The Purview regex Pattern_clearance_phrase matches phrases such as Baseline clearance, Negative Vetting 1/2 clearance, Positive Vetting clearance, NV1/NV2/PV clearance, AGSVA clearance, AGSVA vetting, security clearance level/status/holder/granted/required, and personnel security vetting. Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires clearance context + government security keywords with template exclusion logic; Medium (75) requires clearance context keywords; Low (65) requires only the regex match. Evidence uses 2 keyword groups (5 clearance context terms, 10 government security terms) within 300-character proximity. Template/sample exclusion prevents false positives from training materials.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: keyword-based detection relies on phrase-matching regex within the Purview engine. Corroborative evidence keywords are needed for reliable identification since clearance-related terms can appear in non-vetting contexts.

should_not_match.value: Security guard clearance badge
should_not_match.description: No clearance phrase matched by the Purview regex

should_not_match.value: Clear the security checkpoint
should_not_match.description: No clearance phrase present

false_positives.description: Generic security terms in non-vetting contexts.
false_positives.mitigation: Require AGSVA-specific or clearance level terminology.

patterns.risk_description: The detector finds a security-clearance level, status, or reference rather than a vetting dossier or access credential. Disclosure can reveal personnel trust information and may expose one person's role, suitability status, or targeting value. The normal consequence is credible but limited because no adjudication history, vulnerabilities, or system permissions are included. Risk 6 SENSITIVE Government fits that moderate harm; PROTECTED would require a detailed vetting file, protected operation, or actionable access information.

classification.rationale: Risk 6 matches PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE and SENSITIVE Government because a clearance level or vetting status reveals personnel trust information and raises one person's targeting value. PROTECTED is not met: no adjudication history, vulnerabilities or system permissions are included, so the harm is credible but limited.

generic.rationale: Medium Government handling applies to a person's clearance level or vetting status, which can mark them for targeting. A detailed vetting file, not a status reference, would be needed for High.

patterns.name: Security Incident Report
patterns.description: Detects populated cyber security incident reports: incident report / post-incident review titles together with incident record fields (incident ID, severity, detection time, affected hosts, source IPs) or technical artefacts (IPv4 addresses, CVE identifiers).
patterns.operation: Primary: security incident report/analysis, cyber (security) incident, incident investigation/forensic report, post-incident review/analysis. 65 (discovery only) = primary alone. 75 = primary plus one populated incident record field (incident/ticket ID, severity, priority, detected / date reported, reported by, affected host/system/asset/user, hostname, source/destination IP, malware family, hash) or a technical artefact (IPv4 address, CVE ID). 85 = primary plus two distinct structure hits plus independent response or root-cause evidence (containment, eradication, forensic analysis, indicators of compromise, root cause, contributing factor ...). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. Converted from keyword_list to a tier-gated regex classifier; the legacy top-level keyword list is kept as descriptive metadata only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: incident-report titles also appear in policy, guidance and news, so enforcement requires populated incident fields or technical artefacts; 85 adds response/root-cause evidence.

patterns.risk_description: The keyword list distinguishes cyber incident reports using forensic analysis, root cause, indicators of compromise, attack-vector, and containment evidence, while traffic or guard incidents are explicit non-matches. Disclosure can reveal successful techniques, investigative visibility, threat attribution, and unfinished remediation to the same actor or a copycat. The normal report concerns one incident and affected environment and does not necessarily establish critical-service impact or broad privileged access. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE InfoTech reflect serious contained response exposure; PROTECTED requires severe critical-operations consequences, life-safety effects, or comparably significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 reconciles with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech and Medium because an incident report reveals affected hosts, source IPs, techniques that worked and unfinished containment. PROTECTED is not met because a single-incident report does not by itself establish critical-service impact or broad privileged access.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling fits a report that shows an attacker or copycat what succeeded and what defenders saw, bounded to one incident and environment.

patterns.name: SendGrid API Key
patterns.description: Detects SendGrid (Twilio SendGrid) API keys, formatted as SG. then a 22-character key id, a dot, and a 43-character secret. A leaked key allows sending email and reading account data through the SendGrid API.
patterns.operation: Structured token SG.<22-char id>.<43-char secret> in base64url charset. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the SG. prefix with two fixed-length base64url segments separated by a dot is a distinctive SendGrid structure with very low false-positive risk.

should_match.description: SendGrid API key, SG. + 22 + . + 43
Labelled SendGrid key in an env assignment
Mixed-case SendGrid key
Two distinct SendGrid API Key values in one file with context; the 85 tier needs two distinct tokens (one token, or the same token repeated, stays below 85)

should_not_match.value: SG.ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUV.TOOSHORT
should_not_match.description: Second segment too short to be a valid SendGrid secret

should_not_match.value: SK.ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUV.ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopq
should_not_match.description: Wrong prefix (SK. instead of SG.)

should_not_match.value: set the sendgrid api key in your mail send configuration
should_not_match.description: Prose mention without a token value

false_positives.description: Documentation or examples showing placeholder SG. strings.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative keywords and check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx).

patterns.risk_description: The regex recognises SendGrid API keys through the service-specific SG prefix followed by the expected identifier and secret segments. A usable key can authorise email sending and, depending on scope, expose account functions, enabling convincing phishing, spam campaigns, reputation damage, and service cost. A normal match is one revocable SendGrid credential rather than proof that an organisation-wide messaging estate has been compromised, and sample keys in technical documentation remain possible. Risk 8 SENSITIVE captures the serious operational and impersonation harm of one live key; PROTECTED would require demonstrated broad administrative scope or consequences capable of significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 is consistent with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, SENS_IT, and Medium classification because the matched SendGrid credential can be exploited directly for service abuse within its assigned permissions. The detector does not establish global account control, mass compromise, or an impact level sufficient for PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium with Medium InfoTech is suitable for an email-platform secret that can cause material fraud and operational harm while remaining permission-scoped and replaceable. Generic High would need evidence that the credential controls a critical communications environment or enables significant damage beyond the normal token.

patterns.name: Sentry Token
patterns.description: Detects Sentry auth tokens: organization tokens (sntrys_), user auth tokens (sntryu_), the user-app and internal-integration prefixes from Sentry's own token-type source (sntrya_, sntryi_), and, when labelled with Sentry context in an assignment, the legacy unprefixed 64-hex tokens issued before prefixing. A leaked token grants API access to error and performance data -- which routinely embeds further secrets, PII, and source context -- and to release/CI operations. Sentry DSNs are explicitly NOT matched: Sentry documents DSNs as safe to keep public.
patterns.operation: Two detection branches. Branch 1 (distinctive, value-only capable): sntrys_ organization tokens -- the full structure attested by both gitleaks and Kingfisher: payload beginning with base64-encoded '{"iat":' (sntrys_eyJpYXQiO), a bounded base64 run, an embedded base64-encoded "region_url" JSON marker (one of its three base64 rotations), a second bounded base64 run, optional padding, then an underscore-separated 43-character base64 secret (={0,2}_[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}); sntryu_ user tokens (exactly 64 hex, pinned identically by gitleaks, TruffleHog, and Kingfisher); and sntrya_/sntryi_ (user-app and internal-integration prefixes confirmed by Sentry's own source code -- src/sentry/types/token.py -- with unpublished bodies, so a generous bounded range is used behind the vendor-confirmed distinctive prefixes, the same honest-bound treatment as other vendor-announced-but-unpinned formats in this corpus). Branch 2 (context-gated only): legacy pre-prefix tokens (bare 64 hex, per gitleaks' "old format" rule and TruffleHog's v1 detector), requiring a Sentry label plus an assignment separator before the value. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the sntry?_ prefix family is confirmed by Sentry's own source code (AuthTokenType enum: sntryu_/sntrys_/sntrya_/sntryi_), and the two dominant formats are pinned by multiple independent production detectors -- sntryu_ + 64 hex identically in gitleaks, TruffleHog, and Kingfisher; the sntrys_ branch adopts the full gitleaks/Kingfisher-attested structure (eyJpYXQiO payload head, embedded base64 region_url marker in any of its three rotations, and the trailing ={0,2}_ + 43-character base64 secret; TruffleHog's flat sntrys_eyJ + 197-character body is consistent with this envelope). Sentry is a GitHub secret-scanning partner for both (push protection enabled). The sntrya_/sntryi_ bodies are not published by any source, so they carry an honest bounded range behind their distinctive prefixes rather than an invented exact length. The legacy unprefixed 64-hex form is deliberately context-gated: it is indistinguishable from any SHA-256 hex digest, so it requires a labelled assignment and never fires value-only.

Sentry organization token (sntrys_eyJpYXQiO + base64 + region_url marker + base64 + padding + _ + 43-char secret) in the canonical env var
Internal-integration prefix from Sentry's own token-type source (bounded body)
Legacy pre-prefix token (bare 64 hex) in a labelled Sentry assignment (context-gated branch)
Legacy 64-hex token after the canonical env var with colon separator
Legacy 64-hex token in a quoted dotted-key config assignment
Two distinct Sentry Token values in one file with context; the 85 tier needs two distinct tokens (one token, or the same token repeated, stays below 85)

should_not_match.description: Bare 64-hex value with no Sentry label anywhere (could be any SHA-256 digest)

should_not_match.value: sntryu_0123456789abcdef
should_not_match.description: sntryu_ body far too short (16 hex chars, not 64)

should_not_match.value: unrelated generic text without domain phrases
should_not_match.description: Safe non-domain negative

should_not_match.value: unrelated generic text without domain phrases
should_not_match.description: Safe non-domain negative

should_not_match.value: template example placeholder record identifier
should_not_match.description: Template/sample context should be excluded even when anchor words are present

false_positives.description: Sentry DSNs (https://<32-hex>@o<org>.ingest.sentry.io/<project>) look credential-like but are documented by Sentry as safe to keep public; they are deliberately not matched.
false_positives.mitigation: The legacy branch requires a 64-hex body in a labelled assignment, which a DSN's 32-hex public key cannot satisfy; DSN detection is documented as out of scope rather than flagged as a leak.

false_positives.description: A 64-character hex digest (SHA-256) appearing in a labelled assignment near the word "sentry" in configuration or logs.
false_positives.mitigation: The legacy branch requires label adjacency plus an assignment separator (enforced by the regex) and corroborative keywords; it never fires value-only.

false_positives.description: The sntrya_/sntryi_ body lengths are not published by Sentry or any scanner; a generous bounded range is used behind the vendor-confirmed prefixes. Hypothetical sntrys_ tokens whose payload lacks the leading '{"iat":' or the embedded region_url field would not match the organization-token branch (both gitleaks and Kingfisher assume the same structure).
false_positives.mitigation: Documented as an honest bound; the prefixes themselves come from Sentry's own source and are highly distinctive, and the structured org-token branch mirrors both production scanners exactly.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence detector finds current Sentry organization, user, app, or integration auth tokens and a context-gated legacy 64-hex token, while deliberately excluding public DSNs. A live token can expose error and performance events containing source context, personal data, and secondary secrets, and may authorize release or CI operations within its grants. The affected scale is one Sentry organization, user, or integration, with token role, project access, retention, and revocation limiting harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained observability-platform compromise, while an organization token spanning protected production telemetry and broad release control would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Sentry auth token can reveal material event data and enable operational actions within its grants. PROTECTED is not met because the normal token is role-bounded and the detector excludes public DSNs without establishing broad privileged or critical-service compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium InfoTech handling fit Sentry auth tokens because they can expose detailed application telemetry and CI actions while role and project scope usually contain the damage.

patterns.name: High-Value Session Cookie Token
patterns.description: Detects high-value session cookies by name-plus-value: framework and SSO session cookies (ESTSAUTH / ESTSAUTHPERSISTENT, JSESSIONID, PHPSESSID, connect.sid, _session_id, sessionid) assigned a long token value. A captured session cookie lets an attacker resume an authenticated session and bypass MFA entirely. Bare assignments are discovery-only; HTTP cookie framing and response attributes provide the enforcement tiers.
patterns.operation: A known session-cookie name, an = or : assignment, then a 16+ character token value drawn from the cookie value charset (letters, digits, percent, dot, underscore, hyphen). The 65 tier inventories that assignment. A Cookie or Set-Cookie header raises it to 75, while a Set-Cookie response carrying Path/Domain plus Secure or HttpOnly attributes reaches 85. Enforcing tiers reject template and placeholder values.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: requiring a specific high-value session-cookie name immediately assigned a 16+ character token value is a distinctive structure. Documentation that merely names these cookies without a real value will not match.

should_match.description: Low-tier probe - recognized cookie assignment without HTTP framing
Medium-tier probe - recognized session token in a request Cookie header
High-tier probe - response cookie with path and security attributes

should_not_match.value: JSESSIONID=short
should_not_match.description: Token value too short (under 16 chars)

should_not_match.value: COLORID=A1B2C3D4E5F6A1B2C3D4E5F6A1B2C3D4
should_not_match.description: Unknown cookie name, not a tracked session cookie

should_not_match.value: The JSESSIONID cookie identifies the user session on the server
should_not_match.description: Prose naming the cookie with no assigned token value

should_not_match.value: Cookie: JSESSIONID=REDACTED_SESSION_VALUE
should_not_match.description: Placeholder session value in an otherwise valid Cookie header

should_not_match.value: Documentation example: Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly
should_not_match.description: Documentation quoting a complete response cookie must not enforce

should_not_match.value: Set-Cookie: csrftoken=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef; Secure; HttpOnly
should_not_match.description: Sibling CSRF cookie is not a tracked authenticated-session cookie

false_positives.description: Example or expired cookie values in API documentation, HAR captures used for debugging, or test fixtures.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative session/cookie-theft keywords and treat obvious placeholders (all zeros, "example") as non-sensitive.

patterns.risk_description: This detector finds a long token assigned to a recognised high-value session cookie name such as ESTSAUTH, ESTSAUTHPERSISTENT, JSESSIONID, PHPSESSID, connect.sid, _session_id, or sessionid. A live cookie can permit session replay, account impersonation, and bypass of the authentication step, including multi-factor authentication already completed for that session. The exposure ordinarily concerns one current session, and expired cookies, browser traces, test fixtures, or documentation can match without providing usable access. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious direct account harm from a valid token; PROTECTED would require privileged or broadly reusable session authority with credible significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps coherently to OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, the SENSITIVE InfoTech DLM, SENS_IT, and Medium tier because a recognised cookie-name and token pair can be immediately replayable yet is normally limited by one session, expiry, and server-side revocation. The match does not prove privileged tenant control or the major consequence necessary for PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium InfoTech handling reflects an authentication artefact capable of direct impersonation within a bounded session. Generic High is not automatic because session lifetime, account privilege, and successful replay are not established by the detector.

patterns.name: Sexual Orientation
patterns.description: Detects sexual-orientation information in person-linked workforce, patient, survey, member, relationship, intake, and case records. The detector recognises the explicit sexual orientation phrase, orientation-specific identification statements, coming-out statements, and same-sex partner or spouse references, then raises confidence only for person records and populated attributions. It deliberately excludes transgender status, gender identity, and pronouns because those are distinct attributes. Sexual orientation is protected under GDPR Article 9 and Australian anti-discrimination and privacy law. Topic-grade detector, low confidence by design.
patterns.operation: The primary regex matches the explicit sexual orientation phrase, orientation-specific identification and coming-out statements, and same-sex partner/spouse references. 65 (discovery only): phrase alone - policy, guidance, news and survey-design text naming the category stays here. 75: phrase plus a populated identified-person field (name, DOB, employee/member/customer/patient/participant number or ID, data subject). 85: person field plus a populated orientation value (heterosexual, gay, lesbian, bisexual, pansexual, asexual, queer) that is not part of the primary statement plus independent record evidence (recorded as, response selected, disclosed to, optional demographic question, diversity survey, next of kin). Template framing and guidance/policy/public-aggregate framing are excluded from 75/85. Converted from keyword_list to regex so the tier logic decides matches.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low by design: the attribute has no fixed format. Enforce tiers now require the attribute to be tied to an identified person record (a populated name/DOB/ID field), and 85 also requires a separately populated orientation value plus independent record evidence, so policy text, surveys-in-design and news naming the category stay at 65 discovery.

false_positives.description: The bare word "orientation" appears in unrelated contexts (employee orientation, building/map orientation) that have nothing to do with sexual orientation.
false_positives.mitigation: The regex targets full orientation-specific phrases rather than the bare word "orientation"; enforcement requires a person-record context, and the high tier also requires a populated attribution.

false_positives.description: "Coming out as" can appear in non-disclosure prose unrelated to sexual orientation (e.g. "the album is coming out as a double LP", "the report is coming out as scheduled").
false_positives.mitigation: The regex now requires "coming out as" to be followed by an orientation term, and enforcement requires person-record evidence in the same bounded span.

patterns.risk_description: A true positive attributes sexual orientation or a same-sex relationship to a person. Disclosure can cause involuntary outing, discrimination, harassment, coercion, or safety harm, particularly where orientation carries legal or social risk. The normal single-person record does not by itself establish the scale or severe consequence required for PROTECTED. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy are appropriate.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy because the enforcing tiers require orientation-specific language in a person-linked record; the 85 tier also requires a populated orientation or relationship attribution. The 65 topic branch is discovery-only, and gender identity, transgender status, pronouns, and LGBTQ policy text are not primary matches. PROTECTED is not met without a credible severe threat, protected identity context, bulk exposure, or significant damage.

generic.rationale: A confirmed person-linked sexual-orientation or same-sex relationship record is generically Medium Personal-Privacy because disclosure can cause involuntary outing, discrimination, harassment, coercion, or safety harm. High handling requires a severe threat or broad high-consequence holding.

changelog.description: Add the classification block (tier, rationale, generic classification/DLM/rationale). Text copied verbatim from the reviewed SIT-Reference master, which until now held it only in PurviewDeploy.

Quality pass (2026-09-24): converted keyword_list to regex; 75 was gated only by record-context keywords (HR file, intake form, case record) that appear in policy and survey-design text, and 85 evidence could repeat the primary. 75 now requires the attribute to sit with a populated identified-person field (name, DOB, member/employee/patient ID) and 85 requires person fields plus a separately populated orientation value plus independent record evidence; policy text naming the category stays at 65. Bare-phrase tests replaced with populated person records; added policy, blank-form and news decoys; public-context exclusions folded into the guidance exclusion group.

Consolidate the retired Australian alias into the global detector: add Australian legal and workforce evidence, align the top-level and Purview primaries, remove transgender/gender-identity/LGBTQ-policy scope, retain 65 discovery, and require person-record plus populated orientation evidence at 75/85.

Targeted blocker remediation: add an orientation-only 65 topic-discovery tier, a 75 data-subject-record tier, and an 85 populated orientation-attribution tier, with exact-tier and sibling/public/template probes.

Final-review finding: document the "coming out as" false-positive vector (non-disclosure prose like album/report release timing) in false_positives, matching the precedent files' practice of documenting each broad alternation's FP risk.

New pattern: replaces the deprecated au/global-top500-015-sexual-orientation attribute-value patterns (needs-EDM/ML) with an honest topic-classifier concept, modeled on global-political-opinion. Fills the D-wave coverage gap logged in c3-deprecation-report.md.

patterns.name: SF6 Switchgear and PCB Equipment Inventory or Leak / Test Record
patterns.description: Operational inventories and records for two regulated insulating substances in electrical plant: sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) in gas-insulated switchgear and circuit breakers (stock held in equipment, top-up, leakage and recovery quantities in kg, as reported under Australian NGER Regulations reg 4.16 and Measurement Determination Part 4.5), and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in transformers and capacitors (oil test results in mg/kg classed as scheduled PCB material at or above 50 mg/kg, non-scheduled, or PCB-free at or below 2 mg/kg under the ANZECC PCB Management Plan; notifiable quantities above 10 kg). Records carry asset or serial numbers, substation / site locations and measured quantities. The PCB Management Plan, IChEMS advice, NGER Determination text and vendor guidance are decoys.
patterns.operation: Primary: SF6, sulphur / sulfur hexafluoride, polychlorinated biphenyl(s), PCB(s), scheduled PCB material / waste, non-scheduled PCB, PCB-free. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will also surface printed-circuit-board documents, guidance and news. 75 requires one populated measurement within 300 characters: an inventory row (an asset-style token such as TX-0412 or CB-2231 followed on the same line by a concentration in mg/kg, or by an SF6 quantity in kg) or a labelled measurement with a value (PCB concentration / content / result, concentration (mg/kg), oil test result, SF6 mass / charge / fill / stock / top-up / recovered / leakage, gas / nameplate / rated mass in kg, top-up or quantity added / recovered / lost in kg). 85 requires two distinct inventory rows, or a labelled measurement plus a populated asset / serial / equipment / plant number, functional location, substation, switchyard, site, location or bay field, plus independent evidence (transformer, capacitor, circuit breaker, gas insulated switchgear, kVA / MVA, insulating oil, dielectric, leak, top up, gas cart, recovery, disposal, NATA, laboratory, density monitor, reg 4.16). Every tier excludes template/fixture text; enforce tiers also exclude guidance signals (nepc.gov.au, dcceew.gov.au, legislation.gov.au, "Revised Edition", compilation headers, "this plan / guideline / fact sheet", article disclaimers).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: SF6 and PCB terms are specific to electrical plant, but "PCB" also means printed circuit board, and the ANZECC plan, NGER Determination and vendor guidance quote the thresholds (50 mg/kg, 2 mg/kg, 10 kg, 0.0089). Enforce tiers need populated measurements tied to an asset row or labelled field, and ppm is accepted only in labelled PCB fields (electronics documents use ppm). Asset and serial number formats are organisation-specific, so rows are recognised by an uppercase letters-plus-digits token only. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.
regulations: National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Regulations 2008 (Cth)
National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting (Measurement) Determination 2008 (Cth) Part 4.5
ANZECC Polychlorinated Biphenyls Management Plan (Revised Edition April 2003)

customisation.note: Extend the labelled-field evidence with the customer's asset number / functional location format (see docs/identifiers.md#asset-functional-location). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

They map where regulated hazardous or high-global-warming substances sit in named substations and plant, quantify leakage that feeds NGER reports, and document environmental and disposal liabilities (scheduled PCB material, notifiable quantities) before they are notified or remediated. patterns.name: Shopify Access Token
patterns.description: Detects the Shopify access-token family: Admin API access tokens (shpat_), custom app access tokens (shpca_), legacy private app passwords (shppa_) and app shared secrets (shpss_), each followed by a 32-character hex body. A leaked token grants API access to a Shopify store, including customers, orders and payment-adjacent data.
patterns.operation: Single alternation over the four current Shopify prefixes (shpat_/shpca_/shppa_/shpss_) followed by exactly 32 hex characters. Shopify's own changelog fixes the token at 38 characters total including the 6-character prefix, matching the 32-hex body used by the TruffleHog and gitleaks production detectors. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: all four prefixes are multiply attested (TruffleHog production detectors for shpat_/shppa_/shpss_, gitleaks rules for all four including shpca_, and Shopify's own changelog confirming the 38-character total length), and Shopify is a GitHub secret-scanning partner with push-protection-enabled token types. The distinctive prefix plus fixed-length hex body makes false positives extremely unlikely.

Labelled Shopify custom app access token in an env assignment
Shopify legacy private app password (shppa_)
Shopify app shared secret (shpss_, uppercase hex body)
Two distinct Shopify Access Token values in one file with context; the 85 tier needs two distinct tokens (one token, or the same token repeated, stays below 85)

should_not_match.description: Invalid prefix variant (shpxx_ is not a Shopify token family)

should_not_match.value: shpat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
should_not_match.description: Body too short (31 hex chars, not 32)

should_not_match.value: shpat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
should_not_match.description: Body contains non-hex characters (g-v), not a valid token body

should_not_match.value: rotate the shopify admin api access token
should_not_match.description: Prose mention without a token value

should_not_match.value: template example placeholder record identifier
should_not_match.description: Template/sample context should be excluded even when anchor words are present

false_positives.description: Documentation or examples showing placeholder shpat_/shpca_/shppa_/shpss_ strings.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative Shopify keywords and check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx).

false_positives.description: Pre-2020 Shopify tokens (32 characters total, shorter body) are an older generation not matched by this pattern.
false_positives.mitigation: Documented as a known scope limitation; only the current 38-character (prefix + 32-hex) generation is matched.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex identifies Shopify Admin API, custom-app, legacy private-app, or shared-secret credentials through the shpat_, shpca_, shppa_, and shpss_ prefixes with a fixed hex body. A live value can authorize store API operations, expose customers and orders, alter products or configuration, and access payment-adjacent data within the app's scopes. The affected scale is one Shopify store or app integration, with granted scopes, store role, monitoring, and token revocation limiting harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained commerce-platform compromise, while a broadly scoped token controlling a high-value multi-store estate would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Shopify token can directly expose customer and order data or modify a material store. PROTECTED is not met because the normal credential is scoped to one store or app and does not establish severe irreversible loss or broad privileged control.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification with Medium InfoTech handling is appropriate for Shopify tokens because they enable direct store and customer-data access while app scopes and store boundaries contain impact.

patterns.name: SIM Authentication Key File (Ki / OPc personalisation output)
patterns.description: SIM / USIM personalisation and key files exchanged between SIM vendors, mobile network operators and HSS/AuC provisioning: a header row naming subscriber key columns (Ki, OPc, ADM1, KIC1/KID1/KIK1, EKI) next to ICCID or IMSI, followed by populated rows that pair an ICCID (ITU-T E.118, MII 89, e.g. Australian issuer prefixes 8961 and 8967210 on the ACMA register) and an IMSI (3GPP TS 23.003, MCC + MNC + MSIN, at most 15 digits; Australia MCC 505) with 128-bit key values (32 hex characters, per 3GPP TS 35.206 K and OPc). The file layout is vendor-proprietary; the pySim card-key CSV and pysim-perso column sets are used only as shapes. Excludes the published 3GPP TS 35.208 test-set values, "Test Set" / "35.208" text, test networks (MCC 001) and pySim / Open5GS tutorial or documentation text.
patterns.operation: Primary (65, discovery only): a header line where ICCID or IMSI and a key column name (Ki, OPc, ADM1, KIC1/KID1/KIK1, EKI) appear on the same line within 200 characters. 75: primary plus one populated key row on a single line: an ICCID (89 + 17-18 digits, optional F pad) adjacent to (or one field away from) a 15-digit IMSI with MCC 2xx-7xx, in either order, followed within 240 characters by a standalone 32-hex value (Ki / OPc). 85: primary plus two distinct populated key rows (min_count 2, unique) plus independent personalisation evidence (PIN1/PUK1/PIN2/PUK2, ADM1, transport key, batch, perso/personalisation, HSS/HLR/AuC, MSISDN). Every tier ANDs NOT template/noise exclusion (catches "tutorial", "demo", "template", "test data") and NOT a SIM test-material exclusion (3GPP TS 35.208 test-set K/OP/OPc values, "Test Set n", "35.205-35.208", "test vector", "conformance test", pySim card-key-provider documentation, pySim/Open5GS tutorial or guide text). Proximity is 1000 characters because vendor key files can have 20+ columns per row.
patterns.confidence_justification: High for 75/85: a single line pairing a 19-20 digit ICCID, a 15-digit IMSI and a standalone 32-hex value under a Ki/OPc header has no common benign explanation outside SIM test material, which is excluded explicitly. The ICCID Luhn check digit is not validated inside the row regex (Purview validators apply to whole matches), and the IMSI shape does not validate the MNC, so a malformed or non-issued ICCID/IMSI can still match. The 65 header tier also fires on vendor documentation and news about SIM key theft and is discovery-only. Test rows are synthetic; key values are random hex, not real keys and not 3GPP test vectors.

should_match.description: 85 - Australian SIM vendor output file (8961 02 Optus-range ICCIDs, IMSI 505 02) with header, two populated key rows and PIN/PUK/batch/transport key evidence
85 - IMSI-first whitespace-aligned HSS/AuC import (non-AU MCC) with two populated key rows
75 - card-key CSV (pySim column set) with one populated row (Vodafone-range 8961 03 ICCID, IMSI 505 03)
75 - OTA key file (Ki/OPc plus KIC1/KID1/KIK1) with one populated row

false_positives.description: SIM vendor, pySim and Open5GS documentation and news that name Ki/OPc next to ICCID/IMSI.
false_positives.mitigation: The header alone is 65 discovery; enforce tiers need a populated ICCID + IMSI + 32-hex row. Documentation and tutorial text is also excluded.

false_positives.description: Lab and test SIMs programmed with the 3GPP TS 35.208 test sets, and test networks using MCC 001.
false_positives.mitigation: The TS 35.208 test set 1 K/OP/OPc values and "Test Set" / "35.208" text are excluded; the IMSI shape requires MCC 2xx-7xx, so 001-01 test IMSIs never form a row.

false_positives.description: Real ICCID/IMSI inventory exports without key columns (activation lists, MVNO stock files).
false_positives.mitigation: Not this classifier - no Ki/OPc header, so no primary. Those are covered by global-iccid and the IMSI/phone classifiers.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies SIM authentication key files: rows that bind a card's ICCID and a subscriber IMSI to its 128-bit Ki and OPc (and, where present, OTA keys KIC/KID/KIK and ADM codes). Anyone holding these values can clone the SIM, impersonate the subscriber on the network and derive the session keys that protect calls, SMS and data, so a leaked batch file compromises every card in it and undermines interception safeguards for a whole operator. Header-only documentation, the published 3GPP test sets and tutorials are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 10 supports PROTECTED InfoTech handling.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to PSPF and QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED InfoTech and High because rows binding ICCID and IMSI to Ki and OPc let anyone clone every SIM in the batch, impersonate subscribers and derive session keys for calls and SMS. Operator-wide compromise is inherent; higher national-security levels are outside the QGISCF scheme.

generic.rationale: High with High InfoTech handling applies because a leaked key file compromises every card in it and the confidentiality of subscriber traffic. No higher generic tier exists.
