patterns.name: Safety Instrumented System Cause and Effect Matrix / HAZOP Worksheet
patterns.description: Plant-specific process safety engineering records: HAZOP (hazard and operability) study worksheets with node / guide word / deviation / causes / consequences / safeguards / recommendations columns, and safety instrumented system (SIS) cause and effect matrices and safety requirements with trip tags, voting (1oo2, 2oo3) and SIL ratings. Populated worksheets and matrices tie instrument tags and trip logic to a real facility, which is why enforcement needs populated tags and structure, not the methodology vocabulary that appears in standards, training and textbooks.
patterns.operation: 65 (discovery-only): a HAZOP / hazard and operability / cause and effect matrix / safety instrumented function or system / safety requirements specification phrase. 75: the phrase plus independent populated structure - a HAZOP worksheet header row (at least deviation, causes, consequences and safeguards headings in order within a bounded span), or at least 5 distinct ISA-5.1 style instrument tags from a whitelist of common tag prefixes (FIC-101, PSV-2003, LSHH-310), or a voting / SIL / SIF value. 85: the phrase plus at least 5 distinct instrument tags plus a second distinct structure (worksheet header row or voting / SIL / SIF value) plus independent evidence (a P&ID reference, action owner, node description or trip setpoint). All enforce tiers exclude template / noise text and training, course, textbook and example framing.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the methodology vocabulary (guide words, deviations, SIL, voting) is common to standards, courses and textbooks, so enforce tiers require populated instrument tags and worksheet structure. ISA-5.1 tag shapes are a convention (the standard is paywalled and its full letter table was not verified), so only a whitelist of common tag prefixes is used and at least 5 distinct tags are required. IEC 61882 worksheet columns were verified only from secondary sources. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy; test values are synthetic.

false_positives.mitigation: Enforce tiers need populated worksheet structure, a set of distinct instrument tags or voting / SIL values; training, course, textbook and example framing is excluded.

patterns.risk_description: A populated HAZOP worksheet or SIS cause and effect matrix documents how a specific plant can fail and which instruments, trip setpoints and voting arrangements prevent a major incident. For critical infrastructure (power stations, water treatment, gas facilities) that is sensitive operational information and can be SOCI protected information; it also carries commercial and liability sensitivity. Standards text, training material, blank templates and news are excluded from enforce tiers. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE InfoTech.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 supports PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech and Medium for a populated HAZOP worksheet or SIS cause and effect matrix tying trip tags, voting and SIL ratings to a real plant. PROTECTED is not met by the record alone; it documents failure modes and safeguards but not the network access or control needed to defeat them.

generic.rationale: Medium InfoTech handling reflects plant-specific failure modes, trip setpoints and liability exposure. Sites under SOCI obligations may need stronger handling than this default.

false_positives.description: Code snippets and configuration examples containing credential-related keywords or placeholder values in developer documentation.

patterns.risk_description: The regex recognizes current and legacy Slack bot, user, workspace, and refresh token formats, each representing a bearer credential for a Slack app or identity. A live token can be replayed to read messages, post content, invoke workspace APIs, or access data according to its scopes and token family. The likely scale is one bot, user, app installation, or workspace relationship, while revocation, expiry, legacy formats, examples, and narrow scopes limit impact. Risk 8 SENSITIVE captures serious contained collaboration and account harm; PROTECTED requires confirmed workspace-wide administration or access to significant protected communications.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Slack token is directly replayable within its granted workspace scopes. PROTECTED is not met by token syntax because validity, token owner, scopes, workspace sensitivity, and administrative reach are not known.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls for Slack bearer tokens, requiring revocation, workspace audit, and removal from shared content. High applies only when a validated token grants broad administration or access to highly consequential communications.

patterns.name: Solana Address
patterns.description: Detects Solana public wallet/account addresses: the base58 encoding of a 32-byte ed25519 public key, 32-44 characters long, with NO distinctive prefix. Because a prefix-less base58 run of this length collides heavily with random tokens, other base58 identifiers and prose, detection is context-gated: the single tier is AND-gated by cryptocurrency/wallet domain context and a template/sample noise exclusion. Length/charset bounds verified against the Solana account model (32-byte address displayed as a base58 string) and the base58 alphabet (excludes 0 O I l).
patterns.operation: Single tier at confidence 75. The base58 32-44 char structure alone is weak evidence (no prefix, no expressible checksum), so the tier requires cryptocurrency/wallet domain context (crypto-wallet-context dict) within proximity AND a template/sample noise NOT-group. Case-sensitive base58 matching (alphabet 1-9 A-H J-N P-Z a-k m-z).
patterns.confidence_justification: Gated 75, not high: a prefix-less base58 run of 32-44 chars is the weakest structure in this family (no leading version byte, no HRP, no checksum recoverable in a Purview-safe regex), so structure alone is insufficient. Precision comes from the mandatory cryptocurrency/wallet domain-context gate plus the noise exclusion, never from the bare pattern.
regulations: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)

patterns.name: Square Access Token
patterns.description: Detects Square credential formats: application secrets (sq0csp-, with sandbox- prefixed sandbox variants), legacy personal access tokens (sq0atp-), and current OAuth/personal access tokens (EAAA + 60-character body, context-gated on a nearby Square label because the EAAA base64 shape also occurs in non-Square tokens and encoded blobs). A leaked token or secret enables payment processing and transaction data access in the associated Square account.
patterns.operation: Two detection branches. Branch 1 (distinctive, value-only capable): sq0-family prefixes -- (sandbox-)sq0c??- application secrets (40-50 char base64url body, per TruffleHog's production detector) and sq0atp- legacy personal access tokens (22-60 char body, per gitleaks). Branch 2 (context-gated only): EAAA-prefixed access tokens with an exactly-60-character body, requiring a Square label within 40 characters before the token, mirroring TruffleHog's production requirement of Square context for the EAAA form. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the sq0-family prefixes are Square-specific and multiply attested (TruffleHog squareapp production detector, gitleaks square-access-token rule, GitHub secret-scanning partner entries square_production_application_secret / square_sandbox_application_secret). The EAAA access-token form is attested by TruffleHog (exact 60-char body) and gitleaks but is deliberately context-gated: TruffleHog's own production detector requires the word "square" in the scanned data because bare EAAA matches base64-encoded blobs and other vendors' token families, so this pattern embeds the same label requirement at the regex level.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence detector finds Square application secrets, legacy personal access tokens, and context-gated current EAAA access tokens while excluding public application IDs. A live secret or bearer token can authorize payment processing, expose transaction data, and act within the associated merchant account's permissions. The affected scale is one Square merchant or application, with sandbox status, scopes, account balance, monitoring, and revocation containing financial harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained payment-platform compromise, while a production credential with broad high-value settlement authority would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 supports QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a valid Square token or application secret can directly authorize material merchant and transaction activity. PROTECTED is not met because the normal credential is bounded to one merchant or app and the detector does not establish severe irreversible loss or broad critical-service control.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium InfoTech handling fit Square credentials because they provide direct payment access while environment, merchant scope, permissions, and revocation usually contain the outcome.

patterns.name: Strategic Plan/Roadmap
patterns.description: Detects populated internal strategic plans, product/technology roadmaps and business cases: the plan/roadmap/business-case phrase combined with document-control fields, dated roadmap milestones or financial targets. Public strategy statements and phrase-only mentions stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex). Primary: strategic plan/planning/initiative, 3/5-year plan, product/technical/engineering/technology roadmap, roadmap document, business case, case for change, project initiation/charter. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated structure - document-control field (prepared by, owner, sponsor, approved by, version, review date, classification), a dated milestone line (e.g. 'Q3 FY27: Launch...'), or a financial line (revenue target, EBITDA, budget, investment, capex, funding, NPV, cost estimate) with a dollar value. 85: primary plus two distinct structures (the three above or a labelled KPI/OKR target percentage) plus an internal-distribution marker (confidential, internal only, not for distribution, commercial-in-confidence, embargoed). Template/sample and guidance/public-consultation framing excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers require populated document-control, milestone or financial structure; published strategy statements and consultation pages stay at 65 and 85 additionally needs a confidentiality marker. Medium-low signal: strategy content has no fixed format, and public-sector strategic plans with version tables can reach 75.

patterns.risk_description: The regex matches Stripe keys across secret or publishable prefixes and live or test modes, so one detector spans sensitive server credentials, intentionally exposed client keys, and non-production values. A live secret key can authorize payment-platform API operations within its account permissions, while a publishable key is designed for client use and a test key affects only test-mode objects. The possible impact ranges from negligible for pk_test to serious financial and customer-operation harm for an unrestricted sk_live key, with the key type requiring inspection before action. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE InfoTech fit the serious account-level misuse available through the live secret branch; PROTECTED requires confirmed high-privilege production authority or significant cross-account or payment-system damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 remains aligned with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech for the detector's live secret-key branch, which can cause serious contained payment-platform harm. PROTECTED is not met because account role and privilege are unknown and the same regex also accepts publishable and test keys with much lower consequence.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls at the SIT level, but policy must inspect the sk or pk and live or test segments before deciding containment. High is not justified across a detector that intentionally includes public and test credentials and does not establish broad financial administration.

patterns.name: Supabase Key
patterns.description: Detects Supabase credentials: personal access tokens (sbp_), the new opaque secret API keys (sb_secret_) introduced in 2025 to replace the legacy service_role JWT, and, when labelled with Supabase context in an assignment, the legacy anon/service_role JWT keys that remain valid until late 2026. A leaked secret key or service_role JWT grants full admin access to the project's production Postgres database, bypassing Row Level Security; a leaked personal access token grants account-wide Management API control.
patterns.operation: Two detection branches. Branch 1 (distinctive, value-only capable): sbp_ personal access tokens (40-character body, pinned by both TruffleHog's and Kingfisher's production detectors; charset is their union) and sb_secret_ project secret keys (announced by Supabase's changelog 2025-06-17 as the replacement for service_role JWTs; Kingfisher's production rule and Supabase's own CLI source both pin a 31-character body of the form 22 chars + underscore + 8-char suffix, so a tight 28-36 range is used behind the distinctive 10-character literal prefix -- the attested 31 with a small hedge for minor generation-format drift). Branch 2 (context-gated only): legacy anon/service_role JWTs -- an eyJ-prefixed three-segment JWT requiring a Supabase-specific label (supabase / service_role / anon key) plus an assignment separator before the value, because bare eyJ JWTs are ubiquitous in logs and configuration. sb_publishable_ keys are deliberately not detected: they are safe-to-expose public keys by design. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: both distinctive prefixes are multiply attested. sbp_ is pinned at a 40-character body by two independent production detectors (TruffleHog sbp_[a-z0-9]{40}, Kingfisher sbp_[a-z0-9_-]{40} case-insensitive) and confirmed as the personal-access-token format by Supabase's own Management API and CLI documentation. sb_secret_ is confirmed by Supabase's changelog (new API keys, June 2025), by a literal default key hardcoded in Supabase's own open-source CLI (of the form sb_secret_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUV_abcdefgh -- a 31-character body: 22 chars + underscore + 8-char suffix), and by Kingfisher's production rule (sb_secret_[a-z0-9_-]{31}) -- two convergent sources pinning 31 exactly, so the body is bounded 28-36: the pin plus a small hedge, because the vendor documents the keys only as opaque random strings and a hard 31 would silently miss minor generation-format drift. The legacy JWT branch is deliberately context-gated: eyJ-prefixed JWTs are one of the most common token shapes in any log or config file, so it requires a labelled assignment and never fires value-only.

false_positives.description: Any JWT (session token, OIDC id_token, other vendors' API keys) appearing near the words supabase/service_role in configuration or documentation -- eyJ-prefixed JWTs are ubiquitous and carry no vendor marker in the visible string.
false_positives.mitigation: The JWT branch requires a Supabase-specific label plus an assignment separator (enforced in the regex), is context-gated only, and never fires value-only; corroborative keywords add further gating.

false_positives.description: Supabase publishable keys (sb_publishable_) and the project anon JWT are designed to be public; flagging them as leaked credentials would be noise.
false_positives.mitigation: sb_publishable_ is structurally excluded from the regex; the anon JWT is only reported when it appears in a labelled Supabase assignment, where treating it as sensitive is a reasonable default.

false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative Supabase keywords and check for placeholder markers (example, xxxx).

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence pattern identifies Supabase personal access tokens, opaque sb_secret_ project keys, and context-gated legacy JWT credentials while excluding the newer public sb_publishable_ format. A live personal token can control account management, and a secret or service-role credential can administer a project database and bypass Row Level Security. The affected scale is one account or Supabase project, with key family, role, project boundaries, and revocation limiting harm; public anon-style matches require triage. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained database compromise, while a management token spanning many protected production projects would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because the detector includes personal and service-role credentials that can directly administer a material Supabase account or database. PROTECTED is not met because some JWT context may be public and the normal secret is bounded to one account or project without establishing broad critical-service compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification with Medium InfoTech handling suits Supabase secrets because they can bypass project controls and expose data while key family and project scope contain the normal harm.

patterns.name: Telegram Bot Token
patterns.description: Detects Telegram Bot API tokens: the numeric bot ID, a colon, and a 35-character [A-Za-z0-9_-] secret. A leaked bot token grants full control of the bot -- reading its message traffic, sending messages to every chat it belongs to, and hijacking any workflow automation built on it.
patterns.operation: Structured value: 7-12 digit bot ID, a colon, then exactly 35 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. The 35-character secret length is pinned identically by TruffleHog, gitleaks, and Kingfisher. No first-letter constraint is imposed: only gitleaks pins a leading A; TruffleHog and Kingfisher impose no letter constraint, and TruffleHog's own test fixture treats a B-starting secret as a valid token, so an A-pinned regex would miss real token shapes. The digit range spans the production detectors' attested 7-10 (Kingfisher 7-10, TruffleHog 8-10) with headroom to 12 for bot-ID growth, within gitleaks' looser 5-16 bound (considered too loose to adopt wholesale). Known limitation shared with all three production detectors: a token glued directly to the canonical URL form (api.telegram.org/bot<token>) is not matched, because the digits are letter-adjacent there; the same word-boundary behavior applies to TruffleHog, gitleaks, and Kingfisher. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the shape is structurally pinned by three independent production detectors (35-character secret, numeric-ID:secret layout consistent with Telegram's own Bot API docs example) and Telegram Bot Token appears in GitHub's secret-scanning pattern set, which matches on the bare shape. The evidentiary split on the secret's first letter is disclosed honestly: gitleaks pins a case-sensitive leading A, but TruffleHog and Kingfisher impose no letter constraint and TruffleHog's test fixture contains a valid B-starting secret -- so this pattern follows the 2-of-3 no-pin majority. It is a digits:string layout rather than a literal vendor prefix -- log lines or ratio-like data (epoch:hash) can approximate it -- and both regex-first scanners (TruffleHog, gitleaks) choose to context-gate it in their rules, so the value-only tier is discovery-grade and the recommended confidence tier requires Telegram keywords in proximity.

patterns.risk_description: The medium-confidence regex identifies a Telegram Bot API bearer token as a numeric bot ID, colon, and fixed 35-character secret. A live token gives control of the bot, allowing message access available to it, outbound impersonation, command handling, and abuse of connected automation. The affected scale is the bot and every chat or workflow it can reach, with bot permissions, privacy mode, token rotation, and administrator response containing harm. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained messaging compromise, while a privileged bot embedded in protected operational workflows would raise the impact.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to QGISCF SENSITIVE, PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a Telegram bot token is a complete bearer credential that enables direct control within the bot's chats and integrations. PROTECTED is not met because the normal token is bounded by one bot's permissions and does not establish broad privileged or critical-service compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium InfoTech handling fit Telegram bot tokens because they confer direct automation and messaging control while bot scope and revocation usually contain the damage.

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies Terraform Cloud or Enterprise API tokens from the distinctive atlasv1 segmented format and expected surrounding length. A live token can expose permitted workspaces, state, variables, runs, and infrastructure operations, with consequences determined by whether it belongs to a user, team, or organisation and by the assigned permissions. The normal unit is a single revocable token, and fabricated atlasv1 examples or coincidental dotted strings are possible although the format is specific. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious infrastructure and secret exposure within the granted scope; PROTECTED would require confirmed critical-estate control or consequences amounting to significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, SENS_IT, and Medium because a valid Terraform token can directly affect infrastructure resources while remaining subject to token scope, revocation, and account controls. The syntax does not establish organisation-wide administrative rights or critical infrastructure impact needed for PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium InfoTech appropriately protect an infrastructure automation credential capable of material operational misuse. Generic High is not inherent where the detector cannot determine the token role, workspace reach, or consequence scale.

patterns.risk_description: The Handwritten signatures detector finds phrases such as handwritten signature, wet signature, or signed by in text. It does not capture the ink image, stroke pattern, signatory name, or a completed instrument, so many instructions and workflow descriptions can satisfy the regex. A copied signature image on a financial or legal document could facilitate fraud, but that more consequential object is outside this match. Risk 3 and OFFICIAL assess the ordinary wording signal rather than presuming a reusable signature specimen.

classification.rationale: Risk 3, PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL DLM at Low tier fit wording such as wet, ink or specimen signature; the detector never captures the ink image, stroke pattern or signatory. SENSITIVE is not met because a reusable signature specimen on a financial or legal instrument, which could enable forgery, lies outside this text match.

generic.rationale: Low with Low handling fits signature wording; a scanned specimen signature linked to a signatory is the object that would justify Medium.

patterns.name: Right-to-work verification documents
patterns.description: Detects right-to-work and visa entitlement verification records for an identified employee or candidate: Visa Entitlement Verification Online (VEVO) check results and printouts, work entitlement checks and US Form I-9 records, carrying the holder plus visa fields such as the visa subclass, the 13-digit visa grant number, transaction reference number (TRN) or visa evidence number, grant / expiry / must-not-arrive-after dates, period of stay, and Migration Regulations 1994 Schedule 8 visa conditions (for example 8101, 8104, 8105, 8107, 8547, 8607, 8608).
patterns.operation: Primary: a right-to-work phrase (right to work check, work entitlement check, visa verification, Visa Entitlement Verification Online, VEVO check / result, work rights check, employment eligibility verification, Form I-9). 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and surfaces policies, guidance, blank forms and statistics. 75 requires, within 300 characters, a populated holder field (employee / staff / payroll name or number, candidate, applicant, visa holder, holder / family / given / full name, passport number or date of birth, with a non-placeholder value) plus a populated visa field from at least one of four distinct groups: (a) visa subclass / class / type with a 3-digit subclass; (b) a labelled 13-digit visa grant number, transaction reference number (TRN) or visa evidence number; (c) a visa grant, expiry / expiration or must-not-arrive-after date with a date value, or a period of stay value; (d) a labelled visa / work conditions field with a Schedule 8 condition number (81xx-86xx). 85 requires the holder field plus populated fields from at least two of the four groups. All tiers exclude template/fixture text (template-exclusion); enforce tiers also exclude guidance, policy, training and media-release framing. A bare visa grant number is detected by global-top500-032-visa-grant-number; here it is only one VEVO field among four.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases also appear in policies, guidance, blank forms and news, so enforce tiers require a populated holder field plus at least one populated VEVO / visa field, and 85 needs fields from two distinct groups (subclass, grant or reference number, visa dates, Schedule 8 conditions). Holder values are customer-defined (employee IDs), so the holder regex uses labelled loose values with a placeholder guard. VEVO work-entitlement wording such as "no limitations" was not verified against a Home Affairs source, so it is corroborative only and not part of any tier. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

customisation.note: Extend the populated-field evidence with the customer's employee ID / payroll number format (see docs/identifiers.md#employee-id). The public fallback is the documented label-anchored regex, so the classifier works without customisation at lower precision.

patterns.name: Workplace investigation files
patterns.description: Identifies documents containing references to workplace investigation files in international contexts. This information type is classified as personally identifiable information under applicable data protection regulations.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex engine). Regex uses structural anchors with proximity constraints to match domain-specific content. Corroborative evidence: 7 keywords within 300 characters. Uses additional domain-context evidence and explicit exclusion logic for template/sample/test text.
patterns.confidence_justification: category-aware structural regex with anchor and context constraints replaces phrase-only detection. Added context gating and exclusion rules improve precision and reduce incidental matches.

false_positives.description: In English (as the primary international business language), similar terminology used in formal or administrative contexts (education, professional documentation) that does not constitute sensitive data collection.
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with additional contextual signals such as structured identifiers, form fields, or database column headers to distinguish sensitive records from general references.

patterns.risk_description: The detector recognises workplace-investigation, investigation-report, investigation-findings, and witness-statement language intended to identify an employment investigation file. A substantive file can contain allegations, witness accounts, credibility findings, evidence, and proposed sanctions, exposing employees and witnesses to retaliation, reputational damage, or legal prejudice. Investigation policies can match, but the named file unit is a composite case record rather than a single identifier or topic phrase. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious contained personal and legal harm; PROTECTED would require protected witnesses, criminal or national-security operations, privileged high-impact matters, or a bulk case system whose compromise causes significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, the SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy DLM, SENS_Pvc, and Medium tier for a workplace investigation case file. The next PROTECTED level is not met because an ordinary employment matter is not a protected-witness operation, national-security investigation, privileged major case, or system-wide significant-damage compromise.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium Personal-Privacy handling fit composite workplace investigation files containing allegations, evidence, and witness material with serious but contained consequences.

patterns.name: Exit interview records
patterns.description: Detects exit interview, exit survey and separation interview records for an identified departing employee, with reasons for leaving, last day or resignation date, rehire eligibility or satisfaction scores.
patterns.operation: Primary: an exit phrase (exit interview/survey/questionnaire/feedback, separation interview, departure interview, resignation feedback). 75 tier requires a populated person field (employee/staff name or number, departing employee, leaver, position number or title, work unit) with a non-placeholder value within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires a populated exit detail (reason for leaving, last day/resignation date, rehire eligibility, or satisfaction score) and an independent corroborative term (workload, culture, career, new employer, flexibility). All tiers exclude template/fixture text (template-exclusion); enforce tiers also exclude guidance, policy, training and media-release framing. 65 is discovery-only (primary alone) and will surface policies, guidance, blank forms and statistics.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases also appear in policies, guidance, blank forms and news, so enforce tiers require a populated person field and 85 adds a record-specific populated detail plus independent corroboration. Person values are customer-defined (employee IDs, position numbers), so the field regexes use labelled loose values with a placeholder guard. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

patterns.risk_description: The classifier identifies a exit interview or exit survey response from an identified employee about an identified person, gated on a populated person field (75) plus a record-specific populated detail (85). Disclosure exposes an identifiable former employee's candid comments about managers and colleagues, and sometimes health or harassment concerns. Policies, guidance, blank forms, training and news stay at 65 discovery. Risk 8 supports SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy (OFFICIAL: Sensitive).

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy because completed exit feedback can combine identifiable employment facts, allegations, and candid opinions. PROTECTED is not met for a normal one-person record whose consequences remain within an employment relationship and do not establish significant or irreversible damage.

generic.rationale: Medium with Medium Personal-Privacy handling is appropriate for completed exit feedback because disclosure can materially harm the worker and people discussed. High handling is reserved for exceptional cases carrying significantly greater personal or operational consequences.

patterns.name: Payroll bank account details
patterns.description: Detects employee payroll bank account details: a payroll/salary account or direct-deposit phrase combined with a BSB, a bank account number or a named employee/payee field. Phrase-only mentions (policies, scam warnings) stay discovery-only.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex). Primary: payroll bank (account) details, salary/wage/pay (bank) account (details), direct deposit details/authorisation/form, employee bank details, bank account details for salary/payroll, nominated account for salary/wages. 65 (discovery only): primary alone. 75: primary plus one populated field - BSB (6 digits), bank account number (6-10 digits) or a named employee/staff number/payee/account holder. 85: primary plus two distinct field types (the three above or an allocation line with a percentage/amount) plus payroll evidence (net pay, pay cycle, pay run, pay period, payslip, superannuation, effective from, change of bank details). Template/sample framing and guidance/training framing excluded on every enforce tier.
patterns.confidence_justification: Enforce tiers need a populated BSB, account number or employee field beside the payroll phrase; the previous 75 tier fired on the phrase alone. Payroll-change scam warnings and self-service help pages stay at 65. Medium because HR onboarding correspondence with the same fields is itself sensitive.

patterns.risk_description: The pattern recognises the phrase payroll bank account details with nearby payroll and financial-deposit vocabulary, indicating a payroll banking record rather than validating a specific account format. A genuine record can expose where wages are paid and support payroll diversion, supplier-style impersonation, or targeted fraud when paired with an employee name and change process. Published guidance, HR templates, and accounting discussion can match, and the low-confidence phrase does not prove that complete bank details are present. Risk 7 SENSITIVE reflects credible moderate employee financial harm from a true record; PROTECTED would require a payroll master file, authorisation data, or significant damage. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated records - rows keyed by an identifier, labelled values or identifiers - so topic mentions in guidance, marketing and news stay at 65 discovery.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps coherently to OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Financial, SENS_Fin, and Medium because authentic payroll banking details can materially enable payment diversion. The concept detector does not establish bulk scale, completeness, or direct authority sufficient for PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium Financial handling suit employee payment-account details with moderate fraud and privacy impact. Generic High would require a bulk payroll file or operative authorisation elements.

patterns.name: Employer payroll tax filings
patterns.description: Detects completed employer payroll tax and withholding filings: Queensland (state) payroll tax returns and annual reconciliations, PAYG withholding annual reports, Single Touch Payroll pay events/finalisation summaries and US Form 941/940 returns, with populated wage/withholding totals and an employer identifier or reporting period.
patterns.operation: Primary: an employer payroll tax filing phrase (payroll tax return/lodgement/annual reconciliation, PAYG withholding return/annual report, payment summary annual report, STP pay event/finalisation, Form 941/940). The single enforce tier (75) requires two distinct populated structures within 300 characters: a labelled filing amount (taxable wages, total salary and wages, amounts withheld, payroll tax payable, Form 941 wages/taxes) with a currency value, AND a populated employer identifier (employer name/ABN/EIN, payroll tax client number) or reporting period. Capped at 75 because the record is aggregate entity-level data. Enforce tier excludes template/fixture text and guidance/policy/marketing framing; 65 is discovery-only (primary alone).
patterns.confidence_justification: Low: employer payroll tax and withholding filings are aggregate, entity-level business records (total wages, tax withheld, employer identifiers) that normally carry no person-level data. The pattern is capped at 75: it needs a populated amount line plus a populated employer identifier or reporting period, which separates real returns from guidance, but no tier claims 85 because the record itself is low sensitivity. Tiers are heuristic evidence levels, not measured accuracy.

patterns.name: Pension account identifiers
patterns.description: Detects pension, annuity and retirement income stream account identifiers: a labelled pension/annuity/policy/member number with a populated value, optionally with the account holder name or date of birth.
patterns.operation: Primary: a pension account phrase (pension/annuity/retirement income/account-based pension/income stream account, member, policy, scheme or reference number). 75 tier requires a populated account identifier field (pension/annuity/account/member/policy/scheme number, ID or reference with a value that contains a digit, or a spaced ABN-style number) within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires a populated holder field (member/account holder/pensioner/annuitant/policyholder name, employee name/ID, or date of birth) and an independent corroborative term (income stream, drawdown, nominated bank account, payment frequency, rollover, fund, annuity). Enforce tiers exclude template/fixture text and guidance/scam-warning framing; 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: pension and annuity account numbers are customer-defined with no public format, so the classifier anchors on a labelled account/member/policy number containing a digit (placeholder-guarded) near a pension phrase for 75, and adds a populated holder name or date of birth plus independent corroboration for 85. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

patterns.name: Payroll journal entries
patterns.description: Detects payroll journal postings: pay-run journals, wages journals, payroll accruals and payroll GL exports with populated ledger lines (wages expense, PAYG withholding payable, superannuation payable, net wages payable, payroll clearing) and a journal reference or posting/period date. Aggregate ledger data, capped at 75.
patterns.operation: Primary: a payroll journal phrase (payroll journal/entry, wages journal, payroll accrual, payroll clearing account, payroll GL posting/export, pay run journal). The single enforce tier (75) requires two distinct populated structures within 300 characters: a payroll ledger line with a currency amount (wages/salaries expense or payable, net wages payable, PAYG withholding payable, super payable/expense, payroll clearing, payroll tax, leave provision) AND a journal/batch/pay-run reference or a posting/period/pay date. Capped at 75 because journals are aggregate ledger data. Enforce tier excludes template/fixture and textbook/training framing; 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low: payroll journals are aggregate general-ledger postings (wages expense, PAYG payable, super payable, clearing accounts) that normally carry no employee-level data. The pattern is capped at 75: it needs a populated ledger line with an amount plus a populated journal reference or posting/period date, which separates real postings from accounting textbooks, but it never claims 85 because the record itself is low sensitivity. If a journal lists individual employees, other HR classifiers (pay slip, payroll master file) will detect that content.

patterns.name: Off-cycle payroll approvals
patterns.description: Detects off-cycle and ad hoc payroll payment requests and approvals for an identified employee: off-cycle pay requests, manual/special pay runs, final pay and termination pay calculations, with payment amounts or payment date.
patterns.operation: Primary: an off-cycle payroll phrase (off-cycle payment/pay run request or approval, ad hoc or manual payment request, special or supplementary pay run, urgent payment request, final pay calculation, termination payment calculation). Generic "bonus payment", "one-off payment", "payroll approval" and "final pay" alone were removed. 75 tier requires a populated person field (employee/staff name or number, payroll number, position number, payee) with a non-placeholder value within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires a populated payment detail (gross/net amount, payment amount, amount approved, leave payout, payment in lieu of notice, redundancy pay, or a payment date) and an independent corroborative term (approved, approver, authorised, delegate, reason, termination, urgent, final pay). Enforce tiers exclude template/fixture text (template-exclusion) and policy, guidance, training and media-release framing; 65 is discovery-only (primary alone, template-excluded) and will surface policies, guidance, blank forms and statistics.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: the primary phrases also appear in policies, guidance, blank forms and news, so enforce tiers require a populated field with a non-placeholder value and 85 adds a record-specific populated detail plus independent corroboration. Person and record values are customer-defined, so the field regexes use labelled loose values with a placeholder guard. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

patterns.name: Payroll system access logs
patterns.description: Detects exported payroll system access and audit logs: timestamped log lines showing a user logging in, viewing, changing or exporting payroll records, with a populated user field. Operational security data, capped at 75.
patterns.operation: Primary: a payroll access-log phrase (payroll system access/audit/activity log or trail, access log for the payroll system, payroll audit trail, payroll login history). The single enforce tier (75) requires two distinct populated structures within 300 characters: an ISO-style timestamped event line with an action verb (logged in, login, viewed, updated, changed, exported, downloaded, approved, failed login) AND a populated user field (user, username, user ID, actor, account). Capped at 75 because access logs are operational metadata. Enforce tier excludes template/fixture text and logging-policy framing; 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low: payroll system access logs are operational security records (timestamps, user IDs, actions) rather than payroll content; they identify system users and what they touched but not pay details. The pattern is capped at 75: it needs a timestamped event line with an action verb plus a populated user field near a payroll access-log phrase. It never claims 85 because the record is low sensitivity on its own; pair with security monitoring rather than DLP blocking.

patterns.description: Detects references to consumer bank account numbers in financial and compliance documents. Commonly found in international regulatory filings, transaction records, and audit documentation.

false_positives.description: Financial terminology appearing in published reports, accounting textbooks, regulatory guidance, or template documents without actual transaction data.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords within the proximity window. Cross-reference with structured financial identifiers to confirm actual sensitive data.

false_positives.description: In English (as the primary international business language), standard business terminology overlapping with financial detection keywords in routine correspondence and documentation.
false_positives.mitigation: Increase confidence threshold when scanning business correspondence. Layer with transaction-specific patterns for higher precision.

patterns.risk_description: The detector uses structural and proximity cues to find references to consumer bank account numbers in financial or compliance material, but it is a concept recogniser rather than a country-specific checksum validator. A genuine record can expose a consumer payment destination, support fraudulent mandate setup, or enable convincing impersonation when combined with the account holder and institution. Regulatory filings, audit prose, and templates can trigger the financial vocabulary without containing a usable account number, while one true match remains bounded to an account. Risk 7 SENSITIVE reflects credible moderate consumer financial harm; PROTECTED would require a bulk account register, payment credential, or significant damage beyond the normal record.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps consistently to OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Financial, SENS_Fin, and Medium because an authentic consumer account datum can materially enable fraud or targeting. The concept detector does not establish aggregation, debit authority, or the significant consequence needed for PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium with Medium Financial suits a consumer banking record that can support material but bounded misuse. Generic High would need a master file, authorisation token, or broad direct-loss capability not shown by the match.

changelog.description: Self-corroboration fix (85 needs independent context, as #80 intended for populated-label IdMatches): Purview counts a supporting match that sits inside the IdMatch span when a word break separates it (dev-tenant run 2026-10-19; ":" and "_" break words, "=" does not), so a single labelled value reached 85 on its own label. Removed from Keyword_consumer_bank_account the terms that match inside the IdMatch label: bank account number, account number. Dropped Evidence_generic_data_labels from the 85 tier: the shared dictionary holds "account number", which sits inside the labelled IdMatch (it stays on the 65 tier). 85 now needs context outside the label. Added a 75 tier on Regex_consumer_bank_account alone: a populated label alone is 75 (the #80 convention), so the value stays enforcing.

Local noise filter: every tier above 65 opts in to the per-tenant Local Noise Exclusion dictionary (local_noise_filter: true). When the export enables it, each of those tiers gets a pattern-level TextMatchFilter (EndsWith, Exclude) reading that dictionary, so the organisation's own published values (its remit-to BSB, account number, SWIFT/BIC or IBAN) stop reaching 75/85 while the 65 tier still reports them. Detection logic and entity filters are unchanged, and the filter is inert until the customer adds entries.

patterns.risk_description: Despite its name, the regex recognises international-bank-account, beneficiary-account, wire-transfer, correspondent-bank, cross-border-payment, and account-validation topics rather than an IBAN character structure. A match can locate payment discussion, but it does not provide the country code, checksum, bank component, or account component needed to route funds. Meaningful fraud against a beneficiary requires a populated instruction and authorisation context, while generic international-payment documents are expected matches. Risk 4 OFFICIAL reflects this topic-only rail signal; SENSITIVE would require a real IBAN linked to a person or transaction.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, and Low because the detector neither validates an IBAN nor establishes account authority or ownership. The next higher SENSITIVE classification is not met because no real account value linked to a person, transaction, balance, or actionable fraud context is required.

generic.rationale: Generic Low handling suits IBAN terminology or an isolated routing identifier; contextual controls should rise when ownership, payment instructions, balances, or transaction records are present.

patterns.risk_description: The regex identifies 13- to 16-digit primary account number candidates for major card ranges, supported by payment-card and CVV context and template exclusions. A valid PAN can be combined with cardholder, expiry, or verification data for card-not-present fraud, account testing, or targeted social engineering. The normal match concerns one cardholder and one account, while test numbers, documentation, and digit strings that pass only the range syntax remain possible because the rule does not state a Luhn check. Risk 7 SENSITIVE Financial reflects credible direct payment harm; PROTECTED would require a large cardholder dataset, active acquiring access, or significant systemic compromise.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Financial because a plausible PAN can directly facilitate testing and fraud with moderate contained impact. PROTECTED is not met without validation, security codes, authentication data, or a large cardholder dataset capable of significant damage.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification and Medium Financial DLM fit a payment-card identifier that can enable fraud but is not by itself a complete or privileged payment credential set.

patterns.risk_description: The regex matches the card-dispute-case-record phrase and uses dispute, chargeback, reason-code, arbitration, record-structure, and template-exclusion evidence to identify likely case material. A genuine case record can combine cardholder identity, disputed transactions, partial card data, fraud allegations, evidence, and resolution status, enabling targeted fraud or causing financial and reputational harm. The normal affected scale is one cardholder dispute, while data inventories, training cases, and phrase-only headings remain plausible matches and do not prove a populated file. Risk 7 SENSITIVE Financial is appropriate for the composite case record; PROTECTED would require a large dispute repository, privileged acquiring access, or significant systemic compromise.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Financial, SENS_Fin, and Medium when the phrase is corroborated by an identifiable dispute, transaction, case evidence, and resolution activity. This party-specific financial and allegation harm warrants SENSITIVE handling, while PROTECTED requires a bulk case repository, systemic fraud intelligence, or significant payment-system damage.

generic.rationale: An actual card-dispute case merits Medium Financial handling because it combines attributed transaction information with contested allegations and resolution activity. A catalogue entry or general chargeback reference lacks that composite sensitivity until case fields corroborate it.

patterns.risk_description: The concept regex detects wire transfer, SWIFT code, beneficiary bank, routing number, bank account, transfer instructions, and similar payment language with seven nearby finance or record terms; a standalone code or discussion is not an instruction to move funds. When sender, beneficiary, account, amount, approval, or payment-reference fields accompany the match, disclosure or alteration can redirect money and support business-email-compromise impersonation. The usual exposure concerns one payer, one beneficiary, and one transfer, and exploitation depends on a populated instruction passing the bank's verification controls. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE Financial are appropriate for that actionable record; PROTECTED requires privileged treasury authority, exceptional strategic value, or compromise capable of significant institutional damage.

classification.rationale: OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Financial, and Medium correctly express risk 7 for a corroborated wire instruction because its alteration can cause direct transaction loss. Since the regex can also stop at routing terminology and proves no execution authority, PROTECTED is not met without high-value treasury privilege or broad institutional consequence.

generic.rationale: Medium Financial handling fits a populated transfer instruction whose beneficiary and routing details can be manipulated for a bounded payment. A SWIFT label, routing reference, or instructional template remains lower-content material until transaction and authorisation fields make it actionable.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification and Medium Financial DLM fit a payment-redirection request with direct fraud value but bounded supplier and transaction scope.

A real data-room collection may expose financial forecasts, contracts, liabilities, customer data, technology, personnel, and negotiation weaknesses, allowing a recipient to damage the seller, target, or transaction even without system access. The medium-confidence regex can also match data-room instructions and public diligence guidance, so document density and deal context matter. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Financial fit the composite commercial exposure; PROTECTED would require protected operations, active credentials, or transaction-scale compromise capable of significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy because a real diligence room is a composite record spanning sensitive corporate and participant information. PROTECTED is not met for a normal transaction set unless its contents include protected material, critical operations, or consequences amounting to significant damage.

generic.rationale: Medium with Medium Personal-Privacy handling is appropriate for a transaction data room containing broad but bounded diligence records. High depends on confirmed protected or exceptionally consequential contents, not the data-room topic alone.

patterns.risk_description: The pattern finds release-approval, approval-record, product-release, and batch-release language with seven corroborators, identifying authorization to release a product or batch rather than the underlying design or test dossier. A genuine record may reveal approvers, date, product, batch, checklist status, and disposition, creating modest fraud or timing value if altered or disclosed. The normal approval is routine quality administration and needs attached failures, proprietary criteria, or safety evidence for material confidentiality harm, while templates and policies can also match. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL are appropriate; SENSITIVE requires concealed test failures, strategic launch timing, controlled products, or consequential safety and regulator evidence.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, and Low for release or approval terminology. SENSITIVE is not met because the detector does not establish confidential product status, failed criteria, regulated disposition, approver identity, or an actionable decision record.

generic.rationale: Low classification and Low DLM reflect limited standalone consequence from release terminology without a confidential decision, adverse result, or regulated product context.

patterns.name: Password reset tokens
patterns.description: Detects password reset tokens and recovery URLs in documents, emails, and logs. Reset tokens are high-risk credentials — a leaked token enables account takeover without knowing the current password. No Microsoft built-in SIT exists for this pattern.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex engine). Matches password reset URLs containing long random token parameters, and standalone hex/base64 tokens near reset-context keywords. Corroborative evidence: 3 tiers with reset-specific keywords (high), general credential keywords (medium), and broad match (low) within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: long random strings are common in URLs and logs. Reset-context keywords are essential to distinguish password recovery tokens from session IDs, API tokens, and other opaque identifiers.

should_match.value: Reset your password using this link: https://example.com/reset?token=a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4
should_match.description: Reset URL with token query parameter
Reset token as hex string with label
JWT-style recovery token
Recovery token in URL parameter

should_not_match.value: session_id=abc123def456
should_not_match.description: Session ID too short (under 20 chars)

should_not_match.value: API response code: 200 OK
should_not_match.description: No token pattern present

should_not_match.value: Your password has been changed successfully
should_not_match.description: Password context but no token value

false_positives.description: Session tokens and API tokens in application logs that are not password reset tokens.
false_positives.mitigation: Require reset-specific keywords (reset, recover, forgot) in proximity. Generic token strings without reset context fire at low confidence only.

false_positives.description: OAuth authorization codes and CSRF tokens that share similar format.
false_positives.mitigation: Reset-specific corroborative evidence distinguishes password recovery flows from general authentication tokens.

false_positives.description: Automated email templates containing password reset URL patterns without actual token values.
false_positives.mitigation: Template exclusion filter rejects matches near sample/placeholder/example keywords.

patterns.risk_description: The detector uses several tiers to find password-reset URLs or long token values near reset language, targeting a potentially live recovery artefact rather than only the concept of passwords. A valid token can let an attacker choose a new password and take over the associated account without knowing the old credential. Generic session, API, OAuth, CSRF, and template tokens can match when nearby wording is ambiguous, and one reset token is normally account-bound, expiring, and single use. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious direct harm from a valid reset token; PROTECTED would require privileged or unusually broad account impact capable of significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, SENS_IT, and Medium because a valid reset artefact can directly enable account takeover while remaining bounded by account, expiry, and single-use controls. The detector does not establish elevated privilege or consequence at the PROTECTED threshold.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium with Medium InfoTech is suitable for a temporary account-recovery secret that can cause material direct misuse. Generic High is not inherent because validity, target privilege, and broad impact are unknown and the token is designed to expire.

patterns.risk_description: The detector identifies a TOTP provisioning artefact through an otpauth URI or a base32 seed presented with multi-factor authentication context. A usable seed lets an attacker generate the same time-based one-time codes as the enrolled factor and can defeat that factor when combined with the account identifier and primary credential. Documentation examples and synthetic enrolment fixtures can match, while a normal true positive is one revocable seed for one account rather than a tenant-wide authentication store. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious direct account-security harm; PROTECTED is not supported because the detector does not establish privileged scope, bulk seeds, or significant damage beyond the individual factor.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE InfoTech, SENS_IT, and the Medium tier because an authentic MFA seed can materially undermine one enrolled factor and enable account takeover with complementary credentials. The prior risk 10 PROTECTED outcome overstates the normal standalone unit because no bulk store, critical privilege, or major consequence is detected.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium InfoTech appropriately protect a single authentication-factor secret with serious but account-bounded misuse potential. Generic High would require evidence of privileged or aggregated seeds capable of significant organisational damage.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium InfoTech are suitable for application-authentication material capable of serious scoped misuse. Generic High requires evidence of a privileged client, broad grants, or major downstream impact beyond general OAuth terminology.

patterns.operation: Regex_soc_case_primary (SOC case/ticket/investigation or analyst-notes wording) is discovery-only at 65. 75 requires the primary plus one populated structure: a populated case field (case/ticket/alert/incident ID, severity, analyst, affected host/user, source IP, disposition) or a technical artefact (IPv4, ISO timestamp, internal hostname). 85 requires a populated case field (case/ticket/alert/incident ID, severity, analyst, affected host/user, source IP, disposition) (two distinct hits), a technical artefact (IPv4, ISO timestamp, internal hostname), and independent triage-outcome (true/false positive, escalation, containment, SIEM/EDR) evidence that does not repeat the primary. Every enforce tier rejects template/noise wording (template-exclusion) and guidance, policy, training and news framing (Keyword_soc_case_guidance_exclusion).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the topic phrase alone is discovery-only; enforcement needs populated structure (a populated case field (case/ticket/alert/incident ID, severity, analyst, affected host/user, source IP, disposition) or a technical artefact (IPv4, ISO timestamp, internal hostname)), and 85 needs two distinct structures plus independent triage-outcome (true/false positive, escalation, containment, SIEM/EDR) evidence, so policies, blank forms and training text stay below 75.

patterns.risk_description: The detector recognises DNS zone syntax and enforces only when a directive is accompanied by resource record lines, with internal-zone artefacts required at 85. Many records in a public authoritative zone are already queryable and expose no secret, although an internal or unpublished zone can reveal hostnames, addresses, services, mail routes, and infrastructure relationships useful for reconnaissance. The normal standalone file therefore creates bounded harm that depends on whether the zone is internal, complete, and non-public, affecting the domain owner and mapped systems. Risk 5 OFFICIAL is appropriate for undifferentiated zone data; SENSITIVE requires evidence of internal topology, hidden services, or consequential operational records.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, and OFFICIAL DLM because ordinary public DNS records are intentionally discoverable and even a full zone usually provides reconnaissance rather than direct access. SENSITIVE is not met without evidence that the matched file contains non-public internal records or materially consequential infrastructure detail.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Low with Low controls for undifferentiated DNS zone syntax, while internal split-horizon or hidden-service zones should be escalated when identified. Medium treatment is not warranted for records already exposed through public DNS resolution.

patterns.operation: Regex_registrar_cred_primary (domain registrar account/login, registrar credentials, transfer/auth code or EPP code wording) is discovery-only at 65. 75 requires the primary plus one populated structure: a populated credential field (username/login, account/customer ID, password, PIN, API key, EPP/auth code) or a managed domain name. 85 requires a populated credential field (username/login, account/customer ID, password, PIN, API key, EPP/auth code) (two distinct hits), a managed domain name, and independent domain-administration (renewal/expiry, nameservers, registrant, WHOIS, registrar brand) evidence that does not repeat the primary. Every enforce tier rejects template/noise wording (template-exclusion) and guidance, policy, training and news framing (Keyword_registrar_cred_guidance_exclusion).
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the topic phrase alone is discovery-only; enforcement needs populated structure (a populated credential field (username/login, account/customer ID, password, PIN, API key, EPP/auth code) or a managed domain name), and 85 needs two distinct structures plus independent domain-administration (renewal/expiry, nameservers, registrant, WHOIS, registrar brand) evidence, so policies, blank forms and training text stay below 75.

patterns.risk_description: The pattern recognises support-ticket, ticket-transcript, help-desk, and service-desk language, indicating a support record or transcript rather than proving that a password is present. A leaked transcript can support impersonation by revealing user identities, device details, error messages, troubleshooting steps, and internal escalation paths. Harm ordinarily centres on the user and service involved in one ticket, and an attacker still needs actionable account or system details from the surrounding content. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects the serious contained exposure possible in a genuine transcript; a bulk ticket corpus, privileged credentials, or broad security architecture would be needed for PROTECTED.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE InfoTech because a real ticket transcript may aggregate customer, diagnostic, and internal service information. PROTECTED is not met because the detector does not establish sensitive fields, record volume, privileged secrets, or significant broad consequence.

generic.rationale: Generic handling is Medium with Medium InfoTech controls for support transcripts, including redaction of customer, credential, and internal diagnostic details. High is reserved for bulk ticket exports or exceptionally consequential privileged cases.

patterns.risk_description: The medium-confidence concept regex recognises laboratory and pathology report language - blood test and clinical chemistry results, reference ranges, laboratory reports, and histopathology, cytology and biopsy reports - and enforces only when independent populated structure is present (labelled patient identifiers, specimen fields, result lines with units and a reference range or H/L flag, or a reporting pathologist), with template exclusions on every tier. A patient-linked result or specimen report can reveal infection, organ function, pregnancy, toxicology, malignancy, genetic findings, margins or treatment response, sometimes before the result has been communicated clinically, with serious but normally individual-scale privacy, distress and discrimination harm. Brochures, price lists, research text and teaching cases can still hit the phrase tier. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy are warranted for the corroborated record; PROTECTED requires bulk patient exposure, severe safety consequences, a protected person, or significant health-service damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps consistently to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy, and Medium when the laboratory finding is attributable to a patient. Patient-free research or guidance does not carry that harm, and PROTECTED is not met without exceptional clinical sensitivity, aggregation, life-safety impact, or significant service consequences.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling fits an identifiable patient's laboratory finding because it directly reveals current health evidence and can affect care, reputation, or treatment decisions. General test terminology and de-identified research results require patient or record corroboration before receiving that handling.

patterns.name: Immunization records
patterns.description: Identifies individual immunisation / vaccination records - immunisation history statements, vaccination records and certificates, register extracts and vaccine administration entries - when the phrase sits with populated patient identifiers and vaccine administration fields. Health information under applicable data protection regulations.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex engine). Primary: immunisation/vaccination record phrases (immunisation or immunization record/history/schedule/register/certificate/status, vaccination record/history/certificate/status, vaccine history or administration, booster dose, immunisation history statement). 65 (discovery only): phrase alone. 75: phrase plus a populated patient identifier field (name, DOB, Medicare, IHI, URN/MRN). 85: patient field plus a populated vaccine administration field (vaccine/brand, batch or lot number, dose number, date given, vaccinator, injection site) plus independent vaccine evidence (named vaccine or antigen such as influenza, MMR, DTPa, pneumococcal, hepatitis B, HPV, COVID-19, or AEFI). Template and guidance/training framing excluded from 75/85.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: enforce tiers need a populated patient identifier; 85 also needs a vaccine administration field and a named vaccine. Immunisation schedules, clinic flyers and public health campaigns carry the phrases but no patient field, so they stay at 65.

A true report may disclose the patient's condition, injury, treatment, outcome, product exposure, reporter, and chronology, and misuse can cause stigma or interfere with safety investigation and regulatory follow-up. The record has meaningful clinical and product-safety content but can be de-identified or limited, while public warnings and guidance may produce benign hits. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE are proportionate; risk 8 or PROTECTED requires an identifiable severe outcome, unreleased systemic safety signal, bulk reports, or major public-health consequence.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, Personal-Privacy DLM, and Medium because a genuine adverse-event report can expose health and affect safety review. Risk 8 and PROTECTED require severe identified harm, an unreleased systemic signal, aggregation, or significant public-health damage.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium Personal-Privacy fit an ordinary adverse-event report containing patient and product-safety details. High protection depends on severity, identifiability, aggregation, or unreleased systemic risk.

patterns.risk_description: This regex looks for churn propensity, retention models, predictive scores, and customer-risk language, with the intended unit being a person- or account-linked prediction rather than a generic model description. Disclosure can reveal which customers are considered likely to leave and the factors or interventions attached to them, enabling competitor targeting, manipulative retention, unfair treatment, or reputational harm across the scored population. The medium-confidence concept rule can also match methodology papers, aggregate dashboards, and vendor demonstrations without individual assignments. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy preserve the serious profiling outcome; PROTECTED would require protected attributes or large-scale consequential decisions capable of severe or significant damage. Quality pass 2026-09-24: enforce tiers (75/85) now require populated records - rows keyed by an identifier, labelled values or identifiers - so topic mentions in guidance, marketing and news stay at 65 discovery.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy and Medium because enforce tiers require customer-keyed churn scores or risk bands, exposing which people are predicted to leave and enabling competitor targeting or unfair treatment. PROTECTED is not met without protected attributes or large-scale consequential decisions.

generic.rationale: Medium Personal-Privacy handling applies to person-linked behavioural predictions across a scored customer base. It is not High because the scores do not drive severe individual outcomes.

patterns.name: Criminal history and police identifying particulars records
patterns.description: Identifies criminal history records and police identifying-particulars records (custody / booking photographs, photograph index numbers, fingerprints and other identifying particulars taken, linked to a named person, date of birth and police person numbers). Absorbs the former mugshot-image-repositories classifier. This information is personally identifiable law-enforcement information under applicable privacy regulations.
patterns.operation: Pattern type: regex (boost_regex engine). patterns.name: Protective and Restraining Order Records (International)
patterns.description: Detects domestic abuse protective, restraining and barring orders, police-issued protection notices, and applications for them, when the document names the parties. Covers the generic English-language order names used across jurisdictions plus United States (order of protection, protection from abuse, domestic violence restraining order, temporary restraining order, injunction for protection), United Kingdom (non-molestation order, occupation order, DVPN/DVPO, domestic abuse protection notice/order, non-harassment order), Ireland (barring, interim barring and emergency barring orders; bare "safety order" is excluded as too generic), Canada (emergency protection order, peace bond) and New Zealand (Police Safety Order) instruments. Australian state and territory DFV orders are covered in more depth by au-dfv-protection-order; the slug is retained from the earlier topic-phrase classifier.
patterns.operation: Primary: any of two regexes — a case-insensitive order/notice name list, or a case-sensitive acronym list (DVPN, DVPO, DAPN, DAPO, PFA, TRO, EPO, PSO). 75 tier requires a populated party field (petitioner, respondent, applicant, defendant, plaintiff, protected person/party, person asking for protection, restrained person, victim, perpetrator, aggrieved) with a non-placeholder name within 300 characters. 85 tier additionally requires an order condition (must not / shall not approach, contact, harass…; stay N feet/yards/metres away; within N of; surrender or relinquish firearms; no-contact order). All tiers exclude template/fixture text. 65 is discovery-only.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium: order names appear widely in legal information, court guidance and statistics, and some (occupation order, safety order, protection order) have non-DFV meanings. Enforce tiers therefore require a populated party field; 85 adds an order condition independent of the order name. 85/75 are heuristic evidence tiers, not measured accuracy.

Risk 10 and PROTECTED Government therefore apply to the confirmed record itself. The current concept regex does not validate a code. The ordinary scope is one carrier core or network segment and its subscribers and operators, while standards, architecture papers, and vendor documentation can match the same terms. For the global catalogue analogue, the confirmed substantive record is the consequence unit. Current routing, switching, trust and subscriber-control configuration can enable intrusion, interception or national communications disruption. Significant service and security damage is inherent. Risk 10 and PROTECTED InfoTech therefore apply to the confirmed record itself. Require carrier/core identity plus live routing, switching, profile or trust configuration; architecture brochures remain excluded. This is confidence and exception handling, not a reason to reduce the consequence of a true positive.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 is warranted because current routing, switching, trust and subscriber-control configuration can enable intrusion, interception or national communications disruption. PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, PROTECTED InfoTech, PROT_IT, High and High InfoTech align with that credible significant-damage case. The global expression carries the same consequence once its record structure and operational context are established. Require carrier/core identity plus live routing, switching, profile or trust configuration; architecture brochures remain excluded. Those controls govern match disposition while the confirmed record remains PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: High InfoTech handling is appropriate because current routing, switching, trust and subscriber-control configuration can enable intrusion, interception or national communications disruption. Access should be restricted to operators and engineers responsible for the affected control environment or essential service. Global policy, historical and training references remain lower-confidence exceptions rather than lower-classified records.

patterns.risk_description: This regex recognizes privacy complaints, complaint investigations, findings, breaches, regulatory complaints, corrective action, compliance, and resolution rather than validating a live case file. A genuine investigation can contain a complainant's identity, disputed personal data, witness accounts, findings, and remedial decisions, exposing the person to further privacy harm or prejudicing the inquiry. The normal true-positive unit is one complaint and a small group of subjects, investigators, and respondents, while OAIC guidance, policies, and blank forms can match. Risk 8 and SENSITIVE reflect serious contained case harm; PROTECTED would require exceptional safety risks, bulk highly sensitive records, or significant irreversible consequences.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy, and Medium because a completed investigation combines identities, disputed data, evidence, and findings. PROTECTED is not met for a normal one-complaint case without exceptional sensitivity, severe safety implications, or significant irreversible harm.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium Personal-Privacy handling suit a privacy complaint file containing identifiable evidence and investigative outcomes. High is reserved for exceptional cases with severe or irreversible consequences.

patterns.name: TRON Address
patterns.description: Detects TRON (TRX) mainnet addresses: Base58Check encoding of a 21-byte payload (0x41 version byte + 20-byte address hash), always starting with the letter "T" and exactly 34 characters long. The 0x41 prefix byte fixes the leading character as "T" and the length at 34 (58^34 > 66*256^24; 58^33 insufficient). A single leading letter is weak structure, so detection is context-gated. Prefix/length/charset verified against TRON developer docs and the TRON protocol overview.
patterns.operation: Single tier at confidence 75. The leading "T" plus exactly 33 trailing base58 chars is matched, but a single-letter prefix is weak on its own, so the tier requires cryptocurrency/wallet domain context (crypto-wallet-context dict) within proximity AND a template/sample noise NOT-group. Case-sensitive base58 (the Base58Check checksum is not expressible in a Purview-safe regex).
patterns.confidence_justification: Gated 75, not high: a single leading "T" plus a fixed-length base58 run is weak structure with no regex-expressible checksum, so it collides with other "T..."-leading 34-char base58 tokens. Precision comes from the mandatory cryptocurrency/wallet domain-context gate plus the noise exclusion. The fixed 34-char length is a modest additional constraint but not sufficient alone.
