patterns.risk_description: The detector finds an internal legal assessment quantifying the State's exposure in a specific tort, contract, statutory, or damages matter, often including probability and settlement ranges. Disclosure can reveal the State's own view of liability and likely loss, allowing claimants or counterparties to anchor demands, coordinate related claims, or undermine defence strategy. Published judgments, academic commentary, public accounting provisions, and private insurance assessments are excluded from the normal match. Risk 8 warrants SENSITIVE Legal; PROTECTED would require portfolio-wide exposure, exceptionally large fiscal consequences, or compromise causing significant State damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Legal, and Medium because candid quantum and probability analysis can seriously weaken the State's position. PROTECTED is not met by one liability assessment without significant whole-of-State fiscal or strategic damage.

generic.rationale: Medium with Medium Legal DLM protects non-public liability estimates and settlement posture while distinguishing a single matter from aggregate State exposure.

patterns.description: Detects bulk superannuation member data including individual balances, employer contributions, TFN-linked records, and beneficiary nominations from government super schemes such as QSuper.

false_positives.description: The last nine digits of a space-grouped Australian Business Number ("51 824 753 556") have the same 3-3-3 shape, and every letterhead, signature and invoice carries the organisation's ABN.

false_positives.mitigation: Require bulk indicators (multiple member records, 'extract', 'bulk', 'data file') to distinguish from individual statements

patterns.risk_description: The classifier finds a bulk superannuation member record through fund, balance, contribution, dollar-value, TFN, and member-extract cues rather than merely the word superannuation. Exposure can reveal retirement balances, employer contributions, beneficiary information, and tax-linked identifiers across several members, enabling fraud, identity theft, and targeted coercion. The bulk record joins member identity, balances, beneficiaries and account data across many people, enabling systemic fraud, targeting and enduring financial privacy harm. The normal true-positive unit belongs at risk 9, PROTECTED Financial, while broad or contextual false positives remain a separate detection issue.

classification.rationale: The QLD custom classifier is assessed on its confirmed substantive record rather than an uncorroborated topic hit. The bulk record joins member identity, balances, beneficiaries and account data across many people, enabling systemic fraud, targeting and enduring financial privacy harm. Accordingly the workbook should record risk 9, PROTECTED in both frameworks, PROTECTED Financial, PROT_Fin and High rather than retain the Medium tier.

generic.rationale: Bulk superannuation statements are High Financial information because they aggregate identities, balances, beneficiaries and account data across a member population. The QLD custom classifier carries High Financial handling when its substantive match is confirmed.

patterns.name: Surrogacy Arrangement Record
patterns.description: Detects surrogacy arrangement records including parentage orders, surrogacy agreements, birth mother medical records, and intended parent assessments under the Surrogacy Act 2010 (Qld). These records contain deeply personal information about reproductive choices, medical procedures, and legal parentage transfers — disclosure can cause severe emotional distress and breach court-sealed parentage orders.
patterns.operation: Primary: surrogacy phrases (surrogacy arrangement/agreement, parentage order, gestational carrier/surrogacy, birth mother consent/identity, intended parents assessment, surrogacy counselling report). 65 = phrase only (discovery). 75 = phrase plus a populated party field (birth mother, intended parents, surrogate, child, counsellor, name, date of birth, file number) or a labelled file reference. 85 = phrase plus two distinct populated fields plus independent evidence (Surrogacy Act 2010, counselling certificate, independent legal advice, embryo transfer, IVF ...). patterns.name: Thailand Passport Number
patterns.description: Detects Thai passport numbers issued by the Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand. Documented formats are one letter followed by six digits (older series, e.g. A123456), two letters followed by six digits (e.g. AA123456), or two letters followed by seven digits (current e-passport series, e.g. AA1234567, nine characters total matching the MRZ document-number field). Note: the legacy A123456 / AA123456 forms are documented by a single source (Thai Wikipedia); the current AA1234567 form is corroborated independently via the MRZ document-number field.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern (boost_regex engine). Regex_th_passport_number matches the three documented forms — 1 letter + 6 digits, 2 letters + 6 digits, or 2 letters + 7 digits — at word boundaries. The letter prefix is case-fixed (uppercase, matching the printed document and MRZ document-number field), so the pattern is case-sensitive. Three confidence tiers: High (85) requires passport evidence (min 2 unique terms) with template exclusion; Medium (75) requires passport evidence with template exclusion; Low (65) requires passport evidence. Evidence uses one keyword group (English and Thai passport terms) within 300-character proximity. No public checksum is documented for the printed number, so detection is structural plus keyword evidence.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: short letter-prefixed alphanumeric runs (1-2 letters + 6-7 digits) are common in order codes, bookings and other reference numbers, so corroborating passport keywords are required on every tier. No tier fires on the bare value alone (D1 identifier convention).

patterns.risk_description: The Thai passport SIT detects documented older one- or two-letter formats with six digits and the current two-letter, seven-digit e-passport form near passport terms; it does not find the document image or consular file. Disclosure could help complete a visa or airline form and support an impersonation pretext when the traveller's name and document dates are known. One match normally affects one holder, while bookings, order codes, and unbracketed Hong Kong identity-card-like values can share the shorter shapes. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL recognise the limited standalone harm; SENSITIVE would require the passport page, credentials, or a detailed linked identity and itinerary record.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 and OFFICIAL are proportionate because the Thai passport number is a short, context-gated reference and some legacy format evidence is less authoritative. SENSITIVE is not met without verified document contents, authentication data, or extensive personal information enabling direct fraud.

generic.rationale: The generic Low outcome reflects one travel-document identifier with bounded misuse value and material overlap across short alphanumeric reference formats.

patterns.name: Turkish Passport Number
patterns.description: Detects Turkish (Türkiye) ordinary ("umuma mahsus", bordo/burgundy) passport numbers. New-generation ordinary passports, issued by the General Directorate of Civil Registration and Citizenship (Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü, NVİ) since 2018, carry a nine-character document number consisting of the series letter "U" followed by eight digits (e.g. U12345678), printed in the top-right corner of the data page. Turkish sources report different series letters for the special/green (hususi, "S") and service/grey (hizmet, "Z") passports; those series are NOT covered by this pattern because their letter-plus-digit shape could not be independently corroborated. Ordinary bordo passports are by far the dominant variant.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern (boost_regex engine). Regex_tr_passport matches the letter U followed by exactly eight digits with word boundaries so the value is not found inside longer alphanumeric runs. The document number is case-fixed (uppercase U), so the pattern is case-sensitive. No public checksum is documented for the printed passport number, so detection relies on structure plus corroborating evidence: every tier requires Turkish passport keywords or label context — there is no bare value-only tier. High (85) requires label context plus passport keywords with template exclusion; Medium (75) requires passport keywords with template exclusion; Low (65) requires domain-context keywords. AllDigitsSameFilter suppresses repeated-digit placeholders such as U00000000. Older (pre-2018) non-chip Turkish passports used different serial formats and are not targeted by this pattern. Known false-negative scope: hususi ("S" series, green) and hizmet ("Z" series, grey) passport numbers are reported by secondary sources but not corroborated, so they are deliberately out of scope; extend the leading letter class only if the S/Z + 8-digit shape is confirmed against real documents.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the fixed "U" prefix plus exact eight-digit tail is structurally distinctive, but letter-plus-digits codes occur in invoices, SKUs and other identifiers. The issuing authority (NVİ) publishes no number-format specification and Turkish secondary sources conflict on the digit count (U+6, U+7 and U+8 are all claimed), so the U + 8-digit shape rests on real-world document instances and on consistency with the nine-character ICAO Doc 9303 document-number field rather than on a published standard. All tiers therefore require corroborating passport keywords, which is also why the evidence-gated 75 tier is the recommended workhorse.
regulations: KVKK (Law No. 6698 on Protection of Personal Data) (Turkey)

The ordinary unit is one document reference, while invoices, SKUs, and tracking codes beginning with U can mimic the format and no printed checksum is available. patterns.name: Vergi Kimlik Numarası (Turkish Tax Identification Number)
patterns.description: Detects the Turkish tax identification number (Vergi Kimlik Numarası, VKN) issued by the Turkish Revenue Administration (Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı, GİB). The VKN is a 10-digit number structured as a 3-digit alpha group code (001-999), a 6-digit sequence number and a single check digit. Since 1 July 2006 Turkish citizens use their 11-digit T.C. Kimlik Numarası as their tax number (covered by the separate tr-national-id pattern); the 10-digit VKN remains the tax identifier for legal entities, ordinary partnerships, foreign legal entities and foreign nationals without a Foreign Identity Number.
patterns.operation: Checksum: the 10th digit is a check digit computed over the first nine digits (NOT enforced in this regex-only pattern; structural detection only). Regex_tr_tax_number matches ten digits whose leading 3-digit alpha group code is 001-999 (000 is not issued), with word boundaries so an 11-digit T.C. Kimlik Numarası or longer digit run never partially matches. Every tier requires positive evidence — there is no bare value-only tier: High (85) requires tax label context plus VKN keywords with template exclusion; Medium (75) requires VKN keywords with template exclusion; Low (65) requires domain-context keywords. AllDigitsSameFilter suppresses repeated-digit placeholders such as 1111111111. Relationship to tr-national-id: the two patterns are structurally disjoint (10 digits vs 11 digits, both boundary-guarded), so no value matches both.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: 10-digit numeric strings are common (phone numbers, order numbers, other countries' identifiers such as Saudi national IDs), and the VKN check digit cannot be expressed in a regex, so corroborating tax keywords are required on every tier. The evidence-gated 75 tier is the recommended workhorse per identifier convention.
regulations: KVKK (Law No. 6698 on Protection of Personal Data) (Turkey)
Law No. 4358 on Expanding the Use of Tax Identification Numbers (Türkiye)

Since Turkish citizens use their 11-digit national identity number for tax, the VKN normally identifies legal entities, partnerships, foreign legal entities, or some foreign nationals rather than a resident citizen's personal tax account. Disclosure can aid company profiling or invoice impersonation, yet it does not expose tax filings, financial position, or authentication data and often concerns an organisation. Risk 4 and OFFICIAL are appropriate, while a person-linked foreign-tax file or confidential entity assessment containing the VKN would warrant SENSITIVE.

SENSITIVE is not met unless the number is linked to an individual foreign taxpayer or substantive nonpublic tax records.

patterns.name: Traffic Camera Record
patterns.description: Detects traffic camera and speed camera infringement records containing driver identification details, vehicle registration, and photographic evidence references, and automatic number plate recognition (ANPR / ALPR) read records that place a plate at a camera site, lane, direction and time. These records link specific vehicles and individuals to locations and traffic offences via camera evidence under the Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld). Absorbs the former automated-plate-reader-data classifier.
patterns.operation: Primary: camera phrases (traffic / speed / red light camera record, detection or infringement, infringement notice, penalty infringement notice, registered operator, automatic number plate recognition, ANPR, ALPR, plate reader / plate read). 65 = phrase only (discovery). 75 = phrase plus one populated camera read field (plate / registration / rego / VRM, camera / site / reader ID, lane, direction of travel, read / capture time, timestamp) or a labelled infringement notice number. 85 = phrase plus two distinct read fields, or two different independent evidence types (read fields, notice number, penalty-process terms such as demerit points, enforcement order, km/h, fine). Road safety campaigns, published camera location lists, reviews and statistics excluded.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: requires camera terminology with populated vehicle / site read fields or a labelled notice number; notice-number formats are unpublished, so the reference is a documented label-anchored fallback.

patterns.risk_description: This detector finds a traffic or speed-camera infringement record linking a registered operator or identified driver to a vehicle, location, timestamp, measured conduct, image reference, notice, and penalty, or an ANPR read record placing a plate at a camera site, lane and direction at a given time. Disclosure can reveal a person's movements and alleged offence, expose an address or registration, and support harassment or fraudulent social engineering around a genuine infringement. Published camera locations, road-safety campaigns, motoring articles, and aggregate enforcement statistics are excluded, so the normal match is an attributed administrative enforcement record. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE Legal; PROTECTED would require protected-location tracking, systematic movement surveillance, or compromise of a large enforcement repository.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Legal, and Medium because one attributed camera record exposes movement, vehicle, and offence information with credible direct harm. PROTECTED is not met without protected locations, systematic tracking, or repository-scale compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium and Medium Legal DLM protect attributed infringement and movement evidence while distinguishing one record from a comprehensive surveillance or enforcement database.

changelog.description: Add the classification block (tier, rationale, generic classification/DLM/rationale). Text copied verbatim from the reviewed SIT-Reference master, which until now held it only in PurviewDeploy.

Quality pass (2026-09-24): removed the invented TIN-YYYY-XXX-NNNNNN notice-reference detector family (a primary with its own 65/75/85 tiers), the invented PIN-YYYY-NNNNNNN regex and the invented SC-/RLC-NNNN camera-site regex (camera / site IDs are already covered by the labelled read fields); a labelled infringement notice number now uses the new infringement-notice-number fallback (identifier-format slot); 75 = camera phrase + a populated read field or a labelled notice number; 85 = two distinct read fields, or two different evidence types (read fields, notice number, penalty-process terms); tests converted to labelled notice numbers and site IDs with a blank-form decoy; references added.

Merge global-top500-409-automated-plate-reader-data into this classifier (Qld government classifier review 2026-09-24): camera-phrase regex gains automatic number / licence plate recognition, ANPR, ALPR, number / licence plate recognition / reader and plate read(er), and becomes a second primary family (65 phrase / 75 plus one populated read field, TIN / PIN reference or camera site ID / 85 plus two read fields or two independent evidence types). New Regex_..._read_fields recognises populated ANPR read-record fields: plate / registration / rego / VRM, camera / site / reader ID, lane, direction of travel, read / capture time and timestamp. TIN-reference 85 tier simplified (it required TIN and PIN references, site ID and every keyword group at once, and no test reached it) to camera keyword plus one of read fields, penalty-process terms or a PIN reference; "registered operator" removed from the corroborative list because it is already a primary keyword. Not imported: bare licence plate, number plate, registration plate, plate number, vehicle tracking and vehicle identification (everyday vehicle-sale / insurance vocabulary) and the absorbed self-corroborating label/domain tiers. Added an 85 ANPR read record, a 75 ANPR search result, and ANPR explainer and vendor-copy decoys. Risk unchanged at 7 (ANPR read records of a single vehicle are an administrative movement record; the absorbed classifier rated 8 for bulk tracking data, noted but not adopted).

generic.rationale: Taiwan physical-address indicators are generically Low with Low DLM because fragmentary road and lane markers need hierarchical and personal context for meaningful harm.

patterns.name: Ukrainian Individual Tax Number (RNOKPP)
patterns.description: Detects the Ukrainian individual tax number — the registration number of the taxpayer's account card (РНОКПП / RNOKPP, historically called RNTRC or ІПН), assigned by the State Tax Service of Ukraine to every individual taxpayer in the State Register of Individuals – Taxpayers. Per the OECD AEOI TIN description for Ukraine, the RNOKPP is a ten-digit numerical code (no letters, hyphens, or other symbols) with structure XXXXXNNNNK: a 5-digit birth-date registration sequence, a 4-digit account-card sequence, and a control digit.
patterns.operation: Regex pattern. Matches a contiguous 10-digit numerical code with digit-run boundaries. The mod-11 weighted control-digit algorithm used for the final digit cannot be expressed in regex and is NOT enforced; detection is structural. Because bare 10-digit runs are highly ambiguous (phone numbers, account numbers), every confidence tier requires positive RNOKPP/tax evidence: High (85) requires an RNOKPP/tax label-context match plus specific keywords with template exclusion; Medium (75) requires specific RNOKPP keywords with template exclusion; Low (65) requires domain-context tax keywords with template exclusion. AllDigitsSameFilter suppresses all-zeros and other repeated-digit values.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: a 10-digit run has no distinctive internal structure that regex can enforce (the birth-date sequence and control digit are not range-restricted in public documentation), so corroborating RNOKPP/tax keywords are required on every tier and no bare value-only tier is exposed.

should_match.description: 10-digit RNOKPP with English label

should_not_match.description: 8-digit EDRPOU entity code — wrong length for the 10-digit individual number

should_not_match.value: TIN: 123-456-789 registered with the BIR in Manila
should_not_match.description: Neighbouring format — Philippine dash-grouped 9-digit TIN, no 10-digit run

should_not_match.value: Passport record 31847106912 has too many digits to be a taxpayer number
should_not_match.description: 11-digit run — the 10-digit code must not match inside a longer digit run
Repeated-digit value — matches structurally but is suppressed by AllDigitsSameFilter

false_positives.description: Ukrainian phone numbers written without separators (e.g. 0671234567) and many other 10-digit runs (US phone numbers, account numbers) match the structural regex.
false_positives.mitigation: Every tier requires RNOKPP/tax keyword or label evidence within the 300-character proximity window; no value-only tier is exposed.

false_positives.description: The final control digit uses a weighted mod-11 algorithm that cannot be expressed in regex, so structurally valid but non-issued numbers will match.
false_positives.mitigation: Rely on structure, AllDigitsSameFilter (suppresses all-zeros/repeated-digit values) and mandatory keyword evidence.

patterns.risk_description: The detector finds a contiguous 10-digit Ukrainian RNOKPP with mandatory tax or RNOKPP context and repeated-digit suppression, but it cannot enforce the weighted control digit. A genuine number uniquely identifies an individual taxpayer and embeds a birth-date registration sequence, supporting taxpayer impersonation, identity correlation, and targeted financial fraud. The normal unit concerns one person with credible moderate privacy and tax harm, although phone numbers and other 10-digit values can collide when context is weak. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE are justified, while PROTECTED is not met without authentication factors, a full tax account, bulk register, or significant state-system compromise.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 reconciles with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Financial because a genuine RNOKPP is a persistent individual taxpayer identifier with moderate direct fraud and correlation value. PROTECTED is not met because the identifier does not itself grant access or establish broad high-impact compromise.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification and Medium Financial DLM fit an individual Ukrainian tax identifier with credible fraud value but no standalone authentication capability.

patterns.name: UK Companies House Company Number
patterns.description: Detects UK Companies House company registration numbers (CRNs). A company number is always 8 characters: either 8 digits (England & Wales incorporations), a 2-letter jurisdiction/entity-type prefix followed by 6 digits (e.g. SC Scottish company, NI Northern Ireland company, OC/SO/NC LLPs, RC/SR/NR royal-charter bodies, FC overseas companies, OE overseas entities), or R0 + 6 digits (pre-partition Northern Ireland companies, registered under the R0 prefix). The prefix allow-list is taken from the Companies House Uniform Resource Identifiers (URI) Customer Guide plus the post-2011 additions CE/CS (charitable incorporated organisations), SG (Scottish qualifying partnerships), OE (Register of Overseas Entities, 2022), RS (registered societies, e.g. the live entry RS008375) and FE (further education / sixth form college corporations). Bare 8-digit runs collide heavily with invoice, order and account numbers, so the all-numeric form is only ever matched when directly attached to a company-number label; the more distinctive prefixed form additionally gets a keyword-gated tier without a directly-attached label. Two allow-list prefixes are excluded from that bare prefixed form because they collide with common document-number abbreviations — NO ("INVOICE NO123456") and SO (ERP sales-order numbers such as SO123456) — and are matched only via the label-attached regex.
patterns.operation: Validation: none — Companies House numbers are sequential allocations with no check digit, so no checksum validator exists. Reference: Companies House URI Customer Guide (List of Company Numbers and Prefixes). Detection is label-embedded regex (Regex_uk_companies_house_labelled) for all forms, plus a prefix-allow-list structural regex (Regex_uk_companies_house_prefixed) that is only exported behind Companies House keyword evidence. AllDigitsSameFilter guards the all-numeric form against sentinel values such as 11111111. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the 8-character structure is rigid and the prefix allow-list is verified against Companies House documentation, but there is no check digit, and the all-numeric form is indistinguishable from any other 8-digit reference without its label. Every exported tier is evidence-gated — the all-numeric form requires a directly-attached company-number label (label-embedded-in-regex counts as label gating per the D1 decision record), and the bare prefixed form additionally requires Companies House keywords in proximity. The bare prefixed form also drops the collision-prone NO and SO prefixes (document-number abbreviations that appear near generic keywords like "registered office" in UK letter footers); those two prefixes are covered only when label-attached. There is deliberately no bare unlabelled tier.

should_match.description: Labelled all-numeric England & Wales company number
Labelled Scottish company number with SC prefix
CRN-labelled England & Wales LLP number with OC prefix
Registered-number label with 8-digit company number
Companies House label with Northern Ireland prefix
Pre-partition Northern Ireland company number (R0 prefix + 6 digits)
Bare Register of Overseas Entities number (prefixed structural regex, keyword-gated tier)
Bare registered-society number — live Companies House entry (Nurture Housing Association Limited), RS prefix

should_not_match.value: Invoice number: 12345678
should_not_match.description: 8-digit run attached to a non-company label — the all-numeric form is label-gated

should_not_match.value: Company number: 1234567
should_not_match.description: Only 7 digits, too short for a company number

should_not_match.value: Company number: 123456789
should_not_match.description: 9 digits — the trailing alphanumeric guard rejects longer digit runs

should_not_match.value: Company number: AB123456
should_not_match.description: AB is not a Companies House prefix — fails the verified prefix allow-list

should_not_match.value: Company number: R1234567
should_not_match.description: R followed by a non-zero digit — only the documented R0 + 6 digit form is a valid pre-partition Northern Ireland number

should_not_match.value: INVOICE NO123456
should_not_match.description: NO as the "number" abbreviation in an invoice header — NO is excluded from the bare prefixed regex and only matched label-attached

should_not_match.value: SALES ORDER SO123456
should_not_match.description: SO as an ERP sales-order document prefix — SO is excluded from the bare prefixed regex and only matched label-attached

false_positives.description: Unlabelled 8-digit sequences (invoices, order numbers, phone fragments) share the all-numeric company number shape exactly, and sentinel values such as 11111111 or 00000000 satisfy it too.
false_positives.mitigation: The all-numeric form is only matched when directly attached to a company-number label; AllDigitsSameFilter drops repeated-digit sentinels. There is no bare unlabelled tier.

false_positives.description: Two-letter + 6-digit codes from other schemes (ticket references, product SKUs, non-UK registries) can coincide with the prefixed form, e.g. SC/NI also appear in unrelated codes.
false_positives.mitigation: The prefixed structural regex is restricted to the verified Companies House prefix allow-list and is only exported behind Companies House keyword evidence within the proximity window. In the exported SIT the prefix match is case-sensitive (prefixes are always upper case). NO and SO are additionally removed from the bare prefixed regex — NO is the ubiquitous "number" abbreviation (INVOICE NO123456, ACCOUNT NO123456) and SO is a common ERP sales-order document prefix, both of which co-occur with footer keywords such as "registered office" — so those two prefixes match only in the label-attached form.

patterns.risk_description: The detector recognizes labelled eight-digit UK company numbers and allow-listed two-letter-prefix forms, with extra controls for collision-prone NO and SO prefixes. A Companies House number is a public legal-entity reference used on filings, letterheads, and registry searches, not personal data or corporate authentication. It can help link documents or lend credibility to a false supplier or filing, but the attacker also needs officer or representative information, credentials, and access to a commercial or registry process. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL reflect that bounded corporate-impersonation value; confidential ownership, banking, transaction, or account-control material would raise the context toward SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, DLM OFFICIAL, and Low for a public UK company registration number. SENSITIVE is not met because the number neither exposes personal information nor grants authority to file, contract, change payment details, or control the company.

generic.rationale: Low and Low DLM correctly describe a public entity identifier with bounded document-linkage and spoofing value. The sensitive unit would be a private corporate record, credential, bank instruction, or substantive transaction, not the Companies House number.

patterns.name: UK Marking - OFFICIAL / OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE
patterns.description: Detects the UK Government Security Classifications Policy (GSCP) OFFICIAL classification and its -SENSITIVE marking, written OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE and applied immediately after the OFFICIAL classification per the current policy. Matches the verified structured "CLASSIFICATION - HANDLING INSTRUCTION[- DESCRIPTOR]" format (e.g. OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE - RECIPIENTS ONLY, OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE - COMMERCIAL) using the centrally-defined GSCP handling-instruction and descriptor vocabulary, the bare OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE banner, and — at a lower, UK-government-context gated tier — bare OFFICIAL alone, which is a common English word. Regex logic verified directly against the current Government Security Classifications Policy (gov.uk, version 2.0, August 2024); matched case-sensitively so ordinary lowercase English use of "official"/"official-sensitive" does not trigger it.
patterns.operation: Tier 85 matches the fully structured "OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE - <handling instruction/descriptor>" form using the centrally-defined GSCP vocabulary (RECIPIENTS ONLY, FOR PUBLIC RELEASE, HMG USE ONLY, EMBARGOED, PERSONAL DATA, LEGAL PROFESSIONAL PRIVILEGE/LPP, LEGAL, MARKET SENSITIVE, COMMERCIAL, HR/MANAGEMENT). A second tier 85 matches the bare OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE banner (no descriptor required). Tier 65 matches the bare OFFICIAL classification alone, gated by UK central-government/ GSCP corroborative context and a NOT-exclusion for common non-government OFFICIAL collocations (OFFICIAL WEBSITE, OFFICIAL SPONSOR, OFFICIAL SECRETS ACT, etc).
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence on the OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE hyphenated marking, in both its structured handling-instruction/descriptor form and its bare banner form: both are case-sensitive, structurally distinctive tokens verified directly against the current GSCP primary source, with negligible natural-English collision risk. Bare OFFICIAL alone (65) is the widest tier and is highly collision-prone — a common English adjective used constantly outside government contexts (OFFICIAL WEBSITE, OFFICIAL SPONSOR, OFFICIAL RECEIVER, OFFICIAL SECRETS ACT citations, etc) — so it requires UK central-government/GSCP corroborative evidence within 300 characters plus a dedicated NOT-exclusion for the most common non-marking collocations.

false_positives.mitigation: The bare tier (65) requires UK central-government/GSCP corroborative evidence and excludes this collocation set via a dedicated NOT-group. The structured and banner OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE tiers (both 85) are unaffected — they are structurally distinctive and do not require the gate.

false_positives.description: This SIT's OFFICIAL/OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE vocabulary overlaps with the Australian PSPF scheme: AU's au-marking-official ships its own bare OFFICIAL banner tier (85) ungated apart from a noise-exclusion NOT-group (no AU-context requirement), and au-marking-sensitive's OFFICIAL: Sensitive stem tier (90) uses a different separator convention (colon/space/`//`, not a fixed hyphen). A genuine UK OFFICIAL or OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE document will typically NOT co-fire the AU SITs (different separator syntax), but the bare word "OFFICIAL" appearing in UK government prose could coincidentally satisfy AU's ungated bare-OFFICIAL tier if it also happens to read as an AU marking banner.
false_positives.mitigation: Deploy policies should expect occasional cross-jurisdiction co-fire on the bare-word vocabulary as a corroborating, not conflicting, signal; do not add a UK-exclusion to the AU SIT, as that would break its own (broader, deliberately ungated) intended coverage.

false_positives.description: The GSCP's "[INSERT ORGANISATION(S) NAME] USE ONLY" handling instruction and centrally-allocated Codewords are not machine-matchable: organisation names and codewords are arbitrary text assigned per-asset, not fixed vocabulary, so no regex can enumerate them. Similarly, the GSCP's REL EU releasability marking (used alongside a UK-prefixed OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE asset shared with an EU institution) is rendered inconsistently in the primary source itself (prose text reads "REL EU", the source's own worked example renders it "REL-EU" on the following line) — the exact character-level syntax cannot be pinned down from the primary source, so it is not implemented.
false_positives.mitigation: No mitigation implemented — documented as a known coverage gap rather than guessing at unverified syntax. The structured handling-instruction/descriptor tier and the bare banner tier remain the reliable, verified signals.

patterns.risk_description: The regex identifies UK OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE markings, including structured handling instructions such as recipients only, personal data, legal privilege, market sensitive, or commercial. A genuine match can cover routine government business at the lower branch or materially harmful personal, legal, or commercial information at the sensitive branch. Bare OFFICIAL requires UK context because the word is common, while OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE is a stronger direct signal. Risk 8 preserves SENSITIVE for the combined detector; PROTECTED would require SECRET or TOP SECRET, a protected operation, critical-service exposure, severe safety harm, or another credible significant-damage case.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 maps to SENSITIVE and Medium tiers because the detector includes OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE handling instructions with material but contained consequences. PROTECTED is not met without a higher UK classification or credible significant strategic, safety, operational, or systemic damage.

generic.rationale: A UK OFFICIAL/OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE marking match is generically Medium with Medium Government DLM because the combined detector includes elevated handling but not SECRET-level consequence.

patterns.name: UK Marking - SECRET / TOP SECRET
patterns.description: Detects the UK Government Security Classifications Policy (GSCP) SECRET and TOP SECRET national-security classifications: the verified UK Prefix form (UK SECRET / UK TOP SECRET, applied to assets shared with foreign governments or international organisations), the classification followed by a verified National Caveat handling instruction (SECRET/TOP SECRET - UK EYES ONLY, - UK/US EYES ONLY, - FIVE EYES ONLY, per the GSCP's "CLASSIFICATION - HANDLING INSTRUCTION" additional-marking format — National Caveats apply only to SECRET and TOP SECRET, never OFFICIAL), the distinctive TOP SECRET banner-words phrase, and a UK-government-context-gated bare SECRET banner. Intended to surface content that should not reside on this platform. Regex logic verified directly against the current Government Security Classifications Policy (gov.uk, version 2.0, August 2024); matched case-sensitively.
patterns.operation: Tier 85 matches the UK Prefix form (UK SECRET / UK TOP SECRET). A second tier 85 matches the classification followed directly by a National Caveat handling instruction (UK EYES ONLY, UK/US EYES ONLY, FIVE EYES ONLY). A third tier 85 matches the TOP SECRET banner-words phrase, tolerant of a hyphen or PDF-line-wrap-inserted whitespace between TOP and SECRET. Tier 75 matches the bare SECRET banner, gated by UK central-government/GSCP corroborative context and a NOT-exclusion for common non-government SECRET collocations (TRADE SECRET(S), CLIENT SECRET, API SECRET, SECRET MANAGER, SECRET SANTA).
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence on the UK Prefix form and the National Caveat form: both are verified directly against the current GSCP primary source, structurally distinctive, case-sensitive tokens with low natural-English collision risk. The TOP SECRET banner-words phrase is likewise high confidence (case-sensitive two-word phrase). Bare SECRET alone (75) is a common English word used constantly outside government context (TRADE SECRET, CLIENT SECRET, API SECRET, SECRET MANAGER, SECRET SANTA, etc), so it is the widest tier and is gated by UK central-government/GSCP corroborative evidence plus a dedicated NOT-exclusion for the most common non-government collocations.

false_positives.description: ALL-CAPS prose (legal boilerplate, headers, or documents rendered entirely in capitals) defeats the case-sensitivity signal the bare TOP SECRET banner-words tier relies on — any all-caps rendering of the phrase (e.g. a film or product title) can fire with no protective-marking intent.
false_positives.mitigation: Treat banner-tier-only (85) hits as lower confidence when the surrounding text is itself all-caps; the UK Prefix and National Caveat tiers (both 85, structurally verified) remain the more reliable signal.

false_positives.description: SECRET is an extremely common English word in everyday non-government usage (TRADE SECRET(S), CLIENT SECRET, API SECRET, SECRET MANAGER, SECRET SANTA), all more common in general text than the GSCP classification marking.
false_positives.mitigation: The bare tier (75) requires UK central-government/GSCP corroborative evidence and excludes this collocation set via a dedicated NOT-group (SECRET SANTA is added to this SIT's exclusion group as a hardening beyond the equivalent nz-marking-secret-topsecret exclusion set, which documents SECRET SANTA only as a residual risk rather than excluding it). SECRET KEY is deliberately NOT excluded, as it is plausible inside genuinely classified COMSEC prose. The UK Prefix, National Caveat, and TOP SECRET banner-words tiers (all 85) are unaffected — they are structurally distinctive and do not require the gate.

false_positives.description: This SIT's vocabulary overlaps with the Australian PSPF and New Zealand PSR marking families: au-marking-secret-topsecret and au-marking-protected ship their own bare SECRET/TOP SECRET tiers ungated apart from noise/collocation NOT-groups (no AU-context requirement), and nz-marking-secret-topsecret ships an equivalent gated bare-SECRET tier and its own TOP SECRET banner-words tier. A genuine UK SECRET or TOP SECRET document will therefore typically co-fire the AU SITs (shared bare-word vocabulary, no jurisdiction gate on their side) and may co-fire the NZ SIT if NZ/PSR corroborative context also happens to be present.
false_positives.mitigation: Deploy policies should expect this cross-jurisdiction co-fire and treat the SITs as corroborating, not conflicting, signals; do not add a UK-exclusion to the AU/NZ SITs, as that would break their own intended (broader or independently-gated) coverage.

false_positives.description: us-classification-banner uses the Five-Eyes "//" control/dissemination-marking separator (e.g. SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY), which is structurally distinct from the UK GSCP's own hyphen-separated additional-marking format (CLASSIFICATION - HANDLING INSTRUCTION - CODEWORD - NATIONAL CAVEAT). A UK document using only the native GSCP hyphen format will not co-fire us-classification-banner; a UK document that separately also carries an interoperable Five-Eyes "//"-marked control token would co-fire both, which is expected and correct.
false_positives.mitigation: No mitigation needed — the two SITs detect genuinely different (if occasionally co-occurring) marking syntaxes.

false_positives.description: Two verified GSCP forms are not implemented as machine-matchable regex: (1) Codewords are single arbitrary CAPITALISED words, centrally allocated per-asset — the GSCP's own worked example literally uses the placeholder text "CODEWORD", which is illustrative, not real recurring vocabulary, so no fixed regex can enumerate genuine codewords; (2) the fully-layered "PREFIX CLASSIFICATION - HANDLING INSTRUCTION - CODEWORD - NATIONAL CAVEAT" form (e.g. the GSCP's own "UK SECRET - CODEWORD - UK EYES ONLY" example) is not matched when a handling instruction or codeword segment sits between the classification and the National Caveat — the caveat-tier regex requires the caveat to follow the classification directly.
false_positives.mitigation: No mitigation implemented — documented as a known coverage gap rather than guessing at unverified intervening-segment syntax. The direct-adjacency UK Prefix, National Caveat, and TOP SECRET banner-words tiers remain the reliable, verified signals.

patterns.risk_description: This detector finds UK SECRET and TOP SECRET markings through UK-prefixed forms, national caveats, TOP SECRET banner words, or a government-gated SECRET banner. A confirmed asset can expose defence, intelligence, diplomatic, protected-operation, or human-safety information and cause broad national or allied damage. The rule excludes common trade-secret and API-secret collocations, leaving all-caps titles as the main residual collision. Risk 10 maps to PROTECTED as the maximum Australian crosswalk; no higher QGISCF tier exists, and remediation must preserve the native UK SECRET or TOP SECRET controls.

classification.rationale: Risk 10 maps to the maximum PSPF/QGISCF PROTECTED tier, Marking Protected DLM, and High because compromise can cause strategic, allied, or life-safety damage. No higher QGISCF classification exists, while native UK controls still apply.

generic.rationale: UK SECRET or TOP SECRET markings are generically High with High DLM because they identify national-security information capable of major strategic harm.

patterns.name: UK Phone Number
patterns.description: Detects UK national telephone numbers per Ofcom's National Telephone Numbering Plan: geographic numbers (01/02 prefix) and mobile numbers (07 prefix, second digit restricted to 1-5 or 7-9, plus the 07624 Isle of Man mobile range — the one mobile block inside the otherwise-excluded 076 radiopaging range, allocated to Isle of Man operators under the UK plan; 070 personal-numbering and the rest of 076 remain excluded), both as 11-digit domestic strings (leading 0 + 10 significant digits), plus the +44 international form (10 significant digits, leading 0 dropped per ITU/Ofcom convention). Digit groups after the initial prefix use a flexible per-digit optional separator rather than a single fixed grouping, because Ofcom's numbering plan allows multiple valid group-length conventions (4+6, 3+7, 2+8, 5+5) that vary by area. Two additional conventional renderings are covered: the parenthesised-area-code national notation for geographic numbers, e.g. "(020) 7946 0958" / "(01632) 960960" (ITU-T E.123 national notation, parentheses marking the optionally-dialled area code, for 2-5 digit area codes), and the widespread "+44 (0)20 7946 0958" letterhead form (a common-but-nonstandard practice — E.123 advises against the parenthesised trunk digit in international notation, but it is ubiquitous in UK signatures and letterheads, so it is matched for detection purposes). Non-geographic service numbers (03/08/09) are intentionally out of scope — they are typically organizational/service numbers rather than personal PII, mirroring how au-fixed-line-telephone scopes to geographic numbers only.
patterns.operation: Validation: none (UK numbers have no checksum). Reference: Ofcom National Telephone Numbering Plan, https://www.ofcom.org.uk/phones-and-broadband/phone-numbers/numbering. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: phone-context. Both the domestic and international (+44) sub-regexes are evidence-gated at every tier — no tier fires without positive corroborative evidence, per the phone-family convention — see confidence_justification.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the geographic (01/02) and mobile (07 with second-digit restriction) prefix constraints narrow the format, but UK numbers carry no checksum and an 11-digit UK-shaped domestic sequence still collides with other structured identifiers. Per the phone-family convention set by au-fixed-line-telephone (every tier requires positive corroborative evidence; high digit-collision formats never get a zero-evidence tier), both the domestic and +44 international sub-regexes are evidence-gated at every tier: 75 requires generic phone-context evidence and 85 requires country-specific phone keywords with template/noise exclusion. The literal +44 prefix improves precision when present but is not by itself sufficient gating.

should_match.description: Ofcom-reserved London geographic drama number (020 7946 0XXX range)
Ofcom-reserved 01632 geographic drama number for areas without a specific reserved code
Ofcom-reserved mobile drama number (07700 900XXX range)
International +44 form of the London drama number, leading 0 dropped
Parenthesised-area-code national notation (E.123), London drama number
Parenthesised 5-digit area code (leading 0 + 4 significant digits), Ofcom-reserved drama code
Widespread "+CC (0)" letterhead rendering — nonstandard per E.123 but ubiquitous in UK signatures
07624 Isle of Man mobile range (UK-plan mobile block inside 076), illustrative synthetic value — no Ofcom drama range exists for 07624

should_not_match.description: Non-geographic 03 service number — out of scope for this pattern (see description)
070 is personal-numbering, not mobile — second digit 0 is excluded from the mobile set
One digit short of the required 10 significant digits after the leading 0
Valid-shaped digit run embedded inside a longer reference number, rejected by digit boundaries
Parenthesised area-code notation does not open the door to 03 non-geographic service numbers
Year-like parenthetical followed by digits — parenthesised branch requires a leading-0 geographic code
0763x is radiopaging — only the 07624 Isle of Man block inside 076 is a mobile range

false_positives.description: An 11-digit UK-shaped domestic sequence (geographic or mobile prefix, correct leading digits) can still coincidentally match invoice numbers, order numbers, or other structured identifiers of the same length and leading-digit distribution.
false_positives.mitigation: Every tier — for both the domestic and +44 international sub-regexes — requires positive phone-context or country-specific evidence within 300 characters; no zero-evidence tier exists, so a bare digit run without corroborating context never fires at any confidence level.

false_positives.description: The flexible per-digit separator allows unusual spacing patterns beyond the conventional group boundaries (e.g. a digit-by-digit hyphenated form), which slightly over-generalises acceptable formatting in exchange for covering Ofcom's multiple valid grouping conventions (4+6, 3+7, 2+8, 5+5).
false_positives.mitigation: Corroborative evidence and noise-exclusion gating apply regardless of internal spacing; the structural leading-digit constraints are unaffected by separator placement.

patterns.risk_description: The regex identifies UK geographic and mobile formats, including common parenthesized area codes, international +44 notation, and Isle of Man 07624 mobiles, rather than proving ownership or current service. A real number can enable nuisance calls, phishing, messaging-account discovery, or correlation with a person's workplace or address. The normal unit is one contact and practical harm usually requires a name, vulnerable status, or account relationship; UK-shaped order numbers and flexible separator forms can produce false positives. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL reflect bounded standalone harm, while a confidential protected contact, sensitive case association, or bulk directory would warrant SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, and Low because one UK phone number provides contactability but not identity proof, account access, or a complete personal record. SENSITIVE is not met without vulnerable-person context, a sensitive service or case, persistent targeting, or aggregation causing moderate direct harm.

generic.rationale: Low with Low DLM fits an ordinary UK contact number whose misuse is generally limited and reversible. Protected contacts or bulk linked directories require higher controls.

ITU-T Recommendation E.123: Notation for national and international telephone numbers — national notation with parenthesised area code; the international "(0)" trunk-digit form is documented as common practice that E.123 advises against

Contains address keyword 'road'

classification.rationale: Risk 3 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, and Low tiers because broad English address vocabulary does not establish United Kingdom jurisdiction or a private resident. generic.rationale: United Kingdom address cues are generically Low with Low DLM because ordinary public and business locations dominate unless postcode, occupancy, and personal context converge.

patterns.name: UK Sort Code and Account Number
patterns.description: Detects the paired UK domestic bank sort code (6 digits, written XX-XX-XX, XX XX XX, or XXXXXX) and account number (8 digits) as they normally appear together in UK bank-detail blocks (invoices, remittance advice, payroll/BACS instructions). Both digit groups must be directly attached to their own label ("sort code" / "account number" or "a/c no") in either order — bare unlabelled 6- or 8-digit sequences are never matched, because unlabelled digit sequences of this length collide heavily with dates, phone extensions, invoice numbers, and other structured identifiers.
patterns.operation: Validation: none available as a single generic Purview function. UK modulus checking (Mod 10 / Mod 11 / DB1A1) is prescribed per-bank via weighting tables published by Vocalink/Pay.UK, not a universal algorithm, so no Func_ validator exists for this pairing. Reference: Pay.UK Clearing Code Rules; SWIFT/ISO 13616 GB IBAN structure (4a 6n 8n), which independently confirms the 6-digit sort code + 8-digit account number split. Corroborative evidence: keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: data-record-context.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: both digit groups are structurally anchored to their own label in either order, which materially reduces collision with unrelated digit sequences compared to a bare-digits pattern, but there is no checksum validator to confirm the sort code / account number combination is actually payable (UK modulus checking requires per-bank weight tables that are not expressible as a single Purview function). Evidence tiers exist for reliable production use; there is deliberately no bare/unlabelled 65 tier.

should_match.description: Hyphenated sort code followed by labelled account number
Compact unhyphenated digits with abbreviated account label, sort code first
Reversed order — account number labelled before sort code

should_not_match.value: Sort Code: 12-34-56
should_not_match.description: Sort code alone with no account number anywhere nearby

should_not_match.value: Account Number: 12345678
should_not_match.description: Account number alone with no sort code anywhere nearby

should_not_match.value: Invoice number 12345678 dated 12-34-56
should_not_match.description: Two digit groups of the right shape but attached to unrelated labels (invoice/date, not sort code/account)

false_positives.description: A 6-digit date-like or reference-like token near an unrelated 8-digit invoice/case number could in principle appear close together in a document without being real bank details.
false_positives.mitigation: The regex requires the literal "sort code" label directly attached to the 6-digit group and the literal "account number"/"a/c no" label directly attached to the 8-digit group — bare digits next to unrelated labels (as in the should_not_match example above) do not match.

false_positives.description: No modulus-check validator is available as a generic Purview function, so a structurally-matching sort code / account number pair is not confirmed to be a real, payable combination.
false_positives.mitigation: Rely on the paired label-embedded regex plus evidence/noise-exclusion tiers; consider a downstream per-bank modulus check (Vocalink/Pay.UK weighting tables) for authoritative validation.

patterns.risk_description: The detector finds a labelled UK six-digit sort code paired within 60 characters with a labelled eight-digit account number, in either order. The pair can identify a payment destination and support invoice fraud or targeted impersonation, but it does not confirm a payable combination, identify the holder, or provide transaction authority. The normal exposure is low and correlation-dependent because UK bank details are routinely shared for receiving payments and misuse requires additional identity or mandate information. Risk 4 and OFFICIAL are appropriate, while a holder-linked instruction, direct-debit mandate, balance, or credential set would warrant SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 4 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, and the OFFICIAL DLM because the matched sort-code and account-number pair is a payment destination, not proof of ownership or authority. SENSITIVE is not met without holder linkage, transaction history, mandate data, or authentication material.

generic.rationale: Low generic classification and Low DLM fit a labelled UK payment-routing pair that needs additional personal or authorisation context for material harm.

generic.rationale: The UK UTR is generically Low with Low DLM because meaningful tax or identity misuse requires a confirmed taxpayer and additional fiscal or account data.

patterns.name: UK VAT Number
patterns.description: Detects United Kingdom (and Northern Ireland XI) Value Added Tax registration numbers. Standard trader numbers are GB followed by 9 digits; branch traders use GB plus 12 digits; government departments use GBGD### and health authorities GBHA###. Northern Ireland post-Brexit issues XI-prefixed numbers with the same body formats. Matching is uppercase letter prefixes as issued by HMRC.
patterns.operation: Structural detection of HMRC VAT formats (GB/XI + 9 digits, 12 digits, GD###, or HA###). Checksum (mod-97 weighted) is not enforced in the regex — require corroborative evidence. Corroborative evidence: VAT-specific keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: vat-numbers, tax-id.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence when keywords such as "VAT number" or "VAT registration" appear nearby. The GB/XI prefix plus fixed digit lengths sharply reduce incidental matches versus bare digit runs.

should_match.description: Standard 9-digit GB VAT
12-digit branch trader VAT
Government department GD format
Northern Ireland XI VAT

should_not_match.description: Only 8 digits after GB
French VAT prefix, not UK

should_not_match.value: GBABC123456
should_not_match.description: Letters in numeric body

false_positives.description: Product SKUs or ticket codes starting with GB plus digits in logistics systems.
false_positives.mitigation: Require VAT/registration keywords within proximity; layer with invoice/tax document context.

false_positives.description: IBAN or other GB-prefixed financial strings with different lengths.
false_positives.mitigation: Fixed length classes (9/12/GD/HA) exclude most IBAN bodies; use IBAN SIT for accounts.

patterns.risk_description: This regex identifies a UK or Northern Ireland VAT registration number in standard trader, branch, government-department, or health-authority format, making the match a business registration identifier rather than a tax return. The number commonly appears on invoices and registration certificates and can assist invoice impersonation or company profiling, but misuse requires counterparty, payment, or account context. Fixed prefixes and VAT keywords improve precision, although GB-prefixed logistics codes can collide. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL fit the bounded standalone harm; SENSITIVE would require confidential tax assessments, person-linked financial facts, payment instructions, or an attributable fraud file.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, and Low tiers because a VAT number is a semi-public business registration reference. SENSITIVE is not met without confidential financial, taxpayer, payment, or fraud context.

generic.rationale: A UK VAT registration number is generically Low with Low DLM because it identifies a trader but does not disclose tax filings or authorise transactions.

patterns.name: U.S. Alien Registration Number (A-Number)
patterns.description: Detects USCIS Alien Registration Numbers (A-Numbers). An A-Number is the unique identifier the Department of Homeland Security assigns to a noncitizen: the letter "A" followed by 7-9 digits, written compactly (A012345678) or grouped (A-123-456-789). A-Numbers appear on Green Cards, EADs, immigration court records, and Form I-9 / E-Verify data held by virtually every U.S. employer.
patterns.operation: Two regexes. The first matches a grouped A-Number with optional separators (A-123-456-789, A 12 345 678). The second matches a compact "A" + 8-9 digit body. Corroborative immigration keywords within 300 characters reduce false positives from the broad numeric body.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the mandatory "A" prefix plus a fixed 8-9 digit body and the optional grouping structure make this distinctive. Corroborative USCIS/immigration keywords are recommended because an "A" followed by digits can appear in unrelated reference codes.

should_match.description: Labelled compact 9-digit A-Number
Grouped A-Number with hyphen separators
Compact 8-digit A-Number with USCIS label

should_not_match.description: Only 7 digits after A in compact form (below the 8-digit minimum)
Two leading letters, not a single "A" prefix

should_not_match.value: Please review the alien registration policy before the meeting
should_not_match.description: Prose mentioning alien registration with no number value

false_positives.description: Internal reference codes, asset tags, or invoice numbers of the form "A" + 8-9 digits in logistics or accounting systems unrelated to immigration.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative USCIS/immigration keywords (alien number, green card, Form I-9, USCIS) within the proximity window to confirm an immigration-records context.

false_positives.description: Catalogue or part numbers in technical documentation that share the A+digits shape.
false_positives.mitigation: Combine with document-type detection (HR / immigration forms) and placeholder-marker exclusion.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex finds a USCIS A-Number as the letter A followed by an eight- or nine-digit body, with optional grouping and immigration context. A genuine A-Number persistently links a noncitizen across Green Cards, employment authorisation, immigration court, Form I-9, and E-Verify records, enabling identity fraud or targeted exploitation of immigration status. The normal unit concerns one person and creates credible moderate privacy and legal harm, although it does not authenticate access to DHS systems. Risk 7 and SENSITIVE are justified, while PROTECTED is not met without a complete immigration file, authentication factors, protected-person status, or broad government compromise.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 aligns with PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, and SENSITIVE Personal-Privacy because an A-Number is a persistent immigration identifier with direct identity and status misuse potential. PROTECTED is not met because the identifier alone neither grants access nor establishes severe or large-scale harm.

generic.rationale: Medium generic classification and Medium Personal-Privacy DLM fit a unique noncitizen identifier with moderate direct misuse potential but no authentication capability.

patterns.name: U.S. Bank Account Number
patterns.description: Detects U.S. Bank Account Number patterns. This pattern is based on a Microsoft Purview built-in sensitive information type. Financial account numbers require corroborative evidence for reliable detection due to their generic numeric format.
patterns.operation: Corroborative evidence: 6 keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: banking, us-financial.
patterns.confidence_justification: Low confidence: eight to seventeen digit numbers are extremely common in all contexts. Banking keywords such as 'account number' or 'checking' are essential for reliable US bank account detection.

should_match.description: Eight-digit US bank account number
Seventeen-digit US bank account number
Ten-digit US bank account

should_not_match.description: Seven digits, too short for US bank account
Eighteen digits, exceeds US bank account format

false_positives.description: Generic numeric sequences such as reference numbers, invoice numbers, or identifiers from other domains
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords within the proximity window to distinguish financial account numbers from general numeric data.

false_positives.description: Phone numbers, postal codes, or other structured numbers with similar digit counts
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with other detection patterns to deprioritise matches that overlap with phone number or postal code formats.

patterns.risk_description: The detector seeks a US bank-account-shaped numeric sequence with six banking terms, without a universal checksum that can independently validate the account. A real number can reveal a financial relationship and support unauthorised debit attempts, payment diversion, or tailored impersonation when combined with a holder name and routing number. Invoice references, phone-like values, postal codes, and other structured numbers can match, and the account number alone usually does not confer online-banking access. Risk 8 SENSITIVE reflects serious but account-bounded harm; PROTECTED would require bulk records, direct payment authority, or significant damage.

classification.rationale: Risk 8 aligns with OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, SENSITIVE Financial, SENS_Fin, and Medium because an authentic US account number can materially support fraud. Its low-confidence generic format and lack of direct authority mean the normal unit does not satisfy PROTECTED.

generic.rationale: Generic Medium and Medium Financial handling fit one banking identifier with serious contained misuse potential. Generic High requires aggregation, authentication, or payment-authorising data beyond the number.

patterns.name: U.S. National Security Classification Banner
patterns.description: Detects U.S. national-security classification banner and portion markings (per Executive Order 13526 and the Intelligence Community marking system): a classification level — TOP SECRET, SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL — followed by one or more "//"-separated control or dissemination markings (SI, TK, HCS, SCI, SAP, NOFORN, ORCON, REL TO ...), or a parenthetical portion mark such as (S//NF) or (TS//SI). The bare words "secret" and "confidential" are far too common to match alone, so a match requires the "//" control structure or a parenthetical portion mark.
patterns.operation: Two Purview-safe regexes (no groups containing multi-match .*/.+/.{n} or REL TO[class]+). Banner: level//control with up to four additional //control segments as fixed-token alts, plus a separate REL TO [A-Z]{2,5} branch. Portion mark: (level//control…) with the same bounded //control repeats. Keywords within 300 characters.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the "//" control structure and the parenthetical portion-mark syntax are unique to U.S. classification banners. Requiring the structure prevents the common English words "secret" and "confidential" from triggering matches.

should_not_match.value: This information is secret and must stay confidential
CONFIDENTIAL business plan attached
CUI//SP-PRVCY//NOFORN

false_positives.description: Templates, training decks, or marking guides that quote example banners (TOP SECRET//SI) for instructional purposes rather than marking real classified content.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative classification keywords (declassify on, derived from, portion marking) and exclude known training-material file paths.

false_positives.description: Fiction, news reporting, or historical documents reproducing classification banners.
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with document-source metadata to distinguish operational documents from published/quoted content.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex detects structured United States national-security banners and portion marks such as TOP SECRET//SI//NOFORN, SECRET//REL TO, and bounded parenthetical control markings, identifying a marking signal rather than reading the underlying content. On a genuine operational document, the mark can denote intelligence sources, compartmented capabilities, foreign-release restrictions, or defence operations whose unauthorised transfer could cause significant national-security damage. Training decks, marking guides, news, fiction, and historical reproductions may quote the same syntax, so document source remains important despite the distinctive structure. Risk 9, PROTECTED, and Marking Protected treatment are justified for an authentic classified marking; PROTECTED is already the highest accepted QGISCF tier.

classification.rationale: Risk 9 aligns with PSPF PROTECTED, QGISCF PROTECTED, Marking Protected DLM, and High because a genuine structured banner signals national-security controls with credible significant-damage consequences. The classification is already at the highest accepted tier; false-positive context affects enforcement confidence rather than lowering an authentic marking.

generic.rationale: High Government handling is appropriate for a genuine national-security classification marking, while quoted training or published examples require contextual release rather than weaker classification.

references.title: Authorized Classification and Control Markings Register - ODNI
DoD Manual 5200.01 Vol 2 - Marking of Classified Information

patterns.name: U.S. CUI Banner Marking (32 CFR 2002)
patterns.description: Detects Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) banner and portion markings as defined by 32 CFR 2002.20 and the NARA CUI Registry. A CUI banner is the control marking "CUI" optionally followed by category markings (CUI//SP-PRVCY) and limited-dissemination controls (//NOFORN, //FEDCON, //FED ONLY, //NOCON, //DL ONLY, //REL TO ...), with elements separated by double slashes. The bare token "CUI" is too common to match alone, so a match requires either the "//" banner structure or the spelled-out phrase "Controlled Unclassified Information".
patterns.operation: Two regexes. The first matches a structured CUI banner: "CUI" with at least one "//" category or limited-dissemination segment. The second matches the spelled-out control phrase "Controlled Unclassified Information". Corroborative handling keywords within 300 characters reinforce the marking context.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: the "//" banner structure and the registry-defined dissemination tokens are highly specific to CUI markings, and the spelled-out phrase is unambiguous. Requiring structure or the full phrase eliminates matches on the bare three-letter token "CUI".

should_match.description: Full CUI banner with privacy category and NOFORN dissemination control
CUI banner with category and FEDCON control

should_match.value: This document contains Controlled Unclassified Information per agency policy
should_match.description: Spelled-out CUI control phrase

should_not_match.value: The cui dataset was uploaded to the cluster
should_not_match.description: Bare token "cui" with no banner structure or full phrase

should_not_match.value: SECRET//NOFORN
should_not_match.description: National-security classification banner, not a CUI marking

should_not_match.value: Please review the controlled access list before the meeting
should_not_match.description: Prose using "controlled" without the CUI phrase or banner

false_positives.description: Strings of the shape "CUI//..." appearing in unrelated path-like or URL-like text where slashes separate uppercase tokens.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative CUI handling keywords (controlled unclassified information, limited dissemination, designating authority) within the proximity window.

false_positives.description: Training material or policy documents quoting CUI marking examples rather than applying them.
false_positives.mitigation: Combine with document-classification metadata and exclude known example/training file paths.

patterns.risk_description: This high-confidence regex finds a structured U.S. CUI banner such as CUI//SP-PRVCY//NOFORN or the full phrase Controlled Unclassified Information; it detects a handling marking rather than the protected facts beneath it. Improper release can breach federal safeguarding or dissemination controls, expose privacy, law-enforcement, or infrastructure material, and jeopardise an agency or contractor relationship. The marking establishes controlled government content but not significant damage from every document, and training examples remain possible. Risk 7 supports SENSITIVE marking treatment; PROTECTED would require a category, caveat, operation, or underlying record whose compromise credibly causes major strategic, safety, or system-scale harm.

classification.rationale: Risk 7 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL: Sensitive, QGISCF SENSITIVE, the Marking Sensitive DLM, and Medium because CUI denotes controlled but unclassified government information. PROTECTED is not met by the banner alone without high-consequence contents, protected operations, safety impact, or significant systemic damage.

generic.rationale: A genuine CUI banner is generically Medium with Medium Government DLM because it imposes controlled handling while the underlying category determines any higher consequence.

patterns.name: DEA
patterns.description: Detects DEA patterns. This pattern is based on a Microsoft Purview built-in sensitive information type. Users already running Purview may prefer to enable the built-in SIT directly, or use this version as a starting point for customisation.
patterns.operation: Validation: Checksum: (d1+d3+d5) + 2*(d2+d4+d6). Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DEA_number Corroborative evidence: 19 keywords within 300 characters. Keyword lists: healthcare-identifiers, au-healthcare-medications.
patterns.confidence_justification: High confidence: validated with Checksum: (d1+d3+d5) + 2*(d2+d4+d6) and supported by corroborative keyword evidence.

should_match.description: Standard DEA number
DEA with F prefix
Mid-level practitioner DEA

should_not_match.description: Invalid first character (C not in valid set A/B/F/G/M/P/R/X)
Only 6 digits instead of 7
8 digits instead of 7

false_positives.description: Medical terminology in health education materials, research publications, clinical guidelines, or public health documents without patient-specific data.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative evidence keywords confirming patient context. Look for co-occurrence with patient identifiers such as medical record numbers or dates of birth.

false_positives.description: General wellness and fitness content using medical vocabulary without constituting protected health information.
false_positives.mitigation: Layer with patient identifier patterns or healthcare-specific document structure detection to distinguish clinical records from general health content.

patterns.risk_description: The high-confidence regex recognizes a US DEA registration-number structure with checksum validation and healthcare or medication context; it identifies a registered prescriber or organization, not a prescription pad or signing credential. A valid number can be reused in forged controlled-substance paperwork or provider impersonation, but successful diversion also needs the registrant's name, signature, prescribing details, and a willing processing channel. The normal unit is one professional registration reference, some of which can be verified through legitimate healthcare workflows. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL reflect bounded fraud-enablement value, while a complete prescriber identity package or active diversion record would be SENSITIVE.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 maps to PSPF OFFICIAL, QGISCF OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL DLM, and Low because a DEA number alone neither authorizes dispensing nor supplies a complete prescription. SENSITIVE is not met without correlated prescriber identity, signature, drug, patient, or transaction data capable of moderate direct harm.

generic.rationale: Low with Low DLM fits one validated professional registration reference with limited independent exploitability. Prescribing credentials or fraud packages require stronger handling.

patterns.name: U.S. Driver's License Number (Multi-State)
patterns.description: A multi-state helper for detecting U.S. driver's license numbers using the real structural formats of several high-population states, rather than the broad "letter + 7-12 digits" catch-all. Covers California, New York, Texas, Florida, New Jersey, and Illinois. This is a companion to the generic us-drivers-license pattern (which it does not replace); use it when you want tighter, state-aware matching for those jurisdictions.
patterns.operation: An alternation of state-specific formats: CA (1 letter + 7 digits), NY (1 letter + 18 digits, or 8-9 digits), TX (8 digits), FL (1 letter + 12 digits), NJ (1 letter + 14 digits), IL (1 letter + 11-12 digits). Purely numeric formats are ambiguous, so corroborative DMV/license keywords within 300 characters are strongly recommended.
patterns.confidence_justification: Medium confidence: the letter-prefixed state formats are structurally distinctive, but the purely numeric NY/TX formats (8-9 digits) overlap with generic numbers, so corroborative DMV keywords are required for reliable detection.

should_match.description: California format — 1 letter + 7 digits
Florida format — 1 letter + 12 digits
New Jersey format — 1 letter + 14 digits

should_not_match.description: Six digits — too few for any covered numeric state format
Two leading letters — no covered state uses a two-letter prefix

should_not_match.value: Please bring your driver's license to the DMV appointment
should_not_match.description: Prose about a driver's license with no number value

false_positives.description: Generic 8-9 digit numbers (order IDs, account numbers, ZIP+4 concatenations) that collide with the numeric NY/TX formats.
false_positives.mitigation: Require corroborative DMV/driver-license keywords within the proximity window; prefer the letter-prefixed state formats which are far more distinctive.

false_positives.description: Letter-prefixed product codes or part numbers that coincide with a state license length.
false_positives.mitigation: Combine with state-name or DMV context keywords and exclude known catalogue/SKU document types.

patterns.risk_description: This companion detector applies specific California, New York, Texas, Florida, New Jersey, and Illinois licence formats instead of the generic national catch-all; it still finds only a licence number, not a card or DMV file. A true value can strengthen rental, insurer, or identity-verification impersonation when the driver's name, state, address, and birth date are also known. The state-aware letter forms are relatively distinctive, but the eight- and nine-digit New York and Texas branches overlap account, order, and ZIP-derived numbers. Risk 5 and OFFICIAL fit the isolated identifier; SENSITIVE would require card imagery, credentials, or linked personal and driving records.

classification.rationale: Risk 5 with PSPF and QGISCF OFFICIAL reflects improved state-level precision without changing the bounded harm of one US licence number. SENSITIVE is not met without confirmed holder and state context, document content, authentication factors, or a substantive DMV record.

generic.rationale: The generic Low outcome recognises a more precise licence detector while keeping the standalone identifier below the threshold for material direct harm.

patterns.name: U.S. FERPA Student Education Record ID
patterns.description: Detects student identifiers that appear in education records protected under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA). Student ID formats are institution-specific, so this pattern anchors on an explicit student/enrolment/SIS context label immediately preceding a 6-12 character alphanumeric ID, and relies on education-record keywords (transcript, GPA, enrollment, registrar) for corroboration.
patterns.operation: Matches a "student id"/"student number"/"SIS id"/"enrollment id" context label followed by a 6-12 character alphanumeric ID. The label is part of the primary regex; corroborative FERPA education-record keywords within 300 characters confirm the academic context. Purview tiers: labelled student/SIS/enrollment IDs are discovery-only at 65 without education-record context; 75 requires education-record keywords (transcript/GPA/registrar/…); 85 requires two unique education-record hits. Bare labelled IDs without academic context no longer enforce. Template/training markers and conflicting employee/customer/ member ID labels are modelled as keyword NOT evidence on both tiers.
